### EQ-SYS-CCF-002 — Multiple Greek letter model

`Q_k = (prod_{i=1}^k rho_i)(1 - rho_(k+1)) Q_t / C(m - 1, k - 1)` with
`rho_1 = 1`, `rho_2 = beta`, `rho_3 = gamma`, ..., `rho_(m+1) = 0`.

- Domain: symmetric group; factors in `[0, 1]`.
- Meaning: conditional probabilities that a failure is shared by further
  members.
- Code: `systems.MultipleGreekLetterGroup`.
- Source: [REF-MOSLEH-ETAL-1998], [REF-MOSLEH-ETAL-1988].

### EQ-SYS-CCF-003 — Alpha-factor model

Non-staggered testing:
`Q_k = k / C(m - 1, k - 1) * alpha_k / alpha_t * Q_t`,
`alpha_t = sum_k k alpha_k`; staggered testing:
`Q_k = alpha_k Q_t / C(m - 1, k - 1)`.

- Domain: `alpha_k >= 0`, `sum_k alpha_k = 1`.
- Meaning: `alpha_k` is the fraction of failure events in the group that
  involve exactly `k` members.
- Code: `systems.AlphaFactorGroup`.
- Source: [REF-MOSLEH-ETAL-1998], [REF-MOSLEH-ETAL-1988].

### EQ-SYS-CCF-004 — CCF normalisation

`Q_t = sum_{k=1}^m C(m - 1, k - 1) Q_k^(m)`.

- Domain: every parametric model above.
- Meaning: a member's total failure probability is the (rare-event) sum of
  the probabilities of the basic events that fail it.
- Code: `systems.normalisation`.
- Source: [REF-MOSLEH-ETAL-1998].

### EQ-SYS-CCF-005 — Exact CCF expansion

Member `i` fails iff `IND[i]` or some `CCF[S]` with `i in S`, `|S| >= 2`,
occurs; all events independent with `P(CCF[S]) = Q_|S|`; the member's
marginal is `1 - prod_k (1 - Q_k)^C(m - 1, k - 1) <= Q_t`.

- Domain: symmetric groups, disjoint, members share `Q_t`.
- Meaning: the expanded structure over basic events is evaluated exactly by
  the BDD.
- Code: `systems.expand_common_cause`, `systems.SystemModel`.
- Source: [REF-MOSLEH-ETAL-1998].

### EQ-SYS-MTTF-001 — Mean time to failure

`MTTF = int_0^inf R(t) dt`.

- Domain: non-repairable mission reliability with `R(t) -> 0`.
- Meaning: expected system life; evaluated by adaptive double-exponential
  or Gauss-Kronrod quadrature with an error estimate. Closed forms used as
  checks: series `1 / sum lambda_i`, parallel
  `1/lambda_1 + 1/lambda_2 - 1/(lambda_1 + lambda_2)`.
- Code: `systems.SystemModel.mttf`, `systems.MTTFResult`.
- Source: [REF-RAUSAND-HOYLAND-2004], [REF-PIESSENS-QUADPACK-1983].

### EQ-SYS-PMS-001 — Phased-mission reliability

`R_mission = P(AND_j phi_j(x_{., j}) = 1)` with `x_{i,j} = [j < K_i]`;
`P(K_i = j) = prod_{l<j} s_{i,l} (1 - s_{i,j})` (per-phase models,
`s_{i,j} = R_{i,j}(d_j)`) or `R_i(T_{j-1}) - R_i(T_j)` (one model on the
cumulative time `T_j`); `P(K_i = J + 1)` is the survival probability.

- Domain: non-repairable components, monotone phase structures,
  instantaneous phase changes, independent components.
- Meaning: exact mission success probability; evaluated on a BDD with
  component-major order by enumerating each component's phase of failure at
  the first node of its variable block.
- Code: `systems.PhasedMission`, `systems.Phase`,
  `systems.PhasedMissionResult`.
- Source: [REF-ZANG-SUN-TRIVEDI-1999].

### EQ-SYS-CCF-006 — Time-dependent CCF split (hazard or probability basis)

Probability basis: `Q_k(t) = c_k Q_t(t)`. Hazard basis: with the member's
cumulative hazard `H(t) = -log(1 - Q_t(t))`, `Q_k(t) = 1 - exp(-c_k H(t))`,
so that `1 - prod_k (1 - Q_k)^C(m - 1, k - 1) = Q_t(t)` exactly (by
EQ-SYS-CCF-004); for exponential members this is the rate split
`lambda_k = c_k lambda` (beta factor: `lambda_CCF = beta lambda`).

- Domain: symmetric groups; the two bases agree to first order in `Q_t`.
- Meaning: the hazard basis keeps each member's marginal failure probability
  equal to `Q_t(t)` over long missions (default for mission reliability);
  the probability basis is the NUREG/CR-5485 convention for demand and
  unavailability probabilities (default for availability).
- Code: `systems.SystemModel`, `systems.SystemModel.event_probabilities`.
- Source: [REF-MOSLEH-ETAL-1998], [REF-RAUSAND-HOYLAND-2004].

## Input-law expressiveness: copulas, discrete inputs, epistemic separation (ADR-0064)

### EQ-MOD-COP-SKLAR-001 — Sklar decomposition of a joint law

`F(x) = C(F_1(x_1), ..., F_d(x_d))`, `f(x) = c(u) prod_i f_i(x_i)` with
`u_i = F_i(x_i)` and `c = d^d C / du_1 ... du_d`.

- Domain: continuous marginals (the copula is then unique); for discrete
  marginals `C` is unique only on the range of `(F_1, ..., F_d)`.
- Meaning: separates the marginal laws from the dependence structure; every
  copula boundary condition `C(..., 0, ...) = 0` and `C(..., 1, ...)` = margin
  is used by `Copula.cdf`.
- Code: `modeling.Copula.cdf`, `modeling.Copula.log_density`,
  `modeling.JointInput.log_pdf`.
- Source: [REF-NELSEN-2006, Section 2.3].

### EQ-MOD-COP-ROSEN-001 — Rosenblatt transformation

`w_1 = u_1`, `w_k = C(u_k | u_1, ..., u_{k-1}) = P(U_k <= u_k | U_<k = u_<k)`;
standard space `u'_k = Phi^-1(w_k)`. The inverse solves each conditional for
`u_k` in turn (conditional-inverse construction).

- Domain: `u` in `(0, 1)^d`; depends on the variable order. For the Gaussian
  copula it equals the Nataf map `Phi(L^-1 Phi^-1(u))`, whose FORM results do
  not depend on the order.
- Meaning: an exact isoprobabilistic map to independent uniforms (normals);
  FORM linearizes the limit state in this space, so FORM/SORM approximations
  can change with the order for non-Gaussian copulas.
- Code: `modeling.Copula.rosenblatt`, `modeling.Copula.inverse_rosenblatt`,
  `modeling.JointInput.to_standard_normal`,
  `modeling.JointInput.from_standard_normal`, `modeling.JointInput.from_unit`.
- Source: [REF-ROSENBLATT-1952], [REF-HOHENBICHLER-RACKWITZ-1981],
  [REF-LEBRUN-DUTFOY-2009].

### EQ-MOD-COP-TAU-001 — Population Kendall's tau of a copula

`tau = 4 E[C(U, V)] - 1`; elliptical copulas: `tau = (2/pi) arcsin(rho)`;
Archimedean: `tau = 1 + 4 int_0^1 phi(t)/phi'(t) dt`.

- Domain: bivariate margins of continuous laws.
- Meaning: a margin-free concordance measure in closed form for every family
  implemented here (the Archimedean integral is used as an independent check
  in the tests).
- Code: `modeling.Copula.kendall_tau`.
- Source: [REF-NELSEN-2006, Chapter 5], [REF-MCNEIL-FREY-EMBRECHTS-2015].

### EQ-MOD-COP-TAIL-001 — Tail-dependence coefficients

`lambda_L = lim_{q->0+} C(q, q) / q`,
`lambda_U = lim_{q->1-} (1 - 2q + C(q, q)) / (1 - q)`.

- Domain: bivariate margins.
- Meaning: probability of a joint extreme given one extreme; zero for the
  Gaussian and Frank copulas.
- Code: `modeling.Copula.tail_dependence`.
- Source: [REF-NELSEN-2006, Chapter 5], [REF-JOE-2014].

### EQ-MOD-COP-GAUSS-001 — Bivariate normal CDF by Plackett's identity

`Phi_2(a, b; rho) = Phi(a) Phi(b) + int_0^rho phi_2(a, b; r) dr` with
`phi_2(a, b; r) = exp(-(a^2 - 2abr + b^2) / (2(1 - r^2))) / (2 pi sqrt(1 - r^2))`.

- Domain: `|rho| < 1`, finite `a, b`; the integral is evaluated by adaptive
  Gauss-Kronrod quadrature (relative tolerance `1e-12`).
- Meaning: the bivariate Gaussian-copula CDF `C(u, v) = Phi_2(Phi^-1(u),
  Phi^-1(v); rho)`, derived from `d Phi_2 / d rho = phi_2`.
- Code: `modeling.GaussianCopula.cdf`.
- Source: [REF-PLACKETT-1954].

### EQ-MOD-COP-T-001 — Student-t copula density and stochastic representation

`log c(u) = lgamma((nu+d)/2) + (d-1) lgamma(nu/2) - d lgamma((nu+1)/2)
- (1/2) log det R - ((nu+d)/2) log(1 + x'R^-1 x / nu)
+ ((nu+1)/2) sum_i log(1 + x_i^2 / nu)`, `x_i = T_nu^-1(u_i)`;
samples `U = T_nu(L Z / sqrt(W / nu))`, `Z ~ N(0, I)`, `W ~ chi^2_nu`.

- Domain: `nu > 0` (not necessarily integer), `R` positive-definite
  correlation.
- Meaning: elliptical copula with symmetric tail dependence.
- Code: `modeling.StudentTCopula.log_density`, `modeling.StudentTCopula.sample`.
- Source: [REF-DEMARTA-MCNEIL-2005], [REF-MCNEIL-FREY-EMBRECHTS-2015].

### EQ-MOD-COP-T-002 — Sequential conditionals of the multivariate t

With `x = L y`, `q_k = sum_{j<k} y_j^2`:
`T_k = y_k sqrt((nu + k) / (nu + q_k)) ~ t_{nu+k}`, independent of
`y_<k`, so `w_k = T_{nu+k}(T_k)` (0-based `k`).

- Domain: as [EQ-MOD-COP-T-001].
- Meaning: the conditional law of a multivariate t given earlier
  coordinates is t with `nu + k` degrees of freedom and scale inflated by
  `(nu + q_k)/(nu + k)`; this gives the t-copula Rosenblatt map in closed form.
- Code: `modeling.StudentTCopula.rosenblatt`,
  `modeling.StudentTCopula.inverse_rosenblatt`.
- Source: [REF-DEMARTA-MCNEIL-2005], [REF-ROSENBLATT-1952].

### EQ-MOD-COP-T-003 — t-copula tail dependence

`lambda_L = lambda_U = 2 T_{nu+1}(-sqrt((nu + 1)(1 - rho)/(1 + rho)))`.

- Domain: `|rho| < 1`, `nu > 0`.
- Meaning: positive for every finite `nu` even when `rho = 0`.
- Code: `modeling.StudentTCopula.tail_dependence`.
- Source: [REF-DEMARTA-MCNEIL-2005].

### EQ-MOD-COP-ARCH-001 — Archimedean copula, density

`C(u) = psi(sum_i phi(u_i))`, `phi = psi^-1`,
`c(u) = |psi^(d)(t)| prod_i |phi'(u_i)|` with `t = sum_i phi(u_i)`.

- Domain: `psi` d-monotone (completely monotone for every `d`: Clayton
  `theta > 0`, Gumbel `theta >= 1`, Frank `theta > 0`; bivariate Frank also
  `theta < 0`).
- Meaning: exchangeable dependence from one generator; the CDF is closed
  form in every dimension.
- Code: `modeling.ArchimedeanCopula.cdf`,
  `modeling.ArchimedeanCopula.log_density`.
- Source: [REF-NELSEN-2006, Chapter 4], [REF-MCNEIL-FREY-EMBRECHTS-2015].

### EQ-MOD-COP-ARCH-002 — Archimedean conditional distributions

`C(u_k | u_1, ..., u_{k-1}) = psi^(k-1)(t_k) / psi^(k-1)(t_{k-1})`,
`t_k = sum_{i<=k} phi(u_i)`. The inverse solves
`log|psi^(k-1)(t_{k-1} + s)| - log|psi^(k-1)(t_{k-1})| = log w` for
`s = phi(u_k)` (closed form for Clayton, Brent's method on `log s` otherwise).

- Domain: as [EQ-MOD-COP-ARCH-001]; the left side decreases from 0 to
  `-inf` in `s`, so the root exists and is unique.
- Meaning: the Archimedean Rosenblatt map; a conditional probability within
  `epsilon` of one keeps only absolute accuracy `2^-53` in its complement.
- Code: `modeling.ArchimedeanCopula.rosenblatt`,
  `modeling.ArchimedeanCopula.inverse_rosenblatt`.
- Source: [REF-HOFERT-2008], [REF-ROSENBLATT-1952], [REF-BRENT-1973, Chapter 4].

### EQ-MOD-COP-ARCH-003 — Marshall-Olkin frailty sampling

`V ~ F` with Laplace transform `psi`, `E_i ~ Exp(1)` independent,
`U_i = psi(E_i / V)`.

- Domain: `psi` a Laplace transform (completely monotone generator).
- Meaning: an exact sampler using `d + 1` (or more) random numbers; used by
  `sample` and as an independent check of the conditional-inverse sampler
  that `JointInput.from_unit` uses.
- Code: `modeling.ArchimedeanCopula.sample`.
- Source: [REF-MARSHALL-OLKIN-1988], [REF-HOFERT-2008].

### EQ-MOD-COP-CLAYTON-001 — Clayton generator and properties

`psi(t) = (1 + t)^(-1/theta)`, `phi(u) = u^-theta - 1`,
`|psi^(k)(t)| = prod_{j<k} (1/theta + j) (1 + t)^(-1/theta - k)`,
conditional inverse `s = (1 + t_{k-1}) expm1(-log w / (1/theta + k - 1))`;
`tau = theta / (theta + 2)`, `lambda_L = 2^(-1/theta)`, `lambda_U = 0`;
frailty `V ~ Gamma(1/theta, 1)`.

- Domain: `theta > 0`, any dimension.
- Meaning: lower-tail dependence.
- Code: `modeling.ClaytonCopula`.
- Source: [REF-NELSEN-2006, Chapters 4-5], [REF-HOFERT-2008].

### EQ-MOD-COP-GUMBEL-001 — Gumbel generator, derivatives, and properties

`psi(t) = exp(-t^a)`, `a = 1/theta`, `phi(u) = (-log u)^theta`;
`|psi^(k)(t)| = e^(-t^a) sum_m a_km t^(m a - k)` with `a_00 = 1`,
`a_{k+1,m+1} += a a_km`, `a_{k+1,m} += (k - m a) a_km` (all terms
non-negative for `a <= 1`); `tau = 1 - 1/theta`, `lambda_U = 2 - 2^(1/theta)`,
`lambda_L = 0`.

- Domain: `theta >= 1` (`theta = 1` is independence), any dimension.
- Meaning: upper-tail dependence. The coefficient recursion follows from
  differentiating `e^(-t^a) t^(m a - k)` (derived for this library and
  verified against mpmath derivatives of the CDF).
- Code: `modeling.GumbelCopula`.
- Source: [REF-NELSEN-2006, Chapters 4-5], [REF-HOFERT-MACHLER-MCNEIL-2012].

### EQ-MOD-COP-GUMBEL-002 — Positive stable frailty (Kanter's representation)

`V = sin(a U) sin((1 - a) U)^((1-a)/a) / (sin(U)^(1/a) E^((1-a)/a))` with
`U ~ Uniform(0, pi)`, `E ~ Exp(1)`, has `E[exp(-t V)] = exp(-t^a)`.

- Domain: `0 < a < 1` (`a = 1` gives `V = 1`).
- Meaning: the Gumbel frailty for [EQ-MOD-COP-ARCH-003].
- Code: `modeling.GumbelCopula.sample`.
- Source: [REF-KANTER-1975], [REF-CHAMBERS-MALLOWS-STUCK-1976],
  [REF-HOFERT-2008].

### EQ-MOD-COP-FRANK-001 — Frank generator, derivatives, and properties

`psi(t) = -log(1 - (1 - e^-theta) e^-t) / theta`,
`phi(u) = -log(expm1(-theta u) / expm1(-theta))`;
`psi^(k)(t) = (-1)^k Li_{1-k}(x) / theta`, `x = (1 - e^-theta) e^-t`, with
`Li_0(x) = x/(1-x)` and `Li_{-n}(x) = x P_n(x) / (1 - x)^(n+1)`, `P_n` the
Eulerian polynomial `sum_j A(n, j) x^j`; `tau = 1 + 4 (D_1(theta) - 1)/theta`,
no tail dependence.

- Domain: `theta != 0` for `d = 2`, `theta > 0` for `d >= 3`; `|theta| <= 700`.
- Meaning: symmetric, tail-independent dependence of either sign (bivariate).
- Code: `modeling.FrankCopula`, `modeling.frank_tau`.
- Source: [REF-NELSEN-2006, Chapters 4-5], [REF-NIST-DLMF, Sections 25.12
  and 26.14].

### EQ-MOD-COP-FRANK-002 — Logarithmic frailty (Kemp's algorithm LK)

`P(V = k) = p^k / (-k log(1 - p))`, `p = 1 - e^-theta`; with `U, V'` uniform:
return 1 if `V' >= p`; else `q = 1 - (1 - p)^U` and return
`floor(1 + log V' / log q)` if `V' < q^2`, 1 if `V' > q`, else 2.

- Domain: `0 < p < 1`.
- Meaning: the Frank frailty for [EQ-MOD-COP-ARCH-003]
  (`E[e^(-tV)] = psi(t)`).
- Code: `modeling.FrankCopula.sample`.
- Source: [REF-KEMP-1981], [REF-DEVROYE-1986, Chapter X].

### EQ-MOD-COP-DEBYE-001 — First Debye function

`D_1(x) = (1/x) int_0^x t / (e^t - 1) dt`; for `|x| < 2`
`(D_1(x) - 1)/x = -1/4 + sum_{k>=1} B_2k x^(2k-1) / ((2k + 1)(2k)!)`;
for `x >= 2` `int_0^x = pi^2/6 - sum_{k>=1} e^(-kx)(x/k + 1/k^2)`;
`D_1(-x) = D_1(x) + x/2`.

- Domain: real `x`; Bernoulli numbers `B_n` (with `B_1 = -1/2`) from
  `sum_{j<=m} C(m+1, j) B_j = 0` in exact rational arithmetic.
- Meaning: Kendall's tau of the Frank copula without cancellation near
  `theta = 0` (`tau ~ theta/9`).
- Code: `modeling.frank_tau`, `modeling.FrankCopula.kendall_tau`.
- Source: [REF-NIST-DLMF, Sections 24.2 and 24.5], [REF-NELSEN-2006, Chapter 5].

### EQ-MOD-COP-NCM-001 — Nearest correlation matrix (alternating projections)

`Delta S_0 = 0`, `Y_0 = A`; repeat `R_k = Y_k - Delta S_k`,
`X_k = P_S(R_k)`, `Delta S_{k+1} = X_k - R_k`, `Y_{k+1} = P_U(X_k)`, where
`P_S` clips eigenvalues below `delta` and `P_U` sets the diagonal to one.

- Domain: symmetric `A`; `delta` in `[0, 1)`; stop when
  `||Y_{k+1} - Y_k||_F <= tol ||Y_{k+1}||_F`.
- Meaning: Dykstra-corrected projections converge to the Frobenius-nearest
  unit-diagonal matrix with eigenvalues at least `delta`; used to repair
  pairwise latent correlations that are not jointly positive definite.
- Code: `modeling.nearest_correlation_matrix`, `modeling.JointInput.from_pearson`,
  `modeling.JointInput.from_spearman`, `modeling.JointInput.from_kendall`,
  `modeling.fit_copula`.
- Source: [REF-HIGHAM-NCM-2002].

### EQ-MOD-COPULA-FIT-003 — Sample Kendall's tau-b

`tau_b = (n_c - n_d) / sqrt((n_0 - n_1)(n_0 - n_2))`, `n_0 = n(n-1)/2`.

- Domain: `n >= 2`, neither sample constant; direct `O(n^2)` pair count.
- Meaning: rank concordance with a tie correction; equals tau-a without ties.
- Code: `modeling.kendall_tau`.
- Source: [REF-KENDALL-1938], [REF-HOLLANDER-WOLFE-CHICKEN-2014, Chapter 8].

### EQ-MOD-COPULA-FIT-004 — Archimedean tau inversion

Clayton `theta = 2 tau / (1 - tau)`; Gumbel `theta = 1 / (1 - tau)`; Frank
solves `1 + 4 (D_1(theta) - 1)/theta = tau`; multivariate exchangeable fits
use the average pairwise sample tau.

- Domain: Clayton `tau > 0`, Gumbel `tau >= 0`, Frank `tau != 0`
  (`tau > 0` for `d >= 3`).
- Meaning: method-of-moments estimate of the dependence parameter from ranks.
- Code: `modeling.archimedean_theta_from_tau`, `modeling.fit_copula`.
- Source: [REF-GENEST-RIVEST-1993], [REF-NELSEN-2006, Chapter 5].

### EQ-MOD-COPULA-FIT-005 — Kendall's tau to elliptical latent correlation

`rho = sin(pi tau / 2)`.

- Domain: `tau` in `[-1, 1]`; any elliptical copula (Gaussian, t).
- Meaning: inverts `tau = (2/pi) arcsin(rho)`.
- Code: `modeling.kendall_to_latent_correlation`, `modeling.JointInput.from_kendall`,
  `modeling.fit_copula`.
- Source: [REF-MCNEIL-FREY-EMBRECHTS-2015], [REF-DEMARTA-MCNEIL-2005].

### EQ-MOD-COPULA-FIT-006 — Maximum pseudo-likelihood

`theta_hat = argmax_theta sum_i log c(u_i; theta)`,
`u_ij = rank_ij / (n + 1)`.

- Domain: one-parameter families (Clayton, Gumbel, Frank; t-copula `nu`
  with `R` fixed from tau); grid scan then golden-section search over a
  bounded transformed range.
- Meaning: the rank-based (canonical maximum likelihood) estimator, consistent
  and asymptotically normal; the inverse pseudo-information understates its
  variance, so no standard error is reported.
- Code: `modeling.fit_copula`.
- Source: [REF-GENEST-GHOUDI-RIVEST-1995], [REF-BRENT-1973, Chapter 5],
  [REF-KIEFER-1953].

### EQ-MOD-DISC-001 — Distributional transform of a discrete input

`U = F(X-) + V (F(X) - F(X-))`, `V ~ Uniform(0, 1)` independent of `X`
(`V = 1/2` without a seed); `U ~ Uniform(0, 1)` and `F^-1(U) = X` a.s.

- Domain: integer-valued `X`; `F(X-) = F(X - 1)`.
- Meaning: a randomized probability integral transform; the latent map is not
  one-to-one (the whole interval `(F(x-), F(x)]` maps back to `x`), so
  gradient-based reliability methods are refused for discrete inputs.
- Code: `modeling.JointInput.to_latent`, `modeling.JointInput.to_standard_normal`.
- Source: [REF-RUSCHENDORF-2009].

### EQ-MOD-DISC-002 — Joint mass of discrete inputs under a copula

`P(X = x) = sum_{e in {0,1}^d} (-1)^{|e|} C(F_1(x_1 - e_1), ..., F_d(x_d - e_d))`.

- Domain: integer-valued margins, a copula CDF available (Archimedean any
  `d`, Gaussian `d <= 2`, independence); at most 16 inputs.
- Meaning: rectangle inclusion-exclusion over the copula CDF; mixed
  discrete/continuous inputs under a dependent copula need partial
  derivatives of `C` and are not implemented.
- Code: `modeling.JointInput.log_pdf`.
- Source: [REF-GENEST-NESLEHOVA-2007], [REF-NELSEN-2006, Section 2.10].

### EQ-PROP-MIXED-001 — Nested (double-loop) propagation

For outer epistemic values `e_j` (Latin hypercube over the epistemic
dimensions, plus interval corners and optional compass-search points):
`F_j(y) = (1/n) sum_i 1{g(x_i, e_j) <= y}` with `x_i` the aleatory inner
sample (common to every `j` with common random numbers); statistics
`s(e_j)` = mean, `P(Y > t)`, type-7 quantiles; bounds
`[min_j s(e_j), max_j s(e_j)]`.

- Domain: aleatory and epistemic inputs independent; at least one of each.
- Meaning: separates variability (inner CDF) from lack of knowledge (outer
  spread). The bounds over a finite design are inner approximations of the
  true bounds (exact at the corners for responses monotone in each interval
  input); cost `(outer points) x n` model evaluations.
- Code: `propagation.nested_propagation`.
- Source: [REF-ROY-OBERKAMPF-2011], [REF-OBERKAMPF-ROY-2010].

### EQ-PROP-PBOX-001 — Probability box from a family of CDFs

`F_low(y) = min_j F_j(y)`, `F_up(y) = max_j F_j(y)`;
`P(Y > t)` in `[1 - F_up(t), 1 - F_low(t)]`.

- Domain: the outer points of [EQ-PROP-MIXED-001].
- Meaning: the pointwise envelope of the output CDFs (a p-box); for
  `Y = X + E`, `E` in `[a, b]`, it is `[Phi(y - b), Phi(y - a)]`.
- Code: `propagation.ProbabilityBox.bounds`,
  `propagation.ProbabilityBox.exceedance_bounds`.
- Source: [REF-FERSON-ET-AL-2003].

## Integration: hierarchical systems and mission assessment

### EQ-SYS-ADAPT-001 — Modular decomposition of a coherent system

`phi(x) = psi(chi_1(x^{A_1}), ..., chi_m(x^{A_m}))` for disjoint modules
`A_1, ..., A_m`; with independent modules,
`R_sys = h_psi(R_{chi_1}, ..., R_{chi_m})`, where each module reliability
(or availability) is computed by its own exact model (BDD structure or
continuous-time Markov chain).

- Domain: modules share no component; module states mutually independent
  (no shared repair crews, loads, or common-cause groups across modules).
- Meaning: a subsystem can be replaced by one block whose reliability is the
  subsystem's exact reliability; the composed result is then exact.
- Code: `systems.MarkovComponent`, `systems.SubsystemComponent`.
- Source: [REF-BARLOW-PROSCHAN-1975], [REF-RAUSAND-HOYLAND-2004].

## Automatic differentiation, MCMC diagnostics, and sensitivity estimators (ADR-0065)

### EQ-AD-DUAL-001 — Forward-mode dual-number chain rule

`f(a + b.eps) = f(a) + f'(a) b.eps` with `eps_i eps_j = 0`; for binary
operations `(a + b eps)(c + d eps) = ac + (bc + ad) eps` and
`(a + b eps)/(c + d eps) = a/c + (b - (a/c) d)/c eps`. Seeding `x_i + e_i eps`
gives `f(x) + grad f(x) . eps` from one evaluation (vector-tangent mode).

- Domain: functions composed of `+ - * / **` and elementary functions that
  are differentiable at the evaluation point; at kinks (`abs(0)`,
  `hypot(0, 0)`) the derivative is defined as 0.
- Meaning: exact (to rounding) gradients without a step size; one call of
  the user function per gradient.
- Code: `numerics.Dual`, `numerics.admath`, `numerics.value_and_gradient`,
  `numerics.gradient`, `numerics.jacobian`, `numerics.GradientEvaluator`.
- Source: [REF-GRIEWANK-WALTHER-2008, Chapter 3].

### EQ-AD-HESSIAN-001 — Forward-over-forward Hessian

Seed `x_i = (x_i + e_i eps1) + (e_i + 0 eps1) eps2`; then
`f = (f + grad f . eps1) + sum_j (d_j f + grad d_j f . eps1) eps2_j`, so the
eps1-tangent of the j-th eps2-tangent is column `j` of the Hessian. The
result is symmetrized, `(H + H')/2`.

- Domain: twice differentiable `f`; `trigamma` of a dual (third derivative
  of `lgamma`) is not available.
- Meaning: exact Hessian from one nested evaluation (cost `O(d^2)` per
  operation).
- Code: `numerics.hessian`, `numerics.value_gradient_and_hessian`,
  `inference.laplace_approximation`.
- Source: [REF-GRIEWANK-WALTHER-2008, Chapters 3 and 13].

### EQ-MCMC-ESS-002 — Split, bulk, and tail effective sample size

Split ESS: [EQ-MCMC-ESS-001] on the `2M` half chains. Bulk-ESS: the same on
the rank-normalized split chains `z = Phi^-1((r - 3/8)/(S + 1/4))`.
Quantile ESS at level `p`: [EQ-MCMC-ESS-001] on the split indicator chains
`I(x <= q_p)`, `q_p` the type-7 sample quantile of all draws. Tail-ESS:
`min(ESS_q(0.05), ESS_q(0.95))`.

- Domain: at least four draws per chain; undefined (`nan`) for constant
  draws or constant indicators.
- Meaning: efficiency for the posterior bulk (location) and for central
  90 % intervals; the recommended minimum is 100 per chain.
- Code: `inference.effective_sample_size`, `inference.bulk_effective_sample_size`,
  `inference.quantile_effective_sample_size`,
  `inference.tail_effective_sample_size`, `inference.convergence_warnings`.
- Source: [REF-VEHTARI-ETAL-2021] and [REF-BURKNER-ETAL-POSTERIOR].

### EQ-MCMC-MCSE-002 — Monte Carlo standard error of a quantile

With `S_eff = ESS_q(p)` ([EQ-MCMC-ESS-002]) and `a_1, a_2` the
`Phi(-1)`, `Phi(1)` quantiles of `Beta(S_eff p + 1, S_eff (1-p) + 1)`:
`MCSE(q_p) = (x_(ceil(a_2 S)) - x_(max(floor(a_1 S), 1))) / 2` over the
sorted draws `x_(1) <= ... <= x_(S)`.

- Domain: `0 <= p <= 1`, defined quantile ESS.
- Meaning: half-width of a one-standard-deviation interval for the quantile
  estimate, mapped through the empirical distribution of the draws.
- Code: `inference.mcse_quantile`, `inference.summarize_draws`.
- Source: [REF-VEHTARI-ETAL-2021, Section 4.4] and
  [REF-BURKNER-ETAL-POSTERIOR].

### EQ-NUTS-MULTINOMIAL-001 — Multinomial NUTS state selection

Each trajectory state has weight `w(z) = exp(-H(z) + H_0)`. Merging subtrees
inside the recursion takes the second candidate with probability
`W_2 / (W_1 + W_2)`; at the top level the new subtree's candidate replaces
the current state with probability `min(1, W_new / W_old)`. A leaf is
divergent when `H - H_0 > Delta_max`.

- Domain: trajectories built by the doubling of [EQ-NUTS-UTURN-001].
- Meaning: samples the next state from the canonical distribution
  restricted to the trajectory, favouring states far from the start.
- Code: `inference.no_u_turn_sampler` (`variant="multinomial"`).
- Source: [REF-BETANCOURT-2017, Appendix A.3] and [REF-HOFFMAN-GELMAN-2014].

### EQ-SBC-RANK-001 — Simulation-based calibration rank statistic

`theta~ ~ p(theta)`, `y~ ~ p(y | theta~)`, `theta_1..L ~ p(theta | y~)`:
`r = #{l : theta_l < theta~}` is uniform on `{0, ..., L}` for every scalar
parameter when the posterior draws are exact and independent. Bins
`b = floor(r B / (L + 1))`; Pearson's statistic against the exact expected
counts has `B - 1` degrees of freedom.

- Domain: continuous parameters (ties broken uniformly at random);
  posterior draws thinned to near independence.
- Meaning: detects biased or mis-dispersed inference algorithms.
- Code: `inference.simulation_based_calibration`, `inference.rank_statistic`.
- Source: [REF-TALTS-ETAL-2018].

### EQ-REL-FORM-AD-001 — Limit-state gradient through the Nataf map

With `z = L u`, `x_i = F_i^-1(Phi(z_i))`: `dx_i/dz_i = phi(z_i)/f_i(x_i)`,
so `grad_u G = L' D grad_x g` with `D = diag(phi(z_i)/f_i(x_i))`; `grad_x g`
comes from one dual-number call of the forward model ([EQ-AD-DUAL-001]).

- Domain: `f_i(x_i) > 0`; the tail clamping of the Nataf map (``Phi(z)``
  rounded at about `|z| > 8`) makes both this and finite differences
  inexact there.
- Meaning: exact FORM gradient at one model evaluation instead of `2 d`.
- Code: `reliability.form_hlrf`.
- Source: [REF-LIU-DERKIUREGHIAN-1986] and [REF-GRIEWANK-WALTHER-2008,
  Chapter 3].

### EQ-SENS-RQMC-001 — Replicate (randomized QMC) intervals for Sobol indices

Split the `N` rows into `R` independent randomizations of `m = N // R` rows,
estimate the index on each (`S^(r)`), and report
`Sbar = mean_r S^(r)` with `Sbar +- t_(R-1, (1+c)/2) s_R / sqrt(R)`.

- Domain: `R >= 2`; any randomized design (scrambled Sobol, randomized
  Halton, LHS, Monte Carlo); replicates must use independent
  randomizations.
- Meaning: honest error bars for quasi-random designs, whose rows are not
  i.i.d. and must not be bootstrapped.
- Code: `sensitivity.sobol_analysis`, `sensitivity.sobol_analysis_all`.
- Source: [REF-L-ECUYER-2018] and [REF-OWEN-2013].

### EQ-SENS-DGSM-001 — Derivative-based global sensitivity measure

`nu_i = E[(d f / d x_i)^2]`, estimated by `mean_k (d f/d x_i)(x_k)^2` over
points `x_k` of the input law.

- Domain: `f` differentiable almost everywhere with square-integrable
  partial derivatives.
- Meaning: average squared local sensitivity of the output to input `i`.
- Code: `sensitivity.dgsm`.
- Source: [REF-SOBOL-KUCHERENKO-2009].

### EQ-SENS-DGSM-002 — Poincare upper bound on the total Sobol index

`S_Ti <= C(mu_i) nu_i / D`, `D = Var f(X)`, with `C = (b - a)^2 / pi^2`
for `Uniform(a, b)` (`nu_i / (pi^2 D)` on `[0, 1]`) and `C = sigma^2` for
`Normal(mu, sigma)`.

- Domain: independent inputs; the constants are the optimal Poincare
  constants of the two laws (equality for `cos(pi x)` on `[0, 1]` and for
  linear functions of normal inputs).
- Meaning: a small bound certifies an unimportant input; a large bound
  proves nothing.
- Code: `sensitivity.dgsm`, `sensitivity.poincare_constant`.
- Source: [REF-SOBOL-KUCHERENKO-2009] and [REF-LAMBONI-ETAL-2013].

### EQ-SENS-GIVEN-001 — Given-data first-order index by class partition

Sort by `x_i`, cut into `M` equal-count classes; `SSB = sum_m n_m
(ybar_m - ybar)^2`, `SST = sum (y_k - ybar)^2`, `SSW = SST - SSB`; raw
`eta^2 = SSB/SST`; corrected `epsilon^2 = 1 - (n-1)/(n-M) SSW/SST`.

- Domain: i.i.d. rows, `2 <= M <= n/2`; inputs may be dependent. Tied
  `x_i` values stay in one class (a cut inside a run of ties moves to its
  end), and `M` in the correction is the number `M_i` of classes used.
- Meaning: `Var(E[Y|X_i])/Var(Y)` from existing runs; the raw ratio is
  biased up by about `(M-1)(1-S_i)/(n-1)`, the class averaging biases it
  down by `O(1/M^2)` for a smooth conditional mean.
- Code: `sensitivity.given_data_first_order`.
- Source: [REF-PLISCHKE-BORGONOVO-SMITH-2013] and [REF-KELLEY-1935].

## Central model contract, evaluation engine, and study workflow (ADR-0058)

### EQ-PROP-QCI-001 — Distribution-free order-statistic interval for a quantile

`P(Y_(l) <= xi_p <= Y_(u)) = B(u - 1) - B(l - 1)` with `B` the
`Binomial(n, p)` CDF; `l = max{k >= 1 : B(k - 1) <= alpha/2}`,
`u = min{k <= n : B(k - 1) >= 1 - alpha/2}`.

- Domain: `n` independent draws of a continuous law, `0 < p < 1`; undefined
  (error) when no rank pair reaches the confidence.
- Meaning: an exact, law-free confidence interval for the `p`-quantile whose
  coverage is at least `1 - alpha`, with each tail at most `alpha/2`; for LHS
  or quasi-random samples it is a conservative reference only.
- Code: `propagation.order_statistic_interval`,
  `propagation.OutputDistribution.quantile_interval`.
- Source: [REF-DAVID-NAGARAJA-2003, Section 7.1].

### EQ-PROP-RQMC-CI-001 — Student-t interval over randomized replicates

`theta_hat = (1/r) sum_k theta_k`, `s_r^2 = sum_k (theta_k - theta_hat)^2 /
(r - 1)`, interval `theta_hat +- t_{1 - alpha/2, r - 1} s_r / sqrt(r)`.

- Domain: `r >= 2` independent randomizations (scrambles, shifts, or
  independent Monte Carlo batches) of one design; `theta_k` the replicate
  mean or exceedance fraction.
- Meaning: the honest error statement of randomized quasi-Monte Carlo; the
  replicate estimates are i.i.d. and unbiased, and the t quantile is accurate
  when their distribution is near normal.
- Code: `propagation.replicate_interval`,
  `propagation.OutputDistribution.mean_interval`,
  `propagation.OutputDistribution.exceedance_interval`.
- Source: [REF-L-ECUYER-2018] and [REF-OWEN-2013, Chapter 17].

### EQ-PROP-VARCI-001 — Chi-square interval for a normal variance

`[(n - 1) s^2 / chi2_{1 - alpha/2, n - 1}, (n - 1) s^2 / chi2_{alpha/2, n - 1}]`.

- Domain: `n >= 2` independent normal observations with sample variance
  `s^2`.
- Meaning: exact for normal data because `(n - 1) s^2 / sigma^2 ~
  chi2_{n - 1}`; not robust: for non-normal data its coverage depends on the
  kurtosis even as `n` grows, so the percentile bootstrap
  ([EQ-INF-BOOT-002]) is offered as the alternative.
- Code: `propagation.OutputDistribution.variance_interval`.
- Source: [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002, Chapter 9].

### EQ-WF-SEQ-FRESH-001 — Pilot-sized fresh-sample estimate

A sequential pilot stops at `N = min{n in {n_0, n_0 + h, ...} : r_n <= epsilon}`
(or `N_max`) with `r_n` from [EQ-STAT-STREAM-007] or [EQ-MC-PROB-001]; the
reported estimate is `theta_hat = (1/N) sum_{i=1}^{N} g(X'_i)` with
`X'_1, ..., X'_N` drawn independently of the pilot.

- Domain: any integrable `g`; pilot and final draws on independent streams.
- Meaning: given `N` the fresh sample is a fixed-size Monte Carlo sample, so
  `E[theta_hat | N] = E[g(X)]` and fixed-`n` intervals keep their nominal
  coverage; reusing the pilot instead biases the estimate because stopping
  depends on the values observed (optional stopping). The two-stage idea of
  sizing a sample from a first stage goes back to Stein.
- Code: `workflow.UQStudy.propagate_until` (`final="fresh"`).
- Source: [REF-STEIN-1945] and [REF-ROBERT-CASELLA-2004, Chapters 3-4].

### EQ-WF-EMPIRICAL-001 — Interpolated empirical law of posterior draws

For distinct sorted points `x_1 < ... < x_m`: `F(x) = (k - 1 + (x - x_k) /
(x_{k+1} - x_k)) / (m - 1)` on `[x_k, x_{k+1}]`, density
`1 / ((m - 1)(x_{k+1} - x_k))`, quantile `Q(p) = x_k + (h - k)(x_{k+1} - x_k)`
with `h = 1 + p (m - 1)`, `k = floor(h)`; mean
`sum_k (x_k + x_{k+1}) / (2 (m - 1))`, second moment
`sum_k (x_k^2 + x_k x_{k+1} + x_{k+1}^2) / (3 (m - 1))`.

- Domain: `m >= 2` distinct finite points; support `[x_1, x_m]`.
- Meaning: the continuous law whose quantile function is the type-7 sample
  quantile ([EQ-STAT-QUANT-001]); each gap carries probability `1/(m - 1)`
  spread uniformly, so moments are exact sums of uniform-segment moments.
- Code: `workflow.EmpiricalMarginal`, `workflow.posterior_joint_input`.
- Source: [REF-HYNDMAN-FAN-1996].

### EQ-WF-MISSION-001 — Expected mission-loss frequency

`nu = n Q(T)`, with `n` missions per year and `Q(T) = 1 - R(T)` the exact
mission unreliability.

- Domain: missions statistically independent and identical; `Q(T)` per
  mission from the exact system model.
- Meaning: expected number of mission losses per year; the rate that drives
  the expected cost of unreliability.
- Code: `workflow.MissionAssessment.cost`, `workflow.MissionAssessment.register`.
- Source: [REF-NASA-PRA-2011], [REF-RAUSAND-BARROS-HOYLAND-2021].

### EQ-WF-MISSION-002 — Probability of at least one loss in a campaign

`P(at least one loss in N missions) = 1 - R(T)^N = -expm1(N log1p(-Q(T)))`.

- Domain: `N = n * horizon` independent identical missions.
- Meaning: campaign-level loss probability, evaluated without cancellation
  when `Q(T)` is small.
- Code: `workflow.MissionAssessment.cost`.
- Source: [REF-NASA-PRA-2011].

### EQ-WF-MISSION-003 — Expected total life-cycle cost including losses

`E[C_total] = PV(E[LCC]) + PV(nu c_loss over the horizon)`.

- Domain: life-cycle totals linear in the cost elements; mission losses at the
  constant expected frequency `nu`; one discount rate.
- Meaning: expected present value of ownership plus the expected cost of
  unreliability; uncertainty in the life-cycle part is shown by the cost-risk
  S-curve, not by this expectation.
- Code: `workflow.MissionAssessment.cost`.
- Source: [REF-NASA-CEH-2015], [REF-RAUSAND-BARROS-HOYLAND-2021].

## Numerical core, distributions, sampling designs, and surrogate numerics (ADR-0059)

### EQ-OPT-FD-003 — Relative finite-difference steps

`h_i = c max(|x_i|, typ_i)` with `c = sqrt(eps) ~ 1.5e-8` (forward) or
`c = eps^(1/3) ~ 6.1e-6` (central), rounded so that `x_i + h_i` is exactly
representable; `typ_i` is a typical magnitude (default 1, or `|x0_i|` inside
BFGS). The rounding error of a central quotient is about `eps |f| / h_i`.

- Domain: `f` smooth near `x`; supersedes the step quoted in
  [EQ-OPT-FD-001] for the default; an explicit `relative_step` keeps
  `h = c max(1, |x_i|)` and an explicit `step` is used as given.
- Meaning: steps relative to the variable, balancing truncation
  (`O(h)` forward, `O(h^2)` central) against rounding (`O(eps/h)`).
- Code: `optimization.central_gradient`, `optimization.forward_gradient`,
  `optimization.central_jacobian`.
- Source: [REF-NOCEDAL-WRIGHT-2006, Section 8.1], [REF-DENNIS-SCHNABEL-1996,
  Section 5.4].

### EQ-OPT-FD-004 — One-sided second-order difference

`f'(x) ~= s (-3 f(x) + 4 f(x + s h) - f(x + 2 s h)) / (2 h)`, `s = +-1`;
first order `s (f(x + s h) - f(x)) / h` when `x + 2 s h` also fails.

- Domain: `f` defined on the chosen side; used when `f(x -+ h)` raises or is
  non-finite (domain boundaries); error `O(h^2)`.
- Meaning: gradients next to a domain boundary without leaving the domain.
- Code: `optimization.central_gradient`, `optimization.forward_gradient`.
- Source: [REF-FORNBERG-1988], [REF-NOCEDAL-WRIGHT-2006, Section 8.1].

### EQ-OPT-WOLFE-001 — Strong Wolfe conditions

Accept `alpha` when `f(x + alpha p) <= f(x) + c1 alpha g'p` and
`|grad f(x + alpha p)' p| <= c2 |g'p|`, `c1 = 1e-4`, `c2 = 0.9`; found by
bracketing (doubling) and zoom with safeguarded cubic or quadratic
interpolation.

- Domain: descent direction `g'p < 0`, `f` bounded below along `p`.
- Meaning: guarantees `y's > 0`, so the BFGS update stays positive definite.
- Code: `optimization.minimize_bfgs`.
- Source: [REF-NOCEDAL-WRIGHT-2006, Section 3.5, Algorithms 3.5-3.6].

### EQ-OPT-BFGS-002 — Initial inverse-Hessian scaling and stopping rules

Before the first update `H_0 = (s'y / y'y) I`. Stop when `||g||_2 <= tol`
(absolute), or when `max_i |s_i| / max(|x_i|, typ_i) <= eps^(2/3)`, or when a
line search fails with predicted decrease `-g'p/2 <= 16 eps |f|`; a
finite-difference gradient also stops at `||g|| <= ||(eps |f| / h_i)_i||`
when that resolution exceeds `tol`. Any other line-search failure, and the
iteration limit, are reported as not converged.

- Domain: smooth objectives; the tolerances do not depend on an additive
  constant in `f`; only the two floating-point resolution limits involve
  `eps |f|`.
- Meaning: scale-aware first step and honest convergence reporting.
- Code: `optimization.minimize_bfgs`.
- Source: [REF-NOCEDAL-WRIGHT-2006, Equation 6.20], [REF-DENNIS-SCHNABEL-1996,
  Section 7.2].

### EQ-OPT-BOX-001 — Box-constraint transformations

`x = l + (u - l)(1 + sin z)/2` (two bounds), `x = l - 1 + sqrt(z^2 + 1)`
(lower only), `x = u + 1 - sqrt(z^2 + 1)` (upper only); the optimizer works
in `z` with gradient `(dF/dx)(dx/dz)`.

- Domain: `l < u`; start points on a bound are moved inward by `1e-3` of the
  width (or of `max(1, |bound|)`) because `dx/dz = 0` there.
- Meaning: unconstrained minimization whose every evaluation lies in the box;
  a minimum on a bound is a stationary point in `z`.
- Code: `optimization.BoxTransform`, `optimization.minimize_bfgs`,
  `optimization.minimize_nelder_mead`, `optimization.multi_start`.
- Source: [REF-JAMES-ROOS-1975].

### EQ-NUM-BETA-002 — Large-shape gamma series for the incomplete beta

With `w = -log(1 - t)`, `N = L + (s - 1)/2` and
`(sinh(v/2)/(v/2))^(s-1) = sum_n e_n v^(2n)`, `n e_n = (s-1) sum_(k=1..n) k l_k e_(n-k)`,
`l_k = B_(2k) / (2k (2k)!)`:
`I_t(s, L) = Gamma(L+s)/(Gamma(L) N^s) sum_n e_n [Gamma(s+2n)/Gamma(s)] N^(-2n) P(s+2n, N w)`,
and the same sum with `Q(s+2n, N w)` gives `I_(1-t)(L, s)` (asymptotic).

- Domain: `L >= 1e4`, `w <= 1`, `|s-1| s (s+1) <= 24 N^2`; the series in
  `v` converges for `|v| < 2 pi`.
- Meaning: `I_x(a, b)` for a large first shape near `x = 1` (Student t with
  huge degrees of freedom, F with a huge denominator) to about `1e-13`
  relative, where the continued fraction stops early.
- Code: `distributions._special.regularized_beta_pair`.
- Source: [REF-DIDONATO-MORRIS-1992], [REF-NIST-DLMF-BETA, Section 8.17],
  [REF-NIST-DLMF, Sections 4.19 and 24.2].

### EQ-DIST-BASE-001 — Moments and entropy in probability space

`E[h(X)] = int_0^1 h(Q(u)) du` (with `Q(u) = isf(1 - u)` above the median),
used for `E[(X - mu)^k]` and `H = -E[log f(X)]` by tanh-sinh quadrature;
`nan` when the quadrature does not converge.

- Domain: continuous laws with a quantile function; divergent moments give
  `nan` from the quadrature, so families with heavy tails supply closed
  forms (`inf` for a divergent moment, `nan` for an undefined one).
- Meaning: default `skewness`, excess `kurtosis`, `entropy`, and wrapper
  means and variances.
- Code: `distributions.ContinuousDistribution`, `distributions.Truncated`.
- Source: [REF-TAKAHASI-MORI-1974], [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002, Chapter 2].

### EQ-DIST-BASE-002 — Log tail probabilities

`log F(x) = log1p(-S(x))` when `F(x) > 1/2`, else `log F(x)`; symmetrically
for `log S(x)`.

- Domain: any univariate law with `cdf` and `sf`; accuracy limited by the
  smaller tail's own accuracy (underflow below `1e-308` unless overridden).
- Meaning: default `log_cdf` and `log_sf`.
- Code: `distributions.ContinuousDistribution`,
  `distributions.DiscreteDistribution`.
- Source: [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002, Chapter 1].

### EQ-DIST-BASE-003 — Discrete inverse survival function

`isf(q) = min{k : S(k) <= q}`, found by doubling then bisection on the
integers using `S` directly; equals `quantile(1 - q)` in exact arithmetic.
At `q = 0` it is `quantile(1)`, the largest point with positive mass, so a
degenerate law returns its atom rather than the end of its nominal support.

- Domain: integer support; `q in [0, 1]`.
- Meaning: tail-accurate upper quantiles of count laws.
- Code: `distributions.DiscreteDistribution.isf`.
- Source: [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002, Chapter 2].

### EQ-DIST-BASE-004 — Discrete entropy and central moments

`H = -sum_k p_k log p_k`, `mu_r = sum_k (k - mu)^r p_k`, summed over
`[quantile(1e-17), isf(1e-17)]`.

- Domain: integer laws with finite moments; neglected mass below `2e-17`.
- Meaning: default `entropy`, `skewness`, and excess `kurtosis` of count laws.
- Code: `distributions.DiscreteDistribution`.
- Source: [REF-COVER-THOMAS-2006, Chapter 2], [REF-JKB-2005, Chapter 1].

### EQ-DIST-STT-005 — Student-t shape and entropy

Skewness `0` (`nu > 3`), excess kurtosis `6/(nu - 4)` (`nu > 4`; `inf` for
`2 < nu <= 4`), `H = (nu+1)/2 [psi((nu+1)/2) - psi(nu/2)] + log(sqrt(nu) B(nu/2, 1/2)) + log sigma`.

- Domain: `nu > 0`; undefined moments are `nan` (`nu <= 1` for the mean and
  variance, `nu <= 3` for the skewness, `nu <= 2` for the kurtosis).
- Meaning: closed forms for the heavy-tailed conventions.
- Code: `distributions.StudentT`.
- Source: [REF-JKB-1995, Chapter 28], [REF-COVER-THOMAS-2006, Chapter 8].

### EQ-DIST-TRI-005 — Triangular shape and entropy

Skewness `sqrt 2 (a+b-2c)(2a-b-c)(a-2b+c) / (5 (a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-ac-bc)^(3/2))`
(`a` lower, `b` upper, `c` mode), excess kurtosis `-3/5`,
`H = 1/2 + log((b - a)/2)`.

- Domain: `a < b`, `a <= c <= b`.
- Meaning: closed forms that avoid quadrature across the kink at the mode.
- Code: `distributions.Triangular`.
- Source: [REF-KOTZ-VANDORP-2004, Chapter 1].

### EQ-DIST-CAUCHY-001 — Cauchy law

`f = 1/(pi s (1 + z^2))`, `F = atan2(1, -z)/pi`, `S = atan2(1, z)/pi`,
`Q(p) = loc - s/tan(pi p)` (`p < 1/2`), `H = log(4 pi s)`.

- Domain: `s > 0`; mean, variance, skewness, kurtosis undefined (`nan`).
- Meaning: heavy-tailed input law with tail-accurate CDF and quantiles.
- Code: `distributions.Cauchy`.
- Source: [REF-JKB-1994, Chapter 16].

### EQ-DIST-LAPLACE-001 — Laplace law

`f = exp(-|z|)/(2b)`, `F = exp(z)/2` (`z <= 0`) else `1 - exp(-z)/2`,
`Q(p) = loc + b log(2p)` (`p <= 1/2`), mean `loc`, variance `2 b^2`,
excess kurtosis `3`, `H = 1 + log(2b)`.

- Domain: `b > 0`.
- Meaning: double-exponential input law.
- Code: `distributions.Laplace`.
- Source: [REF-JKB-1995, Chapter 24].

### EQ-DIST-RAYLEIGH-001 — Rayleigh law

`f = x/s^2 exp(-x^2/(2s^2))`, `S = exp(-x^2/(2s^2))`,
`Q(p) = s sqrt(-2 log(1-p))`, mean `s sqrt(pi/2)`, variance
`(4 - pi) s^2/2`, skewness `2 sqrt(pi)(pi-3)/(4-pi)^(3/2)`, excess kurtosis
`-(6pi^2 - 24pi + 16)/(4-pi)^2`, `H = 1 + log(s/sqrt 2) + gamma_E/2`.

- Domain: `s > 0`, `x >= 0`.
- Meaning: magnitude of a bivariate isotropic normal vector.
- Code: `distributions.Rayleigh`.
- Source: [REF-JKB-1994, Chapter 18].

### EQ-DIST-PARETO-001 — Pareto type I law

`S(x) = (x_m/x)^alpha` on `x >= x_m`, `f = alpha x_m^alpha / x^(alpha+1)`,
`Q(p) = x_m (1-p)^(-1/alpha)`, `isf(q) = x_m q^(-1/alpha)`.

- Domain: `x_m > 0`, `alpha > 0`.
- Meaning: power-law tail input law.
- Code: `distributions.Pareto`.
- Source: [REF-JKB-1994, Chapter 20].

### EQ-DIST-PARETO-002 — Pareto moments and entropy

Mean `alpha x_m/(alpha-1)` (`alpha > 1`), variance
`x_m^2 alpha / ((alpha-1)^2 (alpha-2))` (`alpha > 2`), skewness
`2(1+alpha)/(alpha-3) sqrt((alpha-2)/alpha)` (`alpha > 3`), excess kurtosis
`6(alpha^3+alpha^2-6alpha-2)/(alpha(alpha-3)(alpha-4))` (`alpha > 4`),
`H = log(x_m/alpha) + 1/alpha + 1`.

- Domain: divergent moments on the positive support are `inf`; shape
  ratios with an infinite variance are `nan`.
- Meaning: closed forms with the library's moment conventions.
- Code: `distributions.Pareto`.
- Source: [REF-JKB-1994, Chapter 20].

### EQ-DIST-PERT-001 — Beta-PERT law

`X = low + (high - low) B`, `B ~ Beta(alpha, beta)`,
`alpha = 1 + lam (mode - low)/(high - low)`,
`beta = 1 + lam (high - mode)/(high - low)`, `lam = 4` by default.

- Domain: `low < high`, `low <= mode <= high`, `lam > 0`.
- Meaning: three-point (minimum, most likely, maximum) expert-judgement law.
- Code: `distributions.PERT`.
- Source: [REF-MALCOLM-1959], [REF-VOSE-2008].

### EQ-DIST-PERT-002 — Beta-PERT moments and entropy

Mean `(low + lam mode + high)/(lam + 2)`, variance
`(mean - low)(high - mean)/(lam + 3)`, beta skewness and excess kurtosis of
`Beta(alpha, beta)`, `H = log B(alpha, beta) - (alpha-1) psi(alpha) -
(beta-1) psi(beta) + (alpha+beta-2) psi(alpha+beta) + log(high - low)`.

- Domain: as [EQ-DIST-PERT-001].
- Meaning: closed-form summaries of the PERT law.
- Code: `distributions.PERT`.
- Source: [REF-VOSE-2008], [REF-JKB-1995, Chapter 25].

### EQ-DIST-DUNIF-001 — Discrete uniform law

`p_k = 1/n` on `{low, ..., high}`, `n = high - low + 1`,
`F(x) = (floor(x) - low + 1)/n`, mean `(low + high)/2`, variance
`(n^2 - 1)/12`, excess kurtosis `-6(n^2+1)/(5(n^2-1))`, `H = log n`.

- Domain: integers `low <= high`.
- Meaning: equally likely integer outcomes.
- Code: `distributions.DiscreteUniform`.
- Source: [REF-JKB-2005].

### EQ-DIST-HYPERGEOM-001 — Hypergeometric law

`p_k = C(K, k) C(N-K, n-k) / C(N, n)` on `max(0, n+K-N) <= k <= min(n, K)`;
exact rational masses for `N <= 5000`, `lgamma` otherwise; tails summed on
the side of the mode `floor((n+1)(K+1)/(N+2))`.

- Domain: integers `0 <= K, n <= N`.
- Meaning: successes in draws without replacement.
- Code: `distributions.Hypergeometric`.
- Source: [REF-JKB-2005, Chapter 6].

### EQ-DIST-HYPERGEOM-002 — Hypergeometric moments

Mean `n K / N`, variance `n K (N-K)(N-n) / (N^2 (N-1))`.

- Domain: `N >= 2` (variance `0` otherwise).
- Meaning: closed-form moments.
- Code: `distributions.Hypergeometric`.
- Source: [REF-JKB-2005, Chapter 6].

### EQ-DIST-AFFINE-001 — Affine transformation of a law

`X = loc + s Y`: `f_X(x) = f_Y((x-loc)/s)/|s|`; `F_X = F_Y` (`s > 0`) or
`S_Y` (`s < 0`) at `(x-loc)/s`; `Q_X(p) = loc + s Q_Y(p)` (`s > 0`) or
`loc + s isf_Y(p)`; mean `loc + s mu_Y`, variance `s^2 sigma_Y^2`, skewness
`sign(s)` times, kurtosis unchanged, `H_X = H_Y + log|s|`.

- Domain: `s != 0`; any continuous base law.
- Meaning: location-scale families from any law.
- Code: `distributions.Affine`.
- Source: [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002, Section 2.1].

### EQ-DIST-TRUNC-001 — Truncated law

`Z = F(u) - F(l)` (from survival probabilities when `F(l) > 1/2`),
`f_T = f/Z` on `[l, u]`, `F_T(x) = (F(x) - F(l))/Z`,
`Q_T(p) = Q(F(l) + p Z)` or `isf(S(l) - p Z)`.

- Domain: `l < u` (one side may be infinite), `Z > 0`.
- Meaning: conditioning any continuous law on an interval, with
  upper-tail accuracy.
- Code: `distributions.Truncated`.
- Source: [REF-JKB-1994, Chapter 13].

### EQ-DIST-MIXTURE-001 — Finite mixture

`f = sum w_i f_i`, `F = sum w_i F_i`, `S = sum w_i S_i`; `Q(p)` solves
`F(x) = p` (or `S(x) = 1 - p`) by Brent's method in
`[min_i Q_i(p), max_i Q_i(p)]`; mean `sum w_i mu_i`, variance
`sum w_i (sigma_i^2 + (mu_i - mu)^2)`.

- Domain: positive weights summing to one; continuous components.
- Meaning: multimodal or contaminated input laws.
- Code: `distributions.Mixture`.
- Source: [REF-MCLACHLAN-PEEL-2000, Chapter 1], [REF-BRENT-1973, Chapter 4].

### EQ-DIST-EMPIRICAL-001 — Empirical law (step or interpolated)

Step: `F_n(x) = #{x_i <= x}/n`, `Q(p) = x_(ceil(n p))`. Linear:
`Q(p) = x_(j+1) + (h - j)(x_(j+2) - x_(j+1))`, `h = (n-1)p`, `j = floor(h)`
(type 7), CDF linear between `(x_(i), (i-1)/(n-1))`, density
`1/((n-1)(x_(i+1) - x_(i)))` on each gap.

- Domain: at least two observations; ties create atoms (linear) whose mass
  `pdf` does not report.
- Meaning: data-defined input laws; the linear form is continuous.
- Code: `distributions.Empirical`.
- Source: [REF-HYNDMAN-FAN-1996], [REF-VAN-DER-VAART-1998, Chapter 19].

### EQ-DIST-EMPIRICAL-002 — Moments of the interpolated empirical law

Linear: mean `(sum x_i - (x_(1) + x_(n))/2)/(n - 1)`, variance
`sum_gaps ((a-m)^2 + (a-m)(b-m) + (b-m)^2)/(3(n-1))`; step: sample mean and
`sum (x_i - xbar)^2/n`.

- Domain: as [EQ-DIST-EMPIRICAL-001].
- Meaning: exact moments of a uniform mixture over the gaps.
- Code: `distributions.Empirical`.
- Source: [REF-HYNDMAN-FAN-1996].

### EQ-STAT-KDE-002 — Gaussian KDE quantile and moments

`F_h(x) = (1/n) sum Phi((x - x_i)/h)` is solved for `F_h(x) = p` by Brent's
method in `[min x_i + h z_p, max x_i + h z_p]`; mean `xbar`, variance
`sum (x_i - xbar)^2/n + h^2`; draws `x_J + h Z`.

- Domain: `h > 0`, `0 < p < 1`.
- Meaning: the KDE as a continuous model-input law.
- Code: `statistics.KernelDensity.quantile`, `statistics.KernelDensity.draw`.
- Source: [REF-SILVERMAN-1986, Sections 3.3 and 6.4].

### EQ-SAMP-HALTON-002 — Randomized Halton by digit permutations

`x = sum_(k=1..K) pi_(j,k)(d_k(i)) b_j^-k + U b_j^-K`, with independent uniform
permutations `pi_(j,k)` of `{0, ..., b_j - 1}` for every axis `j` and digit
position `k` (zero included), `b_j^-K <= 2^-53`, `U ~ U(0,1)`.

- Domain: prime bases; leading zero digits are permuted too.
- Meaning: every point is uniform on the unit cube (unbiased estimators)
  while van der Corput strata are preserved.
- Code: `sampling.halton`.
- Source: [REF-MATOUSEK-1998], [REF-OWEN-1995].

### EQ-SAMP-OWEN-001 — Owen nested uniform scrambling of a digital net

Digit `k` of each coordinate is XORed with a random bit indexed by
`(k, d_1 ... d_(k-1))`; below the first `m = ceil(log2 n)` digits all bits
are independent uniform.

- Domain: base-2 nets; bits drawn lazily from a seeded stream.
- Meaning: randomized QMC that keeps the net property, makes each point
  uniform, and reduces variance for smooth integrands.
- Code: `sampling.sobol(scramble="owen")`.
- Source: [REF-OWEN-1995].

### EQ-SAMP-MAXIMIN-001 — Morris-Mitchell maximin criterion

`phi_p = (sum_(i<j) d_ij^-p)^(1/p)`, minimized by random within-column swaps
of a Latin hypercube (kept when `phi_p` decreases).

- Domain: distinct points, `p >= 1` (default 15).
- Meaning: space-filling Latin hypercubes with large minimum distances.
- Code: `sampling.maximin_criterion`, `sampling.maximin_latin_hypercube`.
- Source: [REF-MORRIS-MITCHELL-1995].

### EQ-SAMP-IC-001 — Iman-Conover rank-correlation induction

Scores `S` (columns: permuted `Phi^-1(i/(n+1))`), `corr(S) = Q Q'`,
`C = P P'`, `T = S (Q^-1)' P'`; reorder each design column to the ranks of
the matching column of `T`.

- Domain: SPD target correlation with unit diagonal, `n >= d + 2`.
- Meaning: rank correlation close to `C` while every marginal (Latin
  stratum) is unchanged.
- Code: `sampling.iman_conover`.
- Source: [REF-IMAN-CONOVER-1982].

### EQ-SUR-GP-007 — Precision entries from the inverse Cholesky factor

`M = L^-1` by `M_ij = -(sum_(k=j..i-1) L_ik M_kj)/L_ii`; `(K^-1)_ab =
sum_(k >= max(a,b)) M_ka M_kb`; the likelihood gradient uses
`W = alpha alpha' - K^-1` over the upper triangle, and the 1-norm condition
number is `||K||_1 ||K^-1||_1`.

- Domain: `K = L L'` positive definite.
- Meaning: value, gradient, LOO diagonal and conditioning from one
  factorization per hyperparameter point.
- Code: `surrogates.gaussian_process_log_marginal_likelihood`,
  `surrogates.GaussianProcessRegression`.
- Source: [REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013, Sections 2.6 and 3.1],
  [REF-RASMUSSEN-WILLIAMS-2006, Section 5.4].

## Measure-theoretic bridge and completeness (ADR-0071)

### EQ-MEAS-001 — Generated sigma-algebra on a finite set

`sigma(G) = { union of atoms in S : S subset of atoms }`, where outcomes
`omega ~ omega'` share an atom iff `1_C(omega) = 1_C(omega')` for every
generator `C in G`; with `k` atoms, `|sigma(G)| = 2^k`. A family `F` is a
sigma-algebra iff `Omega in F`, `A in F => Omega \ A in F`, and
`A, B in F => A union B in F` (finite unions suffice on a finite set). `G` is
a sub-sigma-algebra of `F` iff every atom of `G` is a union of atoms of `F`.

- Domain: non-empty finite `Omega`; any finite collection `G` of subsets
  (empty `G` gives `{empty, Omega}`, no `G` gives the power set).
- Meaning: the events an observer can distinguish; atoms are the finest
  distinguishable outcomes.
- Code: `probability.FiniteMeasurableSpace`, `probability.is_sigma_algebra`,
  `FiniteMeasurableSpace.is_measurable`,
  `FiniteMeasurableSpace.is_sub_sigma_algebra_of`.
- Source: [REF-BILLINGSLEY-1995, Section 2], [REF-DURRETT-2019, Section 1.1].

### EQ-MEAS-002 — Measure from atom masses

`mu(A) = sum_(a atom, a subset of A) m(a)` with `m(a) >= 0`; `mu` is a
probability measure iff `mu(Omega) = 1`. The restriction to a
sub-sigma-algebra `G` assigns each `G`-atom the `mu`-measure of that atom.

- Domain: `A` measurable; masses exact fractions or finite floats.
- Meaning: non-negativity and countable additivity hold by construction;
  subsets that split an atom have no measure.
- Code: `probability.FiniteMeasure`, `FiniteMeasure.measure_of`,
  `FiniteMeasure.from_point_masses`, `FiniteMeasure.restrict`,
  `FiniteMeasure.counting`.
- Source: [REF-BILLINGSLEY-1995, Section 10], [REF-DURRETT-2019, Section 1.1].

### EQ-MEAS-003 — Measurable maps and pushforward measures

`f : (Omega, F) -> (Omega', F')` is measurable iff `f^-1(B) in F` for every
atom `B` of `F'`; a finite-valued function into its power-set codomain is
measurable iff it is constant on every atom of `F`. The image measure is
`(mu o f^-1)(B) = mu(f^-1(B))`; `sigma(f)` has the level sets
`f^-1({y})` as atoms.

- Domain: finite codomain; values must be target outcomes.
- Meaning: the law of a random element is the pushforward of the
  underlying measure.
- Code: `probability.FiniteMeasurableSpace.is_measurable_map`,
  `FiniteMeasurableSpace.is_measurable_function`,
  `FiniteMeasurableSpace.generated_by_map`, `probability.FiniteMeasure.pushforward`.
- Source: [REF-BILLINGSLEY-1995, Section 13], [REF-DURRETT-2019,
  Sections 1.2-1.3].

### EQ-MEAS-004 — Lebesgue integral of simple and measurable functions

`integral (sum_i c_i 1_(A_i)) dmu = sum_i c_i mu(A_i)`; a measurable `f` on
a finite space is simple on the atom partition, so
`integral f dmu = sum_a f(a) mu(a)` and
`integral_A f dmu = integral f 1_A dmu`.

- Domain: measurable `A_i` (not necessarily disjoint) and measurable real
  `f`.
- Meaning: expectation is integration against the measure; it is the
  finite case of the Lebesgue integral.
- Code: `probability.FiniteMeasure.simple_integral`, `FiniteMeasure.integrate`,
  `FiniteMeasure.integrate_over`.
- Source: [REF-BILLINGSLEY-1995, Sections 15-16], [REF-DURRETT-2019,
  Sections 1.4-1.6].

### EQ-MEAS-005 — Product measure and Fubini-Tonelli

`(mu x nu)(a x b) = mu(a) nu(b)` on the atoms `a x b` of the product
sigma-algebra, and
`integral f d(mu x nu) = integral [integral f(x, y) nu(dy)] mu(dx)
= integral [integral f(x, y) mu(dx)] nu(dy)`.

- Domain: finite factors; `f` measurable for the product sigma-algebra
  (hence integrable).
- Meaning: independent coordinates and the interchange of the order of
  integration.
- Code: `probability.FiniteMeasurableSpace.product`, `probability.FiniteMeasure.product`,
  `FiniteMeasure.fubini_check`, `probability.FubiniCheck`.
- Source: [REF-BILLINGSLEY-1995, Section 18], [REF-DURRETT-2019, Section 1.7].

### EQ-MEAS-006 — Absolute continuity and the Radon-Nikodym derivative

`nu << mu` iff `mu(a) = 0 => nu(a) = 0` for every atom; then
`(d nu / d mu)(a) = nu(a) / mu(a)` on `mu(a) > 0` (any value, here `0`, on
`mu`-null atoms) and `nu(A) = integral_A (d nu / d mu) dmu`. Conversely a
non-negative measurable `g` defines `nu(A) = integral_A g dmu`.

- Domain: both measures on the same finite measurable space.
- Meaning: densities, likelihood ratios, and change of measure; the
  derivative is unique only `mu`-almost everywhere.
- Code: `probability.FiniteMeasure.is_absolutely_continuous_wrt`,
  `FiniteMeasure.radon_nikodym_derivative`, `FiniteMeasure.with_density`.
- Source: [REF-BILLINGSLEY-1995, Sections 16 and 32].

### EQ-MEAS-007 — Chain rule for Radon-Nikodym derivatives

If `lambda << nu << mu`, then `d lambda / d mu = (d lambda / d nu)
(d nu / d mu)` `mu`-almost everywhere.

- Domain: three measures on one finite measurable space.
- Meaning: likelihood ratios compose; importance weights for a two-step
  change of measure multiply.
- Code: verified with `probability.FiniteMeasure.radon_nikodym_derivative` in
  `tests/test_measure_theory.py`.
- Source: [REF-BILLINGSLEY-1995, Section 32].

### EQ-MEAS-008 — Conditional expectation given a sub-sigma-algebra

For a sub-sigma-algebra `G` with atom `A`, `mu(A) > 0`:
`E[X | G](omega) = integral_A X dmu / mu(A)` for `omega in A` (any value on
null atoms). It is `G`-measurable with `integral_B E[X | G] dmu =
integral_B X dmu` for all `B in G`; tower property
`E[E[X | G] | H] = E[X | H]` for `H subset G`; and
`E[Z X | G] = Z E[X | G]` for `G`-measurable `Z`.

- Domain: measurable real `X`, `Z`; `H subset G subset F`.
- Meaning: the best `G`-measurable prediction of `X`, unique almost
  everywhere.
- Code: `probability.FiniteMeasure.conditional_expectation`,
  `FiniteMeasure.verify_tower_property`,
  `FiniteMeasure.verify_taking_out_what_is_known`.
- Source: [REF-BILLINGSLEY-1995, Section 34], [REF-DURRETT-2019, Section 4.1].

### EQ-MEAS-009 — Total-variation distance on a finite space

`TV(P, Q) = sup_(A in F) |P(A) - Q(A)| = (1/2) sum_a |P(a) - Q(a)|`, the
supremum attained at the union of atoms where `P(a) > Q(a)`.

- Domain: probability measures on the same finite measurable space.
- Meaning: the largest disagreement in probability over all events.
- Code: `probability.FiniteMeasure.total_variation_distance`.
- Source: [REF-TSYBAKOV-2009, Chapter 2].

### EQ-MEAS-010 — Completeness of a statistic on a finite family

With parameters `theta_1, ..., theta_m` and statistic values `t_1, ..., t_k`
charged by some `P_theta`, let `A[i, j] = P_(theta_i)(T = t_j)`. `T` is
complete iff `E_theta[g(T)] = sum_j A[i, j] g(t_j) = 0` for all `i` forces
`g = 0`, that is, iff `rank A = k`. A non-zero null vector of `A` is an
unbiased estimator of zero.

- Domain: finite sample space and finite parameter set; exact rank for
  fractions, tolerance-based rank with partial pivoting for floats.
- Meaning: for the binomial count with `n` trials completeness holds iff at
  least `n + 1` distinct `p` in `(0, 1)` are included; the full sample is
  never complete for `n >= 2`.
- Code: `probability.check_completeness`,
  `probability.is_complete_statistic`, `probability.CompletenessCheck`.
- Source: [REF-LEHMANN-CASELLA-1998, Section 1.6],
  [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002, Section 6.2.4], [REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013,
  Section 3.2].

### EQ-SYS-SIFT-001 — Adjacent variable swap and sifting

With `x` directly above `y`,
`f = not x (not y f00 + y f01) + x (not y f10 + y f11)
= not y (not x f00 + x f10) + y (not x f01 + x f11)`,
so a node testing `x` with a child testing `y` is relabelled `y` with
children `ite(x, f10, f00)` and `ite(x, f11, f01)`; a node whose children
do not test `y` keeps its label and moves below `y`. Sifting moves each
variable (largest levels first) through every position by such swaps and
leaves it where the shared size is smallest.

- Domain: reduced ordered BDDs; reference-counted nodes so that the live
  size is exact after every swap.
- Meaning: the swap changes two levels only and preserves every
  represented function, hence every probability; the chosen position is
  the best one seen, so the size never increases. The interleaved function
  `x1 x2 + ... + x(2n-1) x(2n)` drops from `2^(n+1) - 2` to `2n` nodes.
- Code: `systems.BDD.sift`, `systems.BDD.reorder`, `systems.ReorderResult`.
- Source: [REF-RUDELL-1993], [REF-BRYANT-1986].

### EQ-SYS-DFT-001 — Dynamic fault tree as an absorbing Markov chain

State `s = (D, u, V)`: failed basic events `D`, unit in use per spare gate
`u`, PAND gates with an out-of-order failure `V`. A working event `e` fails
at rate `lambda_e` when active, `alpha_e lambda_e` when it is an unused
spare, and `0` when it follows an unfailed SEQ input; after each failure
spare claims and FDEP cascades are resolved at the same instant. Gate
outputs: AND all, OR any, vote at least `k`, PAND all with `g not in V`,
SPARE no unit left, SEQ all. Every state with the top event is merged into
one absorbing state `FAIL`, and `F(t) = Pr(X_t = FAIL)` with
`pi(t) = pi(0) exp(Q t)`.

- Domain: non-repairable basic events with exponential lifetimes;
  dormancy `alpha` in `[0, 1]` (cold `0`, warm, hot `1`); simultaneous
  failures count as in order for PAND; simultaneous spare demands are
  served in gate declaration order.
- Meaning: exact quantification of order- and use-dependent failure
  logic; the transient law carries the uniformization error bound.
- Code: `systems.DynamicFaultTree.state_space`,
  `systems.DynamicFaultTree.unreliability`,
  `systems.DynamicFaultTree.reliability`, `systems.DFTStateSpace`.
- Source: [REF-DUGAN-BAVUSO-BOYD-1992], [REF-NASA-FTH-2002, Chapter 8],
  [REF-NORRIS-1997, Sections 2.1-2.8].

### EQ-SYS-DFT-002 — Mean time to the top event

`MTTF = m(s0)` with `m = (-Q_TT)^-1 1` over the working states; `MTTF = inf`
when a working state without outgoing transitions is reachable (the top
event is then avoided forever with positive probability).

- Domain: the generated chain of EQ-SYS-DFT-001 (acyclic, because failures
  only accumulate).
- Meaning: expected time to system failure, solved by the
  subtraction-free elimination of EQ-PROC-CTMC-006.
- Code: `systems.DynamicFaultTree.mttf`.
- Source: [REF-NORRIS-1997, Section 3.3], [REF-DUGAN-BAVUSO-BOYD-1992].

### EQ-SYS-DFT-003 — Event-time simulation of the gate semantics

Each working event carries a pending failure time: `Exp(lambda)` when
active, `Exp(alpha lambda)` while dormant, and `s + Exp(lambda)` when it is
put into use (or released by its SEQ predecessor) at time `s`, by
memorylessness. Gate times: AND `max`, OR `min`, vote the `k`-th smallest,
PAND `t_m` if `t_1 <= ... <= t_m` else `inf`, SEQ `max`, SPARE the instant
no unit is left. With `K` of `n` histories failing by `t`,
`F_hat(t) = K / n` and the Clopper-Pearson interval of EQ-INF-CI-CP-001.

- Domain: as EQ-SYS-DFT-001; seeded streams.
- Meaning: an independent statistical cross-check of the exact chain; it
  evaluates the gates from failure times instead of chain states.
- Code: `systems.monte_carlo_unreliability`, `systems.DFTMonteCarloEstimate`.
- Source: [REF-DUGAN-BAVUSO-BOYD-1992], [REF-CLOPPER-PEARSON-1934],
  [REF-DEVROYE-1986, Chapter II].

### EQ-SYS-DFT-004 — Closed forms for elementary dynamic gates

For rates `a`, `b`, `lambda`:
`F_PAND(A,B)(t) = int_0^t a e^{-a s} (e^{-b s} - e^{-b t}) ds
= a/(a+b) (1 - e^{-(a+b) t}) - e^{-b t} (1 - e^{-a t})`;
cold spare pair `F = 1 - e^{-lambda t} (1 + lambda t)` (Erlang(2, lambda));
hot spare pair `F = (1 - e^{-lambda t})^2`;
warm spare (primary `a`, spare `b`, dormancy `alpha`, `c = a + alpha b - b`)
`R(t) = e^{-a t} + a e^{-b t} (1 - e^{-c t}) / c`, with mean
`1/(a + alpha b) + a/((a + alpha b) b) + alpha b/((a + alpha b) a)`;
`SEQ(A, B)` with rates `a != b`: `F = 1 - (b e^{-a t} - a e^{-b t})/(b - a)`;
FDEP with trigger `T` on the inputs of `AND(A, B)`: `F = 1 - (1 - F_T)(1 -
F_A F_B)`.

- Domain: independent exponential basic events.
- Meaning: oracles for the state-space quantification; the warm spare is a
  hypoexponential law, and the cold and hot cases are its limits
  `alpha = 0` and `alpha = 1` when `a = b`.
- Code: `systems.dynamic` (module documentation; used as test oracles in
  `tests/test_dynamic_fault_trees.py`).
- Source: [REF-NASA-FTH-2002, Chapter 8], [REF-DUGAN-BAVUSO-BOYD-1992].

### EQ-DIST-DIR-001 — Dirichlet density on the simplex

`f(x) = prod_i x_i^(alpha_i - 1) / B(alpha)`,
`log B(alpha) = sum_i log Gamma(alpha_i) - log Gamma(alpha_0)`,
`alpha_0 = sum_i alpha_i`, on `{x : x_i >= 0, sum_i x_i = 1}`.

- Domain: `K >= 2`, every `alpha_i > 0`; density with respect to Lebesgue
  measure on the first `K - 1` coordinates. On a face (`x_i = 0`) the
  limiting value is reported (`+inf` for `alpha_i < 1`, factor 1 for
  `alpha_i = 1`, 0 for `alpha_i > 1`; `nan` when zero and infinite factors
  meet); a negative component gives `-inf`; a vector off the hyperplane
  `sum x_i = 1` (tolerance `1e-10`) is rejected.
- Meaning: the conjugate prior for categorical probabilities; `K = 2` is the
  beta law.
- Code: `multivariate.Dirichlet.log_pdf`, `multivariate.Dirichlet.pdf`,
  `multivariate.dirichlet.log_multivariate_beta`.
- Source: [REF-BISHOP-2006, Appendix B],
  [REF-KOTZ-BALAKRISHNAN-JOHNSON-2000, Chapter 49].

### EQ-DIST-DIR-002 — Dirichlet mean and covariance

`E[X] = m = alpha / alpha_0`,
`Cov[X] = (diag(m) - m m') / (alpha_0 + 1)`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-DIR-001].
- Meaning: every pair of coordinates is negatively correlated because the
  coordinates share a fixed total; larger `alpha_0` concentrates the law at
  `m`.
- Code: `multivariate.Dirichlet.mean`, `multivariate.Dirichlet.covariance`.
- Source: [REF-BISHOP-2006, Appendix B].

### EQ-DIST-DIR-003 — Dirichlet mode

`mode_i = (alpha_i - 1) / (alpha_0 - K)`.

- Domain: every `alpha_i > 1`; otherwise the density is unbounded or is
  maximized on a face and the library returns a vector of `nan`.
- Meaning: the most probable interior composition.
- Code: `multivariate.Dirichlet.mode`.
- Source: [REF-BISHOP-2006, Appendix B].

### EQ-DIST-DIR-004 — Dirichlet differential entropy

`H = log B(alpha) + (alpha_0 - K) psi(alpha_0)
- sum_i (alpha_i - 1) psi(alpha_i)`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-DIR-001]; `psi` is the digamma function
  ([EQ-NUM-DIGAMMA-001]).
- Meaning: entropy in nats with respect to Lebesgue measure on the simplex
  coordinates; it is negative for concentrated laws.
- Code: `multivariate.Dirichlet.entropy`.
- Source: [REF-BISHOP-2006, Appendix B].

### EQ-DIST-DIR-005 — Beta marginals and aggregation of a Dirichlet

`X_i ~ Beta(alpha_i, alpha_0 - alpha_i)`; for a partition `G_1, ..., G_m`
of the categories,
`(sum_(i in G_1) X_i, ..., sum_(i in G_m) X_i) ~
Dirichlet(sum_(i in G_1) alpha_i, ..., sum_(i in G_m) alpha_i)`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-DIR-001]; `m >= 2` non-empty groups covering every index
  exactly once.
- Meaning: merging categories keeps the Dirichlet family; a single
  coordinate against the rest is the two-group case.
- Code: `multivariate.Dirichlet.marginal`, `multivariate.Dirichlet.aggregate`.
- Source: [REF-KOTZ-BALAKRISHNAN-JOHNSON-2000, Chapter 49],
  [REF-BISHOP-2006, Appendix B].

### EQ-DIST-DIR-006 — Dirichlet variates from normalized gamma variates

`G_i ~ Gamma(alpha_i, 1)` independent, `X_i = G_i / sum_j G_j`. In log space,
`log G_a = log G_(a+1) + log(U) / a` for `a < 1` with `U ~ Uniform(0, 1]`,
and `X_i = exp(log G_i - max_j log G_j) / sum_k exp(log G_k - max_j log G_j)`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-DIR-001].
- Meaning: an exact sampler; the log-space boost keeps very small
  concentrations (for example `1e-3`) from producing `0 / 0`.
- Code: `multivariate.Dirichlet.sample`, `multivariate.DirichletMultinomial.sample`,
  `multivariate._support.log_gamma_variate`.
- Source: [REF-DEVROYE-1986, Chapter XI], [REF-MARSAGLIA-TSANG-2000].

### EQ-DIST-MULT-001 — Multinomial mass function

`P(X = x) = n! / prod_i x_i! * prod_i p_i^(x_i)` for non-negative integer
`x` with `sum_i x_i = n`, and `0^0 = 1`.

- Domain: `n >= 0`, `K >= 2`, `p` a probability vector (sum within
  `1e-10`, then normalized). The coefficient is formed as the exact integer
  `prod_i C(n - x_1 - ... - x_(i-1), x_i)` for `n <= 1000` and as
  `log Gamma(n + 1) - sum_i log Gamma(x_i + 1)` above.
- Meaning: the law of category counts in `n` independent categorical trials.
- Code: `multivariate.Multinomial.log_pmf`, `multivariate.Multinomial.pmf`,
  `multivariate.multinomial.log_multinomial_coefficient`.
- Source: [REF-JOHNSON-KOTZ-BALAKRISHNAN-1997, Chapter 35].

### EQ-DIST-MULT-002 — Multinomial mean and covariance

`E[X] = n p`, `Cov[X] = n (diag(p) - p p')`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-MULT-001].
- Meaning: counts are negatively correlated because they share the total
  `n`; the covariance matrix is singular (`Cov[X] 1 = 0`).
- Code: `multivariate.Multinomial.mean`, `multivariate.Multinomial.covariance`.
- Source: [REF-JOHNSON-KOTZ-BALAKRISHNAN-1997, Chapter 35].

### EQ-DIST-MULT-003 — Binomial marginals of a multinomial

`X_i ~ Binomial(n, p_i)`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-MULT-001].
- Meaning: one category against all others is a binomial count.
- Code: `multivariate.Multinomial.marginal`.
- Source: [REF-JOHNSON-KOTZ-BALAKRISHNAN-1997, Chapter 35].

### EQ-DIST-MULT-004 — Sequential conditional binomial sampling

`X_1 ~ Bin(n, p_1)`; for `i = 2..K-1`,
`X_i | X_1..X_(i-1) ~ Bin(n - sum_(j<i) X_j, p_i / (1 - sum_(j<i) p_j))`;
`X_K = n - sum_(j<K) X_j`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-MULT-001]; ratios above 1 from rounding are clipped to 1.
- Meaning: the chain rule of the multinomial law written as binomial
  factors; each binomial is drawn as a Bernoulli sum, so the cost is `O(n)`.
- Code: `multivariate.Multinomial.sample`,
  `multivariate.DirichletMultinomial.sample`.
- Source: [REF-DEVROYE-1986, Chapter XI].

### EQ-DIST-DIRMULT-001 — Dirichlet-multinomial mass function

`P(X = x) = n! / prod_i x_i! * Gamma(A) / Gamma(n + A)
* prod_i Gamma(x_i + alpha_i) / Gamma(alpha_i)`, `A = sum_i alpha_i`.

- Domain: `n >= 0`, `K >= 2`, every `alpha_i > 0`; non-negative integer `x`
  with `sum_i x_i = n`. Each gamma ratio uses the Stirling-series form of
  [EQ-NUM-STIRLING-001] above argument 100.
- Meaning: `X | p ~ Mult(n, p)` with `p ~ Dirichlet(alpha)` integrated out;
  for integer `alpha` it is the Polya urn law
  `n!/prod x_i! prod_i alpha_i^(x_i rising) / A^(n rising)`.
- Code: `multivariate.DirichletMultinomial.log_pmf`,
  `multivariate.DirichletMultinomial.pmf`.
- Source: [REF-MOSIMANN-1962], [REF-JOHNSON-KOTZ-BALAKRISHNAN-1997, Chapter 35].

### EQ-DIST-DIRMULT-002 — Dirichlet-multinomial moments and overdispersion

`E[X] = n q`, `q = alpha / A`;
`Cov[X] = n (n + A) / (1 + A) (diag(q) - q q')`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-DIRMULT-001].
- Meaning: the multinomial covariance with mean probabilities `q`, inflated
  by `(n + A) / (1 + A) >= 1`; the factor tends to 1 as `A -> inf` and to
  `n` as `A -> 0`.
- Code: `multivariate.DirichletMultinomial.mean`,
  `multivariate.DirichletMultinomial.covariance`,
  `multivariate.DirichletMultinomial.overdispersion`.
- Source: [REF-MOSIMANN-1962].

### EQ-DIST-DIRMULT-003 — Dirichlet-multinomial sampling by composition

`p ~ Dirichlet(alpha)` by [EQ-DIST-DIR-006], then `X | p ~ Mult(n, p)` by
[EQ-DIST-MULT-004].

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-DIRMULT-001].
- Meaning: the hierarchical definition of the compound law, simulated
  directly.
- Code: `multivariate.DirichletMultinomial.sample`.
- Source: [REF-MOSIMANN-1962], [REF-DEVROYE-1986, Chapter XI].

### EQ-NUM-MVLGAMMA-001 — Multivariate log-gamma function

`log Gamma_p(a) = (p (p - 1) / 4) log pi + sum_(j=1..p) log Gamma(a - (j - 1)/2)`.

- Domain: integer `p >= 1`, real `a > (p - 1)/2`.
- Meaning: the normalizing integral `int_(X > 0) etr(-X) |X|^(a - (p+1)/2) dX`
  of the Wishart family; `p = 1` is `log Gamma(a)`.
- Code: `multivariate.multivariate_log_gamma`.
- Source: [REF-NIST-DLMF-MATRIX-ARGUMENT, Section 35.3],
  [REF-ANDERSON-2003, Section 7.2].

### EQ-DIST-MVT-001 — Multivariate Student-t density

`log f(x) = log Gamma((nu + p)/2) - log Gamma(nu/2) - (p/2) log(nu pi)
- (1/2) log|Sigma| - ((nu + p)/2) log(1 + delta/nu)`,
`delta = (x - mu)' Sigma^-1 (x - mu)` as in [EQ-DIST-MVN-002].

- Domain: `p >= 1`, `Sigma` symmetric positive definite, real `nu > 0`.
  The gamma ratio uses the Stirling-series form of [EQ-NUM-STIRLING-001]
  for large `nu`, so the density tends to [EQ-DIST-MVN-001] without loss
  of digits.
- Meaning: an elliptical law with polynomial tails; `p = 1` is the
  location-scale Student t.
- Code: `multivariate.MultivariateStudentT.log_pdf`,
  `multivariate.MultivariateStudentT.pdf`,
  `multivariate.MultivariateStudentT.mahalanobis_squared`.
- Source: [REF-KOTZ-NADARAJAH-2004, Chapter 1],
  [REF-GELMAN-ETAL-2013, Appendix A].

### EQ-DIST-MVT-002 — Multivariate Student-t moments

`E[X] = mu` for `nu > 1`; `Cov[X] = nu / (nu - 2) Sigma` for `nu > 2`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-MVT-001]. For `nu <= 1` the mean and covariance are
  reported as `nan`; for `1 < nu <= 2` the covariance has `inf` diagonal and
  `nan` off-diagonal entries (ADR-0059 moment convention).
- Meaning: `Sigma` is a scale matrix, not the covariance.
- Code: `multivariate.MultivariateStudentT.mean`,
  `multivariate.MultivariateStudentT.covariance`.
- Source: [REF-KOTZ-NADARAJAH-2004, Chapter 1].

### EQ-DIST-MVT-003 — Marginals of a multivariate Student t

`X_S ~ t_nu(mu_S, Sigma_SS)` for any index subset `S`; in particular
`X_i ~ t_nu(mu_i, sqrt(Sigma_ii))`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-MVT-001].
- Meaning: marginalization keeps the degrees of freedom (unlike
  conditioning, which changes them).
- Code: `multivariate.MultivariateStudentT.marginal_subset`,
  `multivariate.MultivariateStudentT.marginal`.
- Source: [REF-KOTZ-NADARAJAH-2004, Chapter 1].

### EQ-DIST-MVT-004 — Multivariate Student-t sampling

`X = mu + L z / sqrt(W / nu)`, `L L' = Sigma`, `z ~ N(0, I_p)`,
`W ~ chi^2(nu)` independent of `z`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-MVT-001].
- Meaning: a normal scale mixture with an inverse-gamma mixing variance.
- Code: `multivariate.MultivariateStudentT.sample`.
- Source: [REF-KOTZ-NADARAJAH-2004, Chapter 1], [REF-DEVROYE-1986, Chapter XI].

### EQ-DIST-WISH-001 — Wishart density

`log f(X) = ((nu - p - 1)/2) log|X| - tr(S^-1 X)/2 - (nu p / 2) log 2
- (nu/2) log|S| - log Gamma_p(nu/2)` ([EQ-NUM-MVLGAMMA-001]).

- Domain: `S` symmetric positive definite, real `nu > p - 1`, `X` symmetric
  positive definite (otherwise the density is 0). Density with respect to
  Lebesgue measure on the `p (p + 1)/2` free entries; `p = 1` is
  `Gamma(nu/2, rate 1/(2 s))`.
- Meaning: the law of `sum_(k=1..nu) z_k z_k'`, `z_k ~ N(0, S)`, for
  integer `nu`.
- Code: `multivariate.Wishart.log_pdf`, `multivariate.Wishart.pdf`.
- Source: [REF-ANDERSON-2003, Section 7.2],
  [REF-MARDIA-KENT-BIBBY-1979, Chapter 3], [REF-GELMAN-ETAL-2013, Appendix A].

### EQ-DIST-WISH-002 — Wishart mean and mode

`E[W] = nu S`; `mode = (nu - p - 1) S` for `nu >= p + 1`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-WISH-001]. The mode follows from [EQ-DIST-WISH-001] by
  setting the matrix gradient `((nu - p - 1)/2) X^-1 - S^-1 / 2` to zero;
  for `nu < p + 1` the density is unbounded at the boundary of the cone and
  the library reports `nan`.
- Meaning: `S` is the scale per degree of freedom.
- Code: `multivariate.Wishart.mean`, `multivariate.Wishart.mode`.
- Source: [REF-GELMAN-ETAL-2013, Appendix A], [REF-ANDERSON-2003, Section 7.2].

### EQ-DIST-WISH-003 — Bartlett decomposition

`A` lower triangular with independent `A_ii^2 ~ chi^2(nu - i + 1)`
(`i = 1..p`) and `A_ij ~ N(0, 1)` (`i > j`) has `A A' ~ Wishart_p(I, nu)`;
with `L L' = S`, `W = (L A)(L A)' ~ Wishart_p(S, nu)`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-WISH-001]; real `nu > p - 1` keeps every chi-square
  degree positive.
- Meaning: a Wishart sampler using `p` chi-square and `p (p - 1)/2` normal
  variates and no factorization per draw.
- Code: `multivariate.Wishart.sample`, `multivariate.wishart._bartlett_factor`.
- Source: [REF-SMITH-HOCKING-1972], [REF-ANDERSON-2003, Section 7.2].

### EQ-DIST-IWISH-001 — Inverse-Wishart density

`log f(X) = (nu/2) log|Psi| - (nu p / 2) log 2 - log Gamma_p(nu/2)
- ((nu + p + 1)/2) log|X| - tr(Psi X^-1)/2`.

- Domain: `Psi` symmetric positive definite, real `nu > p - 1`, `X`
  symmetric positive definite (otherwise the density is 0).
  `X ~ InverseWishart_p(Psi, nu)` if and only if
  `X^-1 ~ Wishart_p(Psi^-1, nu)`; the Jacobian of `X -> X^-1` is
  `|X|^-(p+1)`.
- Meaning: the conjugate prior for a normal covariance matrix.
- Code: `multivariate.InverseWishart.log_pdf`, `multivariate.InverseWishart.pdf`.
- Source: [REF-ANDERSON-2003, Section 7.7], [REF-GELMAN-ETAL-2013, Appendix A].

### EQ-DIST-IWISH-002 — Inverse-Wishart mean and mode

`E[X] = Psi / (nu - p - 1)` for `nu > p + 1`; `mode = Psi / (nu + p + 1)`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-IWISH-001]. The mode follows from [EQ-DIST-IWISH-001] by
  setting the gradient `-((nu + p + 1)/2) X^-1 + X^-1 Psi X^-1 / 2` to zero.
  For `p - 1 < nu <= p + 1` the diagonal means diverge and the library
  reports `inf` diagonal and `nan` off-diagonal entries.
- Meaning: `Psi` acts as a prior scatter matrix.
- Code: `multivariate.InverseWishart.mean`, `multivariate.InverseWishart.mode`.
- Source: [REF-GELMAN-ETAL-2013, Appendix A], [REF-ANDERSON-2003, Section 7.7].

### EQ-DIST-IWISH-003 — Inverse-Wishart sampling by an inverted Bartlett factor

With `Psi = C C'` and `A` as in [EQ-DIST-WISH-003],
`Sigma = (C A^-T)(C A^-T)'`; then `Sigma^-1 = C^-T A A' C^-1 ~
Wishart_p(Psi^-1, nu)`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-IWISH-001].
- Meaning: one triangular inverse of `A` per draw; no inverse of a full
  matrix is formed. The same construction is used by
  `inference.sample_inverse_wishart` ([EQ-MISS-005]).
- Code: `multivariate.InverseWishart.sample`.
- Source: [REF-SMITH-HOCKING-1972], [REF-ANDERSON-2003, Section 7.7].

### EQ-CONJ-DIR-001 — Dirichlet-categorical posterior and evidence

`p | x ~ Dirichlet(alpha + x)` for counts `x` of `n = sum_i x_i`
categorical trials. The prior predictive probability of one observed
sequence with these counts is
`log p(sequence) = log Gamma(A) - log Gamma(A + n)
+ sum_i [log Gamma(alpha_i + x_i) - log Gamma(alpha_i)]`, `A = sum_i alpha_i`;
adding `log(n! / prod_i x_i!)` gives the Dirichlet-multinomial mass
[EQ-DIST-DIRMULT-001] of the unordered counts.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-DIR-001]; non-negative integer counts. Gamma ratios use
  [EQ-NUM-STIRLING-001] above argument 100.
- Meaning: conjugacy turns the update into addition of counts to
  pseudo-counts; the evidence equals the product of the sequential
  predictive probabilities `(alpha_i + x_i^(<t)) / (A + t - 1)`.
- Code: `multivariate.dirichlet_posterior`, `multivariate.DirichletPosterior`.
- Source: [REF-GELMAN-ETAL-2013, Section 3.4], [REF-MURPHY-2012, Sections 3.4
  and 5.3.2].

### EQ-CONJ-DIR-002 — Dirichlet-categorical posterior predictive

`P(next = i | x) = (alpha_i + x_i) / (A + n)`; the counts `y` of `m` future
trials satisfy `y | x ~ DirichletMultinomial(m, alpha + x)`.

- Domain: [EQ-CONJ-DIR-001].
- Meaning: predictions average the multinomial over the Dirichlet
  posterior, so they are overdispersed by [EQ-DIST-DIRMULT-002].
- Code: `multivariate.DirichletPosterior.predictive`,
  `multivariate.DirichletPosterior.predictive_probabilities`.
- Source: [REF-MURPHY-2012, Section 3.4], [REF-MOSIMANN-1962].

### EQ-CONJ-NIW-001 — Normal-inverse-Wishart density

`Sigma ~ InverseWishart_p(Psi, nu)`, `mu | Sigma ~ N(m, Sigma / kappa)`;
`log p(mu, Sigma) = log N(mu | m, Sigma / kappa) + log IW(Sigma | Psi, nu)`
([EQ-DIST-MVN-001], [EQ-DIST-IWISH-001]).

- Domain: `kappa > 0`, `Psi` symmetric positive definite, real
  `nu > p - 1`.
- Meaning: the conjugate prior for a multivariate normal with unknown mean
  and covariance; `kappa` and `nu` act as prior sample sizes for the mean
  and the covariance.
- Code: `multivariate.NormalInverseWishart.log_pdf`,
  `multivariate.NormalInverseWishart.sample`,
  `multivariate.NormalInverseWishart.covariance_marginal`.
- Source: [REF-MURPHY-2007, Section "Normal-inverse-Wishart prior"],
  [REF-GELMAN-ETAL-2013, Section 3.6].

### EQ-CONJ-NIW-002 — Normal-inverse-Wishart posterior update

With `n` observations, `xbar` their mean and
`S = sum_i (x_i - xbar)(x_i - xbar)'`:
`kappa_n = kappa_0 + n`, `nu_n = nu_0 + n`,
`m_n = (kappa_0 m_0 + n xbar) / kappa_n`,
`Psi_n = Psi_0 + S + (kappa_0 n / kappa_n)(xbar - m_0)(xbar - m_0)'`.

- Domain: [EQ-CONJ-NIW-001]; `n >= 1` finite observations of dimension `p`.
  Equivalent raw-moment form:
  `Psi_n = Psi_0 + sum_i x_i x_i' + kappa_0 m_0 m_0' - kappa_n m_n m_n'`.
- Meaning: the posterior is again normal-inverse-Wishart; the mean is a
  precision-weighted average and the scale accumulates the scatter plus the
  prior-data disagreement.
- Code: `multivariate.normal_inverse_wishart_posterior`,
  `multivariate.NormalInverseWishartPosterior`.
- Source: [REF-GELMAN-ETAL-2013, Section 3.6],
  [REF-MURPHY-2007, Section "Normal-inverse-Wishart prior"],
  [REF-MURPHY-2012, Section 4.6.3].

### EQ-CONJ-NIW-003 — Normal-inverse-Wishart marginal and predictive laws

`mu ~ t_(nu-p+1)(m, Psi / (kappa (nu - p + 1)))`;
one new observation `x ~ t_(nu-p+1)(m, Psi (kappa + 1) / (kappa (nu - p + 1)))`
([EQ-DIST-MVT-001]).

- Domain: [EQ-CONJ-NIW-001]; `nu - p + 1 > 0` holds because `nu > p - 1`.
  Applied to the posterior parameters these are the posterior marginal of
  `mu` and the posterior predictive law.
- Meaning: integrating out the covariance turns Gaussian uncertainty into
