  Student-t uncertainty with `nu - p + 1` degrees of freedom.
- Code: `multivariate.NormalInverseWishart.mean_marginal`,
  `multivariate.NormalInverseWishart.predictive`,
  `multivariate.NormalInverseWishartPosterior.predictive`.
- Source: [REF-GELMAN-ETAL-2013, Section 3.6],
  [REF-MURPHY-2007, Section "Normal-inverse-Wishart prior"],
  [REF-MURPHY-2012, Section 4.6.3].

### EQ-CONJ-NIW-004 — Normal-inverse-Wishart marginal likelihood

`log p(x_1..x_n) = -(n p / 2) log pi + log Gamma_p(nu_n / 2)
- log Gamma_p(nu_0 / 2) + (nu_0 / 2) log|Psi_0| - (nu_n / 2) log|Psi_n|
+ (p / 2)(log kappa_0 - log kappa_n)` ([EQ-NUM-MVLGAMMA-001]).

- Domain: [EQ-CONJ-NIW-002].
- Meaning: the prior predictive density of the data, used for model
  comparison; for `n = 1` it equals the predictive density of
  [EQ-CONJ-NIW-003], and it factorizes into sequential predictive densities.
- Code: `multivariate.normal_inverse_wishart_posterior`
  (`log_marginal_likelihood`).
- Source: [REF-MURPHY-2007, Section "Normal-inverse-Wishart prior"],
  [REF-MURPHY-2012, Section 4.6.3].

### EQ-MOD-VINE-001 — Rotated pair copulas and their h-functions

With `(V_1, V_2)` from an exchangeable base copula `C` with density `c` and
`H(a | b) = P(V_2 <= a | V_1 = b)`, the rotated pair is `U_1 = r_1(V_1)`,
`U_2 = r_2(V_2)`, where `r_i(x) = 1 - x` for a reflected coordinate and `x`
otherwise (90 degrees: first reflected; 180: both; 270: second).

`c_rot(u_1, u_2) = c(r_1(u_1), r_2(u_2))`;
`C_90 = u_2 - C(1 - u_1, u_2)`, `C_180 = u_1 + u_2 - 1 + C(1 - u_1, 1 - u_2)`,
`C_270 = u_1 - C(u_1, 1 - u_2)`;
`h_given_first(u_1, u_2) = dC_rot/du_1 = g_2(H(r_2(u_2) | r_1(u_1)))`,
`h_given_second(u_1, u_2) = dC_rot/du_2 = g_1(H(r_1(u_1) | r_2(u_2)))`, with
`g_i(p) = 1 - p` for a reflected coordinate and `p` otherwise; the inverses are
`h_inverse_given_first(u_1, w) = r_2(H^-1(g_2(w) | r_1(u_1)))` and
`h_inverse_given_second(w, u_2) = r_1(H^-1(g_1(w) | r_2(u_2)))`. Kendall's tau
changes sign for 90 and 270 degrees; 180 degrees swaps `lambda_L` and
`lambda_U`.

- Domain: `u` in `(0, 1)^2`; rotations only for the Clayton and Gumbel
  copulas (the other families are radially symmetric); `H` and `H^-1` are the
  second Rosenblatt coordinate and its inverse of the base copula
  ([EQ-MOD-COP-ROSEN-001]).
- Meaning: the Aas et al. h-function `h(u_1 | u_2)` is `h_given_second`; the
  rotations give negative dependence (90, 270) and the opposite tail (180).
- Code: `modeling.PairCopula`.
- Source: [REF-NELSEN-2006, Section 2.4], [REF-AAS-CZADO-FRIGESSI-BAKKEN-2009],
  [REF-JOE-2014].

### EQ-MOD-VINE-002 — Conditional distributions by the h-function recursion

`F(x | v) = dC_{x, v_j | v_-j}(F(x | v_-j), F(v_j | v_-j)) / dF(v_j | v_-j)`,
where `v_j` is one conditioning variable and `v_-j` the others; for one
conditioning variable `F(x | v) = h(x | v)`.

- Domain: absolutely continuous copula; the pair copula of `(x, v_j)` given
  `v_-j` does not depend on the value of `v_-j` (simplified vine).
- Meaning: each tree's pair-copula arguments are the h-function outputs of
  the previous tree.
- Code: `modeling.CVineCopula`, `modeling.DVineCopula`,
  `modeling.fit_vine_copula`.
- Source: [REF-AAS-CZADO-FRIGESSI-BAKKEN-2009], [REF-BEDFORD-COOKE-2002].

### EQ-MOD-VINE-003 — C-vine density

`c(u) = prod_{j=1}^{d-1} prod_{i=1}^{d-j} c_{j, j+i | 1, ..., j-1}(F(u_j | u_1,
..., u_{j-1}), F(u_{j+i} | u_1, ..., u_{j-1}))` in vine positions `1, ..., d`.

- Domain: `u` in `(0, 1)^d`, `d >= 2`; tree `j` is a star with root `j`.
- Meaning: `d (d - 1) / 2` bivariate densities; the first tree couples the
  first root with every other variable.
- Code: `modeling.CVineCopula.log_density`.
- Source: [REF-AAS-CZADO-FRIGESSI-BAKKEN-2009, Algorithms 1-4].

### EQ-MOD-VINE-004 — D-vine density

`c(u) = prod_{j=1}^{d-1} prod_{i=1}^{d-j} c_{i, i+j | i+1, ..., i+j-1}(F(u_i |
u_{i+1}, ..., u_{i+j-1}), F(u_{i+j} | u_{i+1}, ..., u_{i+j-1}))`.

- Domain: `u` in `(0, 1)^d`, `d >= 2`; every tree is a path along the vine
  order.
- Meaning: pairs are conditioned on the variables between them in the path.
  A Gaussian D-vine whose pair copulas are Gaussian with the partial
  correlations of `R` is the Gaussian copula with correlation `R`.
- Code: `modeling.DVineCopula.log_density`.
- Source: [REF-AAS-CZADO-FRIGESSI-BAKKEN-2009, Algorithms 1-4],
  [REF-KUROWICKA-COOKE-2006].

### EQ-MOD-VINE-005 — Vine Rosenblatt transform and its inverse

`w_{p_1} = u_{p_1}`, `w_{p_k} = F(u_{p_k} | u_{p_1}, ..., u_{p_{k-1}})` with
`(p_1, ..., p_d)` the vine order. C-vine: `w_k` is the working value of
position `k` when it becomes the root; inverse
`u_k = h_1^-1(... h_{k-1}^-1(w_k | w_{k-1}) ... | w_1)` along the edges
joining roots `k-1, ..., 1` to `k`. D-vine: `w_k = h_given_first` of the
first edge of tree `k - 1`; the inverse runs the edges ending at `k` from the
top tree down.

- Domain: `u`, `w` in `(0, 1)^d`; values are clamped into
  `[1e-300, 1 - 2^-53]`.
- Meaning: the exact isoprobabilistic map of [EQ-MOD-COP-ROSEN-001] in the
  vine order; the inverse is the vine sampler.
- Code: `modeling.CVineCopula.rosenblatt`,
  `modeling.CVineCopula.inverse_rosenblatt`, `modeling.DVineCopula.rosenblatt`,
  `modeling.DVineCopula.inverse_rosenblatt`.
- Source: [REF-AAS-CZADO-FRIGESSI-BAKKEN-2009, Algorithms 1-4],
  [REF-ROSENBLATT-1952].

### EQ-MOD-VINE-006 — Kendall's tau test of independence

`z = tau_n / sqrt(2 (2n + 5) / (9 n (n - 1)))`, `p = 2 Phi(-|z|)`.

- Domain: `n >= 2` continuous observations; asymptotic normal null law.
- Meaning: an edge is set to the independence copula when `p >= level`.
- Code: `modeling.kendall_independence_p_value`, `modeling.fit_vine_copula`.
- Source: [REF-KENDALL-1938], [REF-HOLLANDER-WOLFE-CHICKEN-2014, Chapter 8],
  [REF-DISSMANN-BRECHMANN-CZADO-KUROWICKA-2013].

### EQ-MOD-VINE-007 — Sequential edge-wise maximum likelihood and selection

`theta_hat_e = argmax_theta sum_i log c_e(a_i, b_i; theta)` for the
pseudo-observations `(a_i, b_i)` of edge `e`, started from Kendall's tau
inversion; `AIC_e = 2 k_e - 2 l_e` selects the family per edge; the vine
totals are `l = sum_e l_e`, `AIC = 2 k - 2 l`, `BIC = k log n - 2 l` with
`k = sum_e k_e`.

- Domain: ranks `u_ij = rank_ij / (n + 1)`; bounded search ranges per family;
  the t pair copula is maximized by profile likelihood over `nu`.
- Meaning: tree-by-tree estimation; the total equals the vine
  log-likelihood of the pseudo-observations at the sequential estimates,
  which are consistent but not the joint maximum-likelihood estimates.
- Code: `modeling.fit_vine_copula`, `modeling.VineCopulaFit`.
- Source: [REF-AAS-CZADO-FRIGESSI-BAKKEN-2009],
  [REF-DISSMANN-BRECHMANN-CZADO-KUROWICKA-2013], [REF-AKAIKE-1974],
  [REF-SCHWARZ-1978].

### EQ-MOD-VINE-008 — Vine structure from absolute Kendall's tau

C-vine: the root of tree `j` maximizes `sum_{k != r} |tau(r, k)|` over the
remaining variables, using that tree's conditional pseudo-observations.
D-vine: a greedy path starts from `argmax |tau(i, j)|` and attaches, at
either end, the unused variable with the largest `|tau|` to that end.

- Domain: pairwise sample Kendall's tau ([EQ-MOD-COPULA-FIT-003]); ties are
  broken by the lower index.
- Meaning: strong dependence is placed in the first trees, where it is
  modelled unconditionally; the greedy path is a heuristic for the
  maximum-weight Hamiltonian path.
- Code: `modeling.fit_vine_copula`.
- Source: [REF-DISSMANN-BRECHMANN-CZADO-KUROWICKA-2013].

### EQ-MC-STEIN-001 — Langevin-Stein operator and polynomial zero-variance controls

`(A phi)(x) = Laplacian phi(x) + grad phi(x) . u(x)` with
`u = grad log pi`; for `phi = x_j`: `A phi = u_j`; for `phi = x_j^2`:
`A phi = 2 + 2 x_j u_j`; for `phi = x_j x_k` (`j < k`):
`A phi = x_k u_j + x_j u_k`. Degree 1 gives `p = d` controls and degree 2
gives `p = d + d(d+1)/2`.

- Domain: `pi` continuously differentiable and positive, `phi pi` and
  `grad phi pi` vanishing at infinity so that integration by parts gives
  `E_pi[A phi] = 0`; only the score is needed, not the normalizing constant.
- Meaning: zero-mean controls built from the target alone. Mira, Solgi and
  Imparato write the renormalized integrand as
  `f - (1/2) Laplacian P + grad P . z` with `z = -(1/2) grad log pi`, which is
  `f - (1/2) A P`; the factor `-1/2` is absorbed into the fitted
  coefficients. For a Gaussian target the degree-2 controls span every
  centred polynomial of degree at most two, so such integrands are
  integrated exactly.
- Code: `monte_carlo.stein_polynomial_controls`,
  `monte_carlo.estimate_zero_variance`.
- Source: [REF-ASSARAF-CAFFAREL-1999], [REF-MIRA-SOLGI-IMPARATO-2013,
  Section 4, Eq. (8)], [REF-OATES-GIROLAMI-CHOPIN-2017, Section 2.2.2].

### EQ-MC-STEIN-002 — Least-squares zero-variance estimator and variance-reduction factor

`(b, theta) = argmin sum_i (f_i - b - theta' h_i)^2 + lambda ||theta||^2`,
`mu_hat = n^-1 sum_i (f_i - theta' h_i)`,
`s_adj^2 = sum_i (c_i - mu_hat)^2 / (n - p - 1)` with
`c_i = f_i - theta' h_i`, `SE = sqrt(s_adj^2 / n)`, and
`VRF = s_f^2 / s_adj^2`.

- Domain: `n >= p + 2` points and a full-rank design `[1, H]` when
  `lambda = 0`; `lambda >= 0` penalizes `theta` only.
- Meaning: the ordinary least-squares `theta` equals the sample version of
  `Cov(h)^-1 Cov(h, f)`, the multivariate form of the optimal coefficient
  `a = -Sigma_zz^-1 sigma(z, f)` of the source. Fitting on the same sample
  introduces an `O(1/n)` bias, and the reported standard error is a plug-in
  value. With `standard_error="mcmc"` the IID formula is replaced by the
  effective-sample-size standard error of the contribution series
  [EQ-MCMC-MCSE-001], scaled by `sqrt(s_adj^2 / s_c^2)`.
- Code: `monte_carlo.estimate_zero_variance(method="same-sample")`.
- Source: [REF-MIRA-SOLGI-IMPARATO-2013, Sections 4 and 5],
  [REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013, Section 5.3].

### EQ-MC-STEIN-003 — Cross-fitted (split-sample) Stein estimator

Indices are cut into `K` contiguous folds `F_1, ..., F_K`; for `i` in `F_k`,
`c_i = f_i - g_(-k)(x_i)`, where `g_(-k)` is fitted without `F_k`
(`theta_(-k)' h` for zero-variance controls, `psi_(-k)` for control
functionals); `mu_hat = n^-1 sum_i c_i` and `SE = sqrt(s_c^2 / n)`.

- Domain: independent draws for exact unbiasedness, `K >= 2`, and enough
  training points per fold for the fit.
- Meaning: since `g_(-k)` has zero mean under `pi` and is independent of the
  held-out point, `E[c_i] = E_pi[f]` exactly. With `K = 2` it is the
  symmetrized form of the source's split estimator on `D_0` and `D_1`. The
  standard error ignores the weak dependence between folds through the
  fitted functions. For Markov-chain input the contiguous folds keep
  training and held-out blocks nearly independent, but unbiasedness then
  holds only asymptotically.
- Code: `monte_carlo.estimate_zero_variance(method="split-sample")`,
  `monte_carlo.estimate_control_functional`.
- Source: [REF-OATES-GIROLAMI-CHOPIN-2017, Sections 2.2.1 and 2.3.2,
  Lemma 3, Eq. (3)].

### EQ-MC-STEIN-004 — Stein reproducing kernel of a radial base kernel

`k0(x, y) = div_x div_y k + u(x) . grad_y k + u(y) . grad_x k +
u(x) . u(y) k`. For `k(x, y) = g(z)`, `z = ||x - y||^2`, `r = x - y`:
`k0 = -4 g''(z) z - 2 d g'(z) - 2 g'(z) (u(x) - u(y)) . r + (u(x) . u(y)) g(z)`;
Gaussian `g(z) = exp(-z / (2 l^2))`; inverse multiquadric
`g(z) = (c^2 + z)^beta`, `c > 0`, `beta` in `(-1, 0)`.

- Domain: twice continuously differentiable base kernel and a score `u`;
  `E_pi[k0(X, y)] = 0` for every `y` under the integration-by-parts
  conditions of the sources.
- Meaning: `k0` is the reproducing kernel of the image of the base-kernel
  Hilbert space under the Langevin-Stein operator, so every function
  `sum_j a_j k0(., x_j)` is a zero-mean control functional. The radial
  expansion follows from `grad_x k = 2 g' r`, `grad_y k = -2 g' r` and
  `div_x div_y k = -4 g'' z - 2 d g'`.
- Code: `monte_carlo.stein_kernel`, `monte_carlo.estimate_control_functional`,
  `monte_carlo.estimate_control_functional_weights`,
  `monte_carlo.kernel_stein_discrepancy`.
- Source: [REF-OATES-GIROLAMI-CHOPIN-2017, Section 2.3.1, Theorem 1],
  [REF-LIU-LEE-JORDAN-2016, Theorem 3.6], [REF-GORHAM-MACKEY-2017,
  Section 3.1, Proposition 2, Eq. (3)].

### EQ-MC-STEIN-005 — Control-functional fit and kernel-quadrature weights

`A = K0 + lambda mean(diag K0) I`, `c = 1' A^-1 f / 1' A^-1 1`,
`a = A^-1 (f - c 1)`, `psi(x) = sum_j a_j k0(x, x_j)`; on all `n` points the
estimate is `c = w' f` with `w = A^-1 1 / (1' A^-1 1)`, `sum_i w_i = 1`.

- Domain: `K0` from [EQ-MC-STEIN-004]; `lambda` starts at the requested
  relative value (default `1e-8`) and is raised by powers of ten until the
  Cholesky factorization of `A` succeeds, up to `1e-2`.
- Meaning: least-squares fit of `f` by a constant plus a control functional;
  `psi` evaluated on held-out points gives the split estimator
  [EQ-MC-STEIN-003], and the constant fitted on all points is the
  simplified estimator, a quadrature rule with possibly negative weights. The
  source picks the smallest power of ten giving condition number below
  `1e10`; the implementation uses Cholesky success instead, which avoids an
  `O(n^3)` condition estimate.
- Code: `monte_carlo.estimate_control_functional`,
  `monte_carlo.estimate_control_functional_weights`.
- Source: [REF-OATES-GIROLAMI-CHOPIN-2017, Sections 2.3.2 and 2.3.4],
  [REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013, Section 4.2].

### EQ-MC-STEIN-006 — Length-scale selection by median heuristic and cross-validation

`l_med = sqrt(H_n / 2)`, `H_n = median_(i<j) ||x_i - x_j||^2`; the
cross-validated choice minimizes
`sum_k sum_(i in F_k) (f_i - c_(-k) - psi_(-k)(x_i))^2` over the grid
`l_med * {1/4, 1/2, 1, 2, 4}` with five contiguous folds of the training
points.

- Domain: at least two distinct points; selection uses only the training
  points of the fit it serves, so the split estimator stays unbiased.
- Meaning: the median heuristic fixes the scale of the grid;
  cross-validation, used by the source for the kernel hyperparameters,
  chooses within it. For an `N(0, 1)` target and `f = cos`, the selected
  value was four times the median heuristic in most seeds.
- Code: `monte_carlo.median_heuristic_length_scale`,
  `monte_carlo.estimate_control_functional(length_scale="cv")`,
  `monte_carlo.estimate_control_functional_weights(length_scale="cv")`.
- Source: [REF-GARREAU-JITKRITTUM-KANAGAWA-2017, Section 2.2, Eq. (2)],
  [REF-OATES-GIROLAMI-CHOPIN-2017, Section 2.3.4].

### EQ-MC-STEIN-007 — Kernel Stein discrepancy V- and U-statistics

`KSD^2_V = n^-2 sum_(i,j) k0(x_i, x_j)`, `KSD = sqrt(KSD^2_V)`,
`KSD^2_U = (n(n-1))^-1 sum_(i != j) k0(x_i, x_j)`; for a weighted sample,
`KSD_w = sqrt(w' K0 w)`.

- Domain: [EQ-MC-STEIN-004] with the default inverse multiquadric kernel
  `c = 1`, `beta = -1/2`; samples from any source.
- Meaning: the V-statistic is the squared discrepancy of the empirical
  measure, the supremum of `|E_Q[div g + g . u]|` over vector fields `g` in
  the unit ball of the `d`-fold product of the base Hilbert space; the U-statistic is unbiased for independent draws and may
  be negative. With `beta` in `(-1, 0)` the IMQ discrepancy detects
  non-convergence for distantly dissipative targets. `KSD_w` is the
  worst-case integration error of the control-functional weights.
- Code: `monte_carlo.kernel_stein_discrepancy`,
  `monte_carlo.estimate_control_functional_weights`.
- Source: [REF-GORHAM-MACKEY-2017, Proposition 2 and Theorem 8],
  [REF-LIU-LEE-JORDAN-2016, Theorem 3.6, Eq. (9), and Section 4, Eq. (14)].

### EQ-AD-REVERSE-001 — Reverse-mode (adjoint) sweep

For an evaluation recorded as elementary operations `v_i = phi_i(v_j, j < i)`
with local partials `c_ij = d phi_i / d v_j`, seed `vbar_y = 1` (or
`vbar_(y_k) = w_k` for a vector function) and all other adjoints 0, then for
`i = N, N-1, ..., 1` set `vbar_j <- vbar_j + vbar_i c_ij` for every parent
`j` of node `i`. The input adjoints are `grad f(x)` (or `w' J(x)`).

- Domain: functions composed of `+ - * / **` and elementary functions that
  are differentiable at the evaluation point; unbounded derivatives
  (`sqrt` at 0, `asin`/`acos` at +-1, `0 ** c` with `c < 1`, `atan2` at the
  origin) are rejected; at the kinks `abs(0)` and `hypot(0, ..., 0)` the
  derivative is defined as 0.
- Meaning: exact (to rounding) gradient from one recorded evaluation and
  one backward sweep; the operation count is a small multiple of that of
  `f`, independent of the number of inputs.
- Code: `numerics.ReverseVariable`, `numerics.reverse_value_and_gradient`,
  `numerics.reverse_gradient`, `numerics.vector_jacobian_product`,
  `numerics.reverse_jacobian`, `numerics.GradientEvaluator`,
  `inference.no_u_turn_sampler`, `inference.hamiltonian_monte_carlo`,
  `inference.laplace_approximation`, `inference.ppl.ModelIR.gradient`.
- Source: [REF-GRIEWANK-WALTHER-2008, Chapters 3 and 4],
  [REF-BAYDIN-ETAL-2018, Section 3.2].

### EQ-AD-FOR-001 — Forward-over-reverse Hessian and Hessian-vector product

Record the tape of EQ-AD-REVERSE-001 on the dual inputs `x_i + t_i eps`;
every value and partial is then a dual, and so is every adjoint. With
`t = e_1, ..., e_d` (vector tangent) the adjoint of input `i` is
`d f / d x_i + sum_j H_ij eps_j`, so its tangent is row `i` of the Hessian;
with a single tangent `t = v` its tangent is `(H v)_i`. The full Hessian is
symmetrized, `(H + H')/2`.

- Domain: twice differentiable `f`; the Hessian of `digamma` (a dual
  `trigamma`) is not available.
- Meaning: exact Hessian at about `d` times the cost of one gradient, and
  an exact Hessian-vector product at a small multiple of one gradient
  without forming `H`.
- Code: `numerics.reverse_hessian`,
  `numerics.reverse_value_gradient_and_hessian`,
  `numerics.hessian_vector_product`, `inference.laplace_approximation`.
- Source: [REF-GRIEWANK-WALTHER-2008, Chapter 5], [REF-PEARLMUTTER-1994].

## Neural building blocks and stochastic optimization

### EQ-NN-MLP-001 — Multilayer perceptron

`h_0 = x`, `h_l = sigma_l(W_l h_{l-1} + b_l)` for `l = 1, ..., L`, with
`sigma_L` the output activation (identity by default); the network output is
`h_L`. Parameters `(W_1, b_1, ..., W_L, b_L)` are stored as one flat vector.

- Domain: real inputs of the declared width; activations `tanh`, logistic
  sigmoid `(1 + tanh(z/2))/2`, softplus `max(z, 0) + log1p(exp(-|z|))`, or
  identity.
- Meaning: a smooth parametric function class; with reverse-mode
  differentiation of a scalar loss its gradient costs a small multiple of one
  evaluation.
- Code: `numerics.MLP`.
- Source: [REF-GOODFELLOW-BENGIO-COURVILLE-2016, Sections 6.1 and 6.3].

### EQ-NN-GLOROT-001 — Normalized (Glorot) uniform initialization

`W_ij ~ U[-r, r]`, `r = sqrt(6 / (n_in + n_out))`, biases zero.

- Domain: a layer with `n_in` inputs and `n_out` outputs.
- Meaning: keeps the variance of activations and back-propagated gradients
  roughly constant across layers at initialization.
- Code: `numerics.MLP.initial_parameters`.
- Source: [REF-GLOROT-BENGIO-2010, Equation 16].

### EQ-OPT-ADAM-002 — Adam descent step

`m_t = b1 m_{t-1} + (1 - b1) g_t`, `v_t = b2 v_{t-1} + (1 - b2) g_t^2`,
`theta_t = theta_{t-1} - alpha (m_t / (1 - b1^t)) / (sqrt(v_t / (1 - b2^t)) + eps)`;
optionally the reported parameters average the iterates of the final
fraction of the iterations.

- Domain: stochastic gradients `g_t` of the objective to minimize;
  `0 <= b1, b2 < 1`, `alpha, eps > 0`.
- Meaning: the minimization form of [EQ-OPT-ADAM-001]; tail averaging
  reduces the noise a constant step leaves around the optimum.
- Code: `optimization.adam_minimize`.
- Source: [REF-KINGMA-BA-2015, Algorithm 1] and [REF-POLYAK-JUDITSKY-1992].

## Score-based diffusion and neural SDEs (ADR-0075)

### EQ-PROC-DIFF-001 — Variance-preserving forward SDE and perturbation kernel

`dx = -beta(t) x / 2 dt + sqrt(beta(t)) dw` on `[0, 1]` with
`beta(t) = beta_min + t (beta_max - beta_min)`;
`B(t) = beta_min t + (beta_max - beta_min) t^2 / 2`;
`x_t | x_0 ~ N(exp(-B(t)/2) x_0, (1 - exp(-B(t))) I)`; prior `N(0, I)`.

- Domain: `0 < beta_min <= beta_max`; defaults `0.1` and `20`; `x` in any
  dimension, coordinates independent given `x_0`.
- Meaning: the continuous limit of the DDPM noising chain; the kernel mean
  and variance solve `m' = -beta m / 2` and `v' = -beta v + beta`, and
  `m(t)^2 + v(t) = 1` for unit-variance data.
- Code: `processes.VariancePreservingSDE`, `processes.perturbation_moments`,
  `processes.perturb`.
- Source: [REF-SONG-ETAL-2021, Equations 11, 32, and 33] and
  [REF-HO-JAIN-ABBEEL-2020, Equation 4].

### EQ-PROC-DIFF-002 — Variance-exploding forward SDE and perturbation kernel

`sigma(t) = sigma_min (sigma_max / sigma_min)^t`,
`dx = sigma(t) sqrt(2 log(sigma_max / sigma_min)) dw`;
`x_t | x_0 ~ N(x_0, (sigma(t)^2 - sigma_min^2) I)`; prior
`N(0, sigma_max^2 I)`.

- Domain: `0 < sigma_min < sigma_max`; defaults `0.01` and `50`.
- Meaning: Brownian motion with a geometric noise schedule; the variance is
  the exact solution of `v' = g(t)^2` from `v(0) = 0`. The source writes
  the kernel variance as `sigma(t)^2`, which differs by the constant
  `sigma_min^2`.
- Code: `processes.VarianceExplodingSDE`, `processes.perturbation_moments`,
  `processes.perturb`.
- Source: [REF-SONG-ETAL-2021, Equations 9, 30, and 31].

### EQ-PROC-DIFF-003 — Diffused Gaussian marginal and its score

For data `N(mu, diag(s^2))` and a kernel `N(m(t) x_0, v(t) I)`:
`p_t = N(m(t) mu, diag(m(t)^2 s^2 + v(t)))` and
`grad log p_t(x)_j = -(x_j - m(t) mu_j) / (m(t)^2 s_j^2 + v(t))`.

- Domain: `s_j^2 > 0`; any affine Gaussian kernel of [EQ-PROC-DIFF-001]
  or [EQ-PROC-DIFF-002].
- Meaning: the exact score of the marginal law (a Gaussian convolved with a
  Gaussian kernel); it lets every sampler be verified against a known
  target without a trained network.
- Code: `processes.GaussianScore`.
- Source: [REF-SONG-ETAL-2021, Section 3.3] and
  [REF-HO-JAIN-ABBEEL-2020, Equation 4].

### EQ-PROC-DIFF-004 — Denoising score matching with weighting and noise parameterization

`theta* = argmin E_t { lambda(t) E_(x_0) E_(z) ||s_theta(x_t, t) + z / sqrt(v(t))||^2 }`,
`x_t = m(t) x_0 + sqrt(v(t)) z`, `z ~ N(0, I)`, `t ~ U(t_floor, 1)`;
`s_theta(x, t) = N_theta(c(t) x, 2 tau(t) - 1) / sqrt(v(t))` with
`c(t) = 1 / sqrt(m^2 + v)` and `tau(t) = sqrt(v / (m^2 + v))`. With the
default `lambda(t) = v(t)` the objective is `E ||N_theta + z||^2`.

- Domain: `0 < t_floor < 1` (default `1e-5`); `lambda(t) > 0`;
  `N_theta` an MLP of [EQ-NN-MLP-001] with `d + 1` inputs and `d` outputs.
- Meaning: `-z / sqrt(v)` is the score of the kernel, and the least-squares
  regression onto it has the marginal score as minimizer;
  `lambda proportional to 1 / E||grad log p_0t||^2 = v` equalizes the scales
  of all times, and the noise parameterization makes the loss the
  noise-prediction loss of DDPM.
- Code: `processes.train_score_network`, `processes.ScoreNetwork`,
  `processes.TrainedScore`.
- Source: [REF-SONG-ETAL-2021, Equation 7 and Section 3.3],
  [REF-VINCENT-2011], and [REF-HO-JAIN-ABBEEL-2020, Equation 14].

### EQ-PROC-DIFF-005 — Reverse-time SDE and its Euler-Maruyama step

`dx = [f(x, t) - g(t)^2 grad log p_t(x)] dt + g(t) dw_bar` run from `t = 1`
to `t = epsilon`; with step `h`:
`x <- x - [f(x, t) - g(t)^2 s(x, t)] h + g(t) sqrt(h) z`, `z ~ N(0, I)`.

- Domain: a forward SDE whose marginals `p_t` have a score; uniform grid
  `h = (1 - epsilon) / N`; default `epsilon = 1e-3` (VP) and `1e-5` (VE).
- Meaning: the time reversal of the forward diffusion has the same
  marginals; started from the prior it generates approximate data draws.
  The step is [EQ-PROC-SDE-001] applied to the reversed equation.
- Code: `processes.reverse_sde_sample`,
  `processes.predictor_corrector_sample` (predictor).
- Source: [REF-ANDERSON-1982], [REF-SONG-ETAL-2021, Equation 6], and
  [REF-KLOEDEN-PLATEN-1992, Section 10.2].

### EQ-PROC-DIFF-006 — Langevin corrector with signal-to-noise step size

`x <- x + eps s(x, t) + sqrt(2 eps) z`,
`eps = 2 alpha (r ||z|| / ||s||)^2`, with `alpha = 1` (VE) and
`alpha = 1 - beta(t) h` (VP); the norms are averaged over the sample batch.

- Domain: `r > 0` (default `0.16`); `beta(t) h < 1`.
- Meaning: an unadjusted Langevin move that leaves `p_t` approximately
  invariant and corrects the error of the predictor at each time.
- Code: `processes.predictor_corrector_sample`,
  `processes.VariancePreservingSDE.corrector_scale`,
  `processes.VarianceExplodingSDE.corrector_scale`.
- Source: [REF-SONG-ETAL-2021, Section 4.2 and Appendix G, Algorithms 4
  and 5].

### EQ-PROC-DIFF-007 — Probability-flow ODE with Runge-Kutta and Heun steps

`dx/dt = f(x, t) - g(t)^2 grad log p_t(x) / 2`; classical Runge-Kutta
`x <- x + h (k1 + 2 k2 + 2 k3 + k4) / 6` and Heun
`x <- x + h (k1 + k2) / 2` with signed step `h`.

- Domain: as [EQ-PROC-DIFF-005]; integration in either time direction.
- Meaning: a deterministic flow with the same marginals as the SDE; it maps
  prior draws to data draws and back. For Gaussian data and the exact score
  the map is affine, `x_e = m_e + (x_1 - m_1) sqrt(V_e / V_1)`.
- Code: `processes.probability_flow_map`, `processes.probability_flow_sample`.
- Source: [REF-SONG-ETAL-2021, Equation 13 and Section 4.3] and
  [REF-HAIRER-NORSETT-WANNER-1993, Section II.1].

### EQ-PROC-NSDE-001 — Euler-Maruyama Gaussian pseudo-likelihood

`-log L(theta) = sum_k sum_j [ log(2 pi b_j(x_k)^2 h_k) / 2
+ (x_(k+1),j - x_k,j - a_j(x_k) h_k)^2 / (2 b_j(x_k)^2 h_k) ]`.

- Domain: autonomous diagonal-noise SDE `dX_j = a_j(X) dt + b_j(X) dW_j`,
  `b_j > 0`, observations at increasing times with steps `h_k`.
- Meaning: the exact likelihood of the Euler-Maruyama chain
  [EQ-PROC-SDE-001]; it approximates the true transition likelihood with an
  `O(h)` bias, so densely observed paths are required.
- Code: `processes.NeuralSDE.transition_negative_log_likelihood`,
  `processes.fit_neural_sde`, `processes.NeuralSDEFit`.
- Source: [REF-IACUS-2008, Chapter 3] and
  [REF-KLOEDEN-PLATEN-1992, Section 10.2].

### EQ-PROC-NSDE-002 — Neural drift and diffusion parameterization

`u = (x - c) / r`; `a_j(x) = r_j N_j(u)`; `b_j = exp(rho_j)` (constant) or
`b_j(x) = b_min + softplus(M_j(u))` (network).

- Domain: `r_j > 0`, `b_min > 0`; `N` and `M` are MLPs of
  [EQ-NN-MLP-001] with `d` inputs and `d` outputs.
- Meaning: inputs standardized by the data mean `c` and spread `r`; the
  diffusion stays positive by construction; the starting diffusion is set
  to the quadratic-variation level `sqrt(mean(dx^2 / h))`.
- Code: `processes.NeuralSDE`, `processes.NeuralSDE.initial_parameters`,
  `processes.NeuralSDEFit.drift_on_grid`.
- Source: [REF-GOODFELLOW-BENGIO-COURVILLE-2016, Sections 6.1 and 6.3] and
  [REF-KLOEDEN-PLATEN-1992, Section 10.2].

## Generative models: normalizing flows and energy-based models

### EQ-GEN-FLOW-001 — Change of variables for a composed flow

`x = T(z) = T_K(... T_1(z))`, `z ~ N(0, I)`;
`log p(x) = log N(T^{-1}(x); 0, I) + sum_k log |det J_{T_k^{-1}}(x_k)|`,
where `x_K = x` and `x_{k-1} = T_k^{-1}(x_k)`; equivalently
`log p(T(z)) = log N(z) - sum_k log |det J_{T_k}(z_{k-1})|`. A permutation
layer has `|det| = 1`.

- Domain: every `T_k` is a diffeomorphism of `R^d`.
- Meaning: the exact density of the pushed-forward base law; the inverse
  direction evaluates the density of data, the forward direction samples
  with the density of each draw.
- Code: `generative.NormalizingFlow.log_density`, `forward`, `inverse`,
  `sample_with_log_density`, `generative.Permutation`.
- Source: [REF-PAPAMAKARIOS-ETAL-2021, Equations 2-6 and 25-28].

### EQ-GEN-FLOW-002 — Planar flow with the invertibility reparameterization

`x = z + u_hat tanh(w'z + b)`,
`u_hat = u + (m(w'u) - w'u) w / |w|^2`, `m(a) = -1 + log(1 + e^a)`, so
`w'u_hat = m(w'u) > -1`;
`log |det dx/dz| = log(1 + (1 - tanh^2(w'z + b)) w'u_hat)`. For `w = 0`
the map is the translation `z + u tanh(b)`.

- Domain: `u, w in R^d`, `b in R`.
- Meaning: a contraction or expansion perpendicular to the hyperplane
  `w'z + b = 0`; `w'u_hat > -1` makes the map strictly monotone along `w`
  and hence invertible.
- Code: `generative.PlanarFlow.forward`.
- Source: [REF-REZENDE-MOHAMED-2015, Equations 10-12 and Appendix A.1].

### EQ-GEN-FLOW-003 — Planar inverse by a scalar root and one Newton step

With `a = w'z`, `c = w'u_hat` and `y = w'x`, the inverse solves
`g(a) = a + c tanh(a + b) - y = 0` (strictly increasing for `c > -1`,
root within `|c|` of `y`) and sets `z = x - u_hat tanh(a + b)`. The root
`a*` is found in floating point; then `a = a* - g(a*) / g'(a*)` is evaluated
on the parameters, whose derivative at the root is `-g_theta / g_a`, the
implicit-function derivative.

- Domain: `c > -1` (guaranteed by EQ-GEN-FLOW-002).
- Meaning: exact inverse to rounding, differentiable in the parameters, so
  planar layers can be fitted by maximum likelihood.
- Code: `generative.PlanarFlow.inverse`.
- Source: [REF-REZENDE-MOHAMED-2015, Equations 21-23],
  [REF-GRIEWANK-WALTHER-2008, Chapter 15].

### EQ-GEN-FLOW-004 — Radial flow and its closed-form inverse

`x = z + beta h (z - z0)`, `h = 1 / (alpha + r)`, `r = |z - z0|`, with
`alpha = log(1 + e^a)` and `beta = -alpha + log(1 + e^c)` for raw
parameters `a, c`;
`log |det dx/dz| = (d - 1) log(1 + beta h) + log(1 + beta alpha h^2)`.
Inverse: `rho = |x - z0| = r (1 + beta / (alpha + r))`, i.e.
`r^2 + (alpha + beta - rho) r - rho alpha = 0`, positive root
`r = (sqrt(B^2 + 4 rho alpha) - B) / 2` (computed as
`2 rho alpha / (B + sqrt(...))` when `B = alpha + beta - rho > 0`), and
`z = z0 + (x - z0) / (1 + beta / (alpha + r))`.

- Domain: `alpha > 0`, `beta > -alpha` (guaranteed by the
  reparameterization).
- Meaning: radial contraction or expansion about `z0`; the determinant
  identity `1 + beta h + beta h' r = 1 + beta alpha h^2` uses
  `h' = -h^2`.
- Code: `generative.RadialFlow.forward`, `generative.RadialFlow.inverse`.
- Source: [REF-REZENDE-MOHAMED-2015, Equation 14 and Appendix A.2
  (Equations 24-26)].

### EQ-GEN-FLOW-005 — Affine coupling layer with bounded log-scale

`x_{1:k} = z_{1:k}`, `x_{k+1:d} = z_{k+1:d} * exp(s) + t`, with
`(r, t) = N_theta(z_{1:k})` and `s = c tanh(r / c)`;
`log |det dx/dz| = sum_j s_j`; inverse
`z_{k+1:d} = (x_{k+1:d} - t(x_{1:k})) * exp(-s(x_{1:k}))`.

- Domain: `1 <= k < d`, any conditioner network `N_theta`
  (EQ-NN-MLP-001), `c > 0`.
- Meaning: a triangular Jacobian whose determinant needs no derivative of
  the network; the bound `|s_j| < c` keeps every scale in
  `(e^{-c}, e^{c})`. Alternating with a permutation updates every
  coordinate.
- Code: `generative.AffineCoupling`, `generative.real_nvp_flow`.
- Source: [REF-DINH-SOHL-DICKSTEIN-BENGIO-2017, Equations 4-8 and
  Section 3.5]; the tanh bound is a design choice of this library.

### EQ-GEN-FLOW-006 — Activation normalization (element-wise affine)

`x_i = b_i + exp(l_i) z_i`, `log |det| = sum_i l_i`, inverse
`z_i = (x_i - b_i) exp(-l_i)`. Data-dependent initialization sets `b_i` to
the mean and `exp(l_i)` to the (`1/n`) standard deviation of coordinate `i`
of the data reaching the layer from the data side.

- Domain: real `b`, `l`; a non-zero spread for the initialization.
- Meaning: the points reaching the layer leave it with zero mean and unit
  variance at the start of training.
- Code: `generative.ActNorm`, `generative.NormalizingFlow.data_initialization`.
- Source: [REF-KINGMA-DHARIWAL-2018, Section 3.1 and Table 1].

### EQ-GEN-FLOW-007 — Maximum-likelihood objective of a flow

`L(theta) = -(1/B) sum_{x in batch} log p_theta(x)` on mini-batches of
size `B` drawn without replacement; minimizing the full-data version
minimizes the forward Kullback-Leibler divergence from the empirical law up
to a constant.

- Domain: training points in `R^d`, EQ-GEN-FLOW-001 for `log p_theta`.
- Meaning: unbiased mini-batch gradients of the negative mean
  log-likelihood, minimized by Adam (EQ-OPT-ADAM-002).
- Code: `generative.fit_flow`.
- Source: [REF-PAPAMAKARIOS-ETAL-2021, Equations 13-15].

### EQ-GEN-EBM-001 — Energy model with a quadratic-plus-network energy

`p(x) = exp(-E(x)) / Z`, `Z = int exp(-E(x)) dx`,
`E(x) = |L'(x - mu)|^2 / 2 + N_theta(x)` with `L` lower triangular and
`L_ii = exp(l_ii)`, so `A = L L'` is positive definite.

- Domain: `x in R^d`; `N_theta` an MLP (EQ-NN-MLP-001) with tanh or sigmoid
  hidden units (bounded slope) or softplus units (linear growth), so the
  quadratic dominates and `Z < inf`.
- Meaning: an unnormalized density whose score `-grad E` needs no `Z`;
  without a network it is `N(mu, A^{-1})`.
- Code: `generative.EnergyModel`, `generative.EnergyFit`.
- Source: [REF-HYVARINEN-2005, Section 2].

### EQ-GEN-EBM-002 — Implicit score-matching objective

With the model score `psi(x) = grad log q(x) = -grad E(x)`,
`J(theta) = int p_x(x) sum_i [d_i psi_i(x) + psi_i(x)^2 / 2] dx + const`,
estimated by
`J_hat = (1/T) sum_t [ |grad E(x_t)|^2 / 2 - Laplacian E(x_t) ]`.

- Domain: differentiable `psi`; `p_x(x) psi(x) -> 0` at infinity; finite
  second moments of `p_x` and `psi`.
- Meaning: equals the expected squared distance between model and data
  scores up to a constant, without the data score or `Z`.
- Code: `generative.score_matching_objective` (Laplacian by
  forward-over-reverse Hessian, EQ-AD-FOR-001),
  `generative.fit_score_matching` (Laplacian by EQ-GEN-EBM-005),
  `generative.EnergyModel.energy_laplacian`, `generative.EnergyModel.score`.
- Source: [REF-HYVARINEN-2005, Equations 1-4 and Theorem 1].

### EQ-GEN-EBM-003 — Score-matching estimate of a Gaussian precision

For `q(x) = exp(-(x - mu)' M (x - mu) / 2)`, `J_hat` is minimized by `mu`
equal to the sample mean and `M = S^{-1}`,
`S = (1/T) sum_t (x_t - mu)(x_t - mu)'`, with minimum value
`-trace(M) / 2`; the estimate coincides with maximum likelihood for every
sample.

- Domain: a positive-definite sample covariance.
- Meaning: the closed-form oracle against which the score-matching fit of a
  quadratic energy is verified.
- Code: `generative.EnergyModel.precision`; verified in
  `tests/test_generative_flows_energy.py`.
- Source: [REF-HYVARINEN-2005, Section 3.1.1, Equations 5-6].

### EQ-GEN-EBM-004 — Denoising score-matching objective (Gaussian kernel)

`J_DSM(theta) = E_{x, x_tilde} [ |psi(x_tilde) - grad log q_s(x_tilde | x)|^2 / 2 ]`,
`q_s(x_tilde | x) = N(x_tilde; x, s^2 I)`, so the gradient with respect to
`x_tilde` is `(x - x_tilde) / s^2 = -xi / s` for `x_tilde = x + s xi`.

- Domain: `s > 0`; first input derivatives of `E` only.
- Meaning: matches the score of the data smoothed by `N(0, s^2 I)`; for a
  quadratic energy and data with `1/n` covariance `S`, the minimizer over
  the noise distribution has precision `(S + s^2 I)^{-1}`.
- Code: `generative.fit_denoising_score_matching`,
  `generative.denoising_score_matching_objective`.
- Source: [REF-VINCENT-2011, Section 4.2, Equations 9-10].

### EQ-GEN-EBM-005 — Forward propagation of value, gradient, and Laplacian

For an intermediate `u` carried as `(u, grad u, Lap u)`: sums and constant
multiples are linear;
`uv -> (uv, u grad v + v grad u, u Lap v + v Lap u + 2 grad u . grad v)`;
`phi(u) -> (phi(u), phi'(u) grad u, phi''(u) |grad u|^2 + phi'(u) Lap u)`
with `tanh' = 1 - t^2`, `tanh'' = -2 t (1 - t^2)`, `exp'' = exp`,
`log1p' = 1 / (1 + u)`, `log1p'' = -1 / (1 + u)^2`. Inputs are seeded as
`(x_i, e_i, 0)`.

- Domain: programs built from these operations (every `MLP` with tanh,
  sigmoid, or softplus units); components may be reverse-mode variables of
  the parameters.
- Meaning: the input gradient and Laplacian of the energy at `O(d)` times
  the cost of one evaluation, as tape variables, so one backward sweep
  returns the exact parameter gradient of EQ-GEN-EBM-002.
- Code: `generative.EnergyModel.jet` (private module `generative._jet`).
- Source: [REF-GRIEWANK-WALTHER-2008, Chapter 13].

### EQ-GEN-LANG-001 — Unadjusted Langevin algorithm

`x_{n+1} = x_n + (h/2) grad log pi(x_n) + sqrt(h) xi_n`,
`xi_n ~ N(0, I)`: the Euler-Maruyama step of
`dX = grad log pi(X) dt / 2 + dW`. For `pi = N(0, sigma^2)` the chain is
AR(1) with coefficient `1 - h / (2 sigma^2)` and stationary variance
`sigma^2 / (1 - h / (4 sigma^2))`.

- Domain: `h > 0`, differentiable `log pi`.
- Meaning: samples `pi` up to an `O(h)` bias without `Z`; it may fail to
  converge for light-tailed targets.
- Code: `generative.sample_langevin` (`adjusted=False`).
- Source: [REF-ROBERTS-TWEEDIE-1996].

### EQ-GEN-LANG-002 — Metropolis-adjusted Langevin acceptance

Proposal `y = x + (h/2) g(x) + sqrt(h) xi`, `g = grad log pi`,
`q(y | x) = N(y; x + (h/2) g(x), h I)`; accept with probability
`min(1, pi(y) q(x | y) / (pi(x) q(y | x)))`, where
`-log q(y | x) = |xi|^2 / 2 + const` and
`-log q(x | y) = |x - y - (h/2) g(y)|^2 / (2h) + const`.

- Domain: `h > 0`; proposals outside the support are rejected.
- Meaning: a reversible Markov chain with stationary law exactly `pi`.
- Code: `generative.sample_langevin` (`adjusted=True`),
  `generative.EnergyFit.sample_langevin`.
- Source: [REF-ROBERTS-TWEEDIE-1996].

### EQ-GEN-DIAG-001 — Normalizing constant by quadrature or importance sampling

Quadrature: `log Z = c + log int exp(log f(x) - c) dx`, `c` the maximum of
`log f` on a coarse grid, the integral by adaptive Gauss-Kronrod (nested in
two dimensions). Importance sampling:
`Z_hat = (1/n) sum_i f(y_i) / q(y_i)`, `y_i ~ q`, with reported error
`SE(Z_hat) / Z_hat` and weight effective sample size `(sum w)^2 / sum w^2`
(EQ-MC-ESS-001).

- Domain: `f >= 0` integrable; for quadrature, a box holding the mass; for
  importance sampling, a normalized `q > 0` where `f > 0` (EQ-MC-IS-001).
- Meaning: turns an energy model into a normalized density, and checks
  that a flow density integrates to one.
- Code: `generative.quadrature_normalizing_constant`,
  `generative.importance_normalizing_constant`.
- Source: [REF-PIESSENS-QUADPACK-1983], [REF-OWEN-2013, Chapter 9].

### EQ-GEN-DIAG-002 — Mean log-likelihood and its standard error

`l_bar = (1/n) sum_t log p(x_t)`, `SE = s / sqrt(n)` with `s` the sample
standard deviation of the terms.

- Domain: a normalized density finite at every point.
- Meaning: the out-of-sample comparison score of fitted densities; the
  difference of two values estimates a difference of cross-entropies.
- Code: `generative.mean_log_likelihood`, `generative.FlowFit`,
  `generative.LangevinResult.mean`.
- Source: [REF-OWEN-2013, Chapter 2],
  [REF-PAPAMAKARIOS-ETAL-2021, Section 2.3.1].

### EQ-GEN-DIAG-003 — Monte Carlo Kullback-Leibler estimate

`KL(p || q) = E_p[log p(X) - log q(X)]`, estimated by
`(1/n) sum_i [log p(x_i) - log q(x_i)]`, `x_i ~ p`, with standard error
`s / sqrt(n)`.

- Domain: normalized `p` and `q`, `q > 0` where `p > 0`.
- Meaning: unbiased for the divergence of a fitted density `q` from a known
  truth `p`; a single estimate can be negative.
- Code: `generative.kl_divergence_estimate`.
- Source: [REF-COVER-THOMAS-2006, Section 2.3],
  [REF-PAPAMAKARIOS-ETAL-2021, Section 2.3.1].

## Semi-Markov processes and epistemic common-cause parameters (ADR-0076)

### EQ-PROC-SMP-001 — Semi-Markov kernel and mean sojourn times

`Q_ij(t) = P(J_(n+1) = j, X_(n+1) <= t | J_n = i) = p_ij F_ij(t)`, with the
embedded jump matrix `P = [p_ij]` and sojourn laws `F_ij` on `(0, inf)`;
`H_i(t) = sum_j Q_ij(t)` is the sojourn-time CDF of state `i` and
`tau_i = sum_j p_ij E[T_ij]` its mean. Exponential sojourns
`F_ij = Exp(q_i)` with `p_ij = q_ij / q_i` give the CTMC with generator `Q`.

- Domain: finite state space; rows of `P` sum to one for non-absorbing
  states; `F_ij(0) = 0`; finite positive means.
- Meaning: the next state is chosen by the jump chain, the holding time may
  depend on both the current and the next state and follow any law.
- Code: `processes.SemiMarkovProcess`, `processes.SemiMarkovProcess.kernel`,
  `processes.SemiMarkovProcess.from_ctmc`,
  `processes.SemiMarkovProcess.mean_sojourn_times`.
- Source: [REF-LIMNIOS-OPRISAN-2001, Chapters 2-3], [REF-CINLAR-1969].

### EQ-PROC-SMP-002 — Markov renewal equation for interval transition probabilities and rewards

`phi_ij(t) = delta_ij (1 - H_i(t)) + sum_k int_0^t phi_kj(t - s) dQ_ik(s)`;
for a reward vector `r`, `u_i(t) = E_i[r(Z_t)]` solves
`u(t) = (1 - H(t)) r + int_0^t dQ(s) u(t - s)`. Availability, reliability
(down states absorbing) and first-passage distributions (targets absorbing)
are rewards with indicator vectors.

- Domain: as EQ-PROC-SMP-001; finitely many jumps in finite time.
- Meaning: condition on the first jump: either the process is still in its
  initial state at `t`, or it jumped to `k` at time `s` and restarts there.
- Code: `processes.SemiMarkovProcess.transition_matrix`,
  `processes.SemiMarkovProcess.transient`,
  `processes.SemiMarkovProcess.expected_reward_curve`,
  `processes.SemiMarkovProcess.probability_curve`,
  `processes.SemiMarkovProcess.first_passage_curve`,
  `systems.SemiMarkovReliabilityModel`.
- Source: [REF-LIMNIOS-OPRISAN-2001, Chapters 3 and 5], [REF-CINLAR-1969].

### EQ-PROC-SMP-003 — Trapezoidal discretisation and Richardson extrapolation

On `t_n = n h` with exact kernel increments `A_l = (Q(t_l) - Q(t_(l-1)))/2`
and `B_l = A_l + A_(l+1)`:
`(I - A_1) u_n = (1 - H(t_n)) r + A_n u_0 + sum_(l=1)^(n-1) B_l u_(n-l)`,
which is the trapezoidal rule `int_(t_(l-1))^(t_l) u(t_n - s) dQ(s) ~
(u_(n-l) + u_(n-l+1)) A_l`. With `u^(N)` and `u^(2N)` the solutions on `N`
and `2N` steps, the reported value is `(4 u^(2N) - u^(N)) / 3` and the error
estimate is `|u^(2N) - u^(N)| / 3`.

- Domain: second-order accuracy and the `h^2` error expansion behind the
  extrapolation require smooth kernel densities; increments use `sf` when
  `F > 1/2` to avoid cancellation.
- Meaning: an implicit, positivity-friendly scheme of cost `O(N^2)` per
  reward column. The error estimate measures the finer trapezoidal
  solution, so it is conservative for the extrapolated value when the
  expansion holds; it is not a rigorous bound.
- Code: `processes.SemiMarkovProcess` (`_grid_solution`, `_extrapolated`),
  `processes.SemiMarkovEstimate`, `processes.RenewalCurve`.
- Source: [REF-CORRADI-JANSSEN-MANCA-2004], [REF-LINZ-1985, Chapters 7-8].

### EQ-PROC-SMP-004 — Absorption and mean time to absorption

With transient states `T` and absorbing states `A`:
`N = (I - P_TT)^(-1)` (expected visits), `B = N P_TA` (absorption
probabilities) and `m = N tau_T` (mean times to absorption); the mean
first-passage time to a set `S` is `m` of the process with `S` absorbing,
and `inf` when a closed class outside `S` is reachable.

- Domain: every closed class of the jump chain is a single absorbing state.
- Meaning: each visit to `j` lasts `tau_j` on average and visits and
  sojourns enter linearly, so only the sojourn means matter; for
  exponential sojourns `m = (-Q_TT)^(-1) 1`.
- Code: `processes.SemiMarkovProcess.absorption`,
  `processes.SemiMarkovProcess.mean_first_passage_time`,
  `processes.SemiMarkovAbsorption`,
  `systems.SemiMarkovReliabilityModel.mean_time_to_failure`.
- Source: [REF-LIMNIOS-OPRISAN-2001, Chapter 5], [REF-KEMENY-SNELL-1976, Chapter III].

### EQ-PROC-SMP-005 — Limiting law of a semi-Markov process

`pi_j = nu_j tau_j / sum_k nu_k tau_k`, where `nu` is the stationary law of
the jump chain (`nu P = nu`) on its unique closed class, computed by GTH
reduction.

- Domain: one closed class; non-lattice sojourn laws; finite means.
- Meaning: the long-run fraction of time in `j` is the visit frequency times
  the mean stay. For an alternating renewal unit (`up -> down -> up`):
  `A_inf = E[U] / (E[U] + E[D])`.
- Code: `processes.SemiMarkovProcess.steady_state`,
  `systems.SemiMarkovReliabilityModel.steady_state_availability`.
- Source: [REF-LIMNIOS-OPRISAN-2001, Chapter 3], [REF-CINLAR-1969].

### EQ-PROC-SMP-006 — Simulation of a semi-Markov path

Draw `J_0 ~ alpha`; given `J_n = i`, draw `J_(n+1) = j` with probability
`p_ij` and `X_(n+1) = F_ij^(-1)(U)` with `U ~ U(0, 1)`. The Monte Carlo
estimate of `P(Z_t in S)` is the fraction `h / n` of `n` paths in `S` at `t`,
with standard error `sqrt(p (1 - p) / n)`.

- Domain: sojourn laws with a quantile function.
- Meaning: an independent cross-check of EQ-PROC-SMP-002 to EQ-PROC-SMP-005.
- Code: `processes.SemiMarkovProcess.simulate`,
  `processes.SemiMarkovProcess.monte_carlo_probabilities`,
  `processes.SemiMarkovMonteCarlo`.
- Source: [REF-LIMNIOS-OPRISAN-2001, Chapter 3], [REF-DEVROYE-1986, Chapter II].

### EQ-SYS-SMP-001 — Semi-Markov reliability measures

With up states `U`, down states `D` and initial law `alpha` on `U`:
`A(t) = sum_(j in U) (alpha phi(t))_j`, `1 - A(t) = sum_(j in D) (alpha
phi(t))_j` (solved separately), `R(t) = sum_(j in U) (alpha phi^D(t))_j`
with `phi^D` the process with `D` absorbing, `MTTF = alpha N tau` on that
process, and `A_inf = sum_(j in U) pi_j`.

- Domain: as EQ-PROC-SMP-001 to EQ-PROC-SMP-005; independence from other
  blocks when used as a component (EQ-SYS-ADAPT-001).
- Meaning: repairable units with general failure and repair laws (Weibull
  wear-out, lognormal repair), reducing to EQ-SYS-MKV-001 for exponential
  sojourns.
- Code: `systems.SemiMarkovReliabilityModel`,
  `systems.alternating_renewal_unit`, `systems.SemiMarkovComponent`.
- Source: [REF-LIMNIOS-OPRISAN-2001, Chapter 5], [REF-BARLOW-PROSCHAN-1975].

### EQ-SYS-ECCF-001 — Exact reliability polynomial in uncertain CCF parameters

Under the probability split `Q_k = c_k Q_t` the beta-factor coefficients
`c_1 = 1 - beta`, `c_m = beta` and the MGL coefficients
`c_k = (prod_(i=2)^k rho_i)(1 - rho_(k+1)) / C(m-1, k-1)` are products of
uncertain factors `theta` or `1 - theta` and a constant
`a = Q_t prod(fixed factors) / C(m-1, k-1)`; `Q_t` may itself be an
uncertain factor. Each CCF event probability is then a monomial
`a prod_l lit_l` in the basis `prod_i theta_i^(j_i) (1 - theta_i)^(k_i)`,
and its complement `1 - a prod_l lit_l` is written with non-negative
coefficients by expanding `1 = prod_l (lit_l + (1 - lit_l))`. The Shannon
recursion `P(f) = p_x P(f_1) + q_x P(f_0)` on the BDD of the expanded
structure yields `R(theta)` and `1 - R(theta)` as exact polynomials with
non-negative coefficients, and
`E[R] = sum_alpha c_alpha prod_i E[theta_i^(j_i) (1 - theta_i)^(k_i)]`
with the mixed moments of EQ-SYS-MOM-002. Equivalently, given the
parameters every event occurs when independent indicators (one constant
indicator and one Bernoulli(`theta`) indicator per factor) all fire, which
is the shared-block model of EQ-SYS-MOM-002.

- Domain: probability split; independent parameters with laws on `[0, 1]`
  (beta laws in closed form, other laws by quadrature of
  `q^j (1 - q)^k f(q)`); alpha-factor parameters and the hazard split are
  not polynomial and use EQ-SYS-ECCF-003.
- Meaning: epistemic CCF parameters are propagated exactly, without
  sampling and without cancellation in the means.
- Code: `systems.ccf_parameter_uncertainty`, `systems.EpistemicCCFResult`.
- Source: [REF-MOSLEH-ETAL-1998], [REF-APOSTOLAKIS-KAPLAN-1981],
  [REF-RAUZY-1993].

### EQ-SYS-ECCF-002 — Exact first-order variance shares

`S_theta = Var(E[R | theta_S]) / Var[R]` with
`Var(E[R | theta_S]) = E[g(theta_S, theta) g(theta_S, theta')] - E[g]^2`,
where `theta'` is an independent copy of the parameters outside `S` and `g`
is the reliability polynomial of EQ-SYS-ECCF-001 or its complement,
whichever has the smaller mean. Grouping the terms of `g` by their
exponents in `theta_S`, the cross moment is
`sum_(s, s') w_s w_s' prod_(i in S) E[theta_i^(j_s + j_s')
(1 - theta_i)^(k_s + k_s')]` with `w_s` the coefficients integrated over the
other parameters. `S` = all parameters gives `Var[R]`; `S` = all CCF
parameters gives the CCF share.

- Domain: as EQ-SYS-ECCF-001.
- Meaning: the fraction of the epistemic variance of `R` explained by
  CCF-parameter uncertainty (one when only CCF parameters are uncertain).
- Code: `systems.ccf_parameter_uncertainty`.
- Source: [REF-SOBOL-1993], [REF-APOSTOLAKIS-KAPLAN-1981].

### EQ-SYS-ECCF-003 — Monte Carlo moments and centred Saltelli first-order estimator

With independent parameter samples `A`, `B` (`N` rows each) and `A_B^S`
(columns in `S` from `B`): `E[R] ~ mean f`, `Var[R] ~` the unbiased sample
variance over `A` and `B`, and
`V_S ~ (1/N) sum_j (f(B)_j - f_bar)(f(A_B^S)_j - f(A)_j)`.

- Domain: any CCF model and either split; parameters independent.
- Meaning: consistent estimates where EQ-SYS-ECCF-001 does not apply;
  centring removes the noise term proportional to `E[R]`.
- Code: `systems.ccf_parameter_uncertainty` (`method="monte-carlo"`).
- Source: [REF-SALTELLI-2010], [REF-SOBOL-1993].

### EQ-SYS-ECCF-004 — Interval CCF parameters: monotone bounds and probability box

For interval parameters `theta in [a, b]` (a box), the unreliability is
scanned along each coordinate and classified as increasing, decreasing,
constant or non-monotone; if it is monotone in every coordinate its range
over the box is attained at corners, `[min_c U(c), max_c U(c)]`. With
further parameters distributed, each corner gives an empirical CDF `F_c` of
`U` from common samples, and the probability box is
`[min_c F_c(y), max_c F_c(y)]`.

- Domain: at most 10 interval parameters; monotonicity checked on a grid
  through the box midpoint (otherwise the bounds are inner approximations).
- Meaning: bounds on the system unreliability that use no distribution
  inside the intervals.
- Code: `systems.ccf_interval_bounds`, `systems.CCFIntervalBounds`.
- Source: [REF-FERSON-ET-AL-2003], [REF-MOSLEH-ETAL-1998].

## Performance profiles and multiple-precision references (ADR-0077)

### EQ-NUM-PROFILE-001 — Performance ratio

`r_(p,s) = t_(p,s) / min{t_(p,u) : u in S}`, with `r_(p,s) = inf` when solver
`s` does not solve problem `p`.

- Domain: a set `S` of solvers and `P` of `n_p` problems; positive costs
  `t_(p,s)` (time, evaluations, or any performance measure).
- Meaning: how many times more expensive solver `s` is on problem `p` than
  the best solver on that problem. Sending the failure value `r_M` of the
  source to infinity changes no profile value for `tau < r_M`.
- Code: `numerics.performance_ratios`, `numerics.performance_profile`.
- Source: [REF-DOLAN-MORE-2002, Section 2].

### EQ-NUM-PROFILE-002 — Performance profile

`rho_s(tau) = |{p in P : r_(p,s) <= tau}| / n_p`; `rho_s(1)` is the fraction
of wins (ties count for every tied solver) and
`rho_s* = lim_(tau -> inf) rho_s(tau)` the fraction of problems solved.

- Domain: ratios of [EQ-NUM-PROFILE-001]; `tau` real.
- Meaning: the distribution function of a solver's performance ratio; a
  nondecreasing, right-continuous step function. `tau_s(f)`, the smallest
  `tau` with `rho_s(tau) >= f`, is the ratio at which the solver solves a
  fraction `f` of the problems.
- Code: `numerics.PerformanceProfile.value`, `wins`, `solved_fraction`,
  `tau_at`, `breakpoints`; `visualization.profile_plots.plot_performance_profile`.
- Source: [REF-DOLAN-MORE-2002, Section 2].

### EQ-NUM-PROFILE-003 — Normalized log2 area of a performance profile

`A_s = (1/L) int_0^L rho_s(2^t) dt = (1/(n_p L)) sum_(p : r_(p,s) <= tau_max)
(L - log2 r_(p,s))`, `L = log2 tau_max`; `A_s = rho_s(1)` when `tau_max = 1`.

- Domain: a profile of [EQ-NUM-PROFILE-002]; `tau_max >= 1`, by default the
  largest finite ratio of any solver so that all solvers share the axis.
- Meaning: a one-number summary of a profile on the logarithmic ratio axis:
  1 for a solver that is best on every problem, 0 for one that solves
  nothing within `tau_max`. It is a summary chosen by this library, not a
  quantity of the source; by Theorem 2.1 of the source, ratio changes of at
  most `epsilon` move the area under `rho_s` on a linear axis by at most
  `epsilon`.
- Code: `numerics.PerformanceProfile.area`.
- Source: [REF-DOLAN-MORE-2002, Section 2].

### EQ-NUM-PROFILE-004 — Data profile and convergence test

`d_s(kappa) = |{p in P : t_(p,s) / (n_p + 1) <= kappa}| / |P|`, where
`t_(p,s)` is the number of function evaluations solver `s` needs to pass the
convergence test `f(x_0) - f(x) >= (1 - tau)(f(x_0) - f_L)` on problem `p`
(`f_L`: best value any solver found; `tau`: accuracy level).

- Domain: problems of dimension `n_p`; `t_(p,s) = inf` when the test is never
  passed; `kappa >= 0` in simplex gradients (`n_p + 1` evaluations each).
- Meaning: the fraction of problems a solver solves within a computational
  budget, independent of the other solvers.
- Code: `numerics.data_profile`, `numerics.DataProfile`,
  `numerics.first_converged_evaluation`; the benchmark report
  (`benchmarks/report.py`) uses an error threshold as the test.
- Source: [REF-MORE-WILD-2009].

### EQ-NUM-REFERENCE-001 — pi from the arcsine series

`pi = 6 arcsin(1/2) = 6 sum_(n >= 0) (2n)! / (4^n (n!)^2 (2n + 1)) (1/2)^(2n+1)`.

- Domain: the series converges for `|z| <= 1`; at `z = 1/2` consecutive terms
  have ratio below `1/4`, so the tail after a term `t` is below `t/3`.
- Meaning: a positive-term series for `pi` with a rigorous truncation bound,
  evaluated in decimal arithmetic at any precision.
- Code: `numerics.reference_pi` (private `_pi` in `numerics.reference`).
- Source: [REF-NIST-DLMF-ELEMENTARY, Equation 4.24.1] and
  [REF-PYTHON-DECIMAL, Recipes].

### EQ-NUM-REFERENCE-002 — Error function series and Laplace continued fraction

`erf x = (2/sqrt pi) exp(-x^2) sum_(n >= 0) 2^n x^(2n+1) / (1 3 ... (2n+1))`;
`sqrt(pi) exp(x^2) erfc x = x/(x^2 + (1/2)/(1 + 1/(x^2 + (3/2)/(1 + 2/(x^2 + ...)))))`;
`Phi(x) = erfc(-x/sqrt 2)/2`.

- Domain: real `x`; the fraction is used for `x >= max(3, sqrt(w)/2)` with `w`
  working digits, the series below.
- Meaning: the series has positive terms with ratio `2x^2/(2n+3)`, so once the
  ratio is at most `1/2` the tail is below the last term; the fraction has
  positive elements, so its convergents bracket the value and the difference
  of successive convergents bounds the truncation error. `erfc` of moderate
  arguments is `1 - erf` recomputed with the digits the cancellation removes;
  `Phi` carries `log10(1 + x^2)` extra digits for the rounding of `x/sqrt 2`.
- Code: `numerics.reference_erf`, `numerics.reference_erfc`,
  `numerics.reference_normal_cdf`.
- Source: [REF-NIST-DLMF, Equations 7.2.2, 7.6.2, and 7.9.1].

### EQ-NUM-REFERENCE-003 — Modified Lentz evaluation and complements

`f_j = f_(j-1) C_j D_j` with `D_j = 1/(b_j + a_j D_(j-1))`,
`C_j = b_j + a_j / C_(j-1)` (zero denominators replaced by a tiny number),
stopped when `|C_j D_j - 1| <= 10^-w`; a complement `1 - v` is accepted when
`-log10(1 - v)`, the number of digits lost to cancellation, is at most the
extra digits carried in `v`.

- Domain: continued fractions `b_0 + a_1/(b_1 + a_2/(b_2 + ...))` with
  `b_0 != 0`; values `v` with relative error `10^-w`.
- Meaning: forward evaluation of a continued fraction without choosing the
  depth in advance; the stopping test compares successive convergents. The
  complement rule turns a relative accuracy of `v` into one of `1 - v`.
- Code: `numerics.reference` (`_lentz`, `_complement`).
- Source: [REF-LENTZ-1976], [REF-THOMPSON-BARNETT-1986], and
  [REF-HIGHAM-2002, Section 1.7].

### EQ-NUM-REFERENCE-004 — Normal quantile by Newton steps on log Phi

`x_(k+1) = x_k - (log Phi(x_k) - log p) Phi(x_k) / phi(x_k)`,
`phi(x) = exp(-x^2/2)/sqrt(2 pi)`, for `0 < p < 1/2`; `Phi^-1(p) = -Phi^-1(1 - p)`
for `p > 1/2`.

- Domain: `0 < p < 1`; the start is the double-precision quantile or, below
  the float range, `x_0 = -sqrt(2L - log(4 pi L))`, `L = -log p`.
- Meaning: Newton's method on the concave function `log Phi`, which converges
  quadratically; iteration stops when a step is below `10^-w |x|`, after
  which the remaining error is of the order of the squared step.
- Code: `numerics.reference_normal_quantile`.
- Source: [REF-NIST-DLMF, Sections 7.2 and 7.17].

### EQ-NUM-REFERENCE-005 — Shifted Stirling series for log Gamma

`log Gamma(x) = log Gamma(x + m) - log(x (x + 1) ... (x + m - 1))` and
`log Gamma(z) ~ (z - 1/2) log z - z + log(2 pi)/2 + sum_(k >= 1) B_(2k) / (2k (2k - 1) z^(2k-1))`,
with Bernoulli numbers from `sum_(k=0..n-1) C(n, k) B_k = 0` (`n >= 2`).

- Domain: `x > 0`; `z = x + m >= 0.37 w + 10` for `w` working digits.
- Meaning: for real `z > 0` the remainder after any number of terms is
  bounded in magnitude by the first neglected term (and has its sign), so the
  truncation error is known; near the zeros `x = 1, 2` the evaluation is
  repeated with `log10(|log Gamma(z)| / |log Gamma(x)|)` extra digits.
- Code: `numerics.reference_log_gamma`.
- Source: [REF-NIST-DLMF-GAMMA, Equations 5.5.1 and 5.11.1, Section 5.11(ii)]
  and [REF-NIST-DLMF-BERNOULLI, Equation 24.5.3].

### EQ-NUM-REFERENCE-006 — Incomplete gamma series and continued fraction

`P(a, x) = x^a e^-x sum_(k >= 0) x^k / Gamma(a + k + 1)` for `x < a + 1`;
`Q(a, x) = (x^a e^-x / Gamma(a)) (1/x)/(1 + ((1-a)/x)/(1 + (1/x)/(1 + ((2-a)/x)/(1 + (2/x)/(1 + ...)))))`
for `x >= a + 1`.

- Domain: `a > 0`, `x >= 0`.
- Meaning: the series has positive terms with ratio `x/(a + k + 1)`, so its
  tail is bounded once the ratio is at most `1/2`; the fraction is evaluated
  by [EQ-NUM-REFERENCE-003] and terminates for integer `a`. The prefactor
  `exp(a log x - x - log Gamma(a))` is formed with `log10` of its exponent in
  extra digits; the other ratio is a complement with full relative accuracy.
- Code: `numerics.reference_regularized_gamma_p`,
  `numerics.reference_regularized_gamma_q`.
- Source: [REF-NIST-DLMF-GAMMA, Equations 8.7.1 and 8.9.2].

### EQ-NUM-REFERENCE-007 — Incomplete beta continued fraction and integer case

`I_x(a, b) = (x^a (1-x)^b / (a B(a, b))) / (1 + d_1/(1 + d_2/(1 + ...)))`,
`d_(2m) = m(b-m)x / ((a+2m-1)(a+2m))`, `d_(2m+1) = -(a+m)(a+b+m)x / ((a+2m)(a+2m+1))`,
for `x < (a + 1)/(a + b + 2)`, otherwise `I_x(a, b) = 1 - I_(1-x)(b, a)`; for
positive integers `I_x(m, n - m + 1) = sum_(j=m..n) C(n, j) x^j (1-x)^(n-j)`.

- Domain: `0 <= x <= 1`, `a, b > 0` (integers for the binomial sum).
- Meaning: the fraction converges fastest below the switch point; the
  binomial sum gives the integer case exactly in rational arithmetic.
- Code: `numerics.reference_regularized_beta`,
  `numerics.exact_regularized_beta`.
- Source: [REF-NIST-DLMF-BETA, Equations 8.17.4, 8.17.5, 8.17.22, and
  8.17.23].

### EQ-NUM-REFERENCE-008 — Error in units in the last place

`ulp_err(y) = |y - v| / ulp(fl(v))`, with `v` the high-precision reference,
`fl(v)` its nearest double, and `ulp` the spacing of doubles at `fl(v)`.

- Domain: finite `v` within the double range; `y` the double result under
  test (`inf` error when `y` is not finite).
- Meaning: a correctly rounded result scores at most `0.5`; a budget of `k`
  ULPs bounds the relative error by about `k 2^-52`.
- Code: `numerics.ulp_error`, `numerics.compare_to_reference`,
  `numerics.ReferenceComparison`.
- Source: [REF-GOLDBERG-1991, Section 1.2] and [REF-PYTHON-MATH].

## Roadmap evidence audit additions (ADR-0079)

### EQ-INF-GOF-CVM-001 — Cramer-von Mises statistic

`W^2 = 1/(12 n) + sum_(i=1..n) (F(x_(i)) - (2i - 1)/(2n))^2`.

- Domain: ordered finite sample `x_(1) <= ... <= x_(n)` and a continuous
  null CDF `F`.
- Meaning: `n` times the integrated squared distance between the empirical
  and null CDFs, weighted by the null law; its null distribution depends on
  whether parameters were estimated from the data.
- Code: `inference.cramer_von_mises_statistic`, `inference.normality_tests`.
- Source: [REF-STEPHENS-1974] and [REF-STEPHENS-1986].

### EQ-INF-GOF-NORM-001 — Lilliefors p-value for the fitted-normal KS distance

With `D` the KS distance to `N(x_bar, s^2)` (divisor `n - 1`), `K = D`,
`m = n` for `n <= 100`, and `K = D (n/100)^0.49`, `m = 100` otherwise:
`p = exp(-7.01256 K^2 (m + 2.78019) + 2.99587 K sqrt(m + 2.78019) -
0.122119 + 0.974598/sqrt(m) + 1.67997/m)`. When this exceeds `0.1`,
`Z = D (sqrt(n) - 0.01 + 0.85/sqrt(n))` and `p = 1` for `Z <= 0.302`, a
quartic polynomial in `Z` on `(0.302, 0.5]`, `(0.5, 0.9]`, and `(0.9, 1.31]`,
and `p = 0` above `1.31`.

- Domain: `n >= 5`; normal null with both parameters estimated.
- Meaning: calibrated tail probability of the Lilliefors statistic; the
  analytic part is reliable for `p <= 0.1`, the polynomial covers the bulk.
- Code: `inference.lilliefors_p_value`, `inference.normality_tests`.
- Source: [REF-DALLAL-WILKINSON-1986] (analytic approximation),
  [REF-STEPHENS-1974] (modified statistic `Z`), and
  [REF-GROSS-LIGGES-2015, function `lillie.test`] (polynomial coefficients
  fitted by simulation).

### EQ-INF-GOF-NORM-002 — Fitted-normal Cramer-von Mises p-value

`W* = W^2 (1 + 0.5/n)`;
`p = 1 - exp(-13.953 + 775.5 W* - 12542.61 W*^2)` for `W* < 0.0275`,
`1 - exp(-5.903 + 179.546 W* - 1515.29 W*^2)` for `W* < 0.051`,
`exp(0.886 - 31.62 W* + 10.897 W*^2)` for `W* < 0.092`,
`exp(1.111 - 34.242 W* + 12.832 W*^2)` for `W* < 1.1`, and `7.37e-10`
beyond.

- Domain: normal null with mean and `n - 1` standard deviation estimated;
  `n >= 8`.
- Meaning: tabulated null law of the fitted statistic, valid for every
  `n` after the modification.
- Code: `inference.normality_tests`.
- Source: [REF-STEPHENS-1986, Table 4.9] as implemented in
  [REF-GROSS-LIGGES-2015, function `cvm.test`].

### EQ-INF-GOF-NORM-003 — Fitted-normal Anderson-Darling p-value

`A* = A^2 (1 + 0.75/n + 2.25/n^2)`;
`p = 1 - exp(-13.436 + 101.14 A* - 223.73 A*^2)` for `A* < 0.2`,
`1 - exp(-8.318 + 42.796 A* - 59.938 A*^2)` for `A* < 0.34`,
`exp(0.9177 - 4.279 A* - 1.38 A*^2)` for `A* < 0.6`,
`exp(1.2937 - 5.709 A* + 0.0186 A*^2)` for `A* < 10`, and `3.7e-24` beyond.

- Domain: normal null with mean and `n - 1` standard deviation estimated;
  `n >= 8`.
- Meaning: tabulated null law of the fitted Anderson-Darling statistic.
- Code: `inference.normality_tests`.
- Source: [REF-STEPHENS-1986, Table 4.9] as implemented in
  [REF-GROSS-LIGGES-2015, function `ad.test`].

### EQ-CONF-ACI-001 — Adaptive conformal level update

`err_t = 1{S_t(X_t, Y_t) > Q_t(1 - alpha_t)}`,
`alpha_(t+1) = alpha_t + gamma (alpha - err_t)`, with `alpha_1` in `[0, 1]`.

- Domain: target miscoverage `alpha` in `(0, 1)`, step `gamma >= 0`, any
  sequence of scores (no exchangeability assumption).
- Meaning: an online step on the single parameter that absorbs distribution
  shift; a miss lowers `alpha_t` (wider sets), a cover raises it.
- Code: `conformal.AdaptiveConformalPredictor.update`,
  `conformal.adaptive_conformal_intervals`.
- Source: [REF-GIBBS-CANDES-2021, Equation 2].

### EQ-CONF-ACI-002 — Adaptive conformal score threshold and interval

For a score history `H` of size `m`: `Q_t(1 - alpha_t) = -inf` if
`alpha_t >= 1`; `+inf` if `alpha_t <= 0`, `m = 0`, or
`k = ceil((1 - alpha_t)(m + 1)) > m`; otherwise the `k`-th smallest score.
The interval is `yhat_t +/- Q_t(1 - alpha_t) s_t`, with score
`S_t = |y_t - yhat_t| / s_t`.

- Domain: non-negative scores; positive spreads `s_t` (`s_t = 1` for
  absolute residuals); optional sliding window over `H`.
- Meaning: the split conformal quantile at the adapted level; the infinite
  thresholds at the boundary levels are what keep `alpha_t` inside
  `[-gamma, 1 + gamma]`.
- Code: `conformal.AdaptiveConformalPredictor.radius`,
  `conformal.AdaptiveConformalPredictor.interval`.
- Source: [REF-GIBBS-CANDES-2021, Equation 1 and Section 4.1] with the
  finite-sample index of [EQ-CONF-001].

### EQ-CONF-ACI-003 — Long-run miscoverage bound

`|(1/T) sum_(t=1..T) err_t - alpha| <= (max(alpha_1, 1 - alpha_1) + gamma) / (gamma T)`
for every `T`, since `alpha_t` stays in `[-gamma, 1 + gamma]`.

- Domain: `gamma > 0`; holds deterministically for every data sequence.
- Meaning: the empirical miscoverage frequency converges to `alpha` at rate
  `1/T` without any assumption on the data-generating process; it says
  nothing about conditional coverage at a given time.
- Code: `conformal.AdaptiveConformalPredictor.long_run_bound`,
  `conformal.AdaptiveConformalResult`.
- Source: [REF-GIBBS-CANDES-2021, Lemma 4.1 and Proposition 4.1].

### EQ-RISK-BANDIT-001 — Beta-Bernoulli posterior update

`(alpha_k, beta_k) <- (alpha_k, beta_k) + (r_t, 1 - r_t)` if `x_t = k`,
unchanged otherwise; posterior mean `alpha_k / (alpha_k + beta_k)`.

- Domain: independent `Beta(alpha_k, beta_k)` priors, `alpha_k, beta_k > 0`;
  rewards `r_t` in `{0, 1}`.
- Meaning: conjugate updating of each action's success probability with
  pseudo-counts; only the played action learns.
- Code: `risk.bernoulli_bandit`, `risk.BanditRun.posterior_means`.
- Source: [REF-RUSSO-ETAL-2018, Example 3.1].

### EQ-RISK-BANDIT-002 — Thompson sampling action choice

`theta_hat_k ~ Beta(alpha_k, beta_k)` independently, `x_t = argmax_k theta_hat_k`,
so `P(x_t = k | history) = P(theta_k = max_j theta_j | history)`.

- Domain: the Beta posteriors of [EQ-RISK-BANDIT-001].
- Meaning: probability matching; each action is played with its posterior
  probability of being optimal, which balances exploration and
  exploitation. The greedy rule replaces the draw by the posterior mean.
- Code: `risk.bernoulli_bandit`, `risk.BanditRun.probability_optimal`.
- Source: [REF-RUSSO-ETAL-2018, Algorithms 3.1 and 3.2] and
  [REF-THOMPSON-1933].

### EQ-RISK-BANDIT-003 — Cumulative pseudo-regret

`Regret(T) = sum_(t=1..T) (max_k theta_k - theta_(x_t))`.

- Domain: known success probabilities (simulation studies only).
- Meaning: expected reward lost against always playing the best action;
  uniform random play has regret linear in `T`.
- Code: `risk.bernoulli_bandit` (`risk.BanditRun.cumulative_regret`).
- Source: [REF-RUSSO-ETAL-2018, Chapter 3].

### EQ-SENS-STOCH-001 — Variance decomposition of a stochastic simulator

`Var(Y) = Var(m(X)) + E[Var(Y | X)]`, `m(x) = E[Y | X = x]`;
`S_i = V_i / Var(m)`, `ST_i = T_i / Var(m)` with `V_i = Var(E[m(X) | X_i])`,
`T_i = E[Var(m(X) | X_(~i))]`; output shares `V_i / Var(Y)` and the
intrinsic-noise index `S_omega = E[Var(Y | X)] / Var(Y)`.

- Domain: `Y = g(X, omega)` with independent inputs `X` and intrinsic
  randomness `omega` independent of `X`; finite `Var(Y)`, `Var(m) > 0`.
- Meaning: `V_i / Var(Y)` is the first-order index of `Y` when `omega` is
  treated as an extra input, and `S_omega` is the total effect of `omega`;
  indices of `m` describe the controllable part alone.
- Code: `sensitivity.stochastic_sobol_indices`,
  `sensitivity.StochasticSobolResult`.
- Source: [REF-IOOSS-RIBATET-MARREL-2009, Equations 15, 19, 20, and 21] and
  [REF-MARREL-ETAL-2012].

### EQ-SENS-STOCH-002 — Replicate mean and within-point variance

At design point `x` with `R >= 2` independent runs `y_1..y_R`:
`ybar(x) = (1/R) sum_r y_r`, `s^2(x) = (1/(R-1)) sum_r (y_r - ybar)^2`, so
`E[s^2(x)] = Var(Y | X = x)` and `Var(ybar(x) | x) = Var(Y | X = x) / R`.

- Domain: runs at one point use independent seeds; runs at different
  points are independent.
- Meaning: the within-point variance estimates the intrinsic noise without
  bias, which the estimators of [EQ-SENS-STOCH-003] subtract.
- Code: `sensitivity.stochastic._replicate`.
- Source: [REF-IOOSS-RIBATET-MARREL-2009, Section 3.2] (dispersion
  component `Var(Y | X)`).

### EQ-SENS-STOCH-003 — Noise-corrected pick-freeze estimators

With design matrices `A`, `B`, `A_B^(i)` of `N` rows and `c` the mean of
`ybar` over `A` and `B`:
`Vhat_i = (1/N) sum_k (ybar_B,k - c)(ybar_ABi,k - ybar_A,k)`,
`That_i = (1/(2N)) sum_k [(ybar_A,k - ybar_ABi,k)^2 - (s^2_A,k + s^2_ABi,k)/R]`,
`noise = mean(s^2)` over all design points,
`Var(m)hat = var(ybar over A and B) - noise / R`.

- Domain: as [EQ-SENS-STOCH-001]; noise independent across design points.
- Meaning: independent noise cancels in the expectation of the first-order
  product, and the subtracted terms remove the noise inflation of the Jansen
  total-effect estimator and of the variance of replicate means.
- Code: `sensitivity.stochastic_sobol_indices`.
- Source: [REF-SALTELLI-2010] and [REF-JANSEN-1999] (pick-freeze
  estimators), applied to replicate means with the noise correction of
  [EQ-SENS-STOCH-002].

### EQ-VAL-STACK-001 — Log-score stacking of predictive distributions

`w* = argmax_(w in simplex) (1/n) sum_(i=1..n) log sum_(k=1..K) w_k p_k,-i(y_i)`,
computed by `w_k <- w_k g_k`, `g_k = (1/n) sum_i p_ik / sum_j w_j p_ij`,
stopped when `max_k g_k - 1 <= tol`, which bounds `f(w*) - f(w)` by
concavity.

- Domain: pointwise out-of-sample (leave-one-out or held-out validation)
  predictive densities `p_ik >= 0`, each row positive for some model.
- Meaning: the weighted mixture of the models' predictive distributions
  with the best expected log score; it keeps several models when each is
  right on part of the data, unlike Bayesian model averaging.
- Code: `validation.stacking_weights`.
- Source: [REF-YAO-ETAL-2018, Section 2.1, Equation 2.2] (objective),
  [REF-MCLACHLAN-PEEL-2000] (EM update of mixing proportions), and
  [REF-NOCEDAL-WRIGHT-2006, Chapter 12] (optimality conditions).

### EQ-VAL-STACK-002 — Pseudo-BMA and pseudo-BMA+ weights

`w_k = exp(elpd_k) / sum_j exp(elpd_j)`, `elpd_k = sum_i log p_k,-i(y_i)`;
pseudo-BMA+: `a ~ Dirichlet(1, ..., 1)`, `z_k = n sum_i a_i log p_k,-i(y_i)`,
`w_k = mean over B draws of exp(z_k) / sum_j exp(z_j)`.

- Domain: as [EQ-VAL-STACK-001]; `B >= 1` Bayesian-bootstrap draws.
- Meaning: AIC-type weights from the estimated expected log predictive
  density; the Bayesian bootstrap accounts for the uncertainty of the elpd
  estimate and moves weights away from 0 and 1.
- Code: `validation.pseudo_bma_weights`.
- Source: [REF-YAO-ETAL-2018, Section 2.4, Equations 2.5 and 2.6].

### EQ-VAL-STACK-003 — Variance of a model-averaged prediction

`mu = sum_k w_k mu_k`,
`Var = sum_k w_k sigma_k^2 + sum_k w_k (mu_k - mu)^2`.

- Domain: simplex weights; per-model predictive means `mu_k` and variances
  `sigma_k^2`.
- Meaning: law of total variance for the mixture `sum_k w_k p_k`; the second
  term is the between-model (model-form) component.
- Code: `validation.model_averaged_prediction`.
- Source: [REF-YAO-ETAL-2018, Equation 2.3] (mixture predictive) and
  [REF-MCLACHLAN-PEEL-2000] (mixture moments).

### EQ-INF-NPE-001 — Gaussian neural posterior estimation

`theta_n ~ p(theta)`, `x_n ~ p(x | theta_n)`, `n = 1..N`;
`q_phi(theta | x) = prod_j N(theta_j; mu_j(x; phi), sigma_j(x; phi)^2)` with
`(mu, log sigma) = MLP_phi(x)` on standardized coordinates;
`phi_hat = argmax_phi sum_n log q_phi(theta_n | x_n)`.

- Domain: a prior that can be sampled and a simulator returning a
  fixed-width vector of finite summaries; the likelihood need not be
  available.
- Meaning: as `N -> infinity`, maximum likelihood over a family that
  contains the posterior recovers `p(theta | x)` for every `x` when the
  proposal is the prior, so one trained network gives the posterior for any
  new observation (amortization). With a diagonal Gaussian family the result
  is exact only for Gaussian posteriors with independent coordinates.
- Code: `inference.fit_amortized_gaussian_posterior`,
  `inference.AmortizedGaussianPosterior`.
- Source: [REF-PAPAMAKARIOS-MURRAY-2016, Proposition 1, Section 2.3, and
  Algorithm 2], trained with [EQ-OPT-ADAM-002].

## Accessibility of figures and reports

### EQ-VIZ-WCAG-001 — Relative luminance of an sRGB colour

`L = 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B`, where each channel `C` in
`{R, G, B}` is linearized from its 8-bit value `C8` by `c = C8 / 255` and
`C = c / 12.92` if `c <= 0.03928`, otherwise `C = ((c + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4`.

- Domain: sRGB colours given as `#RRGGBB` tokens; `0 <= L <= 1`, black 0,
  white 1.
- Meaning: the luminance weight of a colour under the sRGB primaries. The
  threshold `0.03928` is the value written in WCAG 2.1; the sRGB standard
  uses `0.04045`, and no 8-bit channel value lies between the two, so both
  give the same result.
- Code: `visualization.accessibility.relative_luminance`.
- Source: [REF-W3C-WCAG21-2018, definition "relative luminance"].

### EQ-VIZ-WCAG-002 — Contrast ratio of two colours

`CR = (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05)`, with `L1` the larger and `L2` the smaller
relative luminance [EQ-VIZ-WCAG-001] of the two colours.

- Domain: two sRGB colours; `1 <= CR <= 21`, symmetric in its arguments.
- Meaning: legibility of text or marks on a background. Level AA requires
  at least 4.5 for body text (success criterion 1.4.3), 3 for large text,
  and 3 for graphical objects such as plotted lines (criterion 1.4.11).
- Code: `visualization.accessibility.contrast_ratio`,
  `visualization.accessibility.palette_contrast`.
- Source: [REF-W3C-WCAG21-2018, definition "contrast ratio"].

## Dense backend boundary (ADR-0081)

### EQ-LINALG-010 — Explicitly shifted Cholesky factorization

`A + delta I = L L'` with a caller-supplied shift `delta >= 0`; `delta = 0`
is the plain factorization [EQ-LINALG-001].

- Domain: finite symmetric `A` whose shift `A + delta I` is positive
  definite, i.e. `delta > -lambda_min(A)`; otherwise the factorization fails
  and the failure is reported, never repaired by enlarging `delta`.
- Meaning: the jitter policy of every dense backend. The shift is part of
  the caller's model (a nugget or noise variance), so it is always visible
  in the arguments and recorded on the factorization.
- Code: `linalg.DenseBackend.cholesky`, `linalg.DenseBackend.factorize`,
  `linalg.CholeskyFactorization.jitter`.
- Source: [REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013, Section 4.2] and
  [REF-HIGHAM-2002, Chapter 10].

### EQ-LINALG-011 — Inverse from a Cholesky factor

`A^-1 = L^-T L^-1` for `A = L L'`, with `L^-1` obtained by forward
substitution [EQ-LINALG-002] on the columns of `I` (equivalently, column
`j` of `A^-1` solves `L L' x = e_j`); the result is symmetrized as
`(X + X') / 2`.

- Domain: `L` lower triangular with a positive diagonal.
- Meaning: every entry of `A^-1` from one existing factorization, as needed
  by the Gaussian-process likelihood gradient, leave-one-out diagonal, and
  condition number.
- Code: `linalg.inverse_spd`, `linalg.CholeskyFactorization.inverse`,
  `linalg.DenseBackend.inverse_spd`.
- Source: [REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013, Sections 3.1 and 4.2] and
  [REF-HIGHAM-2002, Chapter 14].

### EQ-LINALG-012 — Agreement bound between backward-stable backends

With unit roundoff `u = 2^-53` and `gamma_k = k u / (1 - k u)`:

- Cholesky residual, componentwise: `|A - L L'| <= gamma_(n+1) |L||L'|`.
- Factor agreement: `||L_1 - L_2||_F / ||L||_2 <= 2 kappa_2(A) gamma_(n+1)
  tr(A) / ||A||_2`.
- SPD solve agreement: `||x_1 - x_2|| / ||x|| <= 2 kappa_2(A)
  gamma_(3n+1) tr(A) / ||A||_2`.
- Log-determinant agreement: `|log det_1 - log det_2| <= n` times the
  factor bound.
- Products, componentwise: `|fl_1(AB) - fl_2(AB)| <= (gamma_k + 2u) |A||B|`
  for inner dimension `k`.
- Eigenvalues (Weyl): `|lambda_i,1 - lambda_i,2| <= ||E_1||_2 + ||E_2||_2`,
  each `||E||` bounded by the method's backward error.

- Domain: two implementations that are each backward stable in the sense
  of the cited analyses; first order in `u`.
- Meaning: each result is exact for a matrix within `gamma_k |L||L'|` of
  `A`, so `|| |L||L'| ||_F <= ||L||_F^2 = tr(A)` converts the componentwise
  backward error to `gamma_k tr(A)`; perturbation theory multiplies it by at
  most `kappa_2(A)` in the forward error, and two results differ by at most
  the sum of their errors. The bound is a test tolerance, not an error
  estimate: observed differences are many orders of magnitude smaller.
- Code: `tests/test_linalg_backend.py` (reference comparisons of
  `linalg.NumPyBackend` against `linalg.PythonBackend`).
- Source: [REF-HIGHAM-2002, Chapters 3, 7, 8, and 10] and
  [REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013, Section 8.1].

### EQ-INF-COUNT-001 — Poisson maximum likelihood from counts

`l(lambda) = sum_i (x_i log lambda - lambda - log x_i!)`,
`lambda_hat = x_bar = sum_i x_i / n`, `SE(lambda_hat) = sqrt(lambda_hat / n)`;
for a frequency table `f_k`, `l = sum_k f_k (k log lambda - lambda - log k!)`.

- Domain: `n >= 2` independent non-negative integer counts with a positive
  total.
- Meaning: the sample mean maximizes the Poisson likelihood; the standard
  error is the inverse square root of the observed information
  `n / lambda_hat`. The fitted frequencies are `n p(k; lambda_hat)`.
- Code: `inference.fit_poisson_counts`, `inference.CountFit`.
- Source: [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002, Section 7.2] and [EQ-DIST-POIS-001].

### EQ-INF-COUNT-002 — Negative binomial profile likelihood and its Poisson boundary

`p(k; r, mu) = Gamma(k + r) / (Gamma(r) k!) (r/(r+mu))^r (mu/(r+mu))^k`,
mean `mu`, variance `mu + mu^2 / r`; for fixed `r` the likelihood is
maximized at `mu = x_bar`; the profile score is
`S(r) = sum_k f_k sum_{j=0}^{k-1} 1/(r+j) + n log(r / (r + x_bar))`, and
`d^2 l / dr^2 = -sum_k f_k sum_{j<k} 1/(r+j)^2 + n (1/r - 1/(r+x_bar))`.
As `r -> infinity`,
`l_prof(r) = l_Poisson(x_bar) + n (s_n^2 - x_bar) / (2r) + O(r^-2)` with the
divisor-`n` variance `s_n^2`.

- Domain: real size `r > 0`, `mu > 0`, non-negative integer counts.
- Meaning: the expansion shows that the profile likelihood rises towards the
  Poisson limit when `s_n^2 < x_bar`; the fit then reports `r = inf`
  (Poisson boundary) and the Poisson log-likelihood, counting two
  parameters in AIC and BIC. When `s_n^2 > x_bar`, `S(r) > 0` for small `r`
  and `S(r) < 0` for large `r`, and Brent's method finds the root. The size
  and mean are orthogonal at `mu = x_bar`, so `SE(r_hat)` is
  `(-d^2 l / dr^2)^(-1/2)` and `SE(mu_hat) = sqrt((mu + mu^2/r)/n)`.
- Code: `inference.fit_negative_binomial_counts`, `inference.CountFit`.
- Source: unimodality of the negative binomial likelihood
  [REF-LEVIN-REEDS-1977]; the expansion follows from
  `log Gamma(k + r) - log Gamma(r) = k log r + k(k-1)/(2r) + O(r^-2)` and
  `r log(1 + mu/r) = mu - mu^2/(2r) + O(r^-2)`; the pmf with integer size is
  [EQ-DIST-NBIN-001].

### EQ-INF-COUNT-003 — Garwood exact interval for a Poisson mean

With total `S = sum_i x_i` over `n` units and `alpha = 1 - confidence`:
`lower = chi2_{alpha/2}(2S) / (2n)` (`0` when `S = 0`),
`upper = chi2_{1-alpha/2}(2S + 2) / (2n)`, where `chi2_q(nu)` is the
`q`-quantile of the chi-square law with `nu` degrees of freedom.

- Domain: independent Poisson counts with common mean; `0 < confidence < 1`.
- Meaning: inverts the two one-sided Poisson tail tests through the
  Poisson-gamma identity; the coverage is at least the nominal level.
- Code: `inference.poisson_mean_interval`.
- Source: [REF-GARWOOD-1936].

### EQ-STAT-TRIM-001 — Symmetric trimmed mean

`g = floor(alpha n)`, `T_alpha = (1 / (n - 2g)) sum_{i=g+1}^{n-g} x_(i)` with
order statistics `x_(1) <= ... <= x_(n)`.

- Domain: `0 <= alpha < 1/2`, `n >= 1` finite observations.
- Meaning: removes the `g` smallest and `g` largest observations before
  averaging; `alpha = 0` is the mean and `alpha -> 1/2` approaches the median.
  On real measurement series, light trimming improved somewhat on the
  sample mean [REF-STIGLER-1977, abstract].
- Code: `statistics.trimmed_mean`.
- Source: [REF-STIGLER-1977] (comparison of trimmed means and other location
  estimators on historical measurement series).

### EQ-VIZ-ROOT-001 — Hanging rootogram

For count `k` with observed frequency `O_k` and fitted frequency `E_k`, the
bar spans `[sqrt(E_k) - sqrt(O_k), sqrt(E_k)]`; the curve joins the points
`(k, sqrt(E_k))`.

- Domain: non-negative observed and fitted frequencies.
- Meaning: the square root roughly stabilizes the variance of counts, and
  hanging the bars from the fitted curve moves every comparison to the
  horizontal line at zero, where departures are judged by length rather
  than against a sloping curve.
- Code: `visualization.fit_plots.hanging_rootogram_bars`,
  `visualization.fit_plots.plot_rootogram`.
- Source: [REF-KLEIBER-ZEILEIS-2016].

### EQ-PPL-TRANSFORM-003 — Stick-breaking bijection onto the simplex

For `y` in `R^(K-1)` and one-based `k = 1..K-1`:
`z_k = logistic(y_k - log(K - k))`, `x_k = r_(k-1) z_k`,
`r_k = r_(k-1) (1 - z_k)` with `r_0 = 1`, and `x_K = r_(K-1)`. The absolute
Jacobian determinant of `y -> (x_1, ..., x_(K-1))` is
`prod_k z_k (1 - z_k) r_(k-1)`. Logarithms are carried through the map
(`log z_k = -softplus(-t)`, `log(1 - z_k) = -softplus(t)`), so
