`log x_k = log r_(k-1) + log z_k` is exact even when `x_k` underflows.

- Domain: `K >= 2`; `y = 0` maps to the centre `x = (1/K, ..., 1/K)`.
- Meaning: a smooth bijection from `R^(K-1)` onto the open simplex; a
  density on the first `K - 1` coordinates (the Dirichlet convention of
  [EQ-DIST-DIR-001]) becomes a density on `y` after adding the log-Jacobian.
- Code: `inference.ppl.StructuredSupport` (kind `"simplex"`), used for
  `multivariate.Dirichlet` sites.
- Source: [REF-STAN-REFERENCE-MANUAL-2-36] (section "Unit simplex").

### EQ-PPL-TRANSFORM-004 — Ordered-vector bijection and the order-statistics density

`x_1 = y_1` (or `x_1 = a + exp(y_1)` on `(a, inf)`),
`x_k = x_(k-1) + exp(y_k)` for `k >= 2`;
`log |det J| = sum_(k>=2) y_k` (plus `y_1` with the lower bound). The law of
the sorted vector of `n` i.i.d. draws from a density `f` has density
`n! prod_i f(x_i)` on `x_1 < ... < x_n`.

- Domain: `n >= 2`; the base law has support `R` or `(a, inf)`.
- Meaning: maps `R^n` onto strictly increasing vectors; the order-statistics
  density gives a proper prior that removes the label symmetry of mixture
  components.
- Code: `inference.ppl.StructuredSupport` (kind `"ordered"`),
  `inference.ppl.OrderedVector`.
- Source: [REF-STAN-REFERENCE-MANUAL-2-36] (section "Ordered vector") and
  [REF-DAVID-NAGARAJA-2003, Chapter 2] (joint density of order statistics).

### EQ-PPL-TRANSFORM-005 — Tanh canonical-partial-correlation bijection onto correlation factors

The `d (d - 1) / 2` coordinates `y_ij` (`i > j`, row by row) give
`z_ij = tanh(y_ij)`; row `i` of the lower-triangular factor is
`L_ij = z_ij sqrt(r_ij)` with `r_ij = 1 - sum_(j'<j) L_ij'^2` (computed as
`prod_(j'<j) (1 - z_ij'^2)`) and `L_ii = sqrt(r_ii)`. The log absolute
Jacobian onto the strictly lower entries of `L` is
`sum log(1 - z_ij^2) + (1/2) sum_(i>j) log r_ij`, with
`log(1 - tanh(y)^2) = 2 log 2 - 2|y| - 2 log1p(exp(-2|y|))`. For the
correlation matrix `Omega = L L'` the map from the strictly lower entries of
`L` to those of `Omega` adds `sum_(k=2..d) (d - k) log L_kk`.

- Domain: `d >= 2`; `L L'` has a unit diagonal and is positive definite.
- Meaning: the `z_ij` are canonical partial correlations; a smooth bijection
  from `R^(d(d-1)/2)` onto Cholesky factors of correlation matrices and onto
  correlation matrices.
- Code: `inference.ppl.StructuredSupport` (kinds `"cholesky_correlation"`
  and `"correlation"`), `multivariate.LKJCholesky.sample`.
- Source: [REF-STAN-REFERENCE-MANUAL-2-36] (section "Cholesky factors of
  correlation matrices"); the `L -> L L'` factor is the ratio of the two
  densities in [REF-STAN-FUNCTIONS-REFERENCE-2-36] ([EQ-DIST-LKJ-002]).

### EQ-PPL-TRANSFORM-006 — Cholesky bijection with a log diagonal onto covariance matrices

The `d (d + 1) / 2` coordinates (row by row, `j <= i`) give
`L_ii = exp(y_ii)`, `L_ij = y_ij` for `i > j`, and `Sigma = L L'`. The
absolute Jacobian determinant onto the lower entries of `Sigma` is
`2^d prod_(k=1..d) L_kk^(d - k + 2)` (one-based `k`).

- Domain: `d >= 2`; `Sigma` is symmetric positive definite.
- Meaning: a smooth bijection from `R^(d(d+1)/2)` onto covariance matrices;
  Wishart and inverse-Wishart densities ([EQ-DIST-WISH-001],
  [EQ-DIST-IWISH-001]) on the lower entries become densities on `y`.
- Code: `inference.ppl.StructuredSupport` (kind `"covariance"`).
- Source: [REF-STAN-REFERENCE-MANUAL-2-36] (section "Covariance matrices").

### EQ-DIST-LKJ-001 — LKJ density on correlation matrices and its normalizing constant

`f(Omega | eta) = det(Omega)^(eta - 1) / c_d(eta)` on `d x d` correlation
matrices (Lebesgue measure on the strictly lower entries), with
`c_d(eta) = prod_(k=1..d-1) [2^(2 b_k - 1) B(b_k, b_k)]^(d - k)`,
`b_k = eta + (d - 1 - k) / 2`, equivalently
`2^(sum_k (2 eta - 2 + d - k)(d - k)) prod_k B(b_k, b_k)^(d - k)`.

- Domain: `d >= 2`, `eta > 0`; `eta = 1` is uniform, `c_2(1) = 2` and
  `c_3(1) = pi^2 / 2`.
- Meaning: a one-parameter prior on correlation matrices that concentrates
  on the identity as `eta` grows. The constant is the product of the Beta
  normalizers of the independent partial correlations of
  [EQ-DIST-LKJ-003]; `tests/test_ppl_structured_sites.py` checks it against
  quadrature of `det^(eta - 1)` for `d = 2` (four `eta`) and `d = 3`
  (`eta = 1, 2, 3`).
- Code: `multivariate.lkj_log_normalizer`, `multivariate.LKJCorrelation`.
- Source: [REF-LEWANDOWSKI-KUROWICKA-JOE-2009];
  [REF-STAN-FUNCTIONS-REFERENCE-2-36] (section "LKJ correlation
  distribution").

### EQ-DIST-LKJ-002 — LKJ density of the Cholesky factor

With `Omega = L L'`,
`f(L | eta) = prod_(k=2..d) L_kk^(d - k + 2 eta - 2) / c_d(eta)` on the
strictly lower entries of `L` (one-based `k`); the factor
`prod_k L_kk^(d - k)` is the Jacobian of `L -> Omega`.

- Domain: as [EQ-DIST-LKJ-001]; `L` lower triangular with unit rows and a
  positive diagonal.
- Meaning: the LKJ law expressed on the Cholesky factor, which avoids the
  determinant and the factorization of `Omega` inside a model.
- Code: `multivariate.LKJCholesky.log_pdf`,
  `inference.ppl` structured sites of `LKJCholesky`.
- Source: [REF-STAN-FUNCTIONS-REFERENCE-2-36] (section "Cholesky LKJ
  correlation distribution"), with the constant of [EQ-DIST-LKJ-001].

### EQ-DIST-LKJ-003 — LKJ sampling by independent Beta partial correlations

The canonical partial correlations of column `j` (zero-based) are
independent with `z_ij = 2 B - 1`, `B ~ Beta(b_j, b_j)`,
`b_j = eta + (d - 2 - j) / 2`; the factor is built by
[EQ-PPL-TRANSFORM-005]. Hence each `r_ij` with `j = 0` has variance
`1 / (2 eta + d - 1)`, and by exchangeability so has every off-diagonal
entry.

- Domain: `d >= 2`, `eta > 0`.
- Meaning: exact draws from LKJ(eta) from `d (d - 1) / 2` Beta variates; the
  product of their densities times the Jacobian of [EQ-PPL-TRANSFORM-005]
  equals [EQ-DIST-LKJ-002], which the tests check to eleven digits.
- Code: `multivariate.LKJCholesky.sample`, `multivariate.LKJCorrelation.sample`,
  `multivariate.lkj.cpc_shape`.
- Source: [REF-LEWANDOWSKI-KUROWICKA-JOE-2009] (vine method).

### EQ-PPL-ENUM-001 — Marginalization of finite discrete sites by enumeration

For discrete sites `z` with finite supports and continuous parameters
`theta`, `log p(theta, y) = log sum_z exp(log p(theta, z, y))`, evaluated as
`m + log sum_z exp(l_z - m)` with `m = max_z l_z` held constant. Global
sites are enumerated jointly (`prod_k |Z_k|` executions of the model); the
sites of plate iteration `i` are enumerated with that iteration only:
`log p(theta, y) = l_0(theta) + sum_i log sum_(z_i) exp(l_i(theta, z_i))`,
exact when the iterations are conditionally independent given `theta` and
the global sites.

- Domain: every discrete site follows the continuous latent and
  deterministic sites of its scope; at most 4096 configurations per scope.
- Meaning: the density that the gradient-based engines sample is the
  marginal of the continuous parameters, so HMC, NUTS, ADVI, and Laplace
  apply unchanged; per-iteration enumeration costs `sum_i |Z_i|` instead of
  `prod_i |Z_i|` executions.
- Code: `inference.ppl.ModelHandle.sample` (`marginalize=True`),
  `inference.ppl.ModelHandle.plate`, `inference.ppl.ModelIR.log_density`.
- Source: [REF-STAN-USERS-GUIDE-2-36] (section "The benefits of
  marginalization"), [REF-OBERMEYER-ETAL-2019] (plated variable
  elimination).

### EQ-PPL-ENUM-002 — Recovery of marginalized discrete sites

For a draw `theta^(s)`:
`p(c | theta^(s), y) = exp(l_c - logsumexp_c' l_c')` over global
configurations `c`, and
`p(z_i | theta^(s), c, y) = exp(l_i(z_i) - logsumexp l_i)` for plate
iteration `i`. A joint draw takes `c^(s)` and then each `z_i^(s)`. The
posterior probability of a value is estimated by
`(1/S) sum_s p(z = v | theta^(s), y)` (local sites averaged over `c`), the
Rao-Blackwellized form of the indicator average.

- Domain: as [EQ-PPL-ENUM-001]; `theta^(s)` from any engine.
- Meaning: the exact conditional law gives posterior draws of the discrete
  sites for predictive simulation and lower-variance estimates of their
  posterior probabilities.
- Code: `inference.ppl.ModelIR.discrete_conditional`,
  `inference.ppl.DiscreteDraws`, `inference.ppl.PosteriorSamples.discrete_probabilities`.
- Source: [REF-STAN-USERS-GUIDE-2-36] (sections "Posterior distribution of
  the discrete change point" and "The mathematics of recovering marginalized
  parameters").

### EQ-PPL-ENUM-003 — Joint support of a vector-valued discrete site

A discrete site `z = (z_1, ..., z_n)` of independent elements with finite
supports `Z_k` has the joint support `Z_1 x ... x Z_n` (enumerated in
lexicographic order) and log-mass `log p(z) = sum_k log p_k(z_k)`. A
multinomial count vector `n ~ Mult(N, p)` with `K` cells has the joint
support `{n in N^K : sum_k n_k = N}` of `C(N + K - 1, K - 1)` vectors and the
log-mass of [EQ-DIST-MULT-001]. The site is enumerated as one site with
these joint values in [EQ-PPL-ENUM-001].

- Domain: at most 4096 joint values per site and per scope.
- Meaning: indicators that act on one observation together (a sum, a
  pattern) are written as one vector site; the exact joint conditional law
  of the vector is recovered by [EQ-PPL-ENUM-002].
- Code: `inference.ppl.ModelHandle.sample` (`marginalize=True` with
  `shape`, a list of laws, or `multivariate.Multinomial`),
  `inference.ppl._discrete.product_support`,
  `inference.ppl._discrete.multinomial_support`.
- Source: [REF-STAN-USERS-GUIDE-2-36] (chapter "Latent Discrete
  Parameters": the marginal is a sum over every value of the discrete
  parameters), [REF-JOHNSON-KOTZ-BALAKRISHNAN-1997, Chapter 35]
  (multinomial support and mass).

### EQ-PPL-ENUM-004 — Enumeration in nested plates

For outer plate iterations `g` with local discrete sites `c_g` and inner
iterations `j` with local discrete sites `z_gj`, conditionally independent
given the sites declared before them,
`log p(theta, y) = l_0(theta) + sum_g log sum_(c_g) exp(l_g(theta, c_g)
+ sum_j log sum_(z_gj) exp(l_gj(theta, c_g, z_gj)))`,
where `l_g` collects the terms of iteration `g` after its first discrete
site and `l_gj` those of inner iteration `j`. The recovery of
[EQ-PPL-ENUM-002] draws `c_g` from `p(c_g | theta, y)` and then each `z_gj`
from `p(z_gj | theta, c_g, y)`; the marginal probability of `z_gj` is
`sum_(c_g) p(c_g | theta, y) p(z_gj | theta, c_g, y)`.

- Domain: as [EQ-PPL-ENUM-001] in every scope; the sites of an iteration do
  not depend on the values of its own discrete sites.
- Meaning: the cost is `sum_g |C_g| (1 + sum_j |Z_gj|)` body executions
  instead of the product over all discrete sites, and the result equals the
  sum over every joint configuration.
- Code: `inference.ppl.ModelHandle.plate`,
  `inference.ppl.ModelIR.discrete_conditional`,
  `inference.ppl.DiscreteDraws`.
- Source: [REF-OBERMEYER-ETAL-2019] (variable elimination in plated factor
  graphs, which allows nested plates).

### EQ-PPL-DYNAMIC-001 — Padded density under dynamic site structure

Let the configurations `c` of the discrete sites outside plates declare the
continuous latent sites `S_c`, and let `u` hold the union `S` of all `S_c`.
For a site `s` in `S` but not in `S_c`, let `q_s(u_s | u_<s)` be the density
on `R^(d_s)` of site `s` (prior times Jacobian) in the first configuration
`r(s)` that declares it. Then
`log p(u) = log sum_c exp(log p(c, T_c(u_(S_c)), y) + log |J_c(u)|
+ sum_(s not in S_c) log q_s(u_s | u_<s))`.
Each `q_s` integrates to one over `u_s`, so `int p_c(u) du = p(c, y)` for
every `c`: the marginal of the configurations and the conditional law of
the sites `S_c` given `c` are those of the model, and `p(c | u, y)` is
proportional to the summand of `c`.

- Domain: every prior of a continuous site is proper; at most 4096
  configurations; the structure depends on data and on discrete sites
  outside plates, not on continuous values.
- Meaning: the product-space (composite-space) construction with each
  site's own prior as its pseudo-prior; the engines sample a fixed-dimension
  density, and the posterior probability of a structure is the average of
  `p(c | u^(s), y)` over the draws.
- Code: `inference.ppl.trace`, `inference.ppl.TracedStructure`,
  `inference.ppl.ModelIR.log_density`,
  `inference.ppl.PosteriorSamples.presence_probability`.
- Source: [REF-CARLIN-CHIB-1995] (pp. 473-484: the product space of the
  parameters of all models, with pseudo-priors for the parameters of the
  models not in use that leave the posterior model probabilities
  unchanged), [REF-GODSILL-2001] (pp. 230-248: the composite model space
  that contains the Carlin-Chib method).

### EQ-VIZ-LIK-001 — Binomial likelihood scaled to unit area

`L(p) = p^x (1 - p)^(n - x)` divided by `B(x + 1, n - x + 1)` integrates to
one on `[0, 1]` and equals the `Beta(x + 1, n - x + 1)` density; it is also
the posterior under the uniform `Beta(1, 1)` prior.

- Domain: `0 <= x <= n`, `n >= 0` (for `n = 0` the scaled likelihood is the
  uniform density).
- Meaning: draws the likelihood on the same density axis as the prior and
  the posterior, so the three curves of a Beta-Binomial update can be
  compared directly; the scaling does not change where the likelihood is
  large.
- Code: `visualization.interactive.bayesian_updating_explainer`.
- Source: [REF-GELMAN-ETAL-2013, Chapter 2].

### EQ-DIST-BASE-005 — Density from its logarithm with saturation

`f(x) = exp(log f(x))`, returned as `inf` when `log f(x) > log(DBL_MAX)
~ 709.78` and as `0` when `log f(x) < -745.2` (below the smallest
subnormal).

- Domain: any log density, including `+-inf`; NaN propagates.
- Meaning: a density above the largest float (an integrable singularity
  approached closely, such as `Gamma` with shape below one near zero, or a
  scale near the smallest normal float) saturates to `inf` instead of raising
  `OverflowError`, while `log_pdf` keeps the finite logarithm.
- Code: `distributions._continuous.density_from_log`, the `pdf` methods of the
  continuous families.
- Source: [REF-HIGHAM-2002, Section 2.1], [REF-PYTHON-MATH].

### EQ-DIST-EMPIRICAL-003 — Entropy of the interpolated empirical law

`H = (1/(n-1)) sum_(i=1)^(n-1) log((n-1)(x_(i+1) - x_(i)))` for the linear
(type-7) empirical law, which is uniform with mass `1/(n-1)` on each gap; a
tied pair is an atom and gives `H = -inf`; the step law has no differential
entropy (`nan`).

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-EMPIRICAL-001] with `n >= 2` and a non-constant sample.
- Meaning: exact differential entropy of the interpolated law, replacing a
  probability-space quadrature that returned `nan` for samples with very
  unequal gaps.
- Code: `distributions.Empirical.entropy`.
- Source: [REF-COVER-THOMAS-2006, Chapter 8], [REF-HYNDMAN-FAN-1996].

### EQ-DIST-MIXTURE-002 — Higher central moments and entropy of a mixture

With `mu = sum w_i mu_i`, `d_i = mu_i - mu` and component central moments
`m_ik`:
`E[(X - mu)^3] = sum w_i (m_i3 + 3 d_i m_i2 + d_i^3)` and
`E[(X - mu)^4] = sum w_i (m_i4 + 4 d_i m_i3 + 6 d_i^2 m_i2 + d_i^4)`.
The entropy `H = -int f log f` is integrated adaptively in `x` over pieces
split at every finite support end and median of the components.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-MIXTURE-001]; the moment form needs component skewness and
  kurtosis, otherwise the probability-space quadrature of [EQ-DIST-BASE-001]
  is used.
- Meaning: skewness and kurtosis cost a few component evaluations instead of
  a quadrature over the mixture quantile (each point a root solve), and the
  entropy converges when a component density is singular or kinked inside
  the mixture support.
- Code: `distributions.Mixture._central_moment`, `distributions.Mixture.entropy`.
- Source: [REF-MCLACHLAN-PEEL-2000, Chapter 1], [REF-COVER-THOMAS-2006,
  Chapter 8], [REF-PIESSENS-QUADPACK-1983].

### EQ-PPL-MARKOV-001 — Forward algorithm for a Markov chain of discrete sites

For a chain of steps `t = 0, ..., n - 1` whose discrete sites take the joint
states `j in {1, ..., K_t}`, let `l_0(j)` collect the log-terms of step `0`
in state `j` and `l_t(i, j)` those of step `t` when step `t - 1` is in state
`i` (discrete log-masses, observations, and the log-sum-exp of nested plate
iterations). Then `alpha_0(j) = l_0(j)`,
`alpha_t(j) = log sum_i exp(alpha_(t-1)(i) + l_t(i, j))`, and
`log sum_(z_0..z_(n-1)) exp(l_0(z_0) + sum_t l_t(z_(t-1), z_t))
= log sum_j exp(alpha_(n-1)(j))`, evaluated with a shifted log-sum-exp.

- Domain: first-order dependence (the terms of step `t` depend on the
  discrete sites of steps `t - 1` and `t` only); at most 4096 states per
  step; the sites of a step do not change with its discrete values.
- Meaning: the chain is summed out in `K_0 + sum_(t >= 1) K_(t-1) K_t`
  executions of the step body instead of `prod_t K_t`, so the
  gradient-based engines sample the marginal density of the continuous
  parameters of a hidden Markov model; the recursion is transparent to dual
  numbers and reverse-mode variables.
- Code: `inference.ppl.ModelHandle.markov`,
  `inference.ppl._discrete.forward_log`, `inference.ppl.ModelIR.log_density`.
- Source: [REF-RABINER-1989] (pp. 257-286: the forward procedure, an
  induction over time on the forward variables at `O(n K^2)` cost),
  [REF-BAUM-ETAL-1970] (pp. 164-171: the forward and backward recursions
  for probabilistic functions of Markov chains).

### EQ-PPL-MARKOV-002 — Smoothed marginals and forward filtering, backward sampling

With the forward variables of [EQ-PPL-MARKOV-001], the backward variables
`beta_(n-1)(j) = 0`, `beta_t(i) = log sum_j exp(l_(t+1)(i, j) +
beta_(t+1)(j))`, and `log L = log sum_j exp(alpha_(n-1)(j))`:
`p(z_t = j | theta, y) = exp(alpha_t(j) + beta_t(j) - log L)` and
`p(z_(t-1) = i, z_t = j | theta, y) = exp(alpha_(t-1)(i) + l_t(i, j) +
beta_t(j) - log L)`. A joint draw of the path takes
`z_(n-1) ~ exp(alpha_(n-1)(j) - log L)` and, for `t = n - 2, ..., 0`,
`z_t | z_(t+1) = k ~ exp(alpha_t(i) + l_(t+1)(i, k))` normalized over `i`.

- Domain: as [EQ-PPL-MARKOV-001]; `theta` fixed (one continuous draw).
- Meaning: the exact conditional law of the path given the continuous
  parameters; posterior draws of the discrete states, Rao-Blackwellized
  posterior state probabilities (the average of the smoothed marginals
  over continuous draws), and the weights of the plate iterations nested in
  a step.
- Code: `inference.ppl._discrete.backward_log`,
  `inference.ppl._discrete.recover_discrete`, `inference.ppl.DiscreteDraws`.
- Source: [REF-RABINER-1989] (pp. 257-286: the backward variables, the
  state probabilities from the product of forward and backward variables,
  and the pairwise state probabilities), [REF-CHIB-1996] (pp. 79-97: the
  joint draw of the hidden states of a Markov mixture model by a forward
  pass of filtered probabilities and a backward pass of conditional
  draws).

### EQ-PPL-MARKOV-003 — Viterbi recursion and joint max-product elimination

`delta_0(j) = l_0(j)`, `delta_t(j) = max_i delta_(t-1)(i) + l_t(i, j)` with
back-pointers `psi_t(j) = argmax_i (delta_(t-1)(i) + l_t(i, j))`; the most
probable path ends in `argmax_j delta_(n-1)(j)` and is read back through
`psi`. Across the whole enumeration record, each plate iteration or chain
`g` with log-sum-exp `S_g` and maximum `M_g` contributes the gain
`M_g - S_g` to the log-weight that contains `S_g`, so the jointly most
probable configuration maximizes `l_c + sum_g (M_g - S_g)` over the global
configurations `c`, with nested gains added to the branch and pair weights.

- Domain: as [EQ-PPL-MARKOV-001] and [EQ-PPL-ENUM-004]; ties go to the
  smallest index.
- Meaning: the maximum a posteriori values of every discrete site given the
  continuous parameters, at the cost of the forward pass.
- Code: `inference.ppl._discrete.viterbi`,
  `inference.ppl._discrete.most_probable`,
  `inference.ppl.ModelIR.most_probable_discrete`.
- Source: [REF-VITERBI-1967] (pp. 260-269: the maximum-likelihood decoding
  recursion), [REF-RABINER-1989] (pp. 257-286: the Viterbi algorithm for the
  single best state sequence, with back-pointers).

### EQ-PPL-LOCAL-001 — Per-iteration padding of plate branches

Let the branches `z` of plate iteration `i` declare, after its first
discrete site, the continuous latent sites `S_i(z)`, and let
`S_i = union_z S_i(z)`. For `s` in `S_i` but not in `S_i(z)`, let
`q_s(u_s | u_<s)` be the prior times Jacobian of `s` in the first branch
that declares it (or a tuned pseudo-prior, [EQ-PPL-PSEUDO-001]). Then the
iteration contributes
`log sum_z exp(l_i(z, u) + sum_(s in S_i, s not in S_i(z)) log q_s(u_s))`
to the log-density, where `l_i(z, u)` holds the terms of branch `z` after
its first discrete site (the priors and log-Jacobians of `S_i(z)`
included). Nested iterations pad their own branches, and their union of
sites is declared by the enclosing branch.

- Domain: the discrete sites of an iteration and their supports are the same
  in every branch; a site declared in several branches has the same support
  and transform in each; at most 4096 branches per iteration; the structure
  of a branch depends on the iteration's discrete values, data, and the
  enclosing sites, not on continuous values; every padding density is
  proper.
- Meaning: each `q_s` integrates to one, so integrating `u_(S_i)` out of the
  summand of `z` gives `p(z, y_i | theta)` for every branch: the product-space
  construction of [EQ-PPL-DYNAMIC-001] applied inside each conditionally
  independent iteration. Recovery reports a site of `S_i` only in the draws
  whose drawn branch declares it.
- Code: `inference.ppl.ModelHandle.plate`, `inference.ppl.TracedStructure`,
  `inference.ppl.PosteriorSamples.present`,
  `inference.ppl.PosteriorSamples.presence_probability`.
- Source: [REF-CARLIN-CHIB-1995] (pp. 473-484: pseudo-priors for the
  parameters of the models not in use leave the posterior model
  probabilities unchanged), [REF-OBERMEYER-ETAL-2019] (plated variable
  elimination: each iteration is summed out on its own).

### EQ-PPL-PSEUDO-001 — Moment-matched normal pseudo-priors from a pilot run

For a continuous site `s` that some structure lacks, with pilot draws
`u^(1..S)` and `w_r = P(s declared | u^(r), y)` (the sum of the
configuration and branch probabilities that declare `s`), the pseudo-prior
is `q_s(u_s) = prod_k N(u_(s,k); m_k, v_k)` with
`m_k = sum_r w_r u_(s,k)^(r) / sum_r w_r` and
`v_k = sum_r w_r (u_(s,k)^(r) - m_k)^2 / sum_r w_r`. Because
`E[u 1(s declared) | y] = E[u P(s declared | u, y) | y]`, `m` and `v` are
consistent estimates of the conditional posterior moments of `u_s` given
that `s` exists.

- Domain: at least two effective pilot draws (`(sum w)^2 >= 2 sum w^2`)
  and positive `v_k`; unconstrained coordinates of the site.
- Meaning: any proper `q_s` leaves the posterior probability of every
  structure unchanged; a `q_s` close to the conditional posterior makes the
  summands of different structures overlap on `u_s`, so the sampled density
  has less separated components and the structure probability mixes faster.
  The default (no tuning) keeps the site's prior.
- Code: `inference.ppl.tune_pseudo_priors`, `inference.ppl.PseudoPrior`,
  `inference.ppl.ModelIR.with_pseudo_priors`.
- Source: [REF-CARLIN-CHIB-1995] (pp. 473-484: the pseudo-priors do not
  affect the model probabilities, and pseudo-priors close to the
  conditional posteriors make the sampler efficient),
  [REF-GODSILL-2001] (pp. 230-248: the composite-space sampler and its
  pseudo-priors).

### EQ-SENS-SHAPLEY-005 — Standard error of an estimated Shapley effect

With exact enumeration `Sh_i = A_i / V + 1/d`, where
`A_i = sum_(J proper, non-empty) w_iJ c_hat(J)` collects the estimated
costs (signed subset weights `w_iJ`) and `V` is the estimated `Var Y`, which
also enters `c(D)`. The costs and `V` come from independent draws, so the
delta method gives
`Var(Sh_i) ~ sum_J w_iJ^2 Var(c_hat(J)) / V^2 + (A_i / V)^2 Var(V) / V^2`.
With `m` random permutations `Sh_i = B_i / V + L_i / m` (`L_i` permutations
that end in `i`, whose last increment is `V - c_hat(P_i)`); the permutation
spread `s_i^2` of the increments gives `Var(Sh_i | V) ~ s_i^2 / (m V^2)`,
and the same delta term `(B_i / V)^2 Var(V) / V^2` is added.
`Var(V) ~ (m_4 - V^2) / N_V` from the `N_V` variance draws.

- Domain: `N_V >= 2`; `N_O >= 2` for exact enumeration (otherwise the cost
  variances are unknown and the error is `nan`).
- Meaning: the normalizing variance is shared by every effect, so its
  sampling error does not average out over subsets or permutations; leaving
  it out understates the error of the permutation estimator and, for exact
  enumeration, misstates it in either direction because `V` cancels in part
  between `c(D)` and the denominator.
- Code: `sensitivity.shapley_effects`.
- Source: [REF-SONG-NELSON-STAUM-2016] (the estimators) and
  [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002, Section 5.5.4] (the delta method).

### EQ-GEN-FLOW-008 — Cancellation-free planar and radial log-determinants

Planar flow, with `s = w'z + b`, `t = tanh(s)`, and the margin
`m = 1 + w'u_hat = log(1 + e^(w'u))` computed directly:
`1 + (1 - t^2) w'u_hat = t^2 + m sech^2(s)`,
`sech^2(s) = 4 e / (1 + e)^2` with `e = exp(-2 |s|)`; the same sum is the
slope `g'(a)` of the inverse root `g(a) = a + w'u_hat tanh(a + b) - w'x`.
Radial flow, with `r = |z - z0|` and `m = alpha + beta = log(1 + e^c)`:
`1 + beta h = (r + m) / (alpha + r)`,
`1 + beta alpha h^2 = (r (2 alpha + r) + m alpha) / (alpha + r)^2`, and the
inverse `z = z0 + (x - z0) (alpha + r) / (r + m)`, `B = m - rho`.

- Domain: as in [EQ-GEN-FLOW-002] and [EQ-GEN-FLOW-004]; `m > 0`.
- Meaning: algebraically identical to [EQ-GEN-FLOW-002] and
  [EQ-GEN-FLOW-004], but every factor is a sum of non-negative terms. The
  forms `1 + (1 - t^2) (-1 + m)` and `1 + (-alpha + m) alpha h^2` round the
  margin to zero once `m` is below the spacing of doubles near one or near
  `alpha` (raw parameter below about -37), which gives a log-determinant of
  minus infinity or a domain error where the exact value is finite, and
  `1 - t^2` rounds to zero for `|s|` above about 19, which drops
  `w'u_hat sech^2(s)` from the planar determinant.
- Code: `generative.PlanarFlow.forward`, `generative.PlanarFlow.inverse`,
  `generative.RadialFlow.forward`, `generative.RadialFlow.inverse`.
- Source: [REF-REZENDE-MOHAMED-2015, Equations 10-14 and Appendix A],
  [REF-HIGHAM-2002, Chapter 1] (cancellation in floating-point subtraction).

### EQ-DIST-AD-001 — Accurate value with closed-form derivatives

For a log-density `l(theta)` evaluated by an accurate float-only kernel
`v = K(theta_0)` at the primal parameters `theta_0`, and the same quantity
written in closed form `g(theta)` with differentiable elementary functions,
the automatic-differentiation result is `l~(theta) = v + (g(theta) - g_0)`
with `g_0 = g(theta_0)` held constant. Then `l~(theta_0) = v` and every
derivative of `l~` equals the corresponding derivative of `g`, to every
order the variables carry.

- Domain: `v` finite (a non-finite value is returned without derivatives);
  `g` differentiable at `theta_0`; `theta` dual numbers or reverse-mode
  tape variables.
- Meaning: the value keeps the accuracy of the cancellation-free kernel
  (Stirling differences for large shapes, interval masses of the truncated
  normal), while the derivatives, which do not suffer the cancellation of
  the value (for example `log(lambda x) - digamma(k)` for the gamma shape),
  come from the closed form. Float evaluations are unchanged.
- Code: `distributions._autodiff.with_value`,
  `distributions._autodiff.transfer_derivatives`.
- Source: [REF-GRIEWANK-WALTHER-2008] (Chapter 3: derivatives of a program
  are the derivatives of the elementary functions it composes; a constant
  shift leaves them unchanged).

### EQ-NUM-DD-001 — Error-free transformations and double-double arithmetic

`s = fl(a + b)`, `e = (a - (s - v)) + (b - v)` with `v = s - a` gives
`s + e = a + b` exactly (two-sum); with Veltkamp's splitting
`a = a_h + a_l` (`c = (2^27 + 1) a`, `a_h = c - (c - a)`), `p = fl(a b)`,
`e = ((a_h b_h - p) + a_h b_l + a_l b_h) + a_l b_l` gives `p + e = a b`
exactly (two-product). A double-double `x_h + x_l` (`|x_l| <= ulp(x_h)/2`)
is added, multiplied, and divided with these transformations, with relative
errors of a few `2^-104`; `exp(x_h + x_l) = exp(x_h) (1 + x_l)`.

- Domain: finite floats without overflow; the splitting needs
  `|a| <= 1e300`, and the products are exact unless partial products
  underflow (below `1e-290`).
- Meaning: carries about 106 bits through the exponent of a special-function
  prefactor or the argument of `erfc`, so that the outer function does not
  amplify a rounding of its argument.
- Code: `numerics._double_double.two_sum`,
  `numerics._double_double.two_product`, `numerics._double_double.dd_add`,
  `numerics._double_double.dd_mul`, `numerics._double_double.dd_div`,
  `numerics._double_double.dd_exp`,
  `distributions._continuous.standardized_double_double`.
- Source: [REF-DEKKER-1971] and [REF-HIGHAM-2002, Section 4.3].

### EQ-NUM-DD-002 — Table-driven double-double logarithm and Stirling remainder

`log x = k ln 2 + log(j/64) + 2 atanh(y)`, `x = m 2^k`, `m` in
`[sqrt(1/2), sqrt 2)`, `j = round(64 m)`, `y = (m - j/64)/(m + j/64)`
(`|y| < 0.0056`), `2 atanh y = 2y + 2y (y^2/3 + y^4/5 + y^6/7 + y^8/9)`;
`log(1 + t) - t = -t y + (2/3) y^3 + 2y sum_(k=2..10) y^(2k)/(2k+1)` with
`y = t/(2 + t)` for `|t| <= 1/16`, and `log(1 + t) - t` from the logarithm
otherwise; `sigma(a) = lgamma(a) - (a - 1/2) log a + a - log sqrt(2 pi)`
equals the Stirling series for `a >= 15` and, for smaller `a` with
`z = a + n >= 15`, `sigma(a) = (z - 1/2) log z - (a - 1/2) log a - n +
sigma(z) - log prod_(k<n) (a + k)`.

- Domain: positive finite arguments; `|t| <= 1/2` for the `log1pmx` form.
  The table values `log(j/64)` are computed once in 40-digit decimal
  arithmetic.
- Meaning: absolute errors below `1e-22` (logarithm), relative errors
  below `1e-20` (`log1pmx`), and absolute errors below `2e-18`
  (`sigma`), so that
  exponents of size several hundred are exact to far below one ulp.
- Code: `numerics._double_double.dd_log`,
  `numerics._double_double.dd_log1pmx`,
  `numerics._double_double.dd_stirling_error`,
  `numerics._double_double.half_log_minus_stirling`,
  `numerics._double_double.dd_scaled_log_ratio`.
- Source: [REF-NIST-DLMF-ELEMENTARY, Section 4.24],
  [REF-NIST-DLMF-GAMMA, Sections 5.5 and 5.11], [REF-DEKKER-1971],
  [REF-DIDONATO-MORRIS-1992].

### EQ-NUM-DD-003 — Complementary error function at a double-double argument

`erfc(w_h + w_l) = erfc(w_h) - (2/sqrt(pi)) exp(-w_h^2) w_l
+ O(w_h w_l^2 exp(-w_h^2))`.

- Domain: double-double `w`; the correction is skipped for `|w_h| > 27.5`,
  where `erfc` is 0 or 2 in floats.
- Meaning: a rounded argument `w_h` perturbs `erfc` by the relative amount
  `2 w^2 |w_l/w|`, which is up to `1400` ulp at `w = 26`; the first-order
  term removes it and leaves the error of `math.erfc` at an exact float
  argument (measured at most `2.04` ulp on 300 random arguments in
  `[0, 27]`, CPython 3.12 on Windows).
- Code: `numerics._double_double.erfc_double_double`.
- Source: [REF-NIST-DLMF, Sections 7.2 and 7.10] and [REF-DEKKER-1971].

### EQ-DIST-NORM-007 — Normal CDF, survival, and log tails from a double-double z

`z = (x - mu)/sigma` as `z_h + z_l` ([EQ-NUM-DD-001]);
`1 - Phi(z) = erfc(z/sqrt 2)/2` by [EQ-NUM-DD-003] with `z/sqrt 2` in
double-double arithmetic; `Phi(z) = 1 - Phi(-z)`;
`log(1 - Phi(z)) = log1p(-Phi(z))` for `z < 0` and `log(1 - Phi(z))` for
`0 <= z < 35`; beyond, `-z^2/2 - log sqrt(2 pi) - log R(z)` with the Mills
ratio continued fraction `R` and `z^2` formed exactly.

- Domain: the domain of [EQ-DIST-NORM-001].
- Meaning: the relative condition number of `Phi` in the tails is about
  `z^2`, so a rounded `z` or `z/sqrt 2` costs `(1 + z^2)/2` ulp; the
  double-double standardization keeps `cdf`, `sf`, `log_cdf`, and `log_sf`
  within a few ulp over the whole range. `log1p(-Phi(z))` keeps relative
  accuracy where `log(1 - Phi(z))` is close to zero.
- Code: `distributions.Normal.cdf`, `distributions.Normal.sf`,
  `distributions.Normal.log_cdf`, `distributions.Normal.log_sf`,
  `distributions._continuous.standard_normal_sf_dd`,
  `distributions._continuous.log_standard_normal_sf`,
  `distributions._continuous.log_standard_normal_cdf`.
- Source: [REF-NIST-DLMF, Sections 7.2, 7.9, and 7.10] and
  [REF-DEKKER-1971].

### EQ-NUM-GAMMA-003 — Double-double prefactor of the incomplete gamma ratios

`x^a exp(-x)/Gamma(a) = exp(a log1pmx((x - a)/a) + log(a)/2 - sigma(a)
- log sqrt(2 pi))`, every term of the exponent from [EQ-NUM-DD-002] and
the exponential by [EQ-NUM-DD-001].

- Domain: `a > 0`, `x > 0`; when the float exponent is below `-760` (the
  prefactor underflows) the float exponent is used.
- Meaning: the float exponent `a log x - x - lgamma(a)` has an absolute
  error of about `2^-53` times its largest cancelling term, which `exp`
  turns into a relative error (1400 ulp at `(200, 605)`); the regrouped
  double-double exponent leaves one `exp` rounding.
- Code: `distributions._special.gamma_prefactor`,
  `distributions._special.regularized_gamma_p`,
  `distributions._special.regularized_gamma_q`.
- Source: [REF-DIDONATO-MORRIS-1986], [REF-NIST-DLMF-GAMMA, Section 5.11],
  and [REF-DEKKER-1971].

### EQ-NUM-BETA-003 — Double-double prefactor of the incomplete beta ratio

`x^a (1-x)^b / B(a, b) = exp(a log1pmx(t) + b log1pmx(s) + [log(a)/2 -
sigma(a)] + [log(b)/2 - sigma(b)] - [log(a+b)/2 - sigma(a+b)]
- log sqrt(2 pi))` with `1 + t = x (a+b)/a`, `1 + s = (1-x)(a+b)/b`
(`a t + b s = 0`), every term from [EQ-NUM-DD-002].

- Domain: `a, b > 0`, `0 < x < 1`; the smaller of `x` and `1 - x` is taken
  as exact and the other formed from it by two-sum.
- Meaning: removes the cancellation of `lgamma` values and of `a log x`
  terms that cost up to 770 ulp at shapes up to 400.
- Code: `distributions._special.beta_prefactor`,
  `distributions._special.regularized_beta_pair`.
- Source: [REF-DIDONATO-MORRIS-1992], [REF-NIST-DLMF-BETA, Section 8.17],
  and [REF-DEKKER-1971].

### EQ-NUM-GAMMA-004 — Temme's uniform expansion with thirteen coefficients

`Q(a,x) = erfc(w)/2 + R`, `P(a,x) = erfc(-w)/2 - R`, `w = eta sqrt(a/2)`,
`R = exp(-w^2)/sqrt(2 pi a) sum_(k=0..12) c_k(eta) a^-k`,
`eta = sign(lambda - 1) sqrt(2(lambda - 1 - log lambda))`, `lambda = x/a`;
`c_0 = 1/mu - 1/eta`, `c_k = c_(k-1)'(eta)/eta + (-1)^k g_k/mu`,
`mu = lambda - 1`, with `g_k` the coefficients of
`Gamma(z) ~ e^-z z^z sqrt(2 pi/z) sum g_k z^-k`; each `c_k` summed from 26
Taylor coefficients in `eta` derived in exact rational arithmetic;
`w^2 = -a log1pmx((x - a)/a)` in double-double arithmetic and `erfc` by
[EQ-NUM-DD-003].

- Domain: `a >= 20` and `|x - a| <= 0.3 a` (`|eta| <= 0.34`); the omitted
  Taylor terms are below `1e-22` and the last included term `c_12/a^12` is
  below `2e-18` relative to `R`. Supersedes [EQ-NUM-GAMMA-002].
- Meaning: constant cost and an error of about one ulp for every large
  shape near the mode, where the series and the continued fraction need
  `O(sqrt(a))` terms whose roundings accumulate (26 ulp at `a = 200`,
  570 ulp at `a = 1e5`).
- Code: `distributions._special._gamma_temme`,
  `distributions._special._use_temme`,
  `distributions._special.regularized_gamma_p`,
  `distributions._special.regularized_gamma_q`.
- Source: [REF-TEMME-1979], [REF-NIST-DLMF-GAMMA, Sections 5.11 and 8.12],
  and [REF-DIDONATO-MORRIS-1986].

### EQ-DIST-DIR-007 — Stirling form of the Dirichlet normalizer and entropy

`log B(alpha) = sum_i (alpha_i - 1/2) log m_i - ((K-1)/2) log alpha_0
+ (K-1) log sqrt(2 pi) + sum_i sigma(alpha_i) - sigma(alpha_0)`,
`m_i = alpha_i/alpha_0`;
`H = (1/2) sum_i log m_i - ((K-1)/2) log alpha_0 + (K-1) log sqrt(2 pi)
+ sum_i sigma(alpha_i) - sigma(alpha_0) - (alpha_0 - K) L(alpha_0)
+ sum_i (alpha_i - 1) L(alpha_i)`, `L(a) = log a - psi(a)`.

- Domain: [EQ-DIST-DIR-001]; `sigma` is the Stirling remainder of
  [EQ-NUM-STIRLING-001] and `L` the function of [EQ-NUM-DIGAMMA-001].
- Meaning: the linear terms of the Stirling forms cancel exactly
  (`sum alpha_i = alpha_0`), so no `lgamma` or `alpha psi(alpha)` of size
  `alpha log alpha` is formed; at `alpha_0 = 1e9` the normalizer is within
  half an ulp and the entropy within `1e-15` instead of `1.4e-6` and
  `3.5e-6`.
- Code: `multivariate.dirichlet.log_multivariate_beta`,
  `multivariate.Dirichlet.entropy`.
- Source: [REF-NIST-DLMF-GAMMA, Sections 5.2 and 5.11],
  [REF-BISHOP-2006, Appendix B].

### EQ-SMOOTH-001 — Cox-de Boor recursion for B-splines

`B_{i,0}(x) = 1` for `t_i <= x < t_{i+1}` and `0` otherwise;
`B_{i,p}(x) = (x - t_i)/(t_{i+p} - t_i) B_{i,p-1}(x)
+ (t_{i+p+1} - x)/(t_{i+p+1} - t_{i+1}) B_{i+1,p-1}(x)`, with `0/0 = 0`.

- Domain: non-decreasing knots `t_0, ..., t_{m-1}`, no knot repeated more
  than `p + 1` times; `x` in `[t_p, t_{m-p-1}]`, the last interval closed.
- Meaning: the `m - p - 1` functions are non-negative, sum to one, vanish
  outside `p + 1` knot intervals, and span every spline of degree `p` with
  these knots, including all polynomials of degree `<= p`; only `p + 1`
  of them are non-zero at any `x`.
- Code: `inference.splines.bspline_basis`,
  `inference.splines.bspline_design_matrix`.
- Source: [REF-DE-BOOR-1972].

### EQ-SMOOTH-002 — Penalized least squares and the P-spline

`beta_hat = argmin ||y - X beta||_W^2 + sum_j lambda_j beta' S_j beta
= (X'WX + S_lambda)^-1 X'Wy`, `S_lambda = sum_j lambda_j S_j`; for a P-spline
`X_ik = B_k(x_i)` on equally spaced knots and `S = D_d' D_d`, so that
`beta' S beta = sum_k (Delta^d beta_k)^2`.

- Domain: `W = diag(w_i)`, `w_i > 0`; `S_j` symmetric positive
  semidefinite; `X'WX + S_lambda` positive definite.
- Meaning: the penalty shrinks the fit towards the null space of `S`
  (polynomials of degree `< d` for a P-spline), never towards zero;
  `lambda = 0` is ordinary regression on the basis and `lambda -> infinity`
  the polynomial fit of degree `d - 1`.
- Code: `inference._penalized.PenalizedProblem.solve`,
  `inference.splines.fit_pspline`, `inference.splines.difference_penalty`,
  `inference.splines.uniform_knots`.
- Source: [REF-EILERS-MARX-1996], [REF-WOOD-2017, Chapters 4 and 5].

### EQ-SMOOTH-003 — Effective degrees of freedom and scale

`H = X (X'WX + S_lambda)^-1 X'W`, `edf = tr(H) = tr((X'WX + S_lambda)^-1 X'WX)`,
`phi_hat = RSS_w / (n - edf)`.

- Domain: as [EQ-SMOOTH-002]; `n > edf`.
- Meaning: `edf` decreases from the number of basis functions at
  `lambda = 0` to the null-space dimension of `S` as `lambda -> infinity`;
  it counts the parameters the data effectively estimate, and per-term
  values are sums of the diagonal of `(X'WX + S_lambda)^-1 X'WX` over the
  term's columns.
- Code: `inference._penalized.PenalizedProblem.solve`,
  `inference.splines.fit_pspline`, `inference.splines.fit_smoothing_spline`,
  `inference.additive_models.fit_additive_model`.
- Source: [REF-WOOD-2017, Chapter 6], [REF-HASTIE-TIBSHIRANI-1990].

### EQ-SMOOTH-004 — Generalized cross-validation

`GCV(lambda) = n RSS_w(lambda) / (n - tr H(lambda))^2`.

- Domain: `tr H < n`.
- Meaning: a rotation-invariant approximation of leave-one-out
  cross-validation; its minimizer estimates the `lambda` of smallest
  prediction error, and it is flat (and can undersmooth) when the noise
  is small relative to the signal.
- Code: `inference._penalized.PenalizedProblem.criterion`,
  `inference.splines.fit_smoothing_spline`, `inference.splines.fit_pspline`.
- Source: [REF-CRAVEN-WAHBA-1979], [REF-WOOD-2017, Chapter 6].

### EQ-SMOOTH-005 — Restricted likelihood (REML) of a Gaussian penalized model

`V_R(lambda) = ((n - M_p)/2)(1 + log(2 pi phi_hat)) + (1/2) log|X'WX + S_lambda|
- (1/2) sum_j r_j log lambda_j + c`, with
`phi_hat = (RSS_w + beta_hat' S_lambda beta_hat)/(n - M_p)`, `r_j = rank S_j`,
`M_p = p - sum_j r_j`, and `c` free of `lambda`.

- Domain: `beta ~ N(0, phi S_lambda^-)` improper on the null space,
  `y | beta ~ N(X beta, phi W^-1)`; non-overlapping penalty blocks;
  `n > M_p`, `lambda_j > 0`.
- Meaning: minus the exact restricted log-likelihood of the equivalent
  mixed model with `phi` profiled out, so `lambda` is estimated like a
  variance ratio; it penalizes overfitting more strongly than GCV and has
  fewer spurious minima. For a smoothing spline `X = I`, `S = K`, `M_p = 2`
  and `log|W + lambda K| = log|W| + log|R + lambda Q'W^-1Q| - log|R|`.
- Code: `inference._penalized.PenalizedProblem.criterion`,
  `inference.splines.fit_pspline`, `inference.splines.fit_smoothing_spline`,
  `inference.additive_models.fit_additive_model`.
- Source: [REF-WOOD-2011], [REF-WOOD-2017, Chapter 6].

### EQ-SMOOTH-006 — Bayesian pointwise confidence band

`V_beta = phi_hat (X'WX + S_lambda)^-1`,
`f_hat(x) +/- z_{(1+level)/2} sqrt(b(x)' V_beta b(x))`, `b(x)` the basis row.

- Domain: as [EQ-SMOOTH-005]; `phi_hat` from [EQ-SMOOTH-003].
- Meaning: the posterior covariance under the prior implied by the
  penalty; it includes smoothing bias, so the coverage averaged across the
  function is close to nominal, while at a single point it can be lower
  or higher. The band ignores the uncertainty of `lambda` itself.
- Code: `inference.splines.PSplineFit.band`,
  `inference.splines.SmoothingSplineFit.band`,
  `inference.additive_models.AdditiveTerm.band`.
- Source: [REF-WAHBA-1983], [REF-NYCHKA-1988], [REF-WOOD-2017, Chapter 6].

### EQ-SMOOTH-007 — Cubic smoothing spline (Reinsch algorithm)

Minimizer of `sum_i w_i (y_i - g(x_i))^2 + lambda int g''(x)^2 dx`: the
natural cubic spline with knots `x_1 < ... < x_n`, values `g` and interior
second derivatives `gamma` solving
`(R + lambda Q'W^-1 Q) gamma = Q'y`, `g = y - lambda W^-1 Q gamma`, where
`h_i = x_{i+1} - x_i`, `Q` (`n x (n-2)`) has `q_{j-1,j} = 1/h_{j-1}`,
`q_{jj} = -1/h_{j-1} - 1/h_j`, `q_{j+1,j} = 1/h_j`, and `R` is tridiagonal
with `r_jj = (h_{j-1} + h_j)/3`, `r_{j,j+1} = h_j/6`;
`int g''^2 = gamma' R gamma`.

- Domain: distinct `x_i`, `n >= 3`, `w_i > 0`, `lambda > 0`.
- Meaning: the penalty `g'Kg`, `K = Q R^-1 Q'`, leaves straight lines
  unpenalized; the pentadiagonal system costs `O(n)`. Beyond the end knots
  the spline is linear.
- Code: `inference.splines.fit_smoothing_spline`,
  `inference.splines.SmoothingSplineFit.predict`.
- Source: [REF-REINSCH-1967], [REF-GREEN-SILVERMAN-1994].

### EQ-SMOOTH-008 — Central band of the inverse of a banded matrix

For `M = U'DU` with `U` unit upper triangular of bandwidth `b`:
`(M^-1)_ij = delta_ij / d_i - sum_{k=1}^{b} U_{i,i+k} (M^-1)_{i+k,j}`,
`j = i, ..., i + b`, computed from the last row upward;
`tr H = n - lambda sum_{|j-k|<=2} (M^-1)_jk (Q'W^-1Q)_kj`,
`H_ii = 1 - (lambda / w_i) sum_{j,k} Q_ij (M^-1)_jk Q_ik`.

- Domain: `M` symmetric positive definite and banded.
- Meaning: the entries of `M^-1` within the band are all that the trace
  and the diagonal of the smoother matrix need, so GCV, REML, and the
  pointwise variances `phi H_ii / w_i` of a smoothing spline cost `O(n)`.
- Code: `inference.splines._Band.inverse_band`,
  `inference.splines._ReinschSystem.solve`.
- Source: [REF-HUTCHINSON-DEHOOG-1985].

### EQ-SMOOTH-009 — Locally weighted regression (LOESS)

`f_hat(x0) = a_0`, where `(a_0, ..., a_d)` minimizes
`sum_k delta_k T(|x_k - x0| / h(x0)) (y_k - sum_r a_r (x_k - x0)^r)^2`,
`T(u) = (1 - |u|^3)^3` for `|u| < 1` and `0` otherwise, `h(x0)` the
distance from `x0` to its `q`-th nearest `x_k`, `q = round(f n)`.

- Domain: `0 < f <= 1`, degree `d` in `{0, 1, 2}`, at least `d + 1`
  distinct points with positive weight; `delta_k = 1` without robustness.
- Meaning: a polynomial fitted near each point; the span `f` trades bias
  for variance, and degree 1 avoids the boundary bias of local averaging.
- Code: `inference.smoothing.loess`, `inference.smoothing.LoessFit.predict`.
- Source: [REF-CLEVELAND-1979].

### EQ-SMOOTH-010 — Bisquare robustness weights

`delta_k = B(e_k / (6 s))`, `B(u) = (1 - u^2)^2` for `|u| < 1` and `0`
otherwise, `s = median |e_k|`, `e_k` the current residuals.

- Domain: `s > 0`; for `s = 0` points with zero residual keep weight one
  and the others weight zero.
- Meaning: residuals beyond six median absolute residuals get zero weight
  in the next local fits, so isolated outliers stop pulling the curve.
- Code: `inference.smoothing.loess`.
- Source: [REF-CLEVELAND-1979].

### EQ-SMOOTH-011 — Isotonic regression and the min-max formula

`f_hat = argmin_{f_1 <= ... <= f_n} sum_i w_i (y_i - f_i)^2`,
`f_hat_i = max_{j <= i} min_{k >= i} (sum_{l=j}^{k} w_l y_l) / (sum_{l=j}^{k} w_l)`.

- Domain: `w_i > 0`; the non-increasing fit is minus the isotonic fit of
  `-y`.
- Meaning: the fit is a step function whose levels are weighted means of
  consecutive blocks; pooling adjacent violators finds it in one pass.
- Code: `inference.smoothing.isotonic_regression`.
- Source: [REF-AYER-ETAL-1955], [REF-DE-LEEUW-HORNIK-MAIR-2009].

### EQ-SMOOTH-012 — Nadaraya-Watson and local-linear kernel regression

Nadaraya-Watson: `m_hat(x0) = sum_i K_i y_i / sum_i K_i`,
`K_i = K((x_i - x0)/h)`; local linear:
`m_hat(x0) = (S_2 T_0 - S_1 T_1)/(S_0 S_2 - S_1^2)`,
`S_r = sum_i K_i u_i^r`, `T_r = sum_i K_i u_i^r y_i`, `u_i = (x_i - x0)/h`.

- Domain: `h > 0`; `K` Gaussian `exp(-u^2/2)` or Epanechnikov
  `(1 - u^2)_+` (constants cancel); a positive denominator.
- Meaning: the intercept of a kernel-weighted constant or straight-line
  fit at `x0`; the local-linear form reproduces straight lines exactly
  and removes the first-order boundary bias of Nadaraya-Watson.
- Code: `inference.smoothing.kernel_regression`,
  `inference.smoothing.KernelRegressionFit.predict`.
- Source: [REF-NADARAYA-1964], [REF-FAN-GIJBELS-1996],
  [REF-HASTIE-TIBSHIRANI-FRIEDMAN-2009, Section 6.1].

### EQ-SMOOTH-013 — Leave-one-out cross-validation of the bandwidth

`CV(h) = (1/n) sum_i (y_i - m_hat_{-i}(x_i; h))^2`, `m_hat_{-i}` the
estimate computed without observation `i`; `h_hat = argmin CV(h)` over a
candidate grid.

- Domain: every leave-one-out estimate is defined (otherwise
  `CV(h) = infinity`).
- Meaning: an almost unbiased estimate of the prediction error at the
  design points; the curve is often flat, so neighbouring bandwidths are
  equally supported.
- Code: `inference.smoothing.kernel_regression`.
- Source: [REF-HASTIE-TIBSHIRANI-FRIEDMAN-2009, Section 7.10],
  [REF-FAN-GIJBELS-1996].

### EQ-GAM-001 — Gaussian additive model with centred P-spline terms

`y_i = alpha + sum_j f_j(x_ij) + e_i`, `f_j = B_j beta_j`,
`beta_j = Z_j theta_j` with `1'B_j Z_j = 0`, `Z_j` the last `k_j - 1`
columns of the Householder reflection that maps `B_j'1` to a multiple of
`e_1`; penalties `lambda_j theta_j' Z_j' D'D Z_j theta_j` of rank
`k_j - d`.

- Domain: `e_i ~ N(0, phi / w_i)` independent; difference order `d >= 1`;
  each predictor non-constant.
- Meaning: the constraint `sum_i f_j(x_ij) = 0` identifies the intercept
  without changing the space of fitted curves, because constants are
  unpenalized; each term carries its own smoothing parameter and EDF.
- Code: `inference.additive_models.fit_additive_model`,
  `inference.additive_models.AdditiveModelFit.predict`,
  `inference.additive_models.AdditiveTerm.evaluate`.
- Source: [REF-WOOD-2017, Chapter 4], [REF-HASTIE-TIBSHIRANI-1990].

### EQ-GAM-002 — Backfitting

Repeat until the terms stop changing: for `j = 1, ..., m`,
`f_j <- S_j (y - alpha - sum_{k != j} f_k)` followed by centring,
`S_j = B_j (B_j'WB_j + lambda_j D'D)^-1 B_j'W`, and then
`alpha <- sum_i w_i (y_i - sum_j f_j(x_ij)) / sum_i w_i`.

- Domain: fixed `lambda_j > 0`; symmetric penalized smoothers.
- Meaning: Gauss-Seidel iteration on the penalized normal equations of
  [EQ-GAM-001]; it converges to the joint penalized solution, so the joint
  fit and the backfit agree for the same `lambda_j`.
- Code: `inference.additive_models.backfit_additive_model`.
- Source: [REF-BUJA-HASTIE-TIBSHIRANI-1989], [REF-HASTIE-TIBSHIRANI-1990].

### EQ-GAM-003 — Partial dependence

`PD_j(v) = (1/n) sum_i m_hat(x_i1, ..., x_i(j-1), v, x_i(j+1), ..., x_ip)`.

- Domain: any prediction function `m_hat`; the average is over the data.
- Meaning: the average prediction with feature `j` held at `v`; for an
  additive model with centred terms it equals `alpha + f_j(v)` exactly,
  and for a model with interactions it averages over them.
- Code: `inference.additive_models.partial_dependence`.
- Source: [REF-FRIEDMAN-2001],
  [REF-HASTIE-TIBSHIRANI-FRIEDMAN-2009, Section 10.13].

### EQ-MVA-001 — Principal components

`S = A L A'`, `L = diag(l_1 >= ... >= l_p)`, `A = (a_1, ..., a_p)`
orthonormal; scores `z_ik = a_k' D^-1 (x_i - x_bar)`, explained ratio
`l_k / sum_j l_j`, loadings `a_jk sqrt(l_k)`; `D = I` for the covariance
and `D = diag(s_j)` for the correlation analysis.

- Domain: `S` the unbiased sample covariance (or correlation) of `n >= 2`
  rows; the sign of each `a_k` is fixed by making its largest-magnitude
  entry positive.
- Meaning: `a_k` maximizes `a'Sa` over unit vectors orthogonal to
  `a_1, ..., a_{k-1}`, and the scores are uncorrelated with variances
  `l_k`; the analysis depends on the units unless the variables are
  standardized.
- Code: `inference.multivariate_analysis.principal_components`,
  `inference.multivariate_analysis.PrincipalComponents.transform`,
  `inference.multivariate_analysis.PrincipalComponents.reconstruct`.
- Source: [REF-PEARSON-1901], [REF-HOTELLING-1933], [REF-JOLLIFFE-2002].

### EQ-MVA-002 — Maximum-likelihood factor analysis

`R = Lambda Lambda' + Psi`; for fixed `Psi`,
`Lambda = Psi^(1/2) Omega_q (Theta_q - I)^(1/2)` from the `q` largest
eigenvalues `theta_1 >= ... >= theta_q` and eigenvectors `Omega_q` of
`Psi^(-1/2) R Psi^(-1/2)`, and the discrepancy
`F = log|Sigma| - log|R| + tr(Sigma^-1 R) - p` concentrates to
`F(Psi) = sum_{j>q} (theta_j - log theta_j - 1)` with gradient
`dF/dpsi_j = (Lambda Lambda' + Psi - R)_jj / psi_j^2`.

- Domain: `R` a positive-definite correlation matrix, `1 <= q`,
  `0.005 <= psi_j <= 1`; `theta_j > 1` for the retained factors.
- Meaning: the Gaussian likelihood of the factor model profiled over the
  loadings; at an interior optimum the fitted diagonal equals the observed
  one. The loadings are determined only up to an orthogonal rotation.
- Code: `inference.multivariate_analysis.factor_analysis`.
- Source: [REF-JORESKOG-1967], [REF-LAWLEY-MAXWELL-1971].

### EQ-MVA-003 — Varimax rotation

Maximize `V = sum_k [p sum_i l_ik^4 - (sum_i l_ik^2)^2] / p^2` over
orthogonal rotations `Lambda T`; for columns `a, b` with `x = l_ia`,
`y = l_ib`, `u = x^2 - y^2`, `v = 2xy`, `A = sum u`, `B = sum v`,
`C = sum (u^2 - v^2)`, `D = 2 sum uv`, the optimal planar angle is
`phi = atan2(D - 2AB/p, C - (A^2 - B^2)/p) / 4`.

- Domain: loadings with `p` rows; Kaiser normalization divides each row
  by its length before the rotation and multiplies back afterwards.
- Meaning: the rotation that makes the squared loadings of each factor as
  spread as possible, so each variable loads mainly on few factors; the
  fitted correlations `Lambda Lambda'` are unchanged.
- Code: `inference.multivariate_analysis.varimax`.
- Source: [REF-KAISER-1958].

### EQ-MVA-004 — Bartlett-corrected test of the number of factors

`X^2 = (n - 1 - (2p + 5)/6 - 2q/3) F(Psi_hat)`, referred to chi-square with
`((p - q)^2 - p - q)/2` degrees of freedom.

- Domain: `n` independent multivariate normal observations, positive
  degrees of freedom.
- Meaning: a large statistic says that `q` factors do not reproduce the
  correlations; it is a large-sample likelihood-ratio test.
- Code: `inference.multivariate_analysis.factor_analysis`.
- Source: [REF-LAWLEY-MAXWELL-1971].

### EQ-MVA-005 — Linear discriminant analysis

`delta_k(x) = x' Sigma^-1 mu_k - mu_k' Sigma^-1 mu_k / 2 + log pi_k`,
`P(k | x) = exp(delta_k(x)) / sum_l exp(delta_l(x))`,
`Sigma = sum_k sum_{i in k} (x_i - mu_k)(x_i - mu_k)' / (n - K)`.

- Domain: Gaussian classes with a common covariance; `n - K >= p`.
- Meaning: the Bayes classifier of that model; the boundaries between
  classes are hyperplanes.
- Code: `inference.discriminant.fit_linear_discriminant`,
  `inference.discriminant.LinearDiscriminant.decision_function`.
- Source: [REF-FISHER-1936],
  [REF-HASTIE-TIBSHIRANI-FRIEDMAN-2009, Section 4.3].

### EQ-MVA-006 — Quadratic discriminant analysis

`delta_k(x) = -log|Sigma_k| / 2 - (x - mu_k)' Sigma_k^-1 (x - mu_k) / 2
+ log pi_k`, `Sigma_k` the unbiased covariance of class `k`.

- Domain: Gaussian classes; each class has more than `p` observations.
- Meaning: the Bayes classifier with unequal covariances; the boundaries
  are quadrics, at the cost of `K p (p + 1) / 2` covariance parameters.
- Code: `inference.discriminant.fit_quadratic_discriminant`,
  `inference.discriminant.QuadraticDiscriminant.decision_function`.
- Source: [REF-HASTIE-TIBSHIRANI-FRIEDMAN-2009, Section 4.3].

### EQ-MVA-007 — Fisher's canonical discriminant directions

`a_r = argmax a' B a / a' W a` subject to `a' W a = 1` and `W`-orthogonality
to `a_1, ..., a_{r-1}`, with `B = sum_k pi_k (mu_k - m)(mu_k - m)'`,
`m = sum_k pi_k mu_k`; with `W = L L'`, `a_r = L^-T e_r` for the
eigenvectors `e_r` of `L^-1 B L^-T`, `r = 1, ..., min(K - 1, p)`.

- Domain: `W` the pooled covariance of [EQ-MVA-005], positive definite.
- Meaning: the projections that separate the class means most relative to
  the within-class spread; for two classes `a_1` is proportional to
  `W^-1 (mu_2 - mu_1)`.
- Code: `inference.discriminant.fit_linear_discriminant`,
  `inference.discriminant.LinearDiscriminant.transform`.
- Source: [REF-FISHER-1936],
  [REF-HASTIE-TIBSHIRANI-FRIEDMAN-2009, Section 4.3].

### EQ-MVA-008 — k-means objective and Lloyd's iteration

`W(C) = sum_i ||x_i - m_{C(i)}||^2`; alternate
`C(i) = argmin_k ||x_i - m_k||^2` and `m_k = mean{x_i : C(i) = k}`.

- Domain: `1 <= K <= n` points in `R^p`; ties go to the lowest index.
- Meaning: neither step can increase `W`, and there are finitely many
  partitions, so the iteration stops at a local minimum; restarts from
  k-means++ seeds ([EQ-GMM-003]) reduce the risk of a poor one.
- Code: `inference.clustering.kmeans`.
- Source: [REF-LLOYD-1982], [REF-ARTHUR-VASSILVITSKII-2007],
  [REF-HASTIE-TIBSHIRANI-FRIEDMAN-2009, Section 14.3].

### EQ-MVA-009 — Silhouette width

`s(i) = (b(i) - a(i)) / max(a(i), b(i))`, `a(i)` the mean distance from
`x_i` to the other members of its cluster, `b(i)` the smallest mean
distance to the members of another cluster; `s(i) = 0` for a singleton.

- Domain: Euclidean distance; between 2 and `n - 1` clusters.
- Meaning: `s(i)` near 1 means `x_i` is much closer to its own cluster than
  to the next one, near 0 that it lies between two, and negative that it
  is probably misassigned; the average width compares numbers of clusters.
- Code: `inference.clustering.silhouette_samples`,
  `inference.clustering.silhouette_score`.
- Source: [REF-ROUSSEEUW-1987].

### EQ-TS-GARCH-001 — GARCH(p, q) variance recursion and stationarity

`y_t = mu + e_t`, `e_t = sigma_t z_t`,
`sigma_t^2 = omega + sum_{i=1}^{q} alpha_i e_(t-i)^2 + sum_{j=1}^{p} beta_j sigma_(t-j)^2`;
covariance stationary iff `sum alpha_i + sum beta_j < 1`, then
`Var(e_t) = omega / (1 - sum alpha_i - sum beta_j)`. Pre-sample values
`e_s^2 = sigma_s^2 = (1/n) sum_t e_t^2` (backcast).

- Domain: `omega > 0`, `alpha_i, beta_j >= 0`, `q >= 1`, `p >= 0`; `z_t`
  i.i.d. with mean 0 and variance 1.
- Meaning: today's variance responds to yesterday's squared shock (`alpha`)
  and decays slowly (`beta`); the persistence governs how fast shocks die
  out. The estimator maps unconstrained coordinates onto this region (exp,
  logistic, softmax).
- Code: `timeseries.garch_variances`, `timeseries.fit_garch`,
  `timeseries.GARCHFit.unconditional_variance`, `timeseries.simulate_garch`.
- Source: [REF-BOLLERSLEV-1986], [REF-ENGLE-1982].

### EQ-TS-GARCH-002 — Conditional GARCH log-likelihood (normal and Student-t)

Normal: `log L = -(1/2) sum_t [log 2 pi + log sigma_t^2 + e_t^2 / sigma_t^2]`.
Standardized Student-t with `nu > 2`:
`log L = sum_t [c(nu) - (1/2) log sigma_t^2 - ((nu+1)/2) log(1 + e_t^2 / ((nu - 2) sigma_t^2))]`,
`c(nu) = log Gamma((nu+1)/2) - log Gamma(nu/2) - (1/2) log(pi (nu - 2))`.

- Domain: [EQ-TS-GARCH-001] with every `sigma_t^2 > 0`.
- Meaning: the prediction-error decomposition of the joint density given
  the pre-sample values; the t law has unit variance so `sigma_t^2` stays
  the conditional variance.
- Code: `timeseries.garch_log_likelihood`, `timeseries.fit_garch`.
- Source: [REF-BOLLERSLEV-1986], [REF-BOLLERSLEV-1987].

### EQ-TS-GARCH-003 — GARCH variance forecasts

`sigma_(n+h|n)^2 = omega + sum_i alpha_i E[e_(n+h-i)^2] + sum_j beta_j E[sigma_(n+h-j)^2]`
with `E[e_s^2] = sigma_(s|n)^2` for `s > n`; for GARCH(1, 1)
`sigma_(n+h|n)^2 = sigma_bar^2 + (alpha + beta)^(h-1) (sigma_(n+1)^2 - sigma_bar^2)`.

- Domain: [EQ-TS-GARCH-001], stationary.
- Meaning: volatility forecasts revert geometrically to the unconditional
  variance at the rate of the persistence.
- Code: `timeseries.GARCHFit.forecast`.
- Source: [REF-BOLLERSLEV-1986].

### EQ-TS-ARCHLM-001 — Engle's LM test for ARCH effects

Regress `x_t^2` on `1, x_(t-1)^2, ..., x_(t-m)^2` over `n' = n - m`
observations; `LM = n' R^2 ~ chi^2(m)` asymptotically under no ARCH.

- Domain: `m >= 1`; mean-zero `x_t` (returns minus their mean, or
  standardized residuals).
- Meaning: autocorrelation in squared values signals volatility clustering.
- Code: `timeseries.arch_lm_test`, `timeseries.GARCHFit.diagnostics`.
- Source: [REF-ENGLE-1982].

### EQ-TS-VAR-001 — VAR(p) least-squares estimator

`y_t = nu + A_1 y_(t-1) + ... + A_p y_(t-p) + u_t`; with
`Z_t = (1, y_(t-1)', ..., y_(t-p)')'`, `B = [nu, A_1, ..., A_p]`:
`B_hat = Y Z' (Z Z')^-1`, `Sigma_u_hat = U U' / (T - K p - 1)`,
`Sigma_u_tilde = U U' / T`, `Cov(vec B_hat) = (Z Z')^-1 (x) Sigma_u_hat`,
`log L = -(T/2) (K log 2 pi + log det Sigma_u_tilde + K)`.

- Domain: `T = n - p` equations, `Z Z'` positive definite.
- Meaning: equation-by-equation OLS is efficient because every equation has
  the same regressors.
- Code: `timeseries.fit_var`, `timeseries.simulate_var`.
- Source: [REF-LUTKEPOHL-2005, Chapter 3].

### EQ-TS-VAR-002 — VAR order-selection criteria

On a common sample of `T = n - M` observations, for `m = 0..M`:
`AIC(m) = log det Sigma_u_tilde(m) + 2 m K^2 / T`,
`SC(m) = log det Sigma_u_tilde(m) + log(T) m K^2 / T`,
`HQ(m) = log det Sigma_u_tilde(m) + 2 log(log T) m K^2 / T`,
`FPE(m) = ((T + K m + 1)/(T - K m - 1))^K det Sigma_u_tilde(m)`.

- Domain: [EQ-TS-VAR-001]; the constant term is common to all orders.
- Meaning: SC and HQ estimate the true order consistently; AIC and FPE
  favour forecasting accuracy and tend to overfit.
- Code: `timeseries.select_var_order`, `timeseries.fit_var`.
- Source: [REF-LUTKEPOHL-2005, Chapter 4], [REF-AKAIKE-1974],
  [REF-SCHWARZ-1978], [REF-HANNAN-QUINN-1979].

### EQ-TS-VAR-003 — Companion form, stability, and Hessenberg QR eigenvalues

`Y_t = A Y_(t-1) + U_t`, `Y_t = (y_t', ..., y_(t-p+1)')'`,
`A = [[A_1, ..., A_p], [I_(K(p-1)), 0]]`; the VAR is stable iff every
eigenvalue of `A` has modulus below one. Eigenvalues by reduction to upper
Hessenberg form with elementary stabilized similarities and the implicitly
double-shifted Francis QR iteration with deflation.

- Domain: real `Kp x Kp` matrix.
- Meaning: stability implies stationarity and a convergent moving-average
  representation; a modulus at one signals a unit root.
- Code: `timeseries.VARFit.companion_matrix`, `timeseries.VARFit.eigenvalues`,
  `timeseries.VARFit.is_stable`, `timeseries._eigen.eigenvalues`.
- Source: [REF-LUTKEPOHL-2005, Chapter 2], [REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013,
  Sections 7.4 and 7.5].

### EQ-TS-VAR-004 — Moving-average coefficients and orthogonalized impulse responses

`Phi_0 = I_K`, `Phi_i = sum_{j=1}^{min(i,p)} Phi_(i-j) A_j`;
`Theta_i = Phi_i P` with `P` lower triangular, `P P' = Sigma_u`. For a
VAR(1), `Phi_i = A_1^i`.

- Domain: stable VAR.
- Meaning: `Theta_i[k][j]` is the response of variable `k` after `i`
  periods to a one-standard-deviation orthogonal shock in variable `j`; the
  Cholesky ordering is an identifying assumption.
- Code: `timeseries.VARFit.ma_coefficients`,
  `timeseries.VARFit.impulse_response`.
- Source: [REF-LUTKEPOHL-2005, Chapter 2].

### EQ-TS-VAR-005 — Forecast-error variance decomposition

`omega_(kj)(h) = sum_{i=0}^{h-1} Theta_i[k][j]^2 / sum_{i=0}^{h-1} sum_l Theta_i[k][l]^2`.

- Domain: [EQ-TS-VAR-004].
- Meaning: the share of the `h`-step forecast-error variance of variable
  `k` due to orthogonal shock `j`; each row sums to one.
- Code: `timeseries.VARFit.fevd`.
- Source: [REF-LUTKEPOHL-2005, Chapter 2].

### EQ-TS-VAR-006 — Granger-causality Wald and F tests

`H_0: C vec(B) = 0` (all lag coefficients of the causing variables in the
caused equations); `lambda_W = (C b)' [C ((Z Z')^-1 (x) Sigma_u_hat) C']^-1 (C b)
~ chi^2(N)`, `lambda_F = lambda_W / N ~ F(N, K (T - K p - 1))` approximately.

- Domain: [EQ-TS-VAR-001], stable VAR.
- Meaning: lags of the causing variables do not improve the forecasts of
  the caused variables.
- Code: `timeseries.VARFit.granger_causality`.
- Source: [REF-GRANGER-1969], [REF-LUTKEPOHL-2005, Chapter 3].

### EQ-TS-VAR-007 — VAR forecasts and their MSE

`y_hat_(n+h) = nu + sum_j A_j y_hat_(n+h-j)` (observed values for indices
`<= n`); `Sigma_y(h) = sum_{i=0}^{h-1} Phi_i Sigma_u Phi_i'`.

- Domain: [EQ-TS-VAR-004]; parameter uncertainty ignored.
- Meaning: Gaussian intervals `y_hat +/- z sqrt(diag Sigma_y(h))`.
- Code: `timeseries.VARFit.forecast`.
- Source: [REF-LUTKEPOHL-2005, Chapter 2].


### EQ-TS-VAR-008 — Residual-bootstrap bands for impulse responses

`y*_t = nu_hat + sum_{j=1}^p A_hat_j y*_(t-j) + u*_t` with `u*_t` drawn with
replacement from the centred residuals and `y*_1..y*_p` the observed start;
each replication refits the VAR(p) and recomputes `Theta*_h` (or `Phi*_h`).
Percentile band `[q_(alpha/2), q_(1-alpha/2)]` of the replicated responses;
Hall's band `[2 theta_hat - q_(1-alpha/2), 2 theta_hat - q_(alpha/2)]`.

- Domain: a stable fitted VAR with i.i.d. innovations; bands are pointwise
  in `h`.
- Meaning: sampling uncertainty of the impulse responses; percentile bands
  inherit the small-sample bias of least-squares VAR coefficients.
- Code: `timeseries.VARFit.impulse_response_bands`.
- Source: [REF-RUNKLE-1987], [REF-KILIAN-1998], [REF-HALL-1992].

### EQ-TS-VAR-009 — Bias-corrected bootstrap for impulse responses

`Psi_hat = mean_b(A*_b) - A_hat` from a first residual bootstrap;
`A_tilde = A_hat - delta Psi_hat` with the largest `delta` in
`{1, 0.99, ..., 0}` that keeps the companion spectral radius below one;
second-stage series are generated from `A_tilde` and every refit `A*` is
replaced by `A* - delta* Psi_hat` (same rule) before the responses and
their percentile band are computed.

- Domain: a stable fitted VAR; a non-stable estimate is left uncorrected.
- Meaning: removes the first-order small-sample bias of least-squares VAR
  coefficients, which otherwise drags percentile bands of persistent
  systems toward zero.
- Code: `timeseries.VARFit.impulse_response_bands`.
- Source: [REF-KILIAN-1998].

### EQ-TS-ADF-001 — Augmented Dickey-Fuller regression and statistic

`Delta y_t = D_t' delta + gamma y_(t-1) + sum_{j=1}^{k} phi_j Delta y_(t-j) + e_t`,
`D_t` in `{(), (1), (1, t), (1, t, t^2)}`; `tau = gamma_hat / se(gamma_hat)`
with `s^2 = RSS / (T - m)`; reject a unit root for small `tau`.

- Domain: `T = n - k - 1` regression observations.
- Meaning: under the null `gamma = 0` the statistic has a non-standard
  (Dickey-Fuller) limit; lagged differences absorb serial correlation.
- Code: `timeseries.adf_test`, `timeseries.unit_root._simulated_statistics`.
- Source: [REF-DICKEY-FULLER-1979], [REF-SAID-DICKEY-1984].

### EQ-TS-ADF-002 — MacKinnon response surfaces for Dickey-Fuller critical values

`c(T) = beta_inf + beta_1 / T + beta_2 / T^2 + beta_3 / T^3` with the
`N = 1` coefficients of MacKinnon (2010), Table 2 (`tau_nc`, `tau_c`),
Table 3 (`tau_ct`), and Table 4 (`tau_ctt`), at 1%, 5%, and 10%.

- Domain: `T` = observations in the test regression; i.i.d. normal errors.
- Meaning: finite-sample and (as `T -> inf`) asymptotic critical values
  from large simulation experiments summarized by regression.
- Code: `timeseries.adf_critical_values`.
- Source: [REF-MACKINNON-2010, Tables 2-4].

### EQ-TS-ADF-003 — Simulated Dickey-Fuller p-value

`p = (1 + #{r : tau*_r <= tau}) / (1 + R)`, `se(p) = sqrt(p (1 - p) / R)`,
where `tau*_r` is the Dickey-Fuller statistic of a Gaussian random walk
`y_t = y_(t-1) + z_t` (`y_0 = 0`) with the same deterministic terms and `T`.

- Domain: `R >= 100` replications from a seeded stream.
- Meaning: a valid Monte Carlo test; it replaces interpolation in a table
  whose coefficients could not be checked against the primary source.
- Code: `timeseries.adf_simulated_p_value`, `timeseries.adf_test`.
- Source: [REF-DAVISON-HINKLEY-1997, Chapter 4], [REF-DICKEY-FULLER-1979].

### EQ-TS-KPSS-001 — KPSS statistic and Newey-West long-run variance

`e_t` residuals of `y_t` on `1` (level) or `(1, t)` (trend),
`S_t = sum_{i<=t} e_i`, `eta = sum_t S_t^2 / (T^2 s^2(l))`,
`s^2(l) = gamma_0 + 2 sum_{j=1}^{l} (1 - j/(l+1)) gamma_j`,
`gamma_j = (1/T) sum_{t>j} e_t e_(t-j)`.

- Domain: `0 <= l < T`; the Bartlett weights keep `s^2(l) >= 0`.
- Meaning: large partial sums of residuals contradict stationarity.
- Code: `timeseries.kpss_test`, `timeseries.newey_west_variance`,
  `timeseries.cusum_test`.
- Source: [REF-KPSS-1992], [REF-NEWEY-WEST-1987].

### EQ-TS-KPSS-002 — Limit law of the KPSS statistic and Imhof inversion

`eta -> sum_k lambda_k Z_k^2`; level: `lambda_k = 1/(k pi)^2` (kernel
`min(s,t) - s t`); trend: kernel `min(s,t) - s t - 3 s(1-s) t(1-t)`, whose
eigenvalues are `1/(2 pi j)^2` and `1/(4 x_j^2)` with `tan x_j = x_j`
(the rank-one secular equation `1 = 3 sum_(k odd) c_k^2 / (lambda_k - mu)`,
`c_k^2 = 32/(k pi)^6`, reduces to `tan(omega/2) = omega/2` for
`mu = 1/omega^2`). `P(Q > x) = 1/2 + (1/pi) int_0^inf sin theta(u) / (u rho(u)) du`,
`theta(u) = (1/2) sum arctan(lambda_k u) - x u / 2`,
`rho(u) = prod (1 + lambda_k^2 u^2)^(1/4)`.

- Domain: traces `1/6` (level) and `1/15` (trend).
- Meaning: an exact asymptotic p-value; the level case is the
  Cramer-von Mises limit.
- Code: `timeseries.kpss_asymptotic_sf`, `timeseries.kpss_critical_values`,
  `timeseries.unit_root._tan_fixed_points`.
- Source: [REF-KPSS-1992], [REF-IMHOF-1961], [REF-ANDERSON-DARLING-1952].

### EQ-TS-CP-001 — CUSUM statistic for a mean shift

`S_k = sum_{i<=k} (x_i - x_bar)`, `B = max_{1<=k<n} |S_k| / (sigma_hat sqrt(n))
-> sup_t |W^0(t)|`, `P(sup |W^0| > b) = 2 sum_{j>=1} (-1)^(j-1) exp(-2 j^2 b^2)`;
`k_hat = argmax_k |S_k|`.

- Domain: constant mean under the null; `sigma_hat^2` a consistent
  (long-run) variance estimate.
- Meaning: the partial sums of deviations drift linearly away from zero on
  each side of a shift.
- Code: `timeseries.cusum_test`, `timeseries.kolmogorov_sf`.
- Source: [REF-PAGE-1954], [REF-PLOBERGER-KRAMER-1992].

### EQ-TS-CP-002 — Penalized segmentation and the PELT recursion

`F(t) = min_{tau in R_t} [F(tau) + C(y_(tau+1:t)) + beta]`, `F(0) = -beta`;
`R_(t+1) = {tau in R_t : F(tau) + C(y_(tau+1:t)) + K <= F(t)} U {t}`, valid
when `C(a:b) + C(b+1:c) + K <= C(a:c)`.

- Domain: `K = 0` for maximized `-2 log`-likelihood costs, `K = -log n` with
  the MBIC segment term; with a minimum segment length `L` a pruned
  candidate remains usable for `L - 1` steps.
- Meaning: exact optimal partitioning at expected linear cost when changes
  are spread through the series.
- Code: `timeseries.pelt`.
- Source: [REF-KILLICK-2012].

### EQ-TS-CP-003 — Gaussian segment costs and BIC / MBIC penalties

Mean (known `sigma^2`): `C = sum (x - x_bar)^2 / sigma^2`; variance (known
`mu`): `C = n_i (log 2 pi + log(sum (x - mu)^2 / n_i) + 1)`; mean and
variance: `C = n_i (log 2 pi + log sigma_hat^2 + 1)`. BIC:
`beta = (d + 1) log n`; MBIC: `beta = (d + 2) log n` plus `log n_i` per
segment, `d = 1` (mean or variance) or `2` (both). Robust noise scale:
`sigma_hat = 1.4826 MAD(Delta x) / sqrt(2)`.

- Domain: independent Gaussian segments; variance estimates floored at
  `1e-11` times the sample variance.
- Meaning: `-2` times the maximized segment log-likelihood (up to
  constants common to all segmentations) plus a per-change price.
- Code: `timeseries.pelt`, `timeseries.robust_noise_variance`.
- Source: [REF-KILLICK-ECKLEY-2014], [REF-ZHANG-SIEGMUND-2007],
  [REF-HAMPEL-1974].

### EQ-LMM-001 — Linear mixed model with a relative covariance factor

`y | b ~ N(X beta + Z b, sigma^2 I_n)`, `b = Lambda_theta u`,
`u ~ N(0, sigma^2 I_q)`, so `Var(b) = sigma^2 Lambda_theta Lambda_theta'`
and `Var(y) = sigma^2 (I_n + Z Lambda Lambda' Z')`; `Lambda_theta` is block
diagonal with one lower-triangular `r_k x r_k` block `T_k` per level of
term `k`, and `theta` stacks the lower triangle of each `T_k` column by
column.

- Domain: `n > p`; each term has `l_k >= 2` levels and `l_k r_k < n`;
  `T_k T_k'` is positive semidefinite for every real `theta` (a negated
  column of `T_k` gives the same model, so the reported `theta` has a
  non-negative diagonal).
- Meaning: random intercepts and correlated random slopes per grouping
  factor, independent between terms; nested factors are terms on the
  (outer, inner) label and uncorrelated slopes are separate terms on the
  same factor. A zero diagonal of `T_k` is a boundary (singular) fit.
- Code: `inference.random_effect`, `inference.RandomEffectTerm`,
  `inference.fit_linear_mixed_model`.
- Source: [REF-BATES-ETAL-2015, Sections 2.1-3.1], [REF-LAIRD-WARE-1982].

### EQ-LMM-002 — Penalized least squares by block Cholesky

`L L' = Lambda' Z' Z Lambda + I`, `c_u = L^-1 Lambda' Z' y`,
`R_ZX = L^-1 Lambda' Z' X`, `R_X' R_X = X'X - R_ZX' R_ZX`,
`beta_hat = (R_X' R_X)^-1 (X'y - R_ZX' c_u)`,
`u_hat = L'^-1 (c_u - R_ZX beta_hat)`,
`r^2(theta) = ||y - X beta_hat - Z Lambda u_hat||^2 + ||u_hat||^2`.

- Domain: every `theta`; `Lambda' Z' Z Lambda + I` is positive definite and
  `R_X` exists when `X` has full column rank.
- Meaning: `(beta_hat, u_hat)` minimize the penalized residual sum of
  squares for fixed `theta`, so `beta`, `u` and `sigma` are profiled out and
  only `theta` is optimized. `L` is computed inside the envelope of the
  matrix, so one grouping factor costs `O(l r^3)`.
- Code: `inference.fit_linear_mixed_model`.
- Source: [REF-BATES-ETAL-2015, Section 3.2], [REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013,
  Section 4.3].

### EQ-LMM-003 — Profiled ML deviance

`d(theta) = log |L_theta|^2 + n (1 + log(2 pi r^2(theta) / n))`,
`sigma_hat^2 = r^2(theta_hat) / n`.

- Domain: [EQ-LMM-002] with `r^2 > 0`.
- Meaning: `-2` times the log-likelihood maximized over `beta` and `sigma`
  for fixed `theta`; it is even in every column of every `T_k`, so
  `theta_ii = 0` is a stationary point that may be a boundary minimum or a
  saddle between mirror-image optima (the fit tests trial points to tell
  them apart).
- Code: `inference.fit_linear_mixed_model(method="ML")`.
- Source: [REF-BATES-ETAL-2015, Section 3.4].

### EQ-LMM-004 — Profiled REML deviance

`d_R(theta) = log |L_theta|^2 + log |R_X|^2
+ (n - p) (1 + log(2 pi r^2(theta) / (n - p)))`,
`sigma_hat^2 = r^2(theta_hat) / (n - p)`.

- Domain: [EQ-LMM-002] with `n > p`.
- Meaning: `-2` times the restricted (residual) log-likelihood
  `-(1/2)[(n - p) log 2 pi + log|V| + log|X' V^-1 X| + r' V^-1 r]` profiled
  over `sigma`; it accounts for the degrees of freedom spent on `beta`, so
  REML variance components of balanced designs equal the ANOVA estimators,
  but REML likelihoods of models with different `X` are not comparable.
- Code: `inference.fit_linear_mixed_model(method="REML")`.
- Source: [REF-PATTERSON-THOMPSON-1971], [REF-BATES-ETAL-2015,
  Section 3.4].

### EQ-LMM-005 — Fixed-effect covariance, conditional modes, and conditional variances

`Cov(beta_hat) = sigma^2 (R_X' R_X)^-1 = sigma^2 (X' V^-1 X)^-1`,
`b_hat = Lambda u_hat`, `Var(b | y) = sigma^2 Lambda (L L')^-1 Lambda'`.

- Domain: [EQ-LMM-002] at `theta_hat`.
- Meaning: `b_hat` is the BLUP `Sigma Z' V^-1 (y - X beta_hat)` of Henderson's
  mixed-model equations; the conditional variance treats `theta`, `sigma`
  and `beta` as known (the lme4 convention). For a balanced one-way layout
  `b_i = m s_b^2 (ybar_i - beta) / (m s_b^2 + s^2)` and
  `Var(b_i | y) = (1/s_b^2 + m/s^2)^-1`.
- Code: `inference.LinearMixedModelResult.covariance`,
  `inference.RandomEffectEstimates.values`,
  `inference.RandomEffectEstimates.conditional_covariances`.
- Source: [REF-HENDERSON-1975], [REF-BATES-ETAL-2015, Sections 3.5-3.6].

### EQ-LMM-006 — Satterthwaite denominator degrees of freedom

For a contrast `c`, `V(psi) = c' Cov(beta_hat; psi) c` with
`psi = (theta, sigma)` and `Cov = sigma^2 (R_X' R_X)^-1(theta)`;
`nu = 2 V(psi_hat)^2 / (g' A g)`, `g = dV/dpsi`, `A = 2 H^-1`, where `H` is
the Hessian of the (REML or ML) deviance
`log|L|^2 + r^2/sigma^2 + n log(2 pi sigma^2)
[+ log|R_X|^2 - p log(2 pi sigma^2)]` at `psi_hat`; `t = c' beta_hat /
sqrt(V)` is referred to Student t on `nu` df.

- Domain: interior `psi_hat` with a positive-definite `H`; `nu` is reported
  as `nan` otherwise. `H` and `g` are central differences.
- Meaning: matches the first two moments of `V(psi_hat)` to a scaled
  chi-square. When `Cov(beta)` is one mean square (balanced one-way, nested,
  and random-coefficient designs) `nu` is that mean square's df, `a - 1`.
- Code: `inference.LinearMixedModelResult.degrees_of_freedom`,
  `inference.LinearMixedModelResult.test_contrast`.
- Source: [REF-SATTERTHWAITE-1946], [REF-KUZNETSOVA-ETAL-2017, Section 3].

### EQ-LMM-007 — Likelihood-ratio test with boundary and bootstrap references

`T = 2 (l_full - l_reduced) >= 0`, `df = k_full - k_reduced`;
`p = P(chi^2_df >= T)`, `p_mix = (1/2) P(chi^2_(df-1) >= T) + (1/2)
P(chi^2_df >= T)` (`chi^2_0` a point mass at zero), and
`p_boot = (1 + #{T*_b >= T}) / (B + 1)` with `T*_b` from `B` responses
simulated from the reduced fit and refitted under both models.

- Domain: nested models on the same response; REML only when both share
  the fixed-effect design.
- Meaning: a variance tested at zero lies on the boundary, where the
  chi-square reference is conservative; `p_mix` is the Self-Liang /
  Stram-Lee limit when the full model adds one random effect with its
  covariances, and the parametric bootstrap estimates the finite-sample
  null law in general.
- Code: `inference.mixed_model_likelihood_ratio_test`.
- Source: [REF-SELF-LIANG-1987], [REF-STRAM-LEE-1994],
  [REF-EFRON-TIBSHIRANI-1993, Chapter 6].

### EQ-LMM-008 — Balanced one-way random-effects ANOVA estimators

With `a` groups of size `m`, `N = a m`, `MSA = SSA/(a - 1)`,
`MSE = SSE/(a(m - 1))`: REML `sigma^2 = MSE`,
`sigma_b^2 = (MSA - MSE)/m` when `MSA > MSE`, else `sigma_b^2 = 0`,
`sigma^2 = (SSA + SSE)/(N - 1)`; ML `sigma^2 = MSE`,
`sigma_b^2 = (SSA/a - MSE)/m` when positive, else `sigma_b^2 = 0`,
`sigma^2 = (SSA + SSE)/N`; `Var(beta_hat) = (sigma^2 + m sigma_b^2)/N`.

- Domain: balanced data, one random intercept, `X = 1`.
- Meaning: closed forms reproduced by the profiled deviances; the boundary
  occurs exactly when the ANOVA solution is negative. Under the null
  `sigma_b = 0`, `MSA/MSE ~ F(a - 1, a(m - 1))`, so the ML estimate is zero
  with probability `P(F <= a/(a - 1))`.
- Code: `inference.fit_linear_mixed_model`,
  `tests/test_mixed_models.py::OneWayClosedFormTests`.
- Source: [REF-SEARLE-CASELLA-MCCULLOCH-1992, Chapters 3-4].

### EQ-GLMM-001 — Laplace approximation by penalized IRLS

`h(u) = sum_i log p(y_i | eta_i) - ||u||^2/2`,
`eta = X beta + o + Z Lambda u`; the mode `u_hat` solves Newton steps
`(Lambda' Z' D Z Lambda + I) delta = Lambda' Z' s - u` with
`s_i = w_i (y_i - mu_i)` and `D_i = w_i V(mu_i)` (canonical links);
`-2 log L ~= -2 sum_i log p(y_i | u_hat) + ||u_hat||^2 + log|L|^2`,
`L L' = Lambda' Z' D(u_hat) Z Lambda + I`.

- Domain: binomial with logit link (`y` a proportion, `w` trials) and
  Poisson with log link; `u ~ N(0, I)`, `Var(b) = Lambda Lambda'`.
- Meaning: second-order expansion of the integrand around its mode; the
  error shrinks as the information per random effect grows and is largest
  for small binomial clusters. `theta` and `beta` are optimized jointly and
  `Cov(beta)` is the `beta` block of `2 H^-1`.
- Code: `inference.fit_generalized_linear_mixed_model(method="laplace")`,
  `inference.glmm_deviance`.
- Source: [REF-BATES-ETAL-2015, Section 3], [REF-PINHEIRO-BATES-1995].

### EQ-GLMM-002 — Adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature for a scalar random effect

For group `j`, `h_j(u) = sum_(i in j) log p(y_i | x_i' beta + o_i + theta u)
- u^2/2`, mode `u_j`, `s_j = (-h_j''(u_j))^(-1/2)`;
`L_j ~= s_j sum_(k=1..K) (w_k e^(x_k^2) / sqrt(pi)) exp(h_j(u_j + sqrt(2)
s_j x_k))` with Gauss-Hermite nodes `x_k` and weights `w_k` for
`exp(-x^2)` (Golub-Welsch eigenvalues refined by Newton steps on the
orthonormal Hermite polynomial, Christoffel weights
`1 / sum_(j<K) h_j(x_k)^2`).

- Domain: one random-effect term with one column (a random intercept),
  `1 <= K <= 64`.
- Meaning: the rule is centred and scaled at each group's mode, so it is
  exact for a Gaussian integrand and converges quickly; `K = 1` is the
  Laplace value `s_j exp(h_j(u_j))` of [EQ-GLMM-001].
- Code: `inference.fit_generalized_linear_mixed_model(method="adaptive_quadrature")`,
  `inference.glmm_deviance`, `inference.mixed_models._gauss_hermite`.
- Source: [REF-LIU-PIERCE-1994], [REF-PINHEIRO-BATES-1995],
  [REF-GOLUB-WELSCH-1969].

### EQ-CNT-REG-001 — Log-linear count regression with an exposure offset

`log mu_i = x_i' beta + o_i`, `o_i = log t_i` for an exposure `t_i > 0`
(plus any other offset); `exp(beta_j)` is the incidence-rate ratio, the
factor by which the expected count per unit of exposure changes per unit
of `x_j`.

- Domain: non-negative integer counts `y_i`; full-rank design.
- Meaning: an offset is a covariate whose coefficient is fixed at one, so
  the model is for the rate `mu_i / t_i`.
- Code: `inference.fit_poisson_regression`,
  `inference.CountRegressionResult.incidence_rate_ratios`,
  `inference.CountRegressionResult.predict`.
- Source: [REF-CAMERON-TRIVEDI-2013], [REF-MCCULLAGH-NELDER-1989, Chapter 6].

### EQ-CNT-REG-002 — Sandwich covariance of a count regression

`V = A^-1 B A^-1`, `A = sum_i w_i x_i x_i'`,
`B = sum_i s_i^2 x_i x_i'`, with `w_i = mu_i/(1 + alpha mu_i)` and the
score `s_i = (y_i - mu_i)/(1 + alpha mu_i)` (`alpha = 0` for Poisson).

- Domain: independent observations; the HC0 form without small-sample
  factor.
- Meaning: `beta_hat` of the Poisson model is consistent whenever the mean
  is correctly specified; the sandwich gives standard errors that remain
  valid when the variance is not `mu`.
- Code: `inference.fit_poisson_regression`,
  `inference.fit_negative_binomial_regression`.
- Source: [REF-WHITE-1982], [REF-CAMERON-TRIVEDI-2013].

### EQ-CNT-REG-003 — NB2 regression log-likelihood and scores

`l = sum_i [log Gamma(y_i + theta) - log Gamma(theta) - log y_i!
+ theta log(theta/(theta + mu_i)) + y_i log(mu_i/(theta + mu_i))]`,
`Var(y_i) = mu_i + mu_i^2/theta`, `alpha = 1/theta`;
`dl/d eta_i = (y_i - mu_i) theta/(theta + mu_i)`,
`dl/d theta = sum_(j<y_i) 1/(theta + j) + log(theta/(theta + mu_i)) + 1
- (y_i + theta)/(theta + mu_i)`,
`d^2 l/d eta^2 = -mu theta (theta + y)/(theta + mu)^2`,
`d^2 l/d eta d theta = (y - mu) mu/(theta + mu)^2`,
`d^2 l/d theta^2 = -sum_(j<y) 1/(theta + j)^2 + 1/theta - 1/(theta + mu)
+ (y - mu)/(theta + mu)^2`.

- Domain: `theta > 0`; the maximum lies on the Poisson boundary
  `theta = inf` when `sum [(y_i - mu_i)^2 - y_i] <= 0` at the Poisson fit
  (the leading term of the `theta` score as `theta -> inf`).
- Meaning: gamma-mixed Poisson counts with quadratic variance; the
  coefficient block of the expected information is `X'WX`,
  `W = mu/(1 + alpha mu)`, orthogonal to `theta`.
- Code: `inference.fit_negative_binomial_regression`,
  `inference.count_regression.nb2_log_pmf`.
- Source: [REF-CAMERON-TRIVEDI-2013], [REF-NIST-DLMF-GAMMA, Section 5.5].
