### EQ-CNT-REG-004 — Regression-based overdispersion test

`[(y_i - mu_i)^2 - y_i]/mu_i = alpha z_i + e_i` by least squares without
intercept, `z_i = mu_i` (NB2, `Var = mu + alpha mu^2`) or `z_i = 1` (NB1,
`Var = (1 + alpha) mu`); `t = alpha_hat / se`,
`se^2 = [sum e_i^2 /(n - 1)] / sum z_i^2`, referred to `N(0, 1)`.

- Domain: `mu_i` from a Poisson regression fit; one-sided against
  `alpha > 0` by default.
- Meaning: under the Poisson null `E[(y - mu)^2 - y] = 0`; a positive
  `alpha` estimates the excess variance.
- Code: `inference.poisson_overdispersion_test`.
- Source: [REF-CAMERON-TRIVEDI-1990].

### EQ-CNT-ZI-001 — Zero-inflated count likelihood

`P(y_i = 0) = pi_i + (1 - pi_i) f(0; mu_i)`,
`P(y_i = k) = (1 - pi_i) f(k; mu_i)` for `k > 0`, `logit pi_i = z_i' gamma`,
`log mu_i = x_i' beta + o_i`, `f` Poisson or NB2;
`E[y_i] = (1 - pi_i) mu_i`.

- Domain: at least one zero; `pi_i` near zero makes `gamma` weakly
  identified (the Poisson model is the boundary `pi = 0`).
- Meaning: zeros arise from a structural process and from the count
  process; for `y = 0` the posterior share of the count process is
  `(1 - pi) f(0) / P(y = 0)`.
- Code: `inference.fit_zero_inflated`, `inference.ZeroCountResult.predict`.
- Source: [REF-LAMBERT-1992], [REF-CAMERON-TRIVEDI-2013].

### EQ-CNT-HURDLE-001 — Hurdle count likelihood

`P(y_i = 0) = 1 - p_i`, `P(y_i = k) = p_i f(k; mu_i)/(1 - f(0; mu_i))` for
`k > 0`, `logit p_i = z_i' gamma`; the log-likelihood is the binary logit
of `1{y_i > 0}` plus the zero-truncated count log-likelihood
`sum_(y_i > 0) [log f(y_i; mu_i) - log(1 - f(0; mu_i))]`;
`E[y_i] = p_i mu_i/(1 - f(0; mu_i))`.

- Domain: at least one zero and more positive counts than count
  coefficients.
- Meaning: one process decides whether the count is positive, another how
  large it is; with intercept-only parts the hurdle and zero-inflated
  models have the same maximized likelihood (both reproduce the observed
  zero share).
- Code: `inference.fit_hurdle`, `inference.ZeroCountResult.predict`.
- Source: [REF-MULLAHY-1986], [REF-CAMERON-TRIVEDI-2013].

### EQ-CNT-VUONG-001 — Vuong statistic for non-nested models

`m_i = log f_A(y_i) - log f_B(y_i)`,
`V = (sum m_i - c)/(sqrt(n) omega)`,
`omega^2 = (1/n) sum (m_i - m_bar)^2`, `c = 0`, `k_A - k_B` (AIC), or
`(k_A - k_B) log(n)/2` (BIC); `V -> N(0, 1)` when the strictly non-nested
models are equally close to the truth.

- Domain: strictly non-nested models only. A count model is the
  zero-inflated model at the boundary `pi = 0`, so the normal reference
  does not hold for a zero-inflation comparison.
- Meaning: large positive values favour model A, large negative values
  model B.
- Code: `inference.vuong_test`.
- Source: [REF-VUONG-1989], [REF-WILSON-2015].

### EQ-CAT-ORD-001 — Proportional-odds (cumulative logit) model

`P(Y_i <= k | x_i) = F(theta_k - x_i' beta)`, `k = 1..J-1`,
`theta_1 < ... < theta_(J-1)`, `F(t) = 1/(1 + e^-t)`;
`P(Y_i = k) = F(theta_k - eta_i) - F(theta_(k-1) - eta_i)` with
`theta_0 = -inf`, `theta_J = inf`. Without covariates
`theta_k = logit(N_(<=k)/n)`.

- Domain: ordered categories, each observed; no intercept column (the
  thresholds absorb it).
- Meaning: one slope vector for every cut: `exp(beta_j)` multiplies the
  odds of `Y > k` for every `k`. With `J = 2` the model is the logistic
  regression of `1{Y > 1}` with intercept `-theta_1` and slopes `beta`.
- Code: `inference.fit_ordinal_logistic`,
  `inference.OrdinalRegressionResult.predict_proba`,
  `inference.OrdinalRegressionResult.odds_ratios`.
- Source: [REF-MCCULLAGH-1980], [REF-AGRESTI-2013].

### EQ-CAT-BRANT-001 — Brant test of proportional odds

For each cut `k` a binary logit of `1{Y > k}` on `(1, x)` gives `beta_k`;
`Cov(beta_k, beta_l) = (X'W_kk X)^-1 X'W_kl X (X'W_ll X)^-1`,
`W_kl = diag(pi_(i,max(k,l)) - pi_ik pi_il)`;
`X^2 = (D beta*)' (D V D')^-1 (D beta*)` with `D beta*` the slope
contrasts `beta_1 - beta_k`, `k = 2..J-1`, on `(J - 2) p` degrees of
freedom.

- Domain: `J >= 3`, at least one covariate, no separation in any binary
  logit.
- Meaning: large values say the covariate effects differ across cuts, so a
  single slope summarizes them poorly.
- Code: `inference.brant_test`.
- Source: [REF-BRANT-1990].

### EQ-CAT-MNL-001 — Baseline-category multinomial logit

`P(Y_i = k | x_i) = exp(x_i' beta_k)/sum_l exp(x_i' beta_l)`,
`beta_ref = 0`; `dl/d beta_k = sum_i (y_ik - p_ik) x_i`,
`d^2 l/d beta_k d beta_l' = -sum_i p_ik (delta_kl - p_il) x_i x_i'`.

- Domain: every category observed; estimates do not exist under
  (quasi-)separation.
- Meaning: `exp(beta_kj)` multiplies the relative risk
  `P(Y = k)/P(Y = ref)` per unit of `x_j`. With a single factor the model
  is saturated and `beta_k` are log ratios of cell counts.
- Code: `inference.fit_multinomial_logit`,
  `inference.MultinomialLogitResult.predict_proba`,
  `inference.MultinomialLogitResult.relative_risk_ratios`.
- Source: [REF-AGRESTI-2013].

### EQ-REG-AME-001 — Average marginal effects and their delta-method covariance

`AME_jk = (1/n) sum_i d E_k(x_i; psi)/d x_ij` (derivative) or
`(1/n) sum_i [E_k(x_i, x_ij = 1) - E_k(x_i, x_ij = 0)]` (discrete), with
`E_k` a category probability or the mean count; `Cov(AME) = G V G'`,
`G = d AME/d psi'` at `psi_hat` (central differences), `V = Cov(psi_hat)`.
Poisson/NB2: `d mu/d x_j = beta_j mu`; ordinal:
`d P_k/d x_j = -beta_j [f(theta_k - eta) - f(theta_(k-1) - eta)]`;
multinomial: `d p_k/d x_j = p_k (beta_kj - sum_l p_l beta_lj)`.

- Domain: a non-constant design column; derivative effects of indicator
  columns are approximations, the discrete form is exact for them.
- Meaning: the change of the expected outcome per unit of `x_j`, averaged
  over the sample, on the probability or count scale rather than the link
  scale.
- Code: `inference.MarginalEffects`,
  `inference.CountRegressionResult.average_marginal_effect`,
  `inference.OrdinalRegressionResult.average_marginal_effects`,
  `inference.MultinomialLogitResult.average_marginal_effects`.
- Source: [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002, Section 5.5], [REF-AGRESTI-2013].

### EQ-INF-ROB-001 — Huber and Tukey biweight score functions

Huber: `rho(u) = u^2/2` for `|u| <= k` and `k|u| - k^2/2` beyond,
`psi(u) = max(-k, min(k, u))`, `w(u) = min(1, k/|u|)`. Tukey biweight
(bisquare): `psi(u) = u (1 - (u/c)^2)^2` for `|u| < c` and `0` beyond,
`psi'(u) = (1 - (u/c)^2)(1 - 5 (u/c)^2)`, `w(u) = (1 - (u/c)^2)^2`.

- Domain: `k, c > 0`; the defaults `k = 1.345` and `c = 4.685` give 95%
  asymptotic efficiency at the normal law.
- Meaning: the score bounds the influence of one observation; the
  biweight redescends to zero, so gross outliers are rejected entirely, at
  the price of a non-convex objective.
- Code: `inference.psi_function`, `inference.robust._psi`,
  `inference.robust._psi_derivative`, `inference.robust._weight`.
- Source: [REF-HUBER-1964], [REF-BEATON-TUKEY-1974], and
  [REF-MARONNA-MARTIN-YOHAI-2006].

### EQ-INF-ROB-002 — M-estimator of location with MAD scale and sandwich error

`sum_i psi((x_i - mu)/s) = 0` with `s = 1.4826 median|x_i - median(x)|`
fixed; IRLS `mu <- sum w_i x_i / sum w_i`, `w_i = w((x_i - mu)/s)`, started
at the median; `se(mu) = s sqrt(n/(n-1) sum psi(u_i)^2) / sum psi'(u_i)`,
interval `mu +- t_{n-1, 1-alpha/2} se`.

- Domain: `n >= 2`, `s > 0`, `sum psi'(u_i) > 0`.
- Meaning: the empirical form of the asymptotic variance
  `s^2 E psi^2 / (E psi')^2 / n`; the MAD gives the estimator the 50%
  breakdown point of the median; the scale's own variability is ignored.
- Code: `inference.robust_location`.
- Source: [REF-HUBER-1964], [REF-HUBER-1981], and
  [REF-MARONNA-MARTIN-YOHAI-2006].

### EQ-INF-ROB-003 — Regression M-estimator by IRLS with sandwich covariance

`sum_i psi(r_i/s) x_i = 0`, `r_i = y_i - x_i' beta`,
`s = 1.4826 median_i |r_i|` re-estimated each iteration; IRLS
`beta <- (X'WX)^-1 X'Wy`, `W = diag w(r_i/s)`;
`Cov(beta) = s^2 n/(n-p) A^-1 B A^-1`, `A = sum psi'(u_i) x_i x_i'`,
`B = sum psi(u_i)^2 x_i x_i'`, intervals with `t_{n-p}`.

- Domain: `n > p`, full-rank weighted design, `s > 0`, `A` non-singular.
- Meaning: robust to outlying responses but not to outlying design points
  (breakdown point `1/n` for leverage); the biweight root depends on the
  start (least absolute deviations by default).
- Code: `inference.fit_robust_linear_model`,
  `inference.robust._residual_scale`.
- Source: [REF-HUBER-1981], [REF-BEATON-TUKEY-1974], and
  [REF-MARONNA-MARTIN-YOHAI-2006].

### EQ-INF-ROB-004 — Theil-Sen slope and Sen's interval

`b = median{(y_j - y_i)/(x_j - x_i): i < j, x_i != x_j}`,
`a = median(y_i - b x_i)`; with `N` sorted pairwise slopes `S_(1..N)` and
`C = z_{1-alpha/2} sqrt([n(n-1)(2n+5) - sum_t t(t-1)(2t+5)]/18)` (ties `t`
in `x`), the interval is `[S_(round((N-C)/2)), S_(round((N+C)/2)+1)]`.

- Domain: `n >= 2` with at least two distinct `x`; continuous `y`.
- Meaning: inverts Kendall's test of `beta` on `(x, y - beta x)`; the slope
  stays bounded while good-good pairs, a fraction `(1 - eps)^2` of all
  pairs, form a majority, a breakdown point of `1 - 1/sqrt 2`.
- Code: `inference.theil_sen_slope`.
- Source: [REF-SEN-1968], [REF-KENDALL-1938], and
  [REF-HOLLANDER-WOLFE-CHICKEN-2014, Chapter 9].

### EQ-INF-QR-001 — Regression quantiles as a linear program

`beta(tau) in argmin sum_i rho_tau(y_i - x_i' beta)`,
`rho_tau(r) = r (tau - 1{r < 0})`; some minimizer is an elemental vertex
`beta = X_h^-1 y_h`. Along edge `(j, s)` (`X_h d = -s e_j`) the
directional derivative is
`D = [tau if s = 1 else 1 - tau] + sum_{i not in h} g_i(s c_ij)`,
`c_i = x_i' X_h^-1`, with `g_i(a) = psi_tau(r_i) a` for `r_i != 0` and
`max(tau a, (tau - 1) a)` for `r_i = 0`; the vertex is optimal when no edge
of any elemental basis of the zero-residual set has `D < 0`.

- Domain: `0 < tau < 1`, full-rank design, `n >= p`.
- Meaning: the steepest descending edge is followed to the breakpoint where
  the derivative, increased by `|a_i|` at each residual sign change, first
  becomes non-negative (a weighted-median line search); each step strictly
  lowers the objective.
- Code: `inference.fit_quantile_regression`, `inference.check_loss`,
  `inference.quantile_regression._solve`,
  `inference.quantile_regression._edge_derivatives`.
- Source: [REF-KOENKER-BASSETT-1978], [REF-BARRODALE-ROBERTS-1973], and
  [REF-KOENKER-2005].

### EQ-INF-QR-002 — Pairs bootstrap for regression quantiles

Resample `(x_i, y_i)` pairs `B` times, refit `beta*_b(tau)`, and report
`se_j = sd_b(beta*_bj)` and the percentile interval
`[Q_{alpha/2}(beta*_j), Q_{1-alpha/2}(beta*_j)]` (Hyndman-Fan type 7);
rank-deficient resamples are redrawn.

- Domain: `B >= 50`; independent pairs (heteroscedasticity allowed).
- Meaning: a large-sample interval that does not need the sparsity
  `1/f(F^-1(tau))`.
- Code: `inference.fit_quantile_regression`,
  `inference.quantile_regression._bootstrap`.
- Source: [REF-KOENKER-2005] and [REF-EFRON-TIBSHIRANI-1993, Chapter 9].

### EQ-INF-KW-001 — Kruskal-Wallis statistic and exact permutation law

`H = [12/(N(N+1)) sum_g R_g^2/n_g - 3(N+1)] / (1 - sum(t^3 - t)/(N^3 - N))`
with pooled mid-ranks; exact law: every one of the `N!/prod n_g!`
assignments of the observed mid-ranks to groups is equally likely, and
`p = #{T >= T_obs}/#assignments` with `T = sum_g (L/n_g) S_g^2` in doubled
integer ranks, `L = lcm(n_g)`; otherwise `H ~ chi^2_{k-1}`;
`epsilon^2 = H/(N - 1)`.

- Domain: `k >= 2` non-empty groups, not all observations tied.
- Meaning: tests that the groups come from one distribution, sensitive to
  location shifts; the exact law is conditional on the tie pattern.
- Code: `inference.kruskal_wallis_test`,
  `inference.classical_tests._kruskal_exact_p`.
- Source: [REF-KRUSKAL-WALLIS-1952] and
  [REF-HOLLANDER-WOLFE-CHICKEN-2014, Chapter 6].

### EQ-INF-FRIEDMAN-001 — Friedman statistic for complete blocks

`Q = [12/(n k (k+1)) sum_j R_j^2 - 3 n (k+1)] /
(1 - sum_blocks sum(t^3 - t)/(n (k^3 - k)))` with within-block mid-ranks,
`Q ~ chi^2_{k-1}`; Kendall's `W = Q/(n (k - 1))`.

- Domain: `n >= 2` blocks of `k >= 2` treatments, not every block tied.
- Meaning: the rank analogue of the two-way ANOVA without interaction.
- Code: `inference.friedman_test`.
- Source: [REF-FRIEDMAN-1937] and
  [REF-HOLLANDER-WOLFE-CHICKEN-2014, Chapter 7].

### EQ-INF-SIGN-001 — Sign test

Zero differences dropped; `S = #{d_i > 0} ~ Binomial(m, 1/2)` for the `m`
non-zero differences; p-values from [EQ-INF-BINOM-001].

- Domain: `m >= 1`.
- Meaning: tests that the median difference is the null value without
  assuming symmetry.
- Code: `inference.sign_test`.
- Source: [REF-DIXON-MOOD-1946] and
  [REF-HOLLANDER-WOLFE-CHICKEN-2014, Chapter 3].

### EQ-INF-LEVENE-001 — Levene and Brown-Forsythe tests

`z_ij = |x_ij - c_i|` with `c_i` the group mean (Levene) or median
(Brown-Forsythe); `F` is the one-way ANOVA statistic [EQ-INF-ANOVA-001] of
the `z_ij`, referred to `F(k - 1, N - k)`.

- Domain: `k >= 2` groups of at least two observations; the `z_ij` not
  constant within every group.
- Meaning: compares spreads; the median version keeps its level under
  skewed and heavy-tailed data.
- Code: `inference.levene_test`, `inference.brown_forsythe_test`.
- Source: [REF-BROWN-FORSYTHE-1974].

### EQ-INF-BARTLETT-001 — Bartlett's test of equal variances

`T = [(N - k) ln s_p^2 - sum (n_i - 1) ln s_i^2] /
(1 + (sum 1/(n_i - 1) - 1/(N - k))/(3(k - 1)))`, `T ~ chi^2_{k-1}`.

- Domain: `k >= 2` groups with `n_i >= 2` and `s_i^2 > 0`.
- Meaning: the modified likelihood-ratio test under normality; not robust
  to non-normal tails.
- Code: `inference.bartlett_test`.
- Source: [REF-BARTLETT-1937].

### EQ-INF-SW-001 — Shapiro-Wilk W by Royston's approximation (AS R94)

`m_i = Phi^-1((i - 3/8)/(n + 1/4))`, `u = n^-1/2`;
`a_n = -m_1/||m|| + C1(u)`, `a_{n-1} = -m_2/||m|| + C2(u)` (`n > 5`), other
`a_i = -m_i/phi` with `sum a_i^2 = 1`, where
`C1 = (0, 0.221157, -0.147981, -2.071190, 4.434685, -2.706056)` and
`C2 = (0, 0.042981, -0.293762, -1.752461, 5.682633, -3.582633)` are
polynomial coefficients; `W = corr(a, x_(.))^2`. p-value: `n = 3`:
`(6/pi)(asin sqrt W - pi/3)`; `4 <= n <= 11`:
`y = -ln(gamma - ln(1 - W))`, `gamma = -2.273 + 0.459 n`, mean
`0.544 - 0.39978 n + 0.025054 n^2 - 6.714e-4 n^3`, log sd
`1.3822 - 0.77857 n + 0.062767 n^2 - 0.0020322 n^3`; `n >= 12`:
`y = ln(1 - W)`, mean `-1.5861 - 0.31082 l - 0.083751 l^2 + 0.0038915 l^3`,
log sd `-0.4803 - 0.082676 l + 0.0030302 l^2`, `l = ln n`; `p = P(Z > (y -
mean)/sd)`.

- Domain: `3 <= n <= 5000`, positive range.
- Meaning: small `W` indicates departure from normality; the coefficients
  were checked against the published Fortran listing of AS R94.
- Code: `inference.shapiro_wilk_test`, `inference.shapiro_wilk_coefficients`.
- Source: [REF-SHAPIRO-WILK-1965], [REF-ROYSTON-1992], [REF-ROYSTON-1995],
  and [REF-STATLIB-AS-R94].

### EQ-INF-COCHRANQ-001 — Cochran's Q for matched binary outcomes

`Q = (k - 1)(k sum_j C_j^2 - T^2)/(k T - sum_i R_i^2)` with column totals
`C_j`, row totals `R_i`, `T = sum C_j`; `Q ~ chi^2_{k-1}`.

- Domain: binary `n x k` table with at least one mixed row.
- Meaning: tests equal success probabilities across `k` matched
  conditions; equals McNemar's uncorrected statistic for `k = 2`.
- Code: `inference.cochran_q_test`.
- Source: [REF-COCHRAN-1950].

### EQ-INF-SRANGE-001 — Studentized range distribution

`P(Q <= q) = int_0^inf f_nu(s) P_k(q s) ds`,
`P_k(w) = k int phi(z) [Phi(z) - Phi(z - w)]^(k-1) dz`,
`f_nu(s) = 2 (nu/2)^(nu/2)/Gamma(nu/2) s^(nu-1) exp(-nu s^2/2)`; for
`nu = inf`, `P(Q <= q) = P_k(q)`; for `k = 2`,
`P(Q <= q) = P(|T_nu| <= q/sqrt 2)`.

- Domain: `k >= 2`, `nu >= 1` or `inf`, `q >= 0`.
- Meaning: the law of the range of `k` independent normal means divided by
  an independent root mean square on `nu` degrees of freedom; inner rule
  16-point Gauss-Legendre on nine panels of `[-9, 9]`, outer rule adaptive
  Gauss-Kronrod; absolute error about `1e-12`.
- Code: `inference.studentized_range_cdf`, `inference.studentized_range_sf`,
  `inference.studentized_range_quantile`,
  `inference.studentized_range._range_cdf`.
- Source: [REF-COPENHAVER-HOLLAND-1988], [REF-LUND-LUND-1983], and
  [REF-HOCHBERG-TAMHANE-1987].

### EQ-INF-TUKEY-001 — Tukey-Kramer honestly significant differences

`q_ij = |x_bar_i - x_bar_j| / sqrt(MSE/2 (1/n_i + 1/n_j))`,
`p_ij = P(Q_{k, N-k} > q_ij)`, simultaneous intervals
`x_bar_i - x_bar_j +- q_{1-alpha; k, N-k} sqrt(MSE/2 (1/n_i + 1/n_j))`.

- Domain: `k >= 2` groups, `N > k`, `MSE > 0`; normal errors with a common
  variance.
- Meaning: family-wise error exactly `alpha` for equal sizes and
  conservative (Tukey-Kramer) for unequal sizes.
- Code: `inference.tukey_hsd_test`.
- Source: [REF-KRAMER-1956] and [REF-HOCHBERG-TAMHANE-1987].

### EQ-INF-DUNN-001 — Dunn's pairwise rank comparisons

`z_ij = (R_bar_i - R_bar_j) /
sqrt((N(N+1)/12 - sum(t^3 - t)/(12(N - 1)))(1/n_i + 1/n_j))` with pooled
mid-ranks, two-sided normal p-values, adjusted by [EQ-INF-MT-001] or
[EQ-INF-MT-002].

- Domain: `k >= 2` groups, not all observations tied.
- Meaning: the follow-up to a Kruskal-Wallis rejection that uses the
  pooled ranks of all groups, not separate two-sample rankings.
- Code: `inference.dunn_test`.
- Source: [REF-DUNN-1964] and [REF-HOLLANDER-WOLFE-CHICKEN-2014, Chapter 6].

### EQ-MOD-FLOOD-001 — Dike overflow of the flood model

`S=Z_v+H-H_d-C_b` with `H=(Q/(K_s B sqrt((Z_m-Z_v)/L)))^0.6`.

- Domain: `Q, K_s, B, L > 0` and `Z_m > Z_v`.
- Meaning: water level above the dike crest of a river section under a
  one-dimensional steady-flow (Manning-Strickler) approximation; `S > 0` is
  an overflow.
- Code: `modeling.flood_overflow`, `modeling.flood_model`.
- Source: [REF-IOOSS-LEMAITRE-2015].

### EQ-MOD-FLOOD-002 — Dike maintenance cost of the flood model

`C=1{S>0}+[0.2+0.8(1-exp(-1000/S^4))]1{S<=0}+max(H_d,8)/20`.

- Domain: the overflow `S` of [EQ-MOD-FLOOD-001]; the `S <= 0` branch tends
  to one as `S -> 0`, the value used at `S = 0`.
- Meaning: annual maintenance cost (million euros) that jumps when the dike
  overflows and grows with the dike height above 8 m.
- Code: `modeling.flood_cost`, `modeling.flood_model`.
- Source: [REF-IOOSS-LEMAITRE-2015].

### EQ-REL-WAARTS-001 — Four-branch series limit state

`g(u)=min(3+(u_1-u_2)^2/10-|u_1+u_2|/sqrt(2), k/sqrt(2)-|u_1-u_2|)`.

- Domain: two independent standard-normal coordinates and `k > 0`.
- Meaning: series system of four branches; with `k = 7` two design points
  lie at distance 3 and two at 3.5, so single-point FORM misses about half
  of `P(g <= 0) ~ 2.22e-3`.
- Code: `modeling.four_branch`, `modeling.four_branch_model`.
- Source: [REF-WAARTS-2000], [REF-ECHARD-GAYTON-LEMAIRE-2011].

### EQ-REL-SPLIT-001 — Relative variance of ideal splitting with equal levels

`P(G<=0)=prod_{m=1}^M P_m`, `P_m=P(G<=b_m | G<=b_{m-1})`; with
`P_m=p^{1/M}` and `N/M` independent ideal draws per level,
`delta_0^2=(p^{-1/M}-1)M/N` and `delta^2=(delta_0^2+1)^M-1`.

- Domain: `0 < p < 1`, integer `M >= 1`, total budget `N >= M`; exact
  (independent) conditional sampling at every level.
- Meaning: each level is a binomial estimate with squared c.o.v.
  `delta_0^2`; the independent unbiased level estimates multiply, so the
  relative variances compound. `M = 1` is crude Monte Carlo,
  `delta^2=(1-p)/(pN)`. Markov-chain sampling inflates the real variance.
- Code: `reliability.splitting_coefficient_of_variation`,
  `reliability.optimal_splitting`.
- Source: [REF-LAGNOUX-2006], [REF-AU-BECK-2001].

### EQ-REL-SPLIT-002 — Optimal number of splitting levels

For large `N`, `delta^2 ~ M^2(p^{-1/M}-1)/N = (ln p)^2 (e^x-1)/(x^2 N)` with
`x=-ln(p)/M`; the minimum is at the root `x*=1.5936` of `x e^x=2(e^x-1)`,
so `M* ~ -ln(p)/x* = -0.6275 ln p`, `P_m=exp(-x*)=0.2032` and
`delta^2 ~ (ln p)^2 e^{x*}/(2 x* N) = 1.544 (ln p)^2/N`.

- Domain: the model of [EQ-REL-SPLIT-001] with `M` treated as continuous and
  terms of order `1/N` dropped.
- Meaning: the optimal conditional probability per level does not depend on
  `p` or `N`; in practice `p` is unknown, so the thresholds cannot be set in
  advance and adaptive levels (subset simulation with `p_0 = 0.1` or
  `0.2`, moving particles) approximate the optimum.
- Code: `reliability.optimal_splitting`, `reliability.OPTIMAL_LEVEL_EXPONENT`.
- Source: [REF-LAGNOUX-2006].

### EQ-REL-MP-001 — Moving-particles (last-particle) estimator

With `N` particles and `M` moves until every particle satisfies `G<=0`,
`p_hat=(1-1/N)^M`. Under exact conditional sampling `M ~ Poisson(-N ln p)`,
so `E[p_hat]=p`, `Var(p_hat)=p^2(p^{-1/N}-1)` and
`c.o.v. = sqrt(p^{-1/N}-1) ~ sqrt(-ln(p)/N)`.

- Domain: `N >= 2`, a continuous distribution of `G(U)` (no atoms), and
  exact sampling from the standard normal law restricted to `G < L` at each
  level `L`.
- Meaning: the levels `-ln P(G<=L_k)` form a Poisson process of intensity
  `N`; the scheme is the limit of ideal splitting in which each level
  discards a single particle, at an expected cost of `N(1 - Q ln p)`
  evaluations with `Q` Markov steps per move.
- Code: `reliability.moving_particles`,
  `reliability.moving_particles_coefficient_of_variation`.
- Source: [REF-GUYADER-HENGARTNER-MATZNER-LOBER-2011], [REF-WALTER-2015].

### EQ-REL-MP-002 — Exact Poisson interval of the moving-particles estimate

With `alpha=1-confidence`, `lambda_lo=chi2_{alpha/2}(2M)/2` (`0` when
`M=0`) and `lambda_hi=chi2_{1-alpha/2}(2M+2)/2` (Garwood interval of
[EQ-INF-COUNT-003] for one count), the interval for `p` is
`[exp(-lambda_hi/N), exp(-lambda_lo/N)]`.

- Domain: the assumptions of [EQ-REL-MP-001]; `0 < confidence < 1`.
- Meaning: `p=exp(-lambda/N)` is decreasing in `lambda`, so the upper
  Poisson limit gives the lower probability limit; coverage is at least the
  nominal level under ideal sampling.
- Code: `reliability.moving_particles_interval`,
  `reliability.moving_particles`.
- Source: [REF-GUYADER-HENGARTNER-MATZNER-LOBER-2011], [REF-GARWOOD-1936].

### EQ-REL-PCN-001 — Conditional preconditioned Crank-Nicolson move

`v = rho u + sqrt(1-rho^2) z`, `z ~ N(0, I)`; the new state is `v` if
`G(v) < L` and `u` otherwise.

- Domain: `0 <= rho < 1`, current state `u` with `G(u) < L` (or on the
  level after a tie).
- Meaning: the proposal is reversible with respect to the standard normal
  law, so accepting exactly the proposals inside `{G < L}` leaves the
  standard normal law restricted to that set invariant; the Gaussian
  density ratio cancels, so no per-coordinate accept step is needed, and
  `rho` trades step length against acceptance.
- Code: `reliability.moving_particles`.
- Source: [REF-COTTER-ROBERTS-STUART-WHITE-2013], [REF-WALTER-2015].

### EQ-REL-DIR-002 — Directional simulation with several roots per ray

`P_f=E_A[sum_k (Q(d/2, r_{k,in}^2/2) - Q(d/2, r_{k,out}^2/2))]`, where
`[r_{k,in}, r_{k,out}]` are the failure segments of
`F_A={r>=0 : G(rA)<=0}`, `r_{1,in}=0` when the origin fails, and
`r_{k,out}=inf` when the ray still fails at the scan radius. The antithetic
variant averages the directions `A` and `-A`.

- Domain: independent standard-normal space, `U=RA` with
  `R^2 ~ chi-square_d` independent of the uniform direction `A`; boundary
  crossings at least one radial grid step apart.
- Meaning: integrates the radial chi law exactly over every failure segment
  of the ray, so non-star-shaped failure sets (several roots per direction,
  failing origin) are handled; only the direction is sampled, and a
  spherical limit state has zero variance.
- Code: `reliability.directional_simulation`,
  `reliability.default_radius_max`.
- Source: [REF-BJERAGER-1988], [REF-DITLEVSEN-MADSEN-1996].

### EQ-PROP-WILKS-001 — Wilks one-sided order-statistic bound of a quantile

`P(Y_(k) >= q_a) = P(Binomial(n, a) <= k - 1) = sum_(j=0)^(k-1) C(n, j) a^j (1 - a)^(n - j)`;
the upper Wilks rank is the smallest `k` with this probability at least
`beta`. Lower bound: `P(Y_(k) <= q_a) = P(Binomial(n, a) >= k)`, largest `k`
with this probability at least `beta`.

- Domain: `n` independent draws of one law, `0 < a < 1`, `0 < beta < 1`;
  exact for a continuous law, conservative (confidence at least `beta`) for
  a law with atoms; undefined (error) when even `Y_(n)` (or `Y_(1)`) falls
  short.
- Meaning: the number of draws below `q_a` is `Binomial(n, a)` whatever the
  law, so a fixed order statistic bounds the quantile with a known,
  law-free confidence; the whole risk `1 - beta` sits on one side, unlike
  the equal-tailed interval of EQ-PROP-QCI-001. With `n = 1000` and
  `a = beta = 0.95` the upper rank is `k = 962`.
- Code: `propagation.wilks_rank`, `propagation.wilks_bound`,
  `propagation.wilks._upper_confidence`,
  `propagation.wilks._lower_confidence`.
- Source: [REF-WILKS-1941], [REF-DAVID-NAGARAJA-2003, Section 7.1].

### EQ-PROP-WILKS-002 — Wilks sample size for an order-m quantile bound

Upper bound by the `m`-th largest value: smallest `n` with
`P(Binomial(n, a) <= n - m) >= beta`; for `m = 1`,
`n = ceil(ln(1 - beta) / ln a)`. Lower bound by the `m`-th smallest value:
smallest `n` with `P(Binomial(n, a) >= m) >= beta`.

- Domain: `0 < a < 1`, `0 < beta < 1`, integer `m >= 1`; independent draws
  of a continuous law.
- Meaning: the number of code runs needed before the `m`-th extreme value is
  a `beta`-confidence bound of the `a`-quantile; `a = beta = 0.95` gives 59,
  93, 124, and 153 runs for `m = 1..4`, and the median needs 5 runs at
  `beta = 0.95`. The upper case equals the success-run sample size with
  `m - 1` allowed failures (EQ-REL-DATA-004).
- Code: `propagation.wilks_sample_size`.
- Source: [REF-WILKS-1941], [REF-NUTT-WALLIS-2004].

### EQ-PROP-WILKS-003 — Two-sided distribution-free tolerance interval

The content `C = F(Y_(n-m+1)) - F(Y_(m))` of `[Y_(m), Y_(n-m+1)]` follows
`Beta(n - 2m + 1, 2m)`, so
`P(C >= gamma) = 1 - I_gamma(n - 2m + 1, 2m) = P(Binomial(n, gamma) <= n - 2m)`.

- Domain: `n` independent draws of a continuous law `F`, `0 < gamma < 1`,
  `0 < beta < 1`, `1 <= m <= n/2`.
- Meaning: the interval between the `m`-th smallest and `m`-th largest
  values contains at least a fraction `gamma` of the law with the stated
  probability; a two-sided order `m` costs as many runs as a one-sided order
  `2m` (93 runs for `gamma = beta = 0.95`, `m = 1`).
- Code: `propagation.wilks_tolerance_interval`,
  `propagation.wilks_sample_size`.
- Source: [REF-WILKS-1942], [REF-DAVID-NAGARAJA-2003, Section 7.2].

### EQ-REL-CERT-001 — Monte Carlo certification rule and normal margin

Certify when `p_hat_n + c(n, alpha, beta) <= alpha` with
`p_hat_n = (1/n) sum_i 1{y(x_i) > S}` and
`c(n, alpha, beta) = z_(1-beta) sqrt(alpha (1 - alpha) / n)`;
`max_(p_f >= alpha) P(certify) -> beta` as `n -> infinity`.

- Domain: `n` independent model runs, acceptable risk `0 < alpha < 1`,
  false-certification probability `0 < beta < 1`, `z_(1-beta)` the
  standard-normal quantile.
- Meaning: the margin turns the estimate into a decision whose probability
  of accepting a system with `p_f >= alpha` is asymptotically `beta`; for
  small `n alpha` it is only approximate.
- Code: `reliability.certification_margin`,
  `reliability.certification_probability`,
  `reliability.certification._certifies`,
  `reliability.certification._max_failures`.
- Source: [REF-ROSS-2019, Section 8.3].

### EQ-REL-CERT-002 — Exact certification probability under a binomial count

With `X ~ Binomial(n, p_f)` failures and `k_n` the largest certifying count,
`P(certify) = P(X <= k_n) = I_(1-p_f)(n - k_n, k_n + 1)`. Normal rule:
`k_n = max{k <= n : k/n + c(n, alpha, beta) <= alpha}`. Clopper-Pearson
rule: `k_n = max{k : P(Binomial(n, alpha) <= k) <= beta}`, which gives
`P(certify) <= beta` for every `p_f >= alpha` and every `n`.

- Domain: integer `n >= 1`, `0 <= p_f <= 1`, `0 < alpha, beta < 1`;
  `k_n = -1` (probability zero) when no count certifies.
- Meaning: the decision depends on the failure count only through a
  threshold, so its probability is a binomial distribution function,
  evaluated through the regularized incomplete beta function for `n` up to
  `1e10`; `P(certify)` is not monotone in `n` because `k_n` is an integer.
- Code: `reliability.certification_probability`,
  `reliability.certification_sample_size`,
  `reliability.certification._certifies`,
  `reliability.certification._max_failures`.
- Source: [REF-CLOPPER-PEARSON-1934], [REF-NIST-DLMF-BETA, Section 8.17].

### EQ-REL-CERT-003 — Moving-particles certification under a Poisson count

`M ~ Poisson(-N ln p_f)`, `p_hat = (1 - 1/N)^M`; certify when the
`1 - beta` upper bound `exp(-lambda_L(M)/N)` is at most `alpha`, i.e.
`M >= m* = min{m : P(Poisson(-N ln alpha) >= m) <= beta}`, so
`P(certify) = P(Poisson(-N ln p_f) >= m*)`; expected model calls
`N (1 - Q ln p_f)` with `Q` calls per move.

- Domain: `N >= 1` particles of an idealized moving-particles run with
  exact conditional sampling, `0 <= p_f <= 1`, `0 < alpha, beta < 1`,
  integer `Q >= 1`.
- Meaning: the move count of the particle method is Poisson with mean
  growing like `-ln p_f` instead of `1/p_f`, so far fewer model calls give
  the same certification probability as crude Monte Carlo for small `p_f`;
  the false-certification probability stays at most `beta` for
  `p_f >= alpha`.
- Code: `reliability.moving_particles_certification_probability`.
- Source: [REF-GUYADER-HENGARTNER-MATZNER-LOBER-2011], [REF-WALTER-2015].

### EQ-SENS-EST-001 — Saltelli (2002) product estimator of Sobol indices

With `y_A=f(A)`, `y_B=f(B)`, `y_i=f(A_B^(i))` (`A` with column `i` from
`B`), `N` rows and `V_A` the sample variance of `y_A`:
`S_i=[sum_k y_B,k y_i,k/(N-1) - (1/N) sum_k y_A,k y_B,k]/V_A` and
`S_Ti=1-[sum_k y_A,k y_i,k/(N-1) - mean(y_A)^2]/V_A`.

- Domain: [EQ-SENS-ANOVA-001]; rows of `A` and `B` independent draws of the
  input law; `V_A > 0`.
- Meaning: the squared output mean is estimated by the cross product of the
  two independent samples. Differences of large products make the estimator
  inaccurate when the output mean is large compared with its spread.
- Code: `sensitivity.estimate_sobol_indices`, `sensitivity.sobol_analysis`
  (`estimator="saltelli2002"`).
- Source: [REF-SALTELLI-2002], formulas as in `sobol2002` of
  [REF-R-SENSITIVITY].

### EQ-SENS-EST-002 — Sobol et al. (2007) estimator of Sobol indices

`S_i=sum_k y_B,k (y_i,k - y_A,k)/((N-1) V_A)` and
`S_Ti=sum_k y_A,k (y_A,k - y_i,k)/((N-1) V_A)`, notation of
[EQ-SENS-EST-001].

- Domain: as [EQ-SENS-EST-001].
- Meaning: products of an output with a difference of outputs, so the
  output mean cancels in expectation but not in the sampling error; the
  total index estimates the approximation error of fixing `x_i`.
- Code: `sensitivity.estimate_sobol_indices`, `sensitivity.sobol_analysis`
  (`estimator="sobol2007"`).
- Source: [REF-SOBOL-ETAL-2007], formulas as in `sobol2007` of
  [REF-R-SENSITIVITY].

### EQ-SENS-EST-003 — Jansen estimators of first-order and total indices

`S_i=1-sum_k (y_B,k - y_i,k)^2/((2N-1) V_A)` and
`S_Ti=sum_k (y_A,k - y_i,k)^2/((2N-1) V_A)`, notation of
[EQ-SENS-EST-001].

- Domain: as [EQ-SENS-EST-001].
- Meaning: half the mean squared difference of two outputs that share `x_i`
  (respectively all inputs but `x_i`) estimates the variance left
  unexplained; squared differences make both estimators insensitive to the
  output mean. The `2N - 1` divisor follows the R function `soboljansen`.
- Code: `sensitivity.estimate_sobol_indices`, `sensitivity.sobol_analysis`
  (`estimator="jansen"`).
- Source: [REF-JANSEN-1999], [REF-BAUDIN-ETAL-2016], [REF-R-SENSITIVITY].

### EQ-SENS-EST-004 — Martinez correlation estimator of Sobol indices

`S_i=rho(y_B, y_i)` and `S_Ti=1-rho(y_A, y_i)` with `rho` the sample
Pearson correlation computed from centred products.

- Domain: as [EQ-SENS-EST-001]; non-constant outputs.
- Meaning: for independent inputs `Cov(Y, Y')=Var(E[Y|X_u])` when `Y` and
  `Y'` share only `X_u`, and both have variance `Var(Y)`, so the index is a
  correlation. The centred, well-conditioned formula is robust to a large
  output mean and to small indices.
- Code: `sensitivity.estimate_sobol_indices`, `sensitivity.sobol_analysis`
  (`estimator="martinez"`).
- Source: [REF-BAUDIN-ETAL-2016], formulas as in `sobolmartinez` of
  [REF-R-SENSITIVITY].

### EQ-SENS-EST-005 — Fisher-z interval for the Martinez estimator

`S_i in [tanh(atanh(S_i_hat) - z/sqrt(N-3)), tanh(atanh(S_i_hat) + z/sqrt(N-3))]`
and `S_Ti in [1 - tanh(atanh(1 - S_Ti_hat) + z/sqrt(N-3)),
1 - tanh(atanh(1 - S_Ti_hat) - z/sqrt(N-3))]` with `z` the standard normal
`(1+c)/2` quantile.

- Domain: [EQ-SENS-EST-004] with `N >= 4` independent rows; the coverage is
  exact asymptotically for a bivariate normal pair and approximate
  otherwise.
- Meaning: Fisher's transform makes a sample correlation approximately
  normal with variance `1/(N-3)`, giving intervals with no resampling.
- Code: `sensitivity.sobol_analysis` (`estimator="martinez"`,
  `asymptotic=True`).
- Source: [REF-FISHER-1921], [REF-BAUDIN-ETAL-2016].

### EQ-SENS-EST-006 — Janon et al. estimator of a closed Sobol index

For outputs `y, y'` that share the inputs `X_u`, with
`c=(1/N) sum_k (y_k + y'_k)/2`:
`T_N=[(1/N) sum_k y_k y'_k - c^2]/[(1/N) sum_k (y_k^2 + y'_k^2)/2 - c^2]`;
`S_i=T_N(y_B, y_i)` and `S_Ti=1-T_N(y_A, y_i)`.

- Domain: as [EQ-SENS-EST-001]; non-constant pooled pair.
- Meaning: both outputs of the pair estimate the mean and the variance, so
  the first-order estimator has the smallest asymptotic variance among
  regular estimators built from the pair. The code centres both outputs on
  `c` first, which is algebraically identical and numerically stable.
- Code: `sensitivity.estimate_sobol_indices`, `sensitivity.sobol_analysis`
  (`estimator="janon"`).
- Source: [REF-JANON-ETAL-2014], [REF-R-SENSITIVITY].

### EQ-SENS-EST-007 — Asymptotic interval of the Janon estimator

`sqrt(N)(T_N - S_u) -> Normal(0, Var(U)/Var(Y)^2)` with
`U=(Y - E Y)(Y' - E Y) - (S_u/2)((Y - E Y)^2 + (Y' - E Y)^2)`; the code
plugs in the pair mean, the pooled pair variance, and `T_N`, and reports
`T_N -+ z sd(U)/(sqrt(N) s^2)`.

- Domain: [EQ-SENS-EST-006] with independent rows and finite fourth
  moments of `Y`.
- Meaning: a normal-theory interval at no extra model cost; the total-index
  bounds are `1 -` the reversed closed-index bounds.
- Code: `sensitivity.sobol_analysis` (`estimator="janon"`,
  `asymptotic=True`).
- Source: [REF-JANON-ETAL-2014].

### EQ-SENS-TAYLOR-001 — Quadratic-sum (first-order Taylor) importance factors

`g(X) ~= g(x0) + sum_i dg/dx_i(x0)(X_i - x0_i)` gives
`V_T=sum_i (dg/dx_i(x0))^2 sigma_i^2` and
`eta_i^2=(dg/dx_i(x0))^2 sigma_i^2/V_T`.

- Domain: mutually independent inputs with standard deviations `sigma_i`,
  a differentiable model at `x0`, and `V_T > 0`; with dependent inputs the
  full sandwich `J Sigma J'` of [EQ-MVN-DELTA-001] is needed instead.
- Meaning: local importance measure that sums to one; it equals the Sobol
  first-order index for a linear model and can be badly wrong for a model
  that is not close to linear over the range of the inputs. Central
  differences use `h_i = c |x0_i|` (`c` where `x0_i = 0`) and `2d` runs.
- Code: `sensitivity.taylor_importance_factors`,
  `sensitivity.quadratic_sum_importance`.
- Source: [REF-SALTELLI-2008, Chapter 1], [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002, Section
  5.5.4].

## Sampling-based sensitivity: regression coefficients and HSIC

### EQ-SENS-SRC-001 — Standardized regression coefficients and R squared

`y_k = b_0 + sum_i b_i x_ki + e_k` fitted by least squares;
`SRC_i = b_i s_i / s_y` with sample standard deviations `s_i`, `s_y`;
`R^2 = 1 - RSS / TSS`;
`sum_i SRC_i^2 = R^2 - 2 sum_{i<j} SRC_i SRC_j r_ij`, `r_ij` the sample
correlation of inputs `i` and `j`.

- Domain: `n >= d + 3` i.i.d. rows, no constant or linearly dependent input
  column, non-constant output.
- Meaning: for a linear model with independent inputs,
  `SRC_i^2 = b_i^2 Var(X_i) / Var(Y)` is the share of output variance due
  to `X_i` and `sum_i SRC_i^2 = R^2 = 1`; a small `R^2` means the indices
  describe only the linear part of the response, and correlated inputs make
  the squared coefficients share variance.
- Code: `sensitivity.regression_sensitivity`,
  `sensitivity.model_regression_sensitivity`.
- Source: [REF-SALTELLI-2008, Chapter 1] and [REF-HELTON-ETAL-2006].

### EQ-SENS-PCC-001 — Partial correlation coefficient from the t statistic

`PCC_i = corr(y - y_hat_(-i), x_i - x_hat_i(-i)) = t_i / sqrt(t_i^2 + n - d - 1)`,
where `y_hat_(-i)` and `x_hat_i(-i)` are the least-squares fits on the other
`d - 1` inputs and `t_i = b_i / se(b_i)` is the OLS t statistic of the full
fit.

- Domain: as [EQ-SENS-SRC-001]; `PCC_i` is in `[-1, 1]`.
- Meaning: strength of the linear relation between `x_i` and `y` once the
  linear effect of every other input is removed from both; it ranks inputs
  but does not apportion variance.
- Code: `sensitivity.regression_sensitivity`.
- Source: [REF-HELTON-ETAL-2006] and [REF-MONTGOMERY-PECK-VINING-2021,
  Chapter 3].

### EQ-SENS-RANK-001 — Rank-transformed coefficients SRRC and PRCC

Replace every input column and the output by their mid-ranks
([EQ-STAT-RANK-001]) and apply [EQ-SENS-SRC-001] and [EQ-SENS-PCC-001]:
`SRRC_i`, `PRCC_i`, and the rank `R^2`.

- Domain: as [EQ-SENS-SRC-001]; ties receive average ranks.
- Meaning: measures of monotone association; a rank `R^2` well above the
  raw `R^2` signals a monotone but nonlinear response. The Student
  p-values of the rank fit are nominal.
- Code: `sensitivity.regression_sensitivity` (`rank=True`).
- Source: [REF-IMAN-CONOVER-1979] and [REF-HELTON-ETAL-2006].

### EQ-SENS-HSIC-001 — Biased HSIC estimator and the normalized index

`K_ab = exp(-(x_a - x_b)^2 / (2 h_x^2))`, `L_ab = exp(-(y_a - y_b)^2 / (2 h_y^2))`,
`H = I - 11'/n`; `HSIC_b(X, Y) = tr(K H L H) / n^2`;
`R2_HSIC = HSIC(X, Y) / sqrt(HSIC(X, X) HSIC(Y, Y))`.

- Domain: `n >= 6` i.i.d. pairs, bandwidths `h > 0` (default the sample
  standard deviation; alternatively the median pairwise distance).
- Meaning: squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm of the cross-covariance operator;
  with the characteristic Gaussian kernel it vanishes if and only if `X`
  and `Y` are independent. `R2_HSIC` lies in `[0, 1]` for the biased
  estimator and compares inputs on one scale.
- Code: `sensitivity.hsic_indices`, `sensitivity.model_hsic_indices`.
- Source: [REF-GRETTON-ETAL-2005] and [REF-DA-VEIGA-2015].

### EQ-SENS-HSIC-002 — Unbiased HSIC estimator

With `K~` and `L~` the Gram matrices whose diagonals are set to zero,
`HSIC_u = [tr(K~ L~) + (1'K~1)(1'L~1) / ((n - 1)(n - 2))
- 2 / (n - 2) 1'K~L~1] / (n (n - 3))`.

- Domain: `n >= 6` i.i.d. pairs.
- Meaning: the U-statistic of HSIC; unbiased for every `n` and centred at
  zero under independence, so small negative values occur for
  unimportant inputs.
- Code: `sensitivity.hsic_indices` (`estimator="unbiased"`).
- Source: [REF-SONG-ETAL-2012].

### EQ-SENS-HSIC-003 — Gamma approximation to the null law of n HSIC_b

`n HSIC_b ~ Gamma(shape = m^2 / v, scale = n v / m)` under independence,
with `m = (1 + mu_x mu_y - mu_x - mu_y) / n`,
`mu_x = sum_{a != b} K_ab / (n (n - 1))` (likewise `mu_y`), and
`v = 2 (n - 4)(n - 5) / (n (n - 1)(n - 2)(n - 3))
sum_{a != b} (Kc_ab Lc_ab)^2 / (n (n - 1))` with the centred Gram
matrices `Kc = HKH` and `Lc = HLH`; the p-value is the upper-tail Gamma
probability of the observed `n HSIC_b`.

- Domain: `n >= 6` i.i.d. pairs, kernels with unit diagonal (Gaussian).
- Meaning: a two-moment fit to the null distribution that needs no
  resampling; it is asymptotic and slightly anti-conservative or
  conservative at small `n`.
- Code: `sensitivity.hsic_indices` (`test="gamma"`).
- Source: [REF-GRETTON-ETAL-2008].

### EQ-SENS-HSIC-004 — Permutation p-value of an HSIC statistic

`p = (1 + #{b : T(X, Y_pi_b) >= T(X, Y)}) / (B + 1)` for `B` random
permutations `pi_b` of the output rows, `T` the chosen HSIC estimator.

- Domain: exchangeable (i.i.d.) rows under `H0: X independent of Y`.
- Meaning: an exact-level Monte Carlo test; the `+1` terms keep it valid
  and the p-value positive, so its smallest value is `1 / (B + 1)`.
- Code: `sensitivity.hsic_indices` (`test="permutation"`).
- Source: [REF-GRETTON-ETAL-2008] and [REF-PHIPSON-SMYTH-2010].

### EQ-SENS-HSIC-005 — Target transform for goal-oriented sensitivity

`HSIC(X_i, w(Y))` with `w(y) = 1{y > c}` for a threshold `c`, or a
user-supplied weight function `w`.

- Domain: `w(Y)` not constant on the sample (at least one exceedance and
  one non-exceedance for the indicator).
- Meaning: dependence of each input with the occurrence of the critical
  event `Y > c`, rather than with the whole output distribution.
- Code: `sensitivity.hsic_indices` (`target=`).
- Source: [REF-MARREL-CHABRIDON-2021].

### EQ-REL-SUBSET-004 — Conditional-sampling step for subset simulation

`v_i = rho_i u_i + sigma_i z_i` with `z_i ~ N(0, 1)` and
`rho_i = sqrt(1 - sigma_i^2)`; the state moves to `v` if `G(v) <= b_j` and
repeats otherwise. Plain conditional sampling uses one fixed `rho` for every
coordinate (default `0.8`).

- Domain: independent standard-normal coordinates, `0 <= rho_i < 1`
  (`0 < sigma_i <= 1`), current state in `F_j = {G <= b_j}`.
- Meaning: the proposal is reversible with respect to the standard normal
  law, so no density ratio is needed and the stationary law is
  `phi_n(u) I(u in F_j) / P(F_j)`; unlike a random walk, the acceptance rate
  does not decay with the dimension.
- Code: `reliability.subset_simulation` (`sampler="cs"` and `"acs"`).
- Source: [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-BETZ-ZWIRGLMAIER-STRAUB-2015],
  [REF-COTTER-ROBERTS-STUART-WHITE-2013].

### EQ-REL-SUBSET-005 — Adaptive conditional sampling (aCS)

The `N_s = N p0` seeds are randomly permuted and each starts a chain of
`floor(N / N_s)` states (the remainder goes to the first chains).
`sigma_i = min(lambda sigma_0i, 1)`, `rho_i = sqrt(1 - sigma_i^2)`, with
`sigma_0i = 1` or the sample standard deviation of coordinate `i` over the
seeds. After every `N_a = ceil(100 N_s / N)` chains,
`a_hat = N_a^-1 sum min(1, a_c)` over their acceptance rates `a_c` and
`ln lambda <- ln lambda + (a_hat - a*) / sqrt(i + 1)`, `i = 0, 1, ...`
counting the updates of the level; `a* = 0.44`, `lambda = 0.6` at the first
conditional level and carried over to the next level.

- Domain: `lambda > 0`, `0 < a* < 1`, `N_a >= 1`.
- Meaning: a Robbins-Monro type adaptation of the conditional-sampling
  spread toward the acceptance rate that balances step length and
  rejections; a decreasing gain keeps the kernel nearly fixed late in a
  level.
- Code: `reliability.subset_simulation` (`sampler="acs"`).
- Source: [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-BETZ-ZWIRGLMAIER-STRAUB-2015].

### EQ-REL-SUBSET-006 — Level c.o.v. with chains of unequal length

`delta_j^2 = (1 - P_j) / (N P_j) (1 + gamma_j)`,
`gamma_j = 2 sum_{k >= 1} (n_k / N) rho_j(k)`, `n_k = sum_c max(0, L_c - k)`,
`R_j(k) = n_k^-1 sum_chains sum_l I_l I_{l+k} - P_j^2`,
`rho_j(k) = R_j(k) / (P_j (1 - P_j))`, for chains of lengths `L_c` summing
to `N`.

- Domain: `0 < P_j < 1`, `L_c >= 1`; with equal lengths `L_c = N_s`,
  `n_k / N = 1 - k / N_s` and the formula is [EQ-REL-SUBSET-003].
- Meaning: the variance of the mean of correlated indicators when chain
  lengths differ, counting each lag by its number of state pairs.
- Code: `reliability.subset_simulation` (`_level_cov`).
- Source: [REF-AU-BECK-2001] and
  [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-BETZ-ZWIRGLMAIER-STRAUB-2015].

### EQ-REL-HMCSS-001 — Rejection-sampling Hamiltonian step in standard space

With potential `U(u) = ||u||^2 / 2 - ln I(u in F_j)` and a unit mass
matrix, the Gaussian part of the Hamiltonian flow is exact:
`u(t) = p sin t + u_0 cos t`, `p ~ N(0, I)` drawn afresh for every step;
the end point `u(t_f)` is accepted if `G(u(t_f)) <= b_j` and the chain
repeats `u_0` otherwise.

- Domain: `0 < t_f <= pi/2`, current state in `F_j`; full momentum refresh
  (no partial refreshment).
- Meaning: the flow preserves the standard normal law, so rejecting end
  points outside `F_j` leaves the conditional law invariant without a
  gradient; the step equals conditional sampling with `rho = cos t_f`.
- Code: `reliability.subset_simulation` (`sampler="hmc"`).
- Source: [REF-WANG-BROCCARDO-SONG-2019] and [REF-NEAL-2011].

### EQ-REL-HMCSS-002 — Trajectory-time adaptation for RS-HMC

`t_f` starts at `pi/4`. After every `N_a` chains with mean acceptance `a`:
if `a < 0.3`, `t_f <- arcsin(sin t_f exp((a - 0.3)/2))`; if `a > 0.5`,
`t_f <- arcsin(min(1, sin t_f exp((a - 0.5)/2)))`; otherwise `t_f` is kept.

- Domain: `0 < t_f <= pi/2`, `N_a >= 1`; the adapted value is carried to
  the next level.
- Meaning: shortens the trajectory when too many end points leave `F_j` and
  lengthens it when nearly all stay inside, holding the acceptance rate in
  the band `[0.3, 0.5]`.
- Code: `reliability.subset_simulation` (`sampler="hmc"`).
- Source: [REF-WANG-BROCCARDO-SONG-2019].

### EQ-SUR-SPCE-001 — Least-angle regression step

On centred unit-norm columns `X` with correlations `c = X'(y - mu)`,
`C = max_j |c_j|`, active set `A` and signs `s_j = sign(c_j)`:
`G_A = X_A' X_A`, `A_A = (s' G_A^-1 s)^(-1/2)`,
`u_A = A_A X_A G_A^-1 s`, `a = X' u_A`, and `mu <- mu + gamma u_A` with
`gamma = min+_(j not in A) {(C - c_j)/(A_A - a_j), (C + c_j)/(A_A + a_j)}`,
or `gamma = C / A_A` (least squares on `A`) when no column may enter.

- Domain: `N >= 2` rows; columns constant on the rows, or numerically in
  the span of the active ones, never enter; at most `min(m, N - 1)` steps.
- Meaning: every active column keeps the same absolute correlation with
  the residual, which falls until an inactive column ties; the entry order
  ranks the regressors. Centring absorbs the intercept (the constant PCE
  term, which is always kept and not ranked).
- Code: `surrogates.least_angle_regression`,
  `surrogates.sparse_polynomial_chaos_from_samples`.
- Source: [REF-EFRON-HASTIE-JOHNSTONE-TIBSHIRANI-2004].

### EQ-SUR-SPCE-002 — Orthogonal matching pursuit selection

`j_(k+1) = argmax_(j not in A_k) |psi_j' r_k| / ||psi_j - mean(psi_j)||`,
`r_k = y - Psi_(A_k) c_(A_k)` the least-squares residual on the constant
and the `k` terms selected so far.

- Domain: as [EQ-SUR-SPCE-001]; the residual is recomputed by least squares
  after every addition.
- Meaning: greedy forward selection of the term most correlated with what
  the current fit misses; the nested sets are then scored by
  [EQ-SUR-SPCE-003] exactly as for LAR. It fits the training runs more
  aggressively than LAR, so its corrected LOO error is more optimistic.
- Code: `surrogates.sparse_polynomial_chaos_from_samples` (`method="omp"`).
- Source: [REF-BLATMAN-SUDRET-2011] for the LOO-based choice of the nested
  set; the selection rule is the standard orthogonal matching pursuit.

### EQ-SUR-SPCE-003 — Corrected leave-one-out error

`epsilon*_LOO = T(P, N) epsilon_LOO` with
`T(P, N) = N/(N-P) (1 + tr((Psi'Psi)^-1)) = N/(N-P) (1 + tr(C^-1)/N)`,
`C = Psi'Psi / N`, and `tr((Psi'Psi)^-1) = ||R^-1||_F^2` for `Psi = Q R`.

- Domain: `N > P`, full-rank `Psi`; `epsilon_LOO` from [EQ-SUR-PCE-006].
- Meaning: the plain LOO error is optimistic when `P` is not small next to
  `N`; for an orthonormal design `tr(C^-1) ~= P` and `T ~= (N+P)/(N-P)`.
- Code: `surrogates.PolynomialChaosExpansion.corrected_loo_error`,
  `surrogates.polynomial_chaos_from_samples`,
  `surrogates.SparseChaosSelection.loo_path`.
- Source: [REF-BLATMAN-SUDRET-2011] and [REF-CHAPELLE-VAPNIK-BENGIO-2002].

### EQ-SUR-SPCE-004 — Hybrid LAR selection over degrees and q-norms

`(p*, q*, k*) = argmin epsilon*_LOO(A_k(p, q))` over the requested degrees
`p`, norms `q`, and steps `k`, where `A_k(p, q)` is the constant plus the
first `k` terms ranked by [EQ-SUR-SPCE-001] (or [EQ-SUR-SPCE-002]) on the
truncation set `A_(p,q)` of [EQ-SUR-PCE-004], each refitted by
[EQ-SUR-PCE-005].

- Domain: `N >= 3`; `k <= N - 2`, so the set may be larger than the design.
- Meaning: LAR only ranks the terms; ordinary least squares on each nested
  set removes the LAR shrinkage, and the corrected LOO error chooses the
  sparsity, the degree, and the norm. Early stopping (a computational
  choice) cuts a path after `max(10, ceil(0.1 k_max))` steps without
  improvement and the degree loop after two degrees without improvement.
- Code: `surrogates.sparse_polynomial_chaos_from_samples`,
  `surrogates.fit_sparse_polynomial_chaos`,
  `surrogates.SparseChaosSelection`.
- Source: [REF-BLATMAN-SUDRET-2011].

## Active-learning reliability: learning functions, stopping, benchmarks

### EQ-REL-AL-EFF-001 — Expected feasibility function

With `G(x) ~ N(mu, sigma^2)`, `epsilon = 2 sigma`, `t = -mu / sigma`,
`t_-+ = (-+epsilon - mu) / sigma`:
`EFF = mu [2 Phi(t) - Phi(t_-) - Phi(t_+)] - sigma [2 phi(t) - phi(t_-) -
phi(t_+)] + epsilon [Phi(t_+) - Phi(t_-)]`, which equals
`E[(epsilon - |G|)_+]`; next point `argmax EFF`, stop when
`max EFF <= 0.001`.

- Domain: `sigma > 0` (`EFF = 0` for `sigma = 0`); in the units of `G`, so
  the threshold assumes `G` of order one.
- Meaning: expected amount by which the prediction falls inside the band
  `|G| <= 2 sigma` around the limit state.
- Code: `reliability.learning_value`, `reliability.select_learning_point`,
  `reliability.ak_mcs`.
- Source: [REF-BICHON-ETAL-2008].

### EQ-REL-AL-H-001 — Information-entropy learning function

With `D_+ = (2 sigma - mu) / sigma` and `D_- = (-2 sigma - mu) / sigma`:
`H = |(ln(sqrt(2 pi) sigma) + 1/2) [Phi(D_+) - Phi(D_-)] -
[(D_+ / 2) phi(D_+) - (D_- / 2) phi(D_-)]|`, the absolute value of
`-int_(-2 sigma)^(2 sigma) f ln f dg` for the predictive density `f` of
`G`; next point `argmax H`, stop when `max H <= 0.5`.

- Domain: `sigma > 0` (`H = 0` for `sigma = 0`); contains `ln sigma`, so it
  depends on the scale of `G`.
- Meaning: uncertainty (differential entropy) of the prediction restricted
  to the band around the limit state.
- Code: `reliability.learning_value`, `reliability.select_learning_point`,
  `reliability.ak_mcs`.
- Source: [REF-LV-LU-WANG-2015]; closed form and stopping value as restated
  in [REF-DU-XU-2023].

### EQ-REL-AL-BOUNDS-001 — Failure-probability bounds and bound stopping

`P_f^0 = #{mu_i <= 0} / N`, `P_f^- = #{mu_i + k sigma_i <= 0} / N`,
`P_f^+ = #{mu_i - k sigma_i <= 0} / N` with `k = 1.96`; stop learning when
`(P_f^+ - P_f^-) / P_f^0 <= tolerance` (default `0.1`).

- Domain: a candidate population with predictive means and variances; with
  `P_f^0 = 0` the rule holds only if `P_f^+ = 0`.
- Meaning: the estimate cannot move by more than the tolerance (relative)
  when every sign that is uncertain at level `k` is flipped.
- Code: `reliability.probability_bounds`, `reliability.bounds_satisfied`,
  `reliability.ak_mcs`.
- Source: [REF-SCHOBI-SUDRET-MARELLI-2017].

### EQ-MOD-OSC-001 — Non-linear oscillator limit state

`g = 3 r - |2 F_1 / (m omega_0^2) sin(omega_0 t_1 / 2)|`,
`omega_0 = sqrt((c_1 + c_2) / m)`.

- Domain: `m > 0`, `c_1 + c_2 > 0`; inputs `m ~ N(1, 0.05)`,
  `c_1 ~ N(1, 0.1)`, `c_2 ~ N(0.1, 0.01)`, `r ~ N(0.5, 0.05)`,
  `F_1 ~ N(1, 0.2)`, `t_1 ~ N(1, 0.2)`, independent.
- Meaning: peak displacement of an undamped oscillator under a rectangular
  pulse against three times the yield displacement; `P(g <= 0) ~ 2.86e-2`.
- Code: `modeling.oscillator`, `modeling.oscillator_model`.
- Source: [REF-GAYTON-BOURINET-LEMAIRE-2003],
  [REF-ECHARD-GAYTON-LEMAIRE-2011].

### EQ-MOD-RASTRIGIN-001 — Modified Rastrigin limit state

`g = 10 - sum_(i=1,2) (x_i^2 - 5 cos(2 pi x_i))`.

- Domain: two independent standard-normal inputs.
- Meaning: many small, scattered failure regions; `P(g <= 0) ~ 7.30e-2`.
- Code: `modeling.rastrigin`, `modeling.rastrigin_model`.
- Source: [REF-ECHARD-GAYTON-LEMAIRE-2011].

### EQ-SUR-GP-008 — Matern-3/2 ARD kernel

`k(x,x') = sigma_f^2 (1 + sqrt(3) r) exp(-sqrt(3) r)`,
`r^2 = sum_i ((x_i - x'_i)/ell_i)^2`; `dk/d log ell_i = 3 sigma_f^2
(Delta_i/ell_i)^2 exp(-sqrt(3) r)`.

- Domain: as [EQ-SUR-GP-001].
- Meaning: once mean-square differentiable prior, rougher than Matern 5/2;
  the derivative factor is finite at `r = 0`.
- Code: `surrogates.kernel_value`, `surrogates.fit_gaussian_process`
  (`kernel="matern32"`), `surrogates.fit_universal_kriging`.
- Source: [REF-RASMUSSEN-WILLIAMS-2006, Section 4.2].

### EQ-SUR-UK-001 — Universal kriging trend and process variance

`Y(x) = f(x)' beta + sigma^2 Z(x)` with `Z` a unit-variance stationary
process of correlation `R(x, x'; ell)`; for `N` runs, regression matrix
`F` (`N x P`) and correlation matrix `R` (diagonal `1 + nugget`):
`beta = (F'R^-1F)^-1 F'R^-1 Y`,
`sigma^2 = (1/N) (Y - F beta)' R^-1 (Y - F beta)`; computed with
`R = L L'`, `F~ = L^-1 F`, `Y~ = L^-1 Y` as the least-squares problem
`min ||Y~ - F~ beta||`.

- Domain: `N > P`; `R` positive definite; `F~` of full column rank (a
  whitened column whose squared sine to the earlier ones is below `1e-12`
  is refused).
- Meaning: generalized least squares for the trend and the maximum
  likelihood process variance for given length scales; a constant regressor
  gives ordinary kriging.
- Code: `surrogates.UniversalKriging`, `surrogates.fit_universal_kriging`.
- Source: [REF-SCHOBI-SUDRET-WIART-2015].

### EQ-SUR-UK-002 — Concentrated kriging likelihood and gradient

`psi(theta) = (1/2)(N log sigma^2(theta) + log det R(theta))`, minimized over
`theta = (log ell_1..d[, log nugget])`, which is minimizing
`sigma^2 det(R)^(1/N)`; `d psi / d theta_j = (1/2) tr(W dR/d theta_j)` with
`W = R^-1 - alpha alpha' / sigma^2`, `alpha = R^-1 (Y - F beta)`; the trend
coefficients do not contribute because they minimize the quadratic form.
The concentrated log-likelihood is
`-(N/2)(log(2 pi sigma^2) + 1) - (1/2) log det R`.

- Domain: `log ell_i in [log(0.01 E_i), log(20 E_i)]` with `E_i` the extent
  of input `i`; an estimated nugget in `[nugget, 1]` (computational choices).
- Meaning: maximum likelihood with `beta` and `sigma^2` profiled out; BFGS
  with the exact gradient and seeded multi-starts.
- Code: `surrogates.fit_universal_kriging`, `surrogates.UniversalKriging`.
- Source: [REF-SCHOBI-SUDRET-WIART-2015]; the trace form of the gradient as
  in [REF-RASMUSSEN-WILLIAMS-2006, Section 5.4].

### EQ-SUR-UK-003 — Universal kriging prediction

`mu(x) = f(x)' beta + r(x)' R^-1 (Y - F beta)`;
`s^2(x) = sigma^2 (1 - [f' r'] [[0, F'], [F, R]]^-1 [f; r])
= sigma^2 (1 - r'R^-1 r + u'(F'R^-1F)^-1 u)`, `u = F'R^-1 r - f`.

- Domain: as [EQ-SUR-UK-001]; `r(x)` the correlations with the training runs.
- Meaning: the best linear unbiased predictor; the last term is the variance
  added by estimating `beta`, which grows when `x` leaves the region where
  the trend is well determined.
- Code: `surrogates.UniversalKriging.predict_with_variance`,
  `surrogates.UniversalKriging.predict`, `surrogates.UniversalKriging.trend`,
  `surrogates.PCKriging.predict_with_variance`.
- Source: [REF-SCHOBI-SUDRET-WIART-2015].

### EQ-SUR-UK-004 — Closed-form kriging leave-one-out

`B = [[sigma^2 R, F], [F', 0]]^-1`; `mu_(-i) = Y_i - sum_j (B_ij / B_ii) Y_j`,
`s^2_(-i) = 1 / B_ii`; with `P = R^-1 - R^-1 F (F'R^-1F)^-1 F'R^-1` the
top-left block of `B` is `P / sigma^2` and `P Y = alpha`, so
`mu_(-i) = Y_i - alpha_i / P_ii` and `s^2_(-i) = sigma^2 / P_ii`;
`epsilon_LOO = (1/N) sum_i (Y_i - mu_(-i))^2 / Var(Y)`.

- Domain: fixed length scales and `sigma^2`; `beta` is re-estimated in every
  fold.
- Meaning: cross-validation without refitting; the error used to choose the
  trend of optimal PC-Kriging.
- Code: `surrogates.UniversalKriging.leave_one_out`,
  `surrogates.UniversalKriging.loo_error`, `surrogates.PCKriging.loo_error`.
- Source: [REF-SCHOBI-SUDRET-WIART-2015].

### EQ-SUR-PCK-001 — Sequential and optimal PC-Kriging

`M(x) ~= sum_(alpha in A) beta_alpha Psi_alpha(xi(x)) + sigma^2 Z(xi(x))`:
universal kriging [EQ-SUR-UK-001] with orthonormal polynomial regressors.
Sequential: `A` is the set chosen by hybrid LAR [EQ-SUR-SPCE-004]. Optimal:
with the LAR order `alpha_1, alpha_2, ...` of that set,
`A* = argmin_k epsilon_LOO({0, alpha_1, ..., alpha_k})` [EQ-SUR-UK-004].

- Domain: as [EQ-SUR-UK-001]; `xi(x)` the standardized PCE variables, used
  for the polynomials and the correlation alike.
- Meaning: the polynomials capture the global behaviour and the process the
  local residual. The full trend is fitted with all optimizer starts,
  exactly as the sequential model, so the optimal error is never larger;
  each smaller trend starts from the optimum of the previous size.
- Code: `surrogates.fit_pc_kriging`, `surrogates.pc_kriging_from_samples`,
  `surrogates.PCKriging`, `surrogates.ChaosTrend`.
- Source: [REF-SCHOBI-SUDRET-WIART-2015].

### EQ-SUR-DE-001 — Gaussian negative log-likelihood of a mean-variance network

`l(theta; x, y) = (log(2 pi sigma^2(x)) + (y - mu(x))^2 / sigma^2(x)) / 2`
with `(mu(x), s(x))` the two outputs of an MLP [EQ-NN-MLP-001] and
`sigma^2(x) = exp(clip(s(x), -20, 20)) + 1e-6` (standardized units); a
homoscedastic member replaces `s(x)` by one learned scalar. Each member
minimizes `L(theta) = mean_i l(theta; x_i, y_i) + (lambda / 2) sum w^2` over
the weights `w` by Adam [EQ-OPT-ADAM-002] on mini-batches.

- Domain: standardized inputs and outputs; `lambda >= 0`.
- Meaning: the negative log-likelihood is a proper scoring rule, so it is
  minimized by the true conditional mean and variance; the variance output
  absorbs the noise the network cannot explain. The clip and the floor keep
  `sigma^2` and its inverse finite (computational choices). The source
  passes the variance output through a softplus with a `1e-6` floor; the
  log-variance form is a parameterization choice with the same optimum.
- Code: `surrogates.fit_deep_ensemble`,
  `surrogates.DeepEnsemble.member_predictions`.
- Source: [REF-LAKSHMINARAYANAN-PRITZEL-BLUNDELL-2017, Section 2.2.1 and
  Algorithm 1]; [REF-GOODFELLOW-BENGIO-COURVILLE-2016, Section 7.1.1] for the
  weight penalty.

### EQ-SUR-DE-002 — Deep-ensemble mixture prediction and variance split

`mu*(x) = (1/M) sum_m mu_m(x)`,
`sigma*^2(x) = (1/M) sum_m (sigma_m^2(x) + mu_m^2(x)) - mu*^2(x)
= (1/M) sum_m sigma_m^2(x) + (1/M) sum_m (mu_m(x) - mu*(x))^2`.

- Domain: `M >= 1` members fitted by [EQ-SUR-DE-001]; all quantities in
  original units after undoing the output standardization.
- Meaning: the mean and variance of the uniform mixture of the member
  Gaussians. The first term (aleatoric) is the noise the members attribute
  to the data; the second (epistemic) is the disagreement between members,
  which is small where the data constrain the networks and grows away from
  them. Neither term is a guaranteed bound on the actual error.
- Code: `surrogates.DeepEnsemble.predict_decomposed`,
  `surrogates.DeepEnsemble.predict_with_variance`,
  `surrogates.DeepEnsemble.epistemic_variance`,
  `surrogates.DeepEnsemble.aleatoric_variance`.
- Source: [REF-LAKSHMINARAYANAN-PRITZEL-BLUNDELL-2017, Section 2.4].

## Ordinary differential equations and the parachuted-package laboratory (ADR-0109)

### EQ-NUM-ODE-001 — Explicit one-step methods

`y_{n+1} = y_n + h Phi(t_n, y_n; h)`, `t_n = t_0 + n h`, with
`k_1 = f(t_n, y_n)` and: explicit Euler `Phi = k_1`; Heun
`k_2 = f(t_n + h, y_n + h k_1)`, `Phi = (k_1 + k_2) / 2`; classical
Runge-Kutta `k_2 = f(t_n + h/2, y_n + h k_1 / 2)`,
`k_3 = f(t_n + h/2, y_n + h k_2 / 2)`, `k_4 = f(t_n + h, y_n + h k_3)`,
`Phi = (k_1 + 2 k_2 + 2 k_3 + k_4) / 6`.

- Domain: `f` sufficiently smooth (Lipschitz in `y`) on the solution path;
  fixed step `h > 0`; for a stiff `f` the step must also lie in the stability
  region of the method (`|1 + h lambda| <= 1` for Euler and each eigenvalue
  `lambda` of the Jacobian).
- Meaning: the global error at a fixed time is `O(h^p)` with `p = 1, 2, 4`.
  The grid times are computed as `t_0 + n h`, not by repeated addition.
- Code: `numerics.ode.integrate_to_event`.
- Source: [REF-HAIRER-NORSETT-WANNER-1993, Section II.1];
  [REF-HAIRER-WANNER-1996, Section IV.2] for the stability region.

### EQ-NUM-ODE-002 — Event location inside the last step

With `g(t_n, y_n) > 0 >= g(t_{n+1}, y_{n+1})`: first step
`t* = t_{n+1}`; linear `theta = g_n / (g_n - g_{n+1})`,
`y* = y_n + theta (y_{n+1} - y_n)`; cubic Hermite
`u(theta) = h00 y_n + h10 h f_n + h01 y_{n+1} + h11 h f_{n+1}` with
`h00 = 2 theta^3 - 3 theta^2 + 1`, `h10 = theta^3 - 2 theta^2 + theta`,
`h01 = -2 theta^3 + 3 theta^2`, `h11 = theta^3 - theta^2`, and `theta*` the
root of `g(t_n + theta h, u(theta)) = 0` on `[0, 1]` found by the Illinois
method; `t* = t_n + theta* h`, `y* = u(theta*)`.

- Domain: `g` continuous and positive at the start; the event is the first
  sign change on the grid (a pair of roots inside one step is missed).
- Meaning: the location error is `O(h)` for the first step, `O(h^2)` for
  linear interpolation, and `O(h^4)` for the cubic Hermite interpolant, so
  only the Hermite location keeps the order of every method of
  [EQ-NUM-ODE-001].
- Code: `numerics.ode.integrate_to_event`.
- Source: [REF-HAIRER-NORSETT-WANNER-1993, Section II.6] (dense output and
  event location); [REF-DOWELL-JARRATT-1971] (Illinois method).

### EQ-NUM-ODE-003 — Fixed-step trajectory over a fixed horizon

`t_n = t_0 + n h` and `y_(n+1) = y_n + h Phi(t_n, y_n; h)` for
`n = 0..N-1`, with the increment `Phi` of [EQ-NUM-ODE-001]; the trajectory
is `(t_n, y_n)` for `n = 0..N`.

- Domain: [EQ-NUM-ODE-001]; `N >= 0` steps. Only state entries that are
  plain real numbers are checked for finiteness, so the entries may be
  automatic-differentiation variables.
- Meaning: the discrete flow map `y_0 -> y_N` is a composition of
  arithmetic operations, so reverse-mode differentiation of a functional of
  `y_N` gives the exact gradient of the discrete map (the adjoint of the
  Runge-Kutta scheme), not an approximation of the continuous adjoint.
- Code: `numerics.integrate_fixed_step`, `numerics.FixedStepTrajectory`.
- Source: [REF-HAIRER-NORSETT-WANNER-1993, Section II.1];
  [REF-GRIEWANK-WALTHER-2008, Chapter 3] for differentiating through it.

### EQ-LAB-PARA-001 — Drag-free landing abscissa

`y = x_0 + s_p sqrt(2 z_a / g)`.

- Domain: no drag and no wind, release with horizontal speed `s_p` and zero
  vertical speed from height `z_a > 0`, constant gravity `g`.
- Meaning: the trajectory is a parabola, so Heun and RK4 integrate it
  exactly and the cubic Hermite interpolant locates the landing to
  rounding; explicit Euler errs at order 1.
- Code: `examples.parachute_vvuq_lab.drag_free_landing`.
- Source: [REF-HALLIDAY-RESNICK-WALKER-2014, projectile motion].

### EQ-LAB-PARA-002 — Linear-drag landing through the Lambert W function

With `m x'' = m g - k (x' - s_w)` and `tau = m / k`:
`X(t) = x_0 + s_w t + (s_p - s_w) tau (1 - e^(-t/tau))`,
`Z(t) = z_a - g tau t + g tau^2 (1 - e^(-t/tau))`; `Z(T) = 0` at
`T = tau (1 + c + W_0(-e^(-(1 + c))))` with `c = z_a / (g tau^2)`, and the
landing abscissa is `X(T)`. `W_0` is computed by Halley's iteration from
the branch-point series `-1 + p - p^2/3 + 11 p^3/72`,
`p = sqrt(2 (e x + 1))`.

- Domain: `m, k, z_a > 0`, constant wind `s_w`; the principal branch gives
  the positive root (the branch `W_{-1}` gives a root at negative time).
- Meaning: an exact solution with drag, used for code verification of the
  integrator: the observed orders against it must be 1, 2, and 4.
- Code: `examples.parachute_vvuq_lab.linear_drag_landing`,
  `examples.parachute_vvuq_lab.lambert_w0`.
- Source: [REF-CORLESS-ETAL-1996].

### EQ-LAB-PARA-003 — Power-law wind profile of the synthetic truth

`s_w(z) = s_w,10 (max(z, 1) / 10)^alpha`, `alpha = 0.1`.

- Domain: height `z` in metres; the reference wind is measured at 10 m;
  below 1 m the profile is frozen.
- Meaning: the synthetic truth of the laboratory has a stronger wind aloft
  than the 10 m wind the simulator uses, which creates a model-form error
  that grows with the wind. The exponent is a teaching choice.
- Code: `examples.parachute_vvuq_lab.power_law_wind`.
- Source: [REF-PETERSON-HENNESSEY-1978].

### EQ-LAB-PARA-004 — Euler stability limit of the drag transient

`dt <= m / (A |v_r|)`, `|v_r| = |s_p - s_w|` at release.

- Domain: quadratic drag `-(A/m) |v_r| v_r`, whose Jacobian
  `-(A/m) (|v_r| I + v_r v_r^T / |v_r|)` has eigenvalues `-(A/m)|v_r|` and
  `-2 (A/m)|v_r|`; the relative speed is largest at release.
- Meaning: explicit Euler is stable for `|1 + dt lambda| <= 1`, so the
  stiffest eigenvalue `-2 (A/m)|v_r|` bounds the step.
- Code: `examples.parachute_vvuq_lab.stability_limit`.
- Source: [REF-HAIRER-WANNER-1996, Section IV.2].

### EQ-LAB-PARA-005 — Verified error bound of a production step

`B(dt) = |y(dt) - y_ext| + U`, with the extrapolated value `y_ext` and the
expanded numerical uncertainty `U` of the finest grid from the solution
verification of the grids `dt, dt/2, dt/4` [EQ-VV-UNUM-001].

- Domain: three grids in the asymptotic range; outside it `B` can
  underestimate the error, which the laboratory checks against a reference.
- Meaning: an error bound for the coarse production step obtained from two
  extra runs, so that the step can be chosen against a tolerance.
- Code: `examples.parachute_vvuq_lab.step_bound`.
- Source: [REF-ROACHE-1998, Chapters 4-5]; [REF-ROY-OBERKAMPF-2011].

### EQ-LAB-PARA-006 — Terminal speed under quadratic drag

`v_t = sqrt(m g / A)`.

- Domain: drag `A |v_r| v_r` with `A > 0`, constant gravity, air velocity
  constant along the path.
- Meaning: the speed relative to the air at which drag balances weight;
  after the release transient the package falls at `v_t`.
- Code: `examples.parachute_vvuq_lab.terminal_speed`.
- Source: [REF-HALLIDAY-RESNICK-WALKER-2014, drag force and terminal speed].

### EQ-LAB-GPS-001 — Pseudorange likelihood with uniform satellite, range, and clock errors

For `D_k = beta + ||S_k - r|| + e_k` with `beta ~ Uniform(-b, b)` common to
all satellites, `S_k = C_k + o_k` with `o_k` uniform in a ball of radius
`a`, and `e_k ~ Uniform(-h, h)`, all independent:
`L(r) = (1 / 2b) int_{-b}^{b} prod_k f_z(D_k - beta - ||r - C_k||) dbeta`,
`f_z(z) = (G(z + h) - G(z - h)) / (2h)`,
`G(x) = 1/2 + 3x/(4a) - x^3/(4a^3)` on `[-a, a]` (0 below, 1 above).

- Domain: `h > a > 0`, `b > 0`; `||r - C_k||` much larger than `a`.
- Meaning: `G` is the CDF of the line-of-sight component of `o_k` (the
  projection of a uniform ball has density `3 (a^2 - x^2) / (4a^3)`), and
  `f_z` the density of that component plus the range error; the satellite
  offsets are integrated in closed form and the clock shift by quadrature.
  Replacing `||r - S_k||` by `||r - C_k||` plus the line-of-sight component
  errs by less than `a^2 / ||r - C_k||`. Each `f_z` is a cubic between its
  kinks `z = +-h +- a`, so the integrand is a polynomial of degree at most
  `3k` between kinks and Gauss-Legendre panels with `ceil((3k + 1) / 2)`
  nodes are exact. `L(r) > 0` only inside the polytope
  `|D_k - ||r - C_k||| < h + a + b`, which bounds the importance-sampling
  box.
- Code: `examples.gps_positioning_lab.offset_cdf`,
  `examples.gps_positioning_lab.residual_density`,
  `examples.gps_positioning_lab.marginal_likelihood`,
  `examples.gps_positioning_lab.support_vertices`.
- Source: [REF-SMITH-UQ-2024] for the posterior of the receiver position
  from five pseudoranges; [REF-GOLUB-WELSCH-1969] for the quadrature.

### EQ-LAB-GPS-002 — First-order covariance and dilution of precision of a pseudorange fix

Linearized model `delta D = G delta x + e` at the fix. Known clock: rows
`g_k = (r - C_k)' / ||r - C_k||`, `x = r`. Unknown clock: rows `(g_k, 1)`,
`x = (r, beta)`. Ordinary least squares: `A = (G'G)^-1 G'`,
`Cov(x_hat) = A Sigma A'`; weighted least squares with
`W = diag(sigma_k^-2)`: `Cov(x_hat) = (G'WG)^-1`. With `H = (G'G)^-1` for
the four-column `G` in East-North-Up coordinates:
`GDOP = sqrt(trace H)`, `PDOP = sqrt(H_EE + H_NN + H_UU)`,
`HDOP = sqrt(H_EE + H_NN)`, `VDOP = sqrt(H_UU)`, `TDOP = sqrt(H_bb)`.

- Domain: at least four satellites (three with a known clock) not all on
  one cone around the receiver, so `G'G` is invertible; `Sigma` the
  covariance of the reading errors.
- Meaning: with independent errors of common variance `sigma^2` the fix
  covariance is `sigma^2 H` and the DOPs scale `sigma` into position, clock,
  and combined standard errors. A clock error common to all readings adds
  `s_clock^2 (A 1)(A 1)'` to the known-clock covariance and is absorbed by
  the fourth unknown otherwise. Estimating the clock never lowers the
  position dilution. `(G'WG)^-1` is the smallest covariance of any linear
  unbiased fix (Gauss-Markov) and equals the Gauss-Newton covariance
  [EQ-OPT-LM-002] of the whitened residuals with unit noise variance.
- Code: `examples.gps_positioning_lab.error_map`,
  `examples.gps_positioning_lab.linearized_covariance`,
  `examples.gps_positioning_lab.pdop_known_clock`,
  `examples.gps_positioning_lab.dilution_of_precision`,
  `examples.gps_positioning_lab.clock_fix_covariance`,
  `examples.gps_positioning_lab.fault_position_shift`.
- Source: [REF-MISRA-ENGE-2006, Chapter 6];
  [REF-TEUNISSEN-MONTENBRUCK-2017, Chapters 21 and 22];
  [REF-SEBER-WILD-2003, Section 2.1].

### EQ-LAB-GPS-003 — Residual fault-detection test of a redundant pseudorange fix

`T = || W^(1/2) (D - D_hat) ||^2 = e' W^(1/2) S W^(1/2) e` with
`S = I - G~ (G~'G~)^-1 G~'`, `G~ = W^(1/2) G`; alarm when
`T > chi^2_(n-4, 1 - P_FA)`. A bias `b` on satellite `k` makes
`T ~ chi^2_(n-4)(lambda)` with `lambda = (b / sigma_k)^2 S_kk`; for
`n - 4 = 1`: `P_D(lambda) = Phi(sqrt(lambda) - sqrt(T_a)) +
Phi(-sqrt(lambda) - sqrt(T_a))`, `T_a` the threshold. The minimal
detectable bias solves `P_D(lambda) = P` for `b`.

- Domain: Gaussian, independent errors of known variances; `n > 4`
  satellites; at most one faulty satellite.
- Meaning: `S` projects onto the `n - 4` redundant directions; a fault on a
  satellite with small `S_kk` barely shows in the residuals and moves the
  fix by `b (G'WG)^-1 (g_k, 1)' / sigma_k^2` [EQ-LAB-GPS-002] before it is
  detected. With one redundant reading a fault can be detected but not
  attributed to a satellite.
- Code: `examples.gps_positioning_lab.residual_projector`,
  `examples.gps_positioning_lab.raim_threshold`,
  `examples.gps_positioning_lab.detection_probability`,
  `examples.gps_positioning_lab.fault_noncentrality`,
  `examples.gps_positioning_lab.minimal_detectable_bias`.
- Source: [REF-BROWN-1992].

## Quantile conventions, shape conventions, and further classical tests

### EQ-STAT-QUANT-002 — The nine Hyndman-Fan sample quantiles

Every type is `Q(p) = (1 - gamma) x_(j) + gamma x_(j+1)` with
`x_(0) = x_(1)` and `x_(n+1) = x_(n)`. Discontinuous types use
`j = floor(n p + m)`, `g = n p + m - j`: type 1 (`m = 0`, `gamma = 0` if
`g = 0`, else 1), type 2 (`m = 0`, `gamma = 1/2` if `g = 0`, else 1), type 3
(`m = -1/2`, `gamma = 0` if `g = 0` and `j` is even, else 1). Continuous types
interpolate between the plotting positions `p_k = (k - alpha)/(n + 1 -
alpha - beta)`: `h = alpha + p (n + 1 - alpha - beta)`, `j = floor(h)`,
`gamma = h - j`, with `(alpha, beta) = (0, 1)` (type 4), `(1/2, 1/2)` (5),
`(0, 0)` (6), `(1, 1)` (7), `(1/3, 1/3)` (8), and `(3/8, 3/8)` (9).

- Domain: non-empty finite sample and `p in [0,1]`; the position is formed
  in exact rational arithmetic and taken to be the integer `k` when `p` is
  the floating-point value of the level at which it equals `k`.
- Meaning: types 1-3 are step functions of `p` (inverse empirical CDF,
  averaged at the jumps, nearest even order statistic); types 4-9 are
  continuous. Types 2 and 5-9 give the usual median and satisfy
  `Q_x(p) = -Q_(-x)(1 - p)`; type 8 is approximately median-unbiased for any
  continuous law and type 9 approximately unbiased for normal data.
- Code: `statistics.quantile`, `statistics.quantiles`.
- Source: [REF-HYNDMAN-FAN-1996].

### EQ-STAT-SHAPE-002 — Bias-adjusted skewness and kurtosis (G1, G2, b1, b2)

With `g1 = m3 / m2^(3/2)` and `g2 = m4 / m2^2 - 3` [EQ-STAT-SHAPE-001]:
`G1 = g1 sqrt(n (n - 1)) / (n - 2)`,
`G2 = ((n + 1) g2 + 6)(n - 1) / ((n - 2)(n - 3))`,
`b1 = g1 ((n - 1)/n)^(3/2) = m3 / s^3`, and
`b2 = (g2 + 3)(1 - 1/n)^2 - 3 = m4 / s^4 - 3`, where `s^2` has divisor
`n - 1`.

- Domain: positive `m2`; `n >= 3` for `G1` and `n >= 4` for `G2`.
- Meaning: `G1 = k3 / k2^(3/2)` and `G2 = k4 / k2^2` are ratios of the
  unbiased cumulant estimators (k-statistics); `b1` and `b2` standardize by
  the sample standard deviation. The three conventions agree as `n` grows.
  Under normality every skewness has mean zero by symmetry, and of the
  kurtosis measures only `G2` is unbiased (`E[g2] = -6/(n + 1)`). e1071
  types 1, 2, and 3 are `g`, `G`, and `b`; SAS and SPSS report `G`, MINITAB
  and BMDP `b`.
- Code: `statistics.skewness`, `statistics.excess_kurtosis`.
- Source: [REF-JOANES-GILL-1998].

### EQ-INF-FISHER-RXC-001 — Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test for an r x c table

`P(x) = prod_i r_i! prod_j c_j! / (N! prod_ij x_ij!)` for a table `x` with
row totals `r_i`, column totals `c_j`, and total `N`; two-sided
`p = sum_{y : P(y) <= P(x)(1 + 1e-7)} P(y)` over the tables `y` with the
observed margins. Monte Carlo estimate
`p = (1 + #{b : P(y_b) <= P(x)(1 + 1e-7)}) / (B + 1)` over `B` tables drawn
from the same law.

- Domain: non-negative integer cells; rows and columns with a zero total are
  dropped, after which at least two rows and two columns remain.
- Meaning: the conditional (multiple hypergeometric) law of the table given
  both margins under independence; the p-value is the probability of a table
  no more probable than the observed one. The sum is computed exactly on the
  network of partial column sums: a node with remaining row totals `R_i`,
  column totals `c_k`, and total `n` carries the summed completion weight
  `sum prod 1/x! = n! / (prod R_i! prod c_k!)` and the largest and smallest
  completion weights, so whole sub-networks are added or discarded without
  listing their tables. For a 2 x 2 table it equals [EQ-INF-FISHER-001].
- Code: `inference.fisher_exact_rxc_test`.
- Source: [REF-FREEMAN-HALTON-1951]; [REF-MEHTA-PATEL-1983] for the network
  algorithm; [REF-PHIPSON-SMYTH-2010] for the Monte Carlo estimate.

### EQ-INF-FLIGNER-001 — Fligner-Killeen median-centred test of equal variances

With `d_ij = |x_ij - med_i|`, `r_ij` the mid-rank of `d_ij` among all `N`
deviations, scores `a_ij = Phi^-1((1 + r_ij / (N + 1)) / 2)`, mean score
`abar`, group mean scores `abar_i`, and `V = sum (a_ij - abar)^2 / (N - 1)`:
`X^2 = sum_i n_i (abar_i - abar)^2 / V`, referred to chi-square with `k - 1`
degrees of freedom.

- Domain: `k >= 2` non-empty groups, `N >= 2`, and `V > 0` (not every
  deviation equal).
- Meaning: a rank test of equal spread; centring on the group medians and
  scoring the ranks with normal quantiles keeps its level for skewed and
  heavy-tailed data. `X^2` is the between-group sum of squares of the scores
  divided by their total variance, so the chi-square law is an approximation
  for large groups.
- Code: `inference.fligner_killeen_test`.
- Source: [REF-FLIGNER-KILLEEN-1976]; [REF-CONOVER-JOHNSON-JOHNSON-1981] for
  the median-centred version with chi-square reference.

### EQ-INF-WELCH-ANOVA-001 — Welch's one-way ANOVA for unequal variances

With `w_i = n_i / s_i^2`, `W = sum w_i`, `xbar_w = sum w_i xbar_i / W`, and
`A = sum (1 - w_i / W)^2 / (n_i - 1)`:
`F = [sum w_i (xbar_i - xbar_w)^2 / (k - 1)] / [1 + 2 (k - 2) A / (k^2 - 1)]`,
referred to `F(k - 1, f)` with `f = (k^2 - 1) / (3 A)`.

- Domain: `k >= 2` groups, each with `n_i >= 2` and `s_i^2 > 0`.
- Meaning: tests equal normal means without assuming equal variances; the
  denominator degrees of freedom `f` are fractional. For `k = 2`, `F` is the
  square of the Welch `t` statistic and `f` its Welch-Satterthwaite degrees
  of freedom [EQ-INF-T-003].
- Code: `inference.welch_anova`.
- Source: [REF-WELCH-1951].

### EQ-REL-AKSS-001 — AK-SS: active learning on surrogate subset levels

Round `r`: subset simulation on the surrogate mean `mu_r(u)` with `N`
samples per level and level probability `p0` gives
`P_r = p0^(m-1) #{i : mu_r(u_i^(m)) <= 0} / N` over the `N` samples
`u_i^(m)` of the last level; the pool `C_r` is the set of distinct samples
of all levels. While `min_(u in C_r \ T) U(u) < 2` with
`U = |mu| / sigma`, the model is evaluated at the arg min, which joins the
training set `T`, and the posterior over `C_r` is updated; then round
`r + 1` starts. The iteration stops with `P_r` when the stop of
[EQ-REL-AKSS-002] holds or when `C_r` needs no addition, in both cases on a
GP fitted to all of `T`.

- Domain: GP surrogate of `G` in standard-normal space; every round uses the
  same random stream for the subset run (common random numbers).
- Meaning: the subset levels place the candidates on the path from the bulk
  of the input law to the failure domain, so a few thousand candidates per
  level stand for a failure probability far below `1 / (number of
  candidates)`. `P_r` estimates `P(mu_r <= 0)`; its subset c.o.v. excludes
  the misclassification by the surrogate.
- Code: `reliability.ak_ss`.
- Source: [REF-HUANG-CHEN-ZHU-2016] (subset simulation on the Kriging
  predictor, level samples as candidates); [REF-ECHARD-GAYTON-LEMAIRE-2011]
  (`U` and `min U >= 2`); [REF-AU-BECK-2001] (subset levels). The pool
  definition, the common random numbers, and the stopping logic are
  implementation choices of this library.

### EQ-REL-AKSS-002 — AK-SS stop on the last level's failure-count bounds

`P^- = p0^(m-1) #{i : mu(u_i^(m)) + 1.96 sigma(u_i^(m)) <= 0} / N`,
`P^+ = p0^(m-1) #{i : mu(u_i^(m)) - 1.96 sigma(u_i^(m)) <= 0} / N` over the
`N` samples of the last level (chain repetitions counted); stop when the run
reached the threshold `0`, `P_r > 0`, and `(P^+ - P^-) / P_r <= tolerance`
(default `0.05`).

- Domain: a subset run on the surrogate mean with predictive variances at
  its last-level samples.
- Meaning: flipping every last-level sign that is uncertain at level 1.96
  moves the estimate by at most the tolerance (relative), given the levels.
  The bounds are as overconfident as the surrogate's `sigma` and do not see
  failure regions that the subset run never sampled.
- Code: `reliability.ak_ss`.
- Source: the bound rule of [REF-SCHOBI-SUDRET-MARELLI-2017], applied here
  to the last subset level (an implementation choice of this library).

## Preconditioned Crank-Nicolson, tempered SMC, evidence, and ABC (ADR-0111)

### EQ-MCMC-PCN-001 — Preconditioned Crank-Nicolson proposal and acceptance

For the target `pi(u) proportional to L(u) N(u; 0, I)` with
`Phi(u) = -log L(u)`: propose `v = sqrt(1 - beta^2) u + beta xi`,
`xi ~ N(0, I)`, and accept with probability
`min(1, exp(Phi(u) - Phi(v)))`.

- Domain: `0 < beta <= 1`; the reference law must be exactly `N(0, I)` in
  the sampled coordinates; `L(u) >= 0` (zero likelihood is always rejected).
- Meaning: the AR(1) proposal is reversible with respect to `N(0, I)`, so
  the Gaussian factors cancel and only the likelihood enters the ratio. The
  acceptance rate for a fixed `beta` has a limit as the dimension of a
  discretized field grows, whereas a random walk needs a step of order
  `d^(-1/2)`; `beta = 1` is the independence sampler from the prior.
- Code: `inference.preconditioned_crank_nicolson`,
  `inference.sequential_monte_carlo(mutation="pcn")`,
  `inverse.CalibrationProblem.sample_posterior(method="pcn")`.
- Source: [REF-COTTER-ROBERTS-STUART-WHITE-2013];
  [REF-HAIRER-STUART-VOLLMER-2014] (dimension-independent spectral gap).

### EQ-MCMC-PCN-002 — Warm-up adaptation of the pCN step on its log-odds

`beta_k = 1 / (1 + exp(-eta_k))`,
`eta_k = eta_{k-1} + k^(-0.6) (alpha_k - alpha*)`, where
`alpha_k = min(1, exp(Phi(u_{k-1}) - Phi(v_k)))` is the acceptance
probability of warm-up iteration `k`; `beta` is frozen at the end of
warm-up. Between SMC stages the pCN mutation uses
`eta_{t+1} = eta_t + 4 (r_t - alpha*)` with the stage acceptance rate `r_t`.

- Domain: `0 < alpha* < 1` (default 0.25); warm-up iterations only, so
  the kept chain is time-homogeneous.
- Meaning: a Robbins-Monro recursion that drives the expected acceptance
