  probability to `alpha*`; the log-odds keep `beta` inside `(0, 1)`. The
  default 0.25 follows the tuning practice of Cotter et al. (about 0.234 to
  0.25); no optimal-scaling theorem fixes it for pCN.
- Code: `inference.preconditioned_crank_nicolson`,
  `inference.sequential_monte_carlo`.
- Source: [REF-ANDRIEU-THOMS-2008] (stochastic-approximation
  adaptation); [REF-COTTER-ROBERTS-STUART-WHITE-2013, Section 5]
  (acceptance targets used in practice). The gain exponent 0.6 and the
  between-stage gain 4 are implementation choices of this library.

### EQ-SMC-TEMPER-001 — Tempered targets and incremental weights

`pi_t(x) proportional to p(x) L(x)^beta_t`, `0 = beta_0 < ... < beta_T = 1`;
moving from `beta_{t-1}` to `beta_t` the particle `x_i` receives the
incremental weight `w_{t,i} = L(x_i)^(beta_t - beta_{t-1})`, the population
is resampled with probabilities proportional to `w_{t,i}`, and each
particle is moved by a Markov kernel that leaves `pi_t` invariant.

- Domain: a proper prior that can be sampled; `L` finite or zero; the
  mutation kernel is random-walk Metropolis with covariance
  `s^2 (Sigma_t + eps I)` (`Sigma_t` the weighted particle covariance,
  `s = 2.38 / sqrt(d)` by default) or pCN for an `N(0, I)` prior.
- Meaning: an SMC sampler with the backward kernel that makes the
  incremental weight the ratio `pi_t / pi_{t-1}` of unnormalized targets; the
  final equally weighted population approximates the posterior.
- Code: `inference.sequential_monte_carlo`,
  `inverse.CalibrationProblem.sample_posterior(method="smc")`.
- Source: [REF-DELMORAL-DOUCET-JASRA-2006];
  [REF-CHOPIN-2002] (sequential particle filter for static models).

### EQ-SMC-TEMPER-002 — Adaptive temperature by effective-sample-size bisection

`beta_t = sup { beta in (beta_{t-1}, 1] :
ESS(beta) >= f N_fin }`, with
`ESS(beta) = (sum_i w_i)^2 / sum_i w_i^2`,
`w_i = exp((beta - beta_{t-1}) l_i)`, `l_i = log L(x_i)`, and `N_fin` the
number of particles with finite `l_i`.

- Domain: `0 < f < 1` (default 0.5); at least two finite `l_i`.
- Meaning: `ESS(beta)` is non-increasing in `beta` (its log-derivative is
  twice the difference of the means of `l` under the tilts `w` and `w^2`), so
  bisection finds the largest admissible step; the schedule adapts to the
  information in the likelihood and ends when the full step keeps the ESS
  above the target.
- Code: `inference.sequential_monte_carlo`.
- Source: [REF-JASRA-STEPHENS-DOUCET-TSAGARIS-2011] (adaptive
  tempering by ESS); [EQ-FILT-PF-002] for the ESS.

### EQ-SMC-EVID-001 — SMC estimate of the evidence

`log Z_hat = sum_{t=1}^{T} log( (1/N) sum_i w_{t,i} )`, an estimate of
`log Z = log integral p(x) L(x) dx`.

- Domain: the incremental weights of [EQ-SMC-TEMPER-001]; `L` must include
  every normalizing constant of the data density for `Z` to be the
  marginal likelihood `p(y)`.
- Meaning: for fixed temperatures and kernels `Z_hat` is unbiased for `Z`
  (so `log Z_hat` is biased low by about half its variance); ratios of `Z`
  between models for the same data are Bayes factors.
- Code: `inference.sequential_monte_carlo`, `inference.SMCResult.log_evidence`,
  `inverse.CalibrationProblem.log_evidence`.
- Source: [REF-DELMORAL-DOUCET-JASRA-2006];
  [REF-LEE-WHITELEY-2018, Proposition 1] (lack of bias).

### EQ-SMC-EVID-002 — Lee-Whiteley relative variance of the evidence estimate

`v = 1 - (N / (N - 1))^T (sum_{i,j: E_i != E_j} w_i w_j) / (sum_i w_i)^2
= 1 - (N / (N - 1))^T (1 - sum_e W_e^2)`, where `w_i` are the incremental
weights of the last stage `T`, `E_i` the index of the stage-zero particle
from which particle `i` descends, and `W_e` the normalized weight of the
particles with `E_i = e`; the reported standard error of `log Z_hat` is
`sqrt(v)` when `v >= 0`.

- Domain: multinomial resampling at every stage (not computed for
  systematic resampling); fixed temperatures and kernels for the theorem.
- Meaning: `Z_hat^2 v` estimates `Var(Z_hat)` without bias and `N v` is
  consistent for the asymptotic relative variance, from one run. Adaptive
  temperatures and proposal scales are outside the theorem; `v` degenerates
  when all particles share a few ancestors and ignores the bias of a
  poorly mixing mutation kernel.
- Code: `inference.sequential_monte_carlo`,
  `inference.SMCResult.log_evidence_standard_error`.
- Source: [REF-LEE-WHITELEY-2018, equation (4) and Theorem 1] with
  `phi = G_{T-1}`, the last incremental weight.

### EQ-ABC-REJ-001 — ABC rejection posterior

Keep `theta ~ p(theta)` when `rho(s(y_sim), s(y_obs)) <= eps` for
`y_sim ~ p(y | theta)`; the kept draws follow
`pi_eps(theta | s_obs) proportional to
p(theta) P(rho(s(y_sim), s_obs) <= eps | theta)`.

- Domain: a prior and a simulator that can be sampled; a summary `s` and a
  distance `rho >= 0`; `eps >= 0` fixed, or the `ceil(n / q)`-sample
  order statistic for the quantile rule.
- Meaning: `pi_eps` tends to `p(theta | s_obs)` as `eps -> 0`, and equals
  `p(theta | y_obs)` in that limit only for a sufficient summary; the
  acceptance probability, hence the cost, scales like `eps^q` for a
  `q`-dimensional summary.
- Code: `inference.abc_rejection`, `inference.euclidean_distance`.
- Source: [REF-PRITCHARD-ETAL-1999] (rejection ABC with summaries).

### EQ-ABC-PMC-001 — ABC population Monte Carlo weights and kernel

Generation `t >= 2`: `eps_t = max(eps_min, Q_q(rho_{t-1}))`; draw `theta*`
from `{theta_j^(t-1), w_j^(t-1)}`, propose
`theta ~ N(theta*, 2 Sigma_{t-1})` with
`Sigma_{t-1} = sum_j w_j^(t-1) (theta_j - m)(theta_j - m)'`, keep it when
`rho <= eps_t`, and weight
`w_i^(t) proportional to p(theta_i) / sum_j w_j^(t-1)
N(theta_i; theta_j^(t-1), 2 Sigma_{t-1})`.

- Domain: a prior density that can be evaluated; a nonsingular population
  covariance; `0 < q < 1`.
- Meaning: importance sampling from the kernel mixture keeps each
  generation a weighted sample of `pi_{eps_t}` while the tolerance
  decreases; twice the weighted covariance is the kernel scale proposed by
  Beaumont et al. The quantile schedule is an adaptive choice.
- Code: `inference.abc_smc`.
- Source: [REF-BEAUMONT-CORNUET-MARIN-ROBERT-2009] (ABC-PMC
  with the `2 Sigma` kernel). The quantile tolerance schedule is an
  implementation choice of this library.

### EQ-CAL-STD-002 — Fully standardized calibration coordinates

`v = (u, w)` with `theta = T^-1(u)` (Nataf map of the prior) and
`sigma_q = F_q^-1(Phi(w_q))` for every unknown noise scale; the prior of
`v` is `N(0, I)`, the posterior is
`L(T^-1(u), sigma(w)) N(v; 0, I) / p(y)`, and
`p(y) = integral L(T^-1(u), sigma(w)) N(v; 0, I) dv` is the marginal
likelihood of the original problem.

- Domain: continuous priors with a Gaussian copula for `theta`, continuous
  noise-scale priors; Gaussian or Student-t noise densities with their
  normalizing constants.
- Meaning: the change of variables makes pCN and the SMC evidence
  applicable to unknown-noise problems without changing the posterior; draws
  are mapped back to `(u, log sigma)` and `(theta, sigma)`.
- Code: `inverse.CalibrationProblem.standard_log_likelihood`,
  `inverse.CalibrationProblem.log_evidence`,
  `inverse.CalibrationProblem.sample_posterior`.
- Source: [REF-LIU-DERKIUREGHIAN-1986] (Nataf transformation);
  [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002, Section 4.3] (change of variables).

## Singular value decomposition and classical regularization (ADR-0110)

### EQ-LINALG-SVD-001 — Thin SVD by one-sided Jacobi rotations

`A = U diag(sigma) V'` with `U` (`m x k`) and `V` (`n x k`) having
orthonormal columns, `k = min(m, n)`, `sigma_1 >= ... >= sigma_k >= 0`. For
`m >= n` (after `A = Q R` when `m > n`, so the rotations act on `R`), each
pair of columns `(a_p, a_q)` with `alpha = ||a_p||^2`, `beta = ||a_q||^2`,
`gamma = a_p'a_q` is rotated by
`zeta = (beta - alpha) / (2 gamma)`, `t = sign(zeta) / (|zeta| + sqrt(1 + zeta^2))`,
`c = 1 / sqrt(1 + t^2)`, `s = c t`,
`[a_p, a_q] <- [c a_p - s a_q, s a_p + c a_q]`, and the same rotation is
accumulated in `V`, until `|gamma| <= tol sqrt(alpha beta)` for every pair.
Then `sigma_j = ||a_j||` and `u_j = a_j / sigma_j`. A wide matrix uses
`A' = V diag(sigma) U'`. The condition number is `sigma_1 / sigma_k`.

- Domain: finite `m x n` matrix; relative tolerance `tol` in `(0, 1)`
  (default `1e-15`) and at most `max_sweeps` sweeps (default 60), otherwise
  `ValueError`.
- Meaning: each rotation makes one pair of columns orthogonal; at
  convergence `A V` has orthogonal columns, so their norms are the singular
  values. An exactly zero column gives `sigma_j = 0`, whose `u_j` completes
  an orthonormal set (Gram-Schmidt on coordinate vectors). Signs are fixed
  only up to a joint flip of `u_j` and `v_j`.
- Code: `linalg.singular_value_decomposition`,
  `linalg.SingularValueDecomposition.reconstruct`,
  `linalg.SingularValueDecomposition.condition_number`.
- Source: [REF-HESTENES-1958]; [REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013, Sections 8.5-8.6]
  (Jacobi rotations and computing the SVD).

### EQ-LINALG-SVD-002 — Truncated pseudo-inverse and numerical rank

`A^+ = sum_(sigma_i > tau sigma_1) v_i u_i' / sigma_i`,
`rank(A) = #{i : sigma_i > tau sigma_1}`, default `tau = max(m, n) 2^-52`.

- Domain: the SVD of [EQ-LINALG-SVD-001]; relative tolerance `tau` in
  `[0, 1)`.
- Meaning: with `tau = 0` and no zero singular value this is the
  Moore-Penrose inverse (the unique matrix with `A A^+ A = A`,
  `A^+ A A^+ = A^+`, and symmetric `A A^+` and `A^+ A`); the cut-off treats
  singular values at rounding level as zero. `A^+ b` is the minimum-norm
  least-squares solution.
- Code: `linalg.pseudo_inverse`, `linalg.numerical_rank`,
  `linalg.SingularValueDecomposition.pseudo_inverse`,
  `linalg.SingularValueDecomposition.rank`.
- Source: [REF-PENROSE-1955]; [REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013, Section 5.5].

### EQ-INV-REG-001 — Tikhonov functional and its stacked least-squares form

`x_lambda = argmin_x ||A x - b||^2 + lambda^2 ||L (x - x_bar)||^2`, computed
as the least-squares solution of `[A; lambda L] x = [b; lambda L x_bar]`
(for the linear solver `x_bar = 0`) by Householder QR [EQ-LINALG-009]. For
`L = I` it equals the posterior mean of `x ~ N(0, (s^2 / lambda^2) I)` given
`b = A x + e`, `e ~ N(0, s^2 I)`. The nonlinear version minimizes
`||r(x)||^2 + lambda^2 ||L (x - x_bar)||^2` by Levenberg-Marquardt on the
stacked residual `[r(x); lambda L (x - x_bar)]` [EQ-OPT-LM-001].

- Domain: `lambda >= 0`; the null spaces of `A` and `L` intersect only in
  zero (otherwise the stacked matrix is rank deficient and the solve
  raises); `lambda = 0` needs `A` of full column rank.
- Meaning: the penalty selects, among the solutions that fit the data about
  equally well, one with small (semi)norm; `lambda` sets the trade-off. The
  normal equations `(A'A + lambda^2 L'L) x = A'b` are never formed, so the
  solve sees the condition number of the stacked matrix, not its square.
- Code: `inverse.tikhonov`, `inverse.nonlinear_tikhonov`,
  `inverse.regularization._stacked_qr`.
- Source: [REF-TIKHONOV-1963]; [REF-HANSEN-2008, Sections 2.2 and 2.7.1]
  (functional with `x_bar`, stacked form); [REF-TARANTOLA-2005, Chapter 3]
  (Gaussian interpretation).

### EQ-INV-REG-002 — Tikhonov filter factors

For `L = I` and the SVD of `A`,
`x_lambda = sum_i f_i (u_i'b / sigma_i) v_i` with
`f_i = sigma_i^2 / (sigma_i^2 + lambda^2)` (`f_i = 0` when `sigma_i = 0`).

- Domain: `lambda >= 0`; the SVD of [EQ-LINALG-SVD-001].
- Meaning: components with `sigma_i >> lambda` pass almost unchanged
  (`f_i ~ 1`), those with `sigma_i << lambda` are damped (`f_i ~
  sigma_i^2 / lambda^2`); a discarded component still contributes about
  `sigma_i (u_i'b) / lambda^2`.
- Code: `inverse.tikhonov`, `inverse.TikhonovSolution.filter_factors`,
  `inverse.regularization._filter_factors`.
- Source: [REF-HANSEN-2008, Section 2.4, eq. (2.18)].

### EQ-INV-REG-003 — Generalized cross-validation function

`G(lambda) = ||A x_lambda - b||^2 / trace(I_m - A A^#)^2`, where
`x_lambda = A^# b`. For `L = I`, `trace(I_m - A A^#) = m - sum_i f_i`; for a
general `L`, with `[A; lambda L] = Q R` and `Q_1` the first `m` rows of `Q`,
`A A^# = Q_1 Q_1'`, so `trace(I_m - A A^#) = m - ||Q_1||_F^2`.

- Domain: `lambda > 0` on a grid (default geometric from
  `max(sigma_k, 16 eps sigma_1)` to `sigma_1`, divided by the extreme
  nonzero singular values of `L` for a general `L`); the grid minimum is
  refined by golden-section search in `log lambda`.
- Meaning: an estimate of the predictive risk that needs no noise level.
  For a square operator `G` tends to a finite limit as `lambda -> 0`, which
  can undercut the interior minimum and give a far too small `lambda`.
- Code: `inverse.generalized_cross_validation`, `inverse.regularization._gcv`,
  `inverse.regularization._Curve.point`.
- Source: [REF-CRAVEN-WAHBA-1979]; [REF-GOLUB-HEATH-WAHBA-1979];
  [REF-HANSEN-2008, Section 2.9, eqs. (2.62)-(2.63)]. The `Q_1` trace form
  follows from `A = Q_1 R` (derived for this library).

### EQ-INV-REG-004 — L-curve curvature

With `rho = ||A x_lambda - b||^2`, `eta = ||L x_lambda||^2`, and hats for
`log sqrt(.)`, the curvature of `(rho_hat, eta_hat)` is
`kappa = (rho_hat' eta_hat'' - rho_hat'' eta_hat') / ((rho_hat')^2 + (eta_hat')^2)^(3/2)`
(primes: derivatives in `lambda`). Using `rho' = -lambda^2 eta'` and
`eta' = (4 / lambda) (L x)'(L z)`, `z = (A'A + lambda^2 L'L)^-1 A'(A x - b)`
(for `L = I`: `eta' = -(4 / lambda) sum_i f_i^2 (1 - f_i) (u_i'b)^2 / sigma_i^2`),
`kappa = 2 rho eta (lambda^2 eta' rho + 2 lambda rho eta + lambda^4 eta eta')
/ (|eta'| (lambda^4 eta^2 + rho^2)^(3/2))`.

- Domain: `lambda > 0` with `rho, eta, eta' != 0` (otherwise `nan`); same
  grid and refinement as [EQ-INV-REG-003], maximizing `kappa`.
- Meaning: the corner where the curve turns from the steep branch (noise
  dominated) to the flat branch (regularization dominated). The closed form
  is checked against finite differences of the log norms in the tests.
- Code: `inverse.l_curve`, `inverse.regularization._curvature`,
  `inverse.regularization._Curve.point`.
- Source: [REF-HANSEN-OLEARY-1993, Section 5.1, eq. (8)] (curvature in log
  norms, corner at maximum curvature); [REF-HANSEN-2008, Sections 2.5 and
  2.9]. The reduction to `rho`, `eta`, `eta'` is derived for this library
  from `x' = (2 / lambda) z`.

### EQ-INV-REG-005 — Discrepancy principle

Choose `lambda` with `||A x_lambda - b|| = tau delta`, `delta ~ ||e||`,
`tau >= 1`; the root is found by Brent's method [EQ-OPT-BRENT-001] in
`log lambda` after bracketing on the grid.

- Domain: `||A x_lambda - b||` increases from the least-squares residual
  (`lambda -> 0`) to `||b||` (`lambda -> inf`, for `L = I`); a target
  outside that range raises `ValueError`.
- Meaning: fit the data no better than the noise allows. An underestimated
  `delta` gives an under-regularized solution with a large norm, an
  overestimated one an over-smoothed solution.
- Code: `inverse.discrepancy_principle`.
- Source: [REF-MOROZOV-1966]; [REF-HANSEN-2008, Section 2.9, eq. (2.61)].

### EQ-INV-REG-006 — Truncated SVD solution

`x_k = sum_(i <= k) (u_i'b / sigma_i) v_i`,
`||A x_k - b||^2 = sum_(i > k) (u_i'b)^2 + ||b - U U'b||^2`.

- Domain: `1 <= k <= min(m, n)` with `sigma_k > 0`.
- Meaning: filter factors `1` for `i <= k` and `0` otherwise; `x_k` is the
  minimum-norm least-squares solution for the closest rank-`k` matrix
  `A_k`.
- Code: `inverse.truncated_svd`.
- Source: [REF-HANSEN-2008, Section 2.7.3, eqs. (2.42)-(2.45)].

### EQ-INV-REG-007 — Discrete Picard coefficients

`(sigma_i, |u_i'b|, |u_i'b| / sigma_i)` for `i = 1, ..., k`.

- Domain: the SVD of [EQ-LINALG-SVD-001]; `inf` for `sigma_i = 0 < |u_i'b|`
  and `nan` when both vanish.
- Meaning: the discrete Picard condition holds when `|u_i'b|` decays on
  average faster than `sigma_i`; noise makes `|u_i'b|` level off near its
  standard deviation, and from there on the ratios grow.
- Code: `inverse.picard_coefficients`.
- Source: [REF-HANSEN-2008, Section 2.4].

### EQ-INV-REG-PROB-001 — Discrete backward heat operator

`A = V diag(exp(-T mu_k)) V'`, `V_jk = sqrt(2 h) sin(j k pi h)`,
`mu_k = (4 / h^2) sin^2(k pi h / 2)`, `h = 1 / (n + 1)`, `s_j = j h`;
exact solution `x(s) = (27 / 4) s (1 - s)^2` and `b = A x`.

- Domain: `n >= 2` interior points, `T > 0`.
- Meaning: `V diag(mu) V'` is the second-difference matrix with zero
  boundary values, so `A = exp(-T D)` advances the semi-discrete heat
  equation by `T`; its singular values `exp(-T mu_k)` are known exactly and
  decay like `exp(-T pi^2 k^2)`.
- Code: `inverse.backward_heat_problem`.
- Source: [REF-HANSEN-2008, Sections 2.1 and 2.3] (discrete ill-posed
  problems); the eigenpairs are verified in `tests/test_regularization.py`.

### EQ-INV-REG-PROB-002 — Midpoint discretization of deriv2

`A_ij = h K(s_i, t_j)`, `s_i = t_i = (i - 1/2) h`, `h = 1 / n`,
`K(s, t) = s (t - 1)` for `s < t` and `t (s - 1)` for `s >= t`; exact
solution `x_j = t_j`, `b = A x`.

- Domain: `n >= 2`.
- Meaning: the Green's function of the second derivative on `[0, 1]`; the
  continuous data for `f(t) = t` are `g(s) = (s^3 - s) / 6`, which `A x`
  matches up to the `O(h^2)` quadrature error. Regularization Tools uses a
  Galerkin discretization, so its matrix differs.
- Code: `inverse.second_derivative_problem`.
- Source: [REF-HANSEN-2008, Chapter 4, deriv2] (kernel and the case
  `f(t) = t`).

## Ensemble Kalman inversion and ES-MDA (ADR-0115)

### EQ-INV-EKI-001 — Ensemble Kalman inversion update

For members `u_j`, `j = 1..N`, in the prior's standard-normal coordinates
with predictions `g_j = G(T^-1(u_j))`, ensemble means `u_bar`, `g_bar` and
`C^up = sum_j (u_j - u_bar)(g_j - g_bar)' / (N - 1)`,
`C^pp = sum_j (g_j - g_bar)(g_j - g_bar)' / (N - 1)`:
`u_j <- u_j + C^up (C^pp + Gamma)^-1 (y + eta_j - g_j)` with
`eta_j ~ N(0, Gamma)` drawn afresh at every iteration (or `eta_j = 0`
without perturbation). In whitened form, with `A` and `B` the deviations of
`u` and of `Gamma^-1/2 g` from their means,
`C^up (C^pp + alpha Gamma)^-1 = A'B (B'B + alpha (N - 1) I)^-1 Gamma^-1/2
= A' (B B' + alpha (N - 1) I)^-1 B Gamma^-1/2`.

- Domain: `N >= 2`; `Gamma` symmetric positive definite (here diagonal with
  entries `sigma_q^2 + sigma_delta_q^2` of known Gaussian noise); `alpha > 0`.
- Meaning: a derivative-free iteration that decreases the data misfit; each
  member stays in the affine span of the initial ensemble and the ensemble
  covariance collapses as the iterations proceed, so the method is an
  optimizer and iterative regularizer, not a posterior sampler. Iglesias,
  Law and Stuart normalize the covariances by `N`; this library uses
  `N - 1` in both, as in the ensemble Kalman filter.
- Code: `inverse.ensemble_kalman_inversion`, `inverse.ensemble_smoother_mda`.
- Source: [REF-IGLESIAS-LAW-STUART-2013, Algorithm 1];
  [REF-SCHILLINGS-STUART-2017] (gradient-flow limit and collapse);
  [REF-EVENSEN-2003] (ensemble gain).

### EQ-INV-EKI-002 — Discrepancy-principle stopping of ensemble Kalman inversion

Stop before the first update at which
`|Gamma^-1/2 (y - g_bar_n)| <= tau eta`, where `g_bar_n` is the ensemble
mean of the predictions at iteration `n`, `eta = |Gamma^-1/2 (y - G(u_true))|`
is the noise level, and `tau > 1`.

- Domain: `tau >= 1` (enforced); `eta > 0`. When the noise realization is
  unknown the library uses `eta = sqrt(M)` for `M` observations, the root of
  `E |Gamma^-1/2 eps|^2 = M` for Gaussian errors; the default `tau = 1.5` is
  a library choice.
- Meaning: iterating past the noise level fits the noise of an ill-posed
  problem; stopping there makes the iteration a regularization method. The
  criterion tests the mean of the predictions, not the prediction at the
  mean, so it needs no extra forward run.
- Code: `inverse.ensemble_kalman_inversion(stopping="discrepancy")`,
  `inverse.EnsembleInversionResult.misfit_history`.
- Source: [REF-IGLESIAS-2016, Algorithm 1, Eq. (6)] (criterion on the mean
  prediction, `tau > 1 / rho`); [REF-IGLESIAS-LAW-STUART-2013, Section 2.3]
  (discrepancy principle with `tau > 1`).

### EQ-INV-ESMDA-001 — ES-MDA update and inflation condition

For `i = 1..N_a`: `u_j <- u_j + C^up (C^pp + alpha_i Gamma)^-1
(y + sqrt(alpha_i) Gamma^1/2 z_ij - g_j)`, `z_ij ~ N(0, I)`, with the
covariances of [EQ-INV-EKI-001] recomputed from the current ensemble, and
`sum_{i=1}^{N_a} 1 / alpha_i = 1`.

- Domain: `alpha_i > 0` finite; the sum condition is checked to a relative
  tolerance of `1e-9`; Gaussian errors with known `Gamma`.
- Meaning: the product of the tempered likelihoods `L^(1/alpha_i)` is the
  full likelihood, so for a forward model affine in `u` the composition of
  the `N_a` Gaussian conditionings is the exact Bayesian update and the
  ensemble samples the posterior as `N -> infinity`; `N_a = 1`, `alpha = 1`
  is the one-step ensemble smoother. For nonlinear models it is an
  approximation.
- Code: `inverse.ensemble_smoother_mda`.
- Source: [REF-EMERICK-REYNOLDS-2013].

### EQ-CAL-CORR-001 — Stationary correlation of measurement errors

`M_ij = rho(|c_i - c_j| / ell)` over a numeric experimental condition `c`,
with `rho(h) = exp(-h)` (exponential, Matern 1/2),
`rho(h) = (1 + sqrt(3) h) exp(-sqrt(3) h)` (Matern 3/2), or
`rho(h) = (1 + sqrt(5) h + 5 h^2 / 3) exp(-sqrt(5) h)` (Matern 5/2).

- Domain: `ell > 0`; distinct condition values, or a positive discrepancy
  variance (nugget), for a positive-definite `M`.
- Meaning: errors of one quantity measured under nearby conditions (times,
  loads, positions) are correlated, with correlation decaying over the
  length `ell`; `rho(0) = 1`, so `sigma_q` stays the marginal standard
  deviation.
- Code: `inverse.error_correlation_kernel`,
  `inverse.ErrorCorrelation.correlation_matrix`.
- Source: [REF-RASMUSSEN-WILLIAMS-2006, Section 4.2] (Matern class with
  `nu = 1/2, 3/2, 5/2`).

### EQ-CAL-CORR-002 — Correlated Gaussian calibration log-likelihood

For the `n_q` observations of a correlated quantity with residual vector
`r_q`, `Sigma_q = sigma_q^2 M_q + sigma_delta_q^2 I = L L'` and
`log p(y_q | theta) = -0.5 (n_q log 2 pi + log det Sigma_q
+ r_q' Sigma_q^-1 r_q) = -0.5 n_q log 2 pi - sum_i log L_ii
- 0.5 |L^-1 r_q|^2`; the log-likelihood adds this term for every
correlated quantity to the independent terms of [EQ-CAL-LIK-001]. With
`sigma_delta_q = 0` the factor is `sigma_q L_M` with `M_q = L_M L_M'`
computed once.

- Domain: `sigma_q > 0`, `M_q` symmetric positive definite, Gaussian
  errors (a Student-t law is not combined with correlation).
- Meaning: generalized least squares in likelihood form; `M_q = I`
  reproduces the independent Gaussian likelihood.
- Code: `inverse.CalibrationProblem.log_likelihood`,
  `inverse.CalibrationProblem.standard_log_posterior`,
  `inverse.predict`.
- Source: [REF-SEBER-WILD-2003, Chapter 6] (nonlinear regression with
  correlated errors) and [REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013, Section 4.2] (Cholesky
  evaluation).

### EQ-CAL-CORR-003 — Whitened residuals

`e = W r` with `W' W = Sigma^-1`: `e_i = r_i / s_i` for independent
observations and `e_q = L^-1 r_q` for a correlated quantity
(`Sigma_q = L L'`), so `|e|^2 = r' Sigma^-1 r`. Least squares minimizes
`0.5 |e(theta)|^2`, its Gauss-Newton covariance is `(J_e' J_e)^-1` with
`J_e = -W J`, and an unknown scale of a correlated quantity with
`Sigma_q = sigma_q^2 M_q` is re-estimated as
`s_q^2 = (|L_M^-1 r_q|^2 / n_q) n / (n - d)`.

- Domain: positive-definite `Sigma`; closed-form scale update only without
  a discrepancy variance on a correlated quantity.
- Meaning: generalized least squares by prewhitening; `J_e' J_e` is the
  Fisher information of `theta` under correlated Gaussian errors.
- Code: `inverse.CalibrationProblem.whitened_residuals`,
  `inverse.CalibrationProblem.fit_least_squares`,
  `inverse.CalibrationProblem.identifiability`.
- Source: [REF-SEBER-WILD-2003, Chapters 2 and 6].

### EQ-CAL-AD-001 — First derivative of the prior's standard-normal map

For `x_i = F_i^-1(Phi(z_i))` with `z = L u`,
`d x_i / d u_k = phi(z_i) / f_i(x_i) L_ik`, and for the normal score
`z_i = Phi^-1(F_i(x_i))`, `d z_i / d x_i = f_i(x_i) / phi(z_i)`. A
reverse-mode variable takes its value from the float map and this
derivative through `x~ = x_0 + (g - g_0)` with `g = c sum_k L_ik u_k`
([EQ-DIST-AD-001]).

- Domain: continuous marginals with `f_i(x_i) > 0`; independence or a
  Gaussian copula; first derivatives only (second derivatives through the
  map are refused, not approximated).
- Meaning: the inverse-function rule differentiates the Nataf map without
  differentiating quantile functions, so the calibration log posterior is
  traceable in reverse mode for every continuous prior family.
- Code: `inverse.CalibrationProblem.standard_log_posterior_and_gradient`,
  `inverse.CalibrationProblem.log_posterior_and_gradient`.
- Source: [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002, Section 2.1] (derivative of an inverse
  transformation), [REF-LIU-DERKIUREGHIAN-1986] (Nataf map) and
  [REF-GRIEWANK-WALTHER-2008, Chapter 3] (reverse mode).

## Method laboratory: estimator construction and certification

### EQ-MLAB-MCSE-001 — Monte Carlo standard error of a replicate mean

`se(Z_bar) = sqrt(S^2 / R)` with `S^2 = sum_r (Z_r - Z_bar)^2 / (R - 1)`.

- Domain: `R >= 2` independent replicates of an estimator with finite
  variance.
- Meaning: the uncertainty of an estimated bias or mean that is due to the
  finite number of replicates.
- Code: `methodlab.ReplicateSummary.mean_standard_error`,
  `methodlab.summarize`, `methodlab.check_unbiasedness`.
- Source: [REF-MORRIS-WHITE-CROWTHER-2019, Table 6].

### EQ-MLAB-MCSE-002 — Standard error of a sample variance without normality

`Var[S^2] = (mu_4 - (R - 3) / (R - 1) sigma^4) / R`, estimated with the
sample fourth central moment `m_4` and `S^2`.

- Domain: `R >= 4` independent replicates with a finite fourth moment.
- Meaning: the uncertainty of an empirical variance, valid for non-normal
  estimators (under normality it reduces to `2 sigma^4 / (R - 1)`).
- Code: `methodlab.ReplicateSummary.variance_standard_error`,
  `methodlab.check_variance`, `methodlab.check_efficiency_gain`.
- Source: [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002, Exercise 5.8].

### EQ-MLAB-WNV-001 — Work-normalized variance

`WNV = Var[Z] E[cost(Z)]`; the efficiency gain of `A` over `B` is
`WNV_B / WNV_A`. Delta-method standard error of the logarithm of the
estimate `s^2 c_bar` from `R` replicates:
`Var[log WNV] ~ Var[s^2] / s^4 + (Var[c / c_bar] + 2 Cov[(Z - Z_bar)^2 / m_2, c / c_bar]) / R`.

- Domain: unbiased (or equally biased) estimators with finite variance and
  finite positive expected cost; the standard error also needs a finite
  fourth moment of `Z` and a finite variance of the cost.
- Meaning: with a computing budget `c` the mean of about `c / E[cost]`
  replicates has variance near `WNV / c`, so a smaller product means less
  work for the same accuracy.
- Code: `methodlab.ReplicateSummary.work_normalized_variance`,
  `methodlab.check_efficiency_gain`, `methodlab.rank_by_efficiency`.
- Source: [REF-GLASSERMAN-2003, Section 1.1.3].

### EQ-MLAB-RT-001 — Single-term randomized-truncation estimator

`Z = Delta_N / p_N`, `Delta_n = Y_n - Y_(n-1)`, `Y_(-1) = 0`,
`P(N = n) = p_n > 0` independent of the differences.

- Domain: `E[Y_n] -> mu`; finite variance requires
  `sum_n E[Delta_n^2] / p_n < infinity`.
- Meaning: an estimator with expectation `sum_n E[Delta_n] = mu`, free of
  the truncation bias of any fixed level, at a random cost.
- Code: `methodlab.single_term_estimator`, `methodlab.geometric_levels`,
  `methodlab.finite_levels`, `methodlab.LevelDistribution.probability`.
- Source: [REF-RHEE-GLYNN-2015]; [REF-MCLEISH-2011].

### EQ-MLAB-RT-002 — Independent-sum randomized-truncation estimator

`Z = sum_(n=0)^N Delta_n / P(N >= n)` with the differences drawn
independently across levels;
`E[Z^2] = sum_n (Var[Delta_n] + (mu - mu_(n-1))^2 - (mu - mu_n)^2) / P(N >= n)`,
`mu_n = E[Y_n]`, `mu_(-1) = 0`.

- Domain: [EQ-MLAB-RT-001]; finite variance when
  `sum_n Var[Delta_n] / P(N >= n)` and
  `sum_n (mu - mu_(n-1))^2 / P(N >= n)` converge. (The condition
  `sum_n E[(Y_(n-1) - Y)^2] / P(N >= n) < infinity` belongs to the
  coupled-sum estimator of the source, which draws all levels of a replicate
  from one coupled path and is not implemented.)
- Meaning: every difference up to a random level enters, weighted by the
  inverse probability that its level is reached. The implementing function
  is named `coupled_sum_estimator` for historical reasons.
- Code: `methodlab.coupled_sum_estimator`,
  `methodlab.LevelDistribution.tail`.
- Source: [REF-RHEE-GLYNN-2015].

### EQ-MLAB-RT-003 — Level law minimizing second moment times cost

`(sum_n m_n / p_n)(sum_n p_n c_n) >= (sum_n sqrt(m_n c_n))^2` with equality
at `p_n` proportional to `sqrt(m_n / c_n)`, where `m_n = E[Delta_n^2]`.

- Domain: positive second moments and costs on finitely many levels.
- Meaning: the Cauchy-Schwarz bound on the work-normalized second moment of
  the single-term estimator and the law that attains it; it equals the
  variance-optimal law only when `mu = 0`.
- Code: `methodlab.optimal_level_probabilities`,
  `methodlab.truncation_design`.
- Source: [REF-RHEE-GLYNN-2015] (work-variance trade-off of the level law).

### EQ-MLAB-RICH-001 — Extrapolation weights for a known bias expansion

`sum_i w_i = 1`, `sum_i w_i h_i^(q_k) = 0` for `k = 1, ..., K`.

- Domain: `K + 1` distinct positive steps, `K` distinct positive exponents,
  and `E[Y(h)] = mu + sum_k a_k h^(q_k) + higher terms`.
- Meaning: the combination `sum_i w_i Y(h_i)` has no bias term of the listed
  orders; for one order and steps `h, h/r` the weights are
  `(-1, r^q) / (r^q - 1)`.
- Code: `methodlab.extrapolation_weights`,
  `methodlab.extrapolated_estimator`.
- Source: [REF-ROACHE-1998, Chapters 4-5].

### EQ-MLAB-BLUE-001 — Best linear unbiased combination

`w = Sigma^-1 1 / (1' Sigma^-1 1)`, `Var[w' Z] = 1 / (1' Sigma^-1 1)`.

- Domain: estimators with a common expectation and positive-definite
  covariance `Sigma`; weights fixed independently of the combined draws.
- Meaning: the unbiased linear combination of smallest variance; never worse
  than its best component.
- Code: `methodlab.best_linear_unbiased_weights`,
  `methodlab.combine_unbiased`.
- Source: [REF-SCHADEN-ULLMANN-2020].

### EQ-MLAB-CV-001 — Control variate with frozen coefficients

`Z = Y - beta' (C - nu)`, `beta = Var[C]^-1 Cov[C, Y]`,
`Var[Z] = (1 - R^2) Var[Y]`.

- Domain: controls `C` with known mean `nu` and nonsingular covariance;
  `beta` fixed independently of the corrected draws.
- Meaning: subtracting the predictable part of `Y` keeps the expectation and
  removes the share `R^2` of the variance.
- Code: `methodlab.control_variate_estimator`.
- Source: [REF-GLASSERMAN-2003, Section 4.1].

### EQ-MLAB-ANTI-001 — Antithetic pair on the unit cube

`Z = (f(U) + f(1 - U)) / 2`, `Var[Z] = (1 + rho) Var[f(U)] / 2`.

- Domain: square-integrable `f` on `[0, 1]^d`, `U` uniform,
  `rho = Corr[f(U), f(1 - U)]`.
- Meaning: an unbiased estimator of the integral that beats two independent
  draws exactly when `rho < 0`.
- Code: `methodlab.antithetic_estimator`.
- Source: [REF-GLASSERMAN-2003, Section 4.2].

### EQ-MLAB-JACK-001 — Jackknife bias correction

`theta_J = n theta_hat - (n - 1) mean_i theta_(i)`.

- Domain: a statistic of `n >= 2` observations whose bias expands in powers
  of `1 / n`.
- Meaning: removes the `1 / n` bias term; exact when the bias is exactly
  `a / n`.
- Code: `methodlab.jackknife_bias_corrected`.
- Source: [REF-QUENOUILLE-1956].

### EQ-MLAB-BOOT-001 — Bootstrap bias correction

`theta_B = 2 theta_hat - mean_b theta*_b`.

- Domain: a statistic and `B` resamples drawn with replacement from the
  data.
- Meaning: subtracts the bootstrap estimate of bias
  `mean_b theta*_b - theta_hat`.
- Code: `methodlab.bootstrap_bias_corrected`.
- Source: [REF-EFRON-TIBSHIRANI-1993, Chapter 10].

### EQ-MLAB-IF-001 — Empirical influence value

`I_i = d/d eps T((1 - eps) P_n + eps delta_(x_i))` at `eps = 0`.

- Domain: a functional `T` of weighted samples that is differentiable in the
  weights at the empirical distribution `P_n`.
- Meaning: the first-order effect of observation `x_i` on the estimate; the
  values sum to zero.
- Code: `methodlab.empirical_influence`,
  `methodlab.InfluenceAnalysis.mean_influence`.
- Source: [REF-HAMPEL-1974]; [REF-CARONE-LUEDTKE-VANDERLAAN-2019].

### EQ-MLAB-IF-002 — Infinitesimal-jackknife standard error

`se(T(P_n)) = sqrt(sum_i I_i^2) / n`.

- Domain: [EQ-MLAB-IF-001] with independent, identically distributed
  observations.
- Meaning: the nonparametric delta-method standard error of a smooth
  statistic.
- Code: `methodlab.empirical_influence`.
- Source: [REF-EFRON-TIBSHIRANI-1993]; [REF-HAMPEL-1974].

### EQ-MLAB-ONESTEP-001 — One-step correction of a plug-in estimate

`psi_1 = psi(P_hat) + (1 / n) sum_i phi(x_i; P_hat)`,
`se = sd(phi) / sqrt(n)`.

- Domain: an influence function `phi` of the target functional evaluated at
  the fitted nuisance `P_hat`; asymptotic normality needs second-order
  remainder `o(n^-1/2)` and sample splitting or a Donsker condition.
- Meaning: removes the first-order bias of a plug-in estimate.
- Code: `methodlab.one_step_estimator`.
- Source: [REF-KENNEDY-2022]; [REF-HINES-ETAL-2022].

### EQ-MLAB-VERDICT-001 — Verdict from a confidence interval

With interval `[L, U]`, target `t`, and tolerance `delta`: supported if
`t - delta <= L` and `U <= t + delta`; refuted if `U < t - delta` or
`L > t + delta`; inconclusive otherwise. Without `delta`: refuted if `t` is
outside `[L, U]`, else not refuted.

- Domain: an interval of confidence `1 - alpha` for the tested quantity and
  a tolerance declared before the run.
- Meaning: interval-inclusion equivalence logic; each wrong "refuted" or
  "supported" has probability at most `alpha` when the interval has exact
  level `1 - alpha` (the delta-method intervals of the variance, rate, and
  efficiency checks reach it only for many replicates and light tails).
- Code: `methodlab.interval_verdict`, `methodlab.CheckResult`,
  `methodlab.MethodCard.verdict`, `methodlab.check_coverage`.
- Source: [REF-SCHUIRMANN-1987]; [REF-LEHMANN-ROMANO-2005].

### EQ-MLAB-STAB-001 — Largest share of the sum of squares

`share = max_r (Z_r - Z_bar)^2 / sum_r (Z_r - Z_bar)^2`.

- Domain: `R` replicates.
- Meaning: a heuristic symptom of an infinite variance: one replicate
  carries most of the empirical variance. Not a test.
- Code: `methodlab.check_variance_stability`.
- Source: [REF-OWEN-2013, Chapter 9] (diagnostics for heavy-tailed weights).

### EQ-MLAB-RATE-001 — Fitted decay rate of the mean squared error

`r_hat = -sum_i c_i log MSE_i`, `c_i = (x_i - x_bar) / sum_j (x_j - x_bar)^2`,
`x_i = log n_i`; `Var[r_hat] = sum_i c_i^2 Var[MSE_i] / MSE_i^2`.

- Domain: at least three sizes, independent replicate sets per size.
- Meaning: least-squares slope of `log MSE` on `log n` with a delta-method
  standard error.
- Code: `methodlab.check_convergence_rate`.
- Source: [REF-OBERKAMPF-ROY-2010] (observed order of accuracy);
  [REF-MORRIS-WHITE-CROWTHER-2019, Table 6].

### EQ-MLAB-META-001 — Metamorphic relation

`procedure(g(x)) = h(procedure(x))` for an input transformation `g` and the
implied output transformation `h`.

- Domain: a deterministic procedure and generated inputs `x`.
- Meaning: a necessary property checkable without knowing the correct
  output.
- Code: `methodlab.check_invariance`.
- Source: [REF-CHEN-ETAL-2018].

### EQ-MLAB-ADEMP-001 — Bias and its Monte Carlo standard error

`bias = theta_bar - theta`, `se = S / sqrt(n)`.

- Domain: `n >= 2` simulated estimates with known estimand `theta`.
- Meaning: average error of a method over data sets.
- Code: `methodlab.performance_measures`,
  `methodlab.repetitions_for_standard_error`.
- Source: [REF-MORRIS-WHITE-CROWTHER-2019, Table 6].

### EQ-MLAB-ADEMP-002 — Empirical standard error

`EmpSE = S`, `se = S / sqrt(2 (n - 1))`.

- Domain: [EQ-MLAB-ADEMP-001]; the standard error assumes normal estimates.
- Meaning: the true sampling variability of a method.
- Code: `methodlab.performance_measures`.
- Source: [REF-MORRIS-WHITE-CROWTHER-2019, Table 6].

### EQ-MLAB-ADEMP-003 — Mean squared error

`MSE = mean_i (theta_i - theta)^2`,
`se = sqrt(sum_i ((theta_i - theta)^2 - MSE)^2 / (n (n - 1)))`.

- Domain: [EQ-MLAB-ADEMP-001].
- Meaning: squared bias plus variance.
- Code: `methodlab.performance_measures`.
- Source: [REF-MORRIS-WHITE-CROWTHER-2019, Table 6].

### EQ-MLAB-ADEMP-004 — Average model-based standard error

`ModSE = sqrt(mean_i se_i^2)`, `se = sqrt(Var[se^2] / (4 n ModSE^2))`.

- Domain: every repetition reports a standard error.
- Meaning: what the method believes its sampling variability is.
- Code: `methodlab.performance_measures`.
- Source: [REF-MORRIS-WHITE-CROWTHER-2019, Table 6].

### EQ-MLAB-ADEMP-005 — Relative error of the model-based standard error

`ModSE / EmpSE - 1` with standard error
`(ModSE / EmpSE) sqrt(Var[se^2] / (4 n ModSE^4) + 1 / (2 (n - 1)))`.

- Domain: [EQ-MLAB-ADEMP-002] and [EQ-MLAB-ADEMP-004].
- Meaning: whether reported standard errors are calibrated (zero when they
  are).
- Code: `methodlab.performance_measures`.
- Source: [REF-MORRIS-WHITE-CROWTHER-2019, Table 6].

### EQ-MLAB-ADEMP-006 — Coverage and bias-eliminated coverage

`p = mean_i 1{L_i <= theta <= U_i}`, `se = sqrt(p (1 - p) / n)`; the
bias-eliminated version replaces `theta` by `theta_bar`.

- Domain: every repetition reports an interval.
- Meaning: how often intervals contain the truth, and how often they would
  if the method were unbiased.
- Code: `methodlab.performance_measures`,
  `methodlab.repetitions_for_standard_error`.
- Source: [REF-MORRIS-WHITE-CROWTHER-2019, Table 6].

### EQ-MLAB-ADEMP-007 — Paired relative gain in precision

`gain = (EmpSE_ref / EmpSE)^2 - 1`,
`se = 2 (EmpSE_ref / EmpSE)^2 sqrt((1 - rho^2) / (n - 1))`.

- Domain: two methods applied to the same `n >= 3` data sets; `rho` is the
  correlation of their estimates.
- Meaning: relative increase in precision of a method against a reference,
  sharpened by pairing.
- Code: `methodlab.SimulationStudyResult.compare_precision`.
- Source: [REF-MORRIS-WHITE-CROWTHER-2019, Table 6].

### EQ-MLAB-SH-001 — Sequential-halving schedule

Rounds `r = 0, ..., ceil(log2 n) - 1`; each survivor gets
`floor(T / (|S_r| ceil(log2 n)))` evaluations; the better
`ceil(|S_r| / 2)` survive.

- Domain: `n >= 2` candidates, budget `T >= n ceil(log2 n)`.
- Meaning: a fixed-budget selection of the best candidate whose error
  probability decays exponentially in the budget for bounded losses.
- Code: `methodlab.sequential_halving`.
- Source: [REF-KARNIN-KOREN-SOMEKH-2013].

### EQ-MLAB-SUM-001 — Sum of independent estimators

`Z = sum_i Z_i`, `E[Z] = sum_i E[Z_i]`, `Var[Z] = sum_i Var[Z_i]`,
`cost(Z) = sum_i cost(Z_i)`.

- Domain: estimators drawn on independent streams, each with finite
  variance.
- Meaning: a telescoping target can be split into a directly estimated base
  term and separately estimated corrections.
- Code: `methodlab.sum_of_estimators`.
- Source: [REF-GILES-2015]; [REF-RHEE-GLYNN-2015].

### EQ-MLAB-THIN-001 — Thinned estimator

`Z = B Z' / q`, `B ~ Bernoulli(q)` independent of `Z'`;
`E[Z] = E[Z']`, `Var[Z] = E[Z'^2] / q - E[Z']^2`,
`E[cost(Z)] = q E[cost(Z')]`.

- Domain: `0 < q <= 1`, `Z'` with finite second moment.
- Meaning: an expensive correction with a small second moment is evaluated
  rarely and weighted by the inverse probability, keeping the expectation.
- Code: `methodlab.thinned_estimator`.
- Source: [REF-RHEE-GLYNN-2015].

## Conformal prediction beyond exchangeability and conformal risk control

### EQ-CONF-006 — Weighted conformal quantile under covariate shift

`p_i(x) = w(X_i) / (sum_j w(X_j) + w(x))`,
`p_(n+1)(x) = w(x) / (sum_j w(X_j) + w(x))`,
`q(x) = inf{q : sum_(i : S_i <= q) p_i(x) >= 1 - alpha}`, the `1 - alpha`
quantile of `sum_i p_i(x) delta_(S_i) + p_(n+1)(x) delta_(+inf)`; interval
`mu(x) +/- q(x) s(x)`.

- Domain: calibration inputs from `P`, test input from `Q`, the same
  conditional law of `Y` given `X`, and `w = dQ/dP` known up to a constant
  factor; `w >= 0`, not all zero; `0 < alpha < 1`. The quantile is located
  in exact rational arithmetic.
- Meaning: marginal coverage at least `1 - alpha` under the test law `Q`;
  with `w = 1` it is the split conformal quantile [EQ-CONF-001]. With
  estimated weights the guarantee is only approximate.
- Code: `conformal.weighted_conformal_quantile`,
  `conformal.weighted_split_conformal_regression`,
  `conformal.WeightedConformalRegressor.interval`.
- Source: [REF-TIBSHIRANI-ETAL-2019].

### EQ-CONF-007 — Nonexchangeable conformal with fixed weights and its coverage gap

`w~_i = w_i / (sum_j w_j + 1)`, `w~_(n+1) = 1 / (sum_j w_j + 1)`,
`q_hat` the `1 - alpha` quantile of
`sum_i w~_i delta_(S_i) + w~_(n+1) delta_(+inf)`, and
`P(Y_(n+1) in C(X_(n+1))) >= 1 - alpha - sum_i w~_i d_TV(R(Z), R(Z^i))`,
where `Z^i` is the data with points `i` and `n + 1` swapped and `R` the
vector of scores.

- Domain: weights `w_i` in `[0, 1]` fixed before seeing the data; a
  predictor fitted without the calibration data; no exchangeability
  assumption.
- Meaning: exchangeable data have zero gap for any fixed weights; otherwise
  small weights on points whose law differs from the test point's keep the
  gap small. The total-variation terms depend on the unknown data law, so
  the gap cannot be computed from data; the code only evaluates the sum for
  user-supplied bounds.
- Code: `conformal.nonexchangeable_conformal_quantile`,
  `conformal.nonexchangeable_split_conformal_regression`,
  `conformal.nonexchangeable_coverage_gap`.
- Source: [REF-BARBER-ETAL-2023].

### EQ-CONF-008 — Conformal risk control

`Rhat_n(lambda) = (1/n) sum_i L_i(lambda)`,
`lambda_hat = inf{lambda : (n/(n+1)) Rhat_n(lambda) + B/(n+1) <= alpha}`,
and `E[L_(n+1)(lambda_hat)] <= alpha`.

- Domain: exchangeable loss functions `L_1, ..., L_(n+1)`, each
  non-increasing in `lambda` and bounded above by `B`. The implementation
  takes the infimum over a finite increasing grid (the smallest grid value
  meeting the inequality), which keeps the guarantee for losses evaluated
  on the grid and can only be more conservative; if no grid value
  qualifies the largest is returned and flagged.
- Meaning: the expected loss, marginal over calibration set and test
  point, is bounded for any monotone bounded loss; with
  `L_i = 1{S_i > lambda}` and `B = 1` it is the split conformal quantile
  [EQ-CONF-001].
- Code: `conformal.conformal_risk_control`,
  `conformal.ConformalRiskControlResult`.
- Source: [REF-ANGELOPOULOS-ETAL-2024].

### EQ-CONF-009 — Conformal p-value

`p_j = (1 + #{i in calibration : s_i >= s_j}) / (n + 1)`, with
`P(p_j <= u) <= u` for every `u` in `[0, 1]` when test point `j` is an
inlier.

- Domain: scores for which larger means more unusual, computed by a
  function fitted without the calibration points; calibration and inlier
  test scores exchangeable.
- Meaning: marginally super-uniform (on average over the calibration set,
  not for one fixed calibration set); exactly uniform on
  `{1/(n+1), ..., 1}` when scores are almost surely distinct.
- Code: `conformal.conformal_p_values`.
- Source: [REF-BATES-ETAL-2023], [REF-VOVK-GAMMERMAN-SHAFER-2005].

### EQ-CONF-010 — False discovery rate of Benjamini-Hochberg on conformal p-values

Reject test point `j` when its Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted conformal
p-value is at most `alpha` ([EQ-INF-MT-002]); then
`FDR = E[#{rejected inliers} / max(1, #{rejected})] <= pi0 alpha <= alpha`,
`pi0` the fraction of inliers among the test points.

- Domain: conformal p-values [EQ-CONF-009] of several test points sharing
  one calibration set; independent test points; calibration points and
  test inliers independent draws from one law (the source states the PRDS
  property for scores without ties).
- Meaning: the p-values are positively dependent (PRDS), which is the
  condition under which Benjamini-Hochberg controls the FDR; the
  expectation is marginal over the calibration set.
- Code: `conformal.conformal_outlier_detection`,
  `conformal.ConformalOutlierResult`.
- Source: [REF-BATES-ETAL-2023], [REF-BENJAMINI-HOCHBERG-1995].

### EQ-CONF-011 — Mondrian (group-conditional) split conformal

For each group label `g` with `n_g` calibration scores:
`k_g = ceil((1 - alpha)(n_g + 1))`, `q_g` the `k_g`-th smallest score of
the group (`+inf` when `k_g > n_g` or `n_g = 0`), interval
`mu(x) +/- q_g s(x)` for a test point of group `g`, and
`P(Y in C(X) | G = g) >= k_g / (n_g + 1) >= 1 - alpha`.

- Domain: a group label determined by the observation and fixed before
  seeing the scores; calibration and test points exchangeable within each
  group.
- Meaning: coverage holds conditionally on the group (not on `x` within a
  group); each group pays the infinite-interval rule of [EQ-CONF-001] on
  its own sample size.
- Code: `conformal.mondrian_conformal_regression`,
  `conformal.MondrianConformalRegressor.interval`,
  `conformal.MondrianGroup`.
- Source: [REF-VOVK-GAMMERMAN-SHAFER-2005].

### EQ-CONF-012 — CV+ interval

With `K` disjoint folds `S_1, ..., S_K`, `k(i)` the fold of point `i`, and
`mu_(-S_k)` fitted without fold `k`: `R_i = |y_i - mu_(-S_k(i))(x_i)|`;
lower limit the `floor(alpha (n + 1))`-th smallest of
`mu_(-S_k(i))(x) - R_i` (`-inf` if that index is 0), upper limit the
`ceil((1 - alpha)(n + 1))`-th smallest of `mu_(-S_k(i))(x) + R_i` (`+inf`
if it exceeds `n`), over `i = 1..n`.

- Domain: exchangeable training and test data; a fitting rule symmetric in
  its training points; folds assigned without reference to the data
  values; `2 <= K <= n`.
- Meaning: `K` fits instead of the `n` of jackknife+ [EQ-CONF-004], which
  it equals for `K = n`; marginal coverage is at least
  `1 - 2 alpha - sqrt(2/n)` for every `K` (Theorem 4 of the source, for
  equal-size folds; a sharper slack depending on `n` and `K` is given
  there), and `1 - 2 alpha` for `K = n`.
- Code: `conformal.cv_plus_regression`,
  `conformal.CVPlusRegressor.interval`.
- Source: [REF-BARBER-ETAL-2021].

### EQ-CONF-013 — Online quantile-tracking update

`err_t = 1{s_t > q_t}`, `q_(t+1) = q_t + eta_t (err_t - alpha)`,
`eta_t = eta t^(-c)` with `c = 0` (fixed step) or `c = 1/2 + eps`
(decaying steps); interval `yhat_t +/- q_t sigma_t` with score
`s_t = |y_t - yhat_t| / sigma_t`.

- Domain: `0 < alpha < 1`, `eta > 0`, `0 <= c <= 1`, non-negative scores;
  no assumption on the data sequence.
- Meaning: an online subgradient step on the pinball loss of level
  `1 - alpha`; a miss raises the threshold by `eta_t (1 - alpha)`, a cover
  lowers it by `eta_t alpha`; decaying steps let the threshold settle when
  the score law is stable.
- Code: `conformal.OnlineQuantileTracker.update_score`,
  `conformal.OnlineQuantileTracker.step_size`,
  `conformal.online_quantile_intervals`.
- Source: [REF-ANGELOPOULOS-CANDES-TIBSHIRANI-2023] (fixed step),
  [REF-ANGELOPOULOS-BARBER-BATES-2024] (decaying steps).

### EQ-CONF-014 — Long-run miscoverage bound for quantile tracking

`|(1/T) sum_(t=1..T) err_t - alpha| <= (b + eta_1) / (eta_T T)` for every
`T`; for a fixed step `(b + eta) / (eta T)`.

- Domain: scores in `[0, b]`, `q_1` in `[0, b]`, positive non-increasing
  steps; holds deterministically for every score sequence. Derivation:
  `q_t` stays in `[-alpha eta_1, b + (1 - alpha) eta_1]` by induction,
  `err_t - alpha = (q_(t+1) - q_t) / eta_t`, and summation by parts
  against the non-decreasing `1/eta_t` bounds the sum by
  `(b + eta_1) / eta_T`.
- Meaning: the miss frequency converges to `alpha` at rate `1/T` for a
  fixed step and `T^(c - 1)` for `eta_t = eta t^(-c)` (no convergence is
  implied at `c = 1`); a long-run statement, not finite-sample or
  conditional coverage at any step.
- Code: `conformal.OnlineQuantileTracker.long_run_bound`,
  `conformal.OnlineQuantileResult`.
- Source: [REF-ANGELOPOULOS-CANDES-TIBSHIRANI-2023],
  [REF-ANGELOPOULOS-BARBER-BATES-2024]; the proof for non-increasing steps
  is the telescoping argument recorded in the domain bullet.

## E-values, betting confidence sequences, universal and prediction-powered inference (ADR-0119)

### EQ-INF-EVAL-001 — E-values, Markov's bound, and the e-to-p calibrator

`E >= 0` with `E_P[E] <= 1` for every law `P` of the null hypothesis. Then
`P(E >= 1/alpha) <= alpha` for `0 < alpha < 1`, and `p = min(1, 1/E)`
satisfies `P(p <= u) <= u`.

- Domain: `E` in `[0, inf]`; the bound holds for a level `alpha` fixed in
  advance.
- Meaning: rejecting when `E >= 1/alpha` is a level-`alpha` test by Markov's
  inequality; `min(1, 1/E)` is the admissible conversion of an e-value into
  a (conservative) p-value.
- Code: `inference.e_to_p_value`.
- Source: [REF-VOVK-WANG-2021].

### EQ-INF-EVAL-002 — p-to-e calibrators

`f_kappa(p) = kappa p^(kappa - 1)` for a fixed `kappa` in `(0, 1)`, and the
mixture `F(p) = integral_0^1 kappa p^(kappa - 1) d kappa
= (1 - p + p log p) / (p (log p)^2)`, with `F(1) = 1/2`, `F(0) = inf`.
Both are decreasing with `integral_0^1 f(p) dp = 1`; for the mixture
`integral_eps^1 F(p) dp = 1 - (1 - eps) / log(1/eps)`. Evaluated as
`(expm1(-L) + L) / L^2` with `L = log p`, and by the series
`1/2 - L/6 + L^2/24` for `|L| < 1e-4`.

- Domain: `p` in `[0, 1]`; `kappa` chosen before the data are seen.
- Meaning: if `P` is a p-value then `f(P)` is an e-value, because a
  decreasing `f` with unit integral has `E[f(P)] <= integral_0^1 f = 1` when
  `P` is stochastically no smaller than uniform. The mixture needs no
  tuning.
- Code: `inference.calibrate_p_value`.
- Source: [REF-VOVK-WANG-2021] (calibrators and the mixture over `kappa`);
  the closed form of the integral is rederived here by integration by parts.

### EQ-INF-EVAL-003 — Merging e-values

Arithmetic mean `sum_k w_k e_k` with fixed `w_k >= 0`, `sum_k w_k = 1`;
product `prod_k e_k`.

- Domain: the mean under arbitrary dependence; the product for independent
  e-values or sequential ones with `E[E_k | E_1, ..., E_{k-1}] <= 1`.
- Meaning: the mean is an e-value by linearity of expectation; the product
  by the tower property. For `E_1 = E_2 = 2 1{U < 1/2}` the mean has
  expectation 1 and the product 2, so the product is not valid under
  dependence.
- Code: `inference.merge_e_values`.
- Source: [REF-VOVK-WANG-2021].

### EQ-INF-EVAL-004 — The e-BH procedure

For e-values sorted as `e_(1) >= ... >= e_(K)`:
`k* = max{k : k e_(k) / K >= 1/alpha}` (zero if empty); reject the `k*`
largest. `FDR <= alpha K_0 / K` with `K_0` the number of true nulls.

- Domain: `K >= 1` e-values, each with null expectation at most one;
  arbitrary dependence between them.
- Meaning: Benjamini-Hochberg ([EQ-INF-MT-002]) applied to `1/e_k`; the
  bound needs no assumption of independence or positive dependence and no
  harmonic correction factor.
- Code: `inference.e_benjamini_hochberg`.
- Source: [REF-WANG-RAMDAS-2022].

### EQ-INF-EVAL-005 — Split and cross-fit likelihood-ratio statistics

With the data split into independent parts `D0` and `D1`,
`theta_1 = theta_1(D1)` any estimator and
`theta_0 = argmax_{theta in Theta_0} L_D0(theta)`:
`T = L_D0(theta_1) / L_D0(theta_0)`, `E_{theta*}[T] <= 1` for every
`theta*` in `Theta_0`; reject when `T >= 1/alpha`. Cross-fit:
`(T + T_swap) / 2` with the roles of the parts exchanged. For `N(theta, 1)`
and `H0: theta = 0`: `T = exp(theta_1 S_0 - n_0 theta_1^2 / 2)` with `S_0`
the sum of `D0`, and `E_0[T | D1] = 1` exactly.

- Domain: a correctly specified dominated model with likelihood `L`;
  independent parts; an exact null maximizer (or any null parameter whose
  likelihood on `D0` is at least that of the truth).
- Meaning: `E[L_D0(theta_1) / L_D0(theta*) | D1] = integral p_theta_1 <= 1`
  and `L_D0(theta_0) >= L_D0(theta*)`, so `T` is an e-value in finite
  samples without regularity conditions; the average of two e-values is an
  e-value ([EQ-INF-EVAL-003]).
- Code: `inference.split_likelihood_ratio_test`.
- Source: [REF-WASSERMAN-RAMDAS-BALAKRISHNAN-2020].

### EQ-INF-CS-001 — Betting capital process and Ville's inequality

For `x_t` in `[0, 1]` and a candidate mean `m`:
`K_t(m) = prod_{i <= t} (1 + lambda_i (x_i - m))`, `K_0 = 1`, with
`lambda_i` a function of `x_1, ..., x_{i-1}` and
`-1/(1 - m) < lambda_i < 1/m`. If `E[x_t | past] = m` for all `t` then
`K_t(m)` is a non-negative martingale and
`P(exists t >= 1 : K_t(m) >= 1/alpha) <= alpha`. For Bernoulli data and a
constant bet `K_t = (1 + lambda (1 - m))^s (1 - lambda m)^(t - s)` with `s`
successes.

- Domain: observations in a known interval `[a, b]`, rescaled by
  `x = (X - a) / (b - a)`; bets truncated to
  `[-c/(1 - m), c/m]` with `0 < c < 1`.
- Meaning: the wealth of a gambler betting against the hypothesis that the
  conditional mean is `m`; Ville's inequality bounds the probability that a
  non-negative supermartingale started at one ever reaches `1/alpha`, which
  licenses monitoring after every observation. Validity holds for every
  predictable bet; only power depends on it.
- Code: `inference.betting_mean_test`.
- Source: [REF-WAUDBY-SMITH-RAMDAS-2024]; [REF-RAMDAS-ETAL-2023] and
  [REF-HOWARD-ETAL-2021] (Ville's inequality).

### EQ-INF-CS-002 — Hedged capital and the betting confidence sequence

`K_t^+(m) = prod (1 + lambda_i^+(m)(x_i - m))`,
`K_t^-(m) = prod (1 - lambda_i^-(m)(x_i - m))` with
`lambda_i^+(m) = min(b_i, c/m)`, `lambda_i^-(m) = min(b_i, c/(1 - m))` and
sizes `b_i >= 0` that do not depend on `m`;
`K_t^pm(m) = max(theta K_t^+(m), (1 - theta) K_t^-(m))`;
`C_t = {m in [0, 1] : K_t^pm(m) < 1/alpha}` and the running intersection
`intersection_{s <= t} C_s`. `P(mu in C_t for all t) >= 1 - alpha`.

- Domain: `0 < theta < 1`; conditional means equal to `mu` at all times.
- Meaning: `K^pm <= theta K^+ + (1 - theta) K^-`, a martingale at `m = mu`,
  so Ville's inequality applies. Each factor of `K^+` is non-increasing in
  `m` and each factor of `K^-` non-decreasing, hence `C_t = (a_t, b_t)` is
  an interval with `a_t = sup{m : theta K_t^+(m) >= 1/alpha}` and
  `b_t = inf{m : (1 - theta) K_t^-(m) >= 1/alpha}`. On a grid the largest
  grid point rejected by `K^+` and the smallest rejected by `K^-` enclose
  `C_t`, so the reported interval keeps the coverage guarantee and is at
  most one cell wider on each side. With bets that depend on `m` (aGRAPA)
  the set need not be an interval. The code reports the hull of the
  surviving grid points widened by one cell, or the cells next to the
  smallest grid capital when no grid point survives, and intersects these
  intervals over time. That encloses `C_t` if `m -> K_t(m)` is
  quasi-convex, which is observed (up to bumps near 0.01 in `log K_t`) but
  not proved; the aGRAPA sequence has no unconditional guarantee.
- Code: `inference.betting_confidence_sequence`,
  `inference.ConfidenceSequence.interval`.
- Source: [REF-WAUDBY-SMITH-RAMDAS-2024] (hedged capital);
  [REF-HOWARD-ETAL-2021] (confidence sequences and running intersections).
  The monotonicity argument for the truncated bets is derived here.

### EQ-INF-CS-003 — Predictable bets

With `mu_t = (1/2 + sum_{i <= t} x_i) / (t + 1)` and
`s2_t = (1/4 + sum_{i <= t} (x_i - mu_i)^2) / (t + 1)`: plug-in size
`b_t = sqrt(2 log(1/a) / (s2_{t-1} t log(t + 1)))` with `a = alpha/2`
(two-sided) or `alpha` (one-sided); approximate GRAPA
`lambda_t(m) = (mu_{t-1} - m) / (s2_{t-1} + (mu_{t-1} - m)^2)`, clipped to
`[-c/(1 - m), c/m]`; or a constant size.

- Domain: `t >= 1`; `mu_0 = 1/2`, `s2_0 = 1/4`.
- Meaning: aGRAPA solves the first-order condition
  `sum (x_i - m) / (1 + lambda (x_i - m)) = 0` of the empirical log-growth
  after replacing `1/(1 + y)` by `1 - y`. Both rules, the regularized
  lagged moments (prior mean 1/2, prior variance 1/4, one pseudo-observation)
  and the truncation to `[-c/(1 - m), c/m]` agree with `lambda_predmix_eb`
  and `lambda_aKelly` in the source code of the authors' `confseq` package;
  the printed paper was not read. The levels `a = alpha/2` (two-sided) and
  `a = alpha` (one-sided) are a library choice. Every predictable bet in
  the admissible range gives a valid test, so the choice affects power
  only.
- Code: `inference.betting_mean_test`,
  `inference.betting_confidence_sequence`.
- Source: [REF-WAUDBY-SMITH-RAMDAS-2024].

### EQ-INF-CS-004 — One-sided sequential test and anytime-valid p-value

For `H0: E[x_t | past] <= m0` for all `t`: `K_t^+(m0)` with
`lambda_i^+ >= 0` is a non-negative supermartingale; stop and reject at
`tau = inf{t : K_t >= 1/alpha}`; `p_t = min(1, 1 / max_{s <= t} K_s)` is
valid at every stopping time. `H0: E[x_t | past] >= m0` uses `K_t^-`. Paired
streams: `D_t = A_t - B_t` in `[-B, B]`, tested through
`x_t = (D_t + B) / (2B)` and `m = (d_0 + B) / (2B)`.

- Domain: bounded observations; no independence or identical distribution
  is required, only the bound on the conditional means.
- Meaning: `E[1 + lambda (x - m0) | past] <= 1` when `lambda >= 0` and the
  conditional mean is at most `m0`; Ville's inequality gives
  `P(tau < inf) <= alpha` and `P(exists t : p_t <= u) <= u`.
- Code: `inference.betting_mean_test`, `inference.paired_betting_test`.
- Source: [REF-WAUDBY-SMITH-RAMDAS-2024], [REF-RAMDAS-ETAL-2023].

### EQ-INF-PPI-001 — Prediction-powered mean estimator

`theta_hat_w = mean_n(Y) + w (mean_N(F) - mean_n(f))` with labels `Y_i`,
predictions `f_i = f(X_i)` on the `n` labelled units and `F_j = f(X~_j)` on
`N` unlabelled units. `E[theta_hat_w] = E[Y]` for every fixed `w`.

- Domain: labelled and unlabelled units drawn independently from one
  population; `f` fixed in advance.
- Meaning: `w = 0` is the classical mean; `w = 1` is
  `mean_N(F) + mean_n(Y - f)`, the prediction mean corrected by the
  rectifier.
- Code: `inference.prediction_powered_mean`.
- Source: [REF-ANGELOPOULOS-ETAL-2023] (`w = 1`),
  [REF-ANGELOPOULOS-DUCHI-ZRNIC-2023] (general weight).

### EQ-INF-PPI-002 — Variance and normal-approximation interval

`Var(theta_hat_w) = Var(Y - w f) / n + w^2 Var(f) / N
= (Var(Y) - 2 w Cov(Y, f) + w^2 Var(f)) / n + w^2 Var(f) / N`. Estimated by
`V(w) = s^2(Y - w f) / n + w^2 s^2(F) / N` with sample variances; interval
`theta_hat_w +- z_{(1 + gamma)/2} sqrt(V(w))`.

- Domain: finite second moments; `n >= 2`, `N >= 2` for the estimate. The
  variance formula is exact for fixed `w`; the interval is asymptotic.
- Meaning: `theta_hat_w = mean_n(Y - w f) + w mean_N(F)` is a sum of two
  independent sample means (derived here).
- Code: `inference.prediction_powered_variance`,
  `inference.prediction_powered_mean`.
- Source: [REF-ANGELOPOULOS-DUCHI-ZRNIC-2023],
  [REF-ANGELOPOULOS-ETAL-2023].

### EQ-INF-PPI-003 — Power-tuned weight

`w* = Cov(Y, f) / ((1 + n/N) Var(f))`, with minimum variance
`Var(Y) (1 - rho^2 / (1 + n/N)) / n`. Sample version, the exact minimizer of
`V(w)`: `w_hat = (s_Yf / n) / (s_f^2 / n + s_F^2 / N)`.

- Domain: `Var(f) > 0` (otherwise `w* = 0`).
- Meaning: the root of
  `d Var / d w = -2 Cov(Y, f)/n + 2 w Var(f)(1/n + 1/N)`; since `V` is a
  convex quadratic, `V(w_hat) <= V(w)` for all `w`, in particular for the
  classical `w = 0` and the original `w = 1`.
- Code: `inference.prediction_powered_weight`,
  `inference.prediction_powered_mean`.
- Source: [REF-ANGELOPOULOS-DUCHI-ZRNIC-2023]; the derivation and the
  two-sample plug-in `w_hat` are worked out here.

## Importance-sampling diagnostics and further samplers (ADR-0122)

### EQ-INF-PSIS-001 — Pareto smoothing of the largest importance ratios

For `S` ratios `r_s` with order statistics `r_(1) <= ... <= r_(S)`, tail
size `M = ceil(min(S / 5, 3 sqrt(S)))`, and threshold `u = r_(S-M)`: fit a
generalized Pareto law `F(x) = 1 - (1 + k x / sigma)^(-1/k)` to the
exceedances `r_(S-M+z) - u`, and replace
`r_(S-M+z) <- min(u + F^-1((z - 1/2) / M), r_(S))`, `z = 1, ..., M`, with
`F^-1(p) = sigma ((1 - p)^(-k) - 1) / k`.

- Domain: `S` draws from the proposal; the tail is smoothed only when
  `5 <= M < S` and the fit is not degenerate, otherwise the raw ratios are
  kept and `k-hat = inf` is reported. The ceiling in `M` follows the
  reference implementation of the source.
- Meaning: the largest ratios, which carry most of the variance, are
  replaced by the expected order statistics of their fitted tail law; the
  truncation keeps the smoothed weights no larger than the largest raw one.
- Code: `inference.pareto_smooth`, `inference.psis_tail_size`,
  `inference.GeneralizedParetoFit.quantile`, `inference.psis_expectation`.
- Source: [REF-VEHTARI-ETAL-2024, Algorithm 1].

### EQ-INF-PSIS-002 — Profile estimator of the generalized Pareto tail

With sorted exceedances `x_(1) <= ... <= x_(N)` and `theta = -k / sigma`:
`k(theta) = (1/N) sum_i log(1 - theta x_i)`,
`l(theta) = N (log(-theta / k(theta)) - k(theta) - 1)`,
`theta_j = 1 / x_(N) + (1 - sqrt(G / (j - 1/2))) / (3 x*)`, `j = 1..G`,
`G = 30 + floor(sqrt(N))`, `x* = x_(floor(N/4 + 1/2))`,
`theta_hat = sum_j theta_j exp(l(theta_j)) / sum_j exp(l(theta_j))`,
`k_hat = k(theta_hat)`, `sigma_hat = -k_hat / theta_hat`, and with the weak
prior `k_hat <- (N k_hat + 5) / (N + 10)`.

- Domain: `N >= 5` non-negative exceedances with `x* > x_(1)` and
  `x_(N) > 0`.
- Meaning: an empirical-Bayes posterior mean of `theta` under the profile
  likelihood (the Zhang-Stephens estimator as used by PSIS); the prior on
  `k` is worth ten observations at `0.5` and stabilizes small tails.
- Code: `inference.fit_generalized_pareto`.
- Source: [REF-VEHTARI-ETAL-2024]; the grid and prior constants follow
  the reference implementation of that paper.

### EQ-INF-PSIS-003 — Self-normalized estimate, k-hat threshold, and ESS

With smoothed weights `w_s` and `w~_s = w_s / sum_t w_t`:
`mu_hat = sum_s w~_s h(x_s)`, `se^2 = sum_s w~_s^2 (h(x_s) - mu_hat)^2`,
`ESS = 1 / sum_s w~_s^2`; the estimate is flagged reliable when
`k_hat < min(1 - 1 / log10(S), 0.7)`.

- Domain: independent draws for the standard error; the threshold needs
  `S >= 2` and is non-positive for `S <= 10`.
- Meaning: `1 - 1 / log10(S)` is the largest shape for which `S` exceeds
  the minimum sample size `10^(1 / (1 - k))` of the source. For a proposal
  `N(0, 1)` and target `N(0, s^2)`, `s > 1`, the ratio is
  `exp(x^2 (1 - 1/s^2) / 2) / s`, so `P(r > t)` decays like
  `t^(-1 / (1 - 1/s^2))` up to a logarithmic factor and the tail shape is
  `k = 1 - 1 / s^2`.
- Code: `inference.PSISResult.expectation`, `inference.pareto_k_threshold`,
  `inference.PSISResult.reliable`, `inference.ImportanceEstimate`.
- Source: [REF-VEHTARI-ETAL-2024].

### EQ-INF-PSIS-004 — PSIS leave-one-out predictive density

For draws `theta_s` from the full posterior and ratios
`r_s^(i) = 1 / p(y_i | theta_s)` with smoothed weights `w_s^(i)`:
`elpd_loo,i = log( sum_s w_s^(i) p(y_i | theta_s) / sum_s w_s^(i) )`,
`elpd_loo = sum_i elpd_loo,i`, `se = sqrt(n Var_i(elpd_loo,i))`,
`p_loo = sum_i [ log((1/S) sum_s p(y_i | theta_s)) - elpd_loo,i ]`.

- Domain: observations conditionally independent given the parameters;
  `S x n` pointwise log-likelihoods with all normalizing constants.
- Meaning: importance sampling from the full posterior to each
  leave-one-out posterior, which is proportional to the full posterior
  divided by `p(y_i | theta)`; the per-observation `k-hat` flags
  observations whose removal changes the posterior too much for the
  estimate to be trusted.
- Code: `inference.psis_loo`, `inference.PSISLOOResult`.
- Source: [REF-VEHTARI-GELMAN-GABRY-2017].

### EQ-INF-NRHAT-001 — Nested R-hat

For draws `f_(nmk)` (draw `n`, chain `m`, superchain `k`), chain means
`f_(.mk)` and superchain means `f_(..k)`:
`B = (1/(K-1)) sum_k (f_(..k) - f_(...))^2`,
`B~_k = (1/(M-1)) sum_m (f_(.mk) - f_(..k))^2` (zero if `M = 1`),
`W~_k = (1/M) sum_m (1/(N-1)) sum_n (f_(nmk) - f_(.mk))^2` (zero if
`N = 1`), `W = (1/K) sum_k (B~_k + W~_k)`, `nR-hat = sqrt(1 + B / W)`.

- Domain: `K >= 2` superchains of `M` chains of `N` draws, not
  `M = N = 1`; chains of a superchain share their starting point.
- Meaning: compares the variance of superchain means with the variance
  inside superchains; for stationary independent chains `B / W` is about
  `1 / (M (N + 1))`, so the statistic approaches one as the number of
  chains per superchain grows. With `M = 1` its square exceeds the square
  of the non-split `R-hat` of [EQ-MCMC-RHAT-001] by exactly `1 / N`.
- Code: `inference.nested_rhat`, `inference.NestedRhat`.
- Source: [REF-MARGOSSIAN-ETAL-2024, Eqs. 6-8].

### EQ-INF-SVGD-001 — Stein variational gradient direction

`x_i <- x_i + eps phi(x_i)`,
`phi(x) = (1/n) sum_j [ k(x_j, x) grad log p(x_j) + grad_{x_j} k(x_j, x) ]`.

- Domain: differentiable `log p`; a positive-definite kernel `k`; fixed
  step `eps > 0` in this library.
- Meaning: the direction of steepest descent of the Kullback-Leibler
  divergence to `p` within the unit ball of the kernel's RKHS. With
  `n = 1` it is gradient ascent on `log p`. The particles are not
  independent draws, and few particles in several dimensions underestimate
  the variance of `p`.
- Code: `inference.svgd_direction`,
  `inference.stein_variational_gradient_descent`, `inference.SVGDResult`.
- Source: [REF-LIU-WANG-2016, Algorithm 1].

### EQ-INF-SVGD-002 — RBF kernel with the median-heuristic bandwidth

`k(x, x') = exp(-|x - x'|^2 / h)`, `grad_{x'} k(x', x) = (2 / h) (x - x') k`,
`h = med^2 / log n` with `med` the median pairwise distance of the
particles.

- Domain: `n >= 2` particles with a positive median distance (otherwise
  the library uses `h = 1`).
- Meaning: a heuristic that makes `sum_j k(x_i, x_j)` about one, so the
  attraction and repulsion terms of [EQ-INF-SVGD-001] are balanced.
- Code: `inference.median_bandwidth`, `inference.svgd_direction`.
- Source: [REF-LIU-WANG-2016, Section 5].

### EQ-INF-SLICE-001 — Univariate slice sampling with stepping out and shrinkage

Given `x_0`: `log y = log f(x_0) - E`, `E ~ Exp(1)`;
`L = x_0 - w U`, `R = L + w`; while `f(L) > y`: `L <- L - w`; while
`f(R) > y`: `R <- R + w` (at most `J = floor(m V)` and `m - 1 - J` steps
when a limit `m` is set); repeat `x_1 ~ U(L, R)` until `f(x_1) > y`,
setting `L <- x_1` if `x_1 < x_0` and `R <- x_1` otherwise after each
failure.

- Domain: any `w > 0`; applied to each coordinate in turn with the others
  fixed.
- Meaning: uniform sampling under the graph of `f`; the interval-finding
  and shrinkage rules are constructed so that the transition is reversible
  with respect to the uniform law on the slice, hence leaves `f` invariant
  without a tuned proposal scale.
- Code: `inference.slice_sampler`.
- Source: [REF-NEAL-2003, Figures 3 and 5].

### EQ-INF-SLICE-002 — Elliptical slice sampling

For `pi(f) proportional to L(f) N(f; mu, Sigma)`: `nu ~ N(0, Sigma)`,
`log y = log L(f) + log U`, `theta ~ U[0, 2 pi)`,
`[theta_min, theta_max] = [theta - 2 pi, theta]`;
`f' = mu + (f - mu) cos(theta) + nu sin(theta)`; accept if
`log L(f') > log y`, else set `theta_min = theta` if `theta < 0` or
`theta_max = theta` otherwise, redraw `theta ~ U[theta_min, theta_max]`,
and repeat.

- Domain: Gaussian prior with positive-definite `Sigma`; a start with
  positive likelihood.
- Meaning: every point of the ellipse through `f` and `nu` has the prior
  law, so the prior cancels and slice sampling over the angle needs only
  the likelihood; there is no step size and no rejection.
- Code: `inference.elliptical_slice_sampler`.
- Source: [REF-MURRAY-ADAMS-MACKAY-2010, Figure 2].

### EQ-INF-MALA-001 — Metropolis-adjusted Langevin proposal and acceptance

`x' = x + (eps^2 / 2) grad log pi(x) + eps xi`, `xi ~ N(0, I)`;
`q(x' | x) = N(x'; x + (eps^2 / 2) grad log pi(x), eps^2 I)`;
`alpha = min(1, pi(x') q(x | x') / (pi(x) q(x' | x)))`.

- Domain: differentiable `log pi`; fixed `eps > 0`.
- Meaning: the Euler step of the Langevin diffusion used as a
  Metropolis-Hastings proposal; the correction removes the discretization
  bias. Not geometrically ergodic when the gradient grows faster than
  linearly in the tails.
- Code: `inference.metropolis_adjusted_langevin`,
  `inference.mala_log_acceptance_ratio`.
- Source: [REF-ROBERTS-TWEEDIE-1996].

### EQ-INF-STRETCH-001 — Affine-invariant stretch move

For walker `x_k` and a partner `x_j` from the complementary ensemble:
`z = ((a - 1) U + 1)^2 / a` (density proportional to `1 / sqrt(z)` on
`[1/a, a]`), `y = x_j + z (x_k - x_j)`, accept with probability
`min(1, z^(d - 1) pi(y) / pi(x_k))`.

- Domain: `a > 1` (2 by default); more walkers than the dimension `d`,
  not confined to a lower-dimensional affine subspace. The library updates
  two half-ensembles alternately, each walker drawing its partner from the
  other half.
- Meaning: the proposal uses only differences of walkers, so the Markov
  chain of the ensemble is equivariant under affine maps of the target;
  `g(1/z) = z g(z)` gives the factor `z^(d - 1)` in the ratio.
- Code: `inference.stretch_move_sampler`, `inference.EnsembleResult`.
- Source: [REF-GOODMAN-WEARE-2010].

### EQ-INF-PT-001 — Replica exchange acceptance with even-odd swaps

For replicas `x_i ~ pi_i(x) proportional to p(x) L(x)^beta_i` and
`l = log L`, the exchange of `x_i` and `x_{i+1}` is accepted with
probability `min(1, exp((beta_i - beta_{i+1}) (l(x_{i+1}) - l(x_i))))`;
pairs with even `i` are proposed at even iterations and pairs with odd `i`
at odd iterations.

- Domain: `beta_0 < ... < beta_T = 1`, `beta_0 >= 0`; a proper prior when
  `beta_0 = 0`.
- Meaning: the Metropolis ratio
  `pi_i(x_{i+1}) pi_{i+1}(x_i) / (pi_i(x_i) pi_{i+1}(x_{i+1}))` of a swap,
  in which the prior cancels; the deterministic alternation is the
  non-reversible scheme whose round-trip rate does not vanish as the
  ladder is refined.
- Code: `inference.parallel_tempering`,
  `inference.ParallelTemperingResult`.
- Source: [REF-HUKUSHIMA-NEMOTO-1996] (exchange acceptance);
  [REF-SYED-ETAL-2022] (deterministic even-odd scheme, rejection rates,
  round trips).

### EQ-INF-PT-002 — Stepping-stone evidence from the tempering ladder

With `Z(beta) = integral p(x) L(x)^beta dx`:
`Z(beta') / Z(beta) = E_{pi_beta}[ L^(beta' - beta) ]`, so
`log Z(1) - log Z(beta_0) =
sum_i log( (1/n) sum_t exp((beta_{i+1} - beta_i) l(x_i^(t))) )` in the
limit of long runs.

- Domain: `beta_0 = 0` and a normalized prior give `Z(beta_0) = 1`; `L`
  must include its normalizing constants for `Z(1)` to be the marginal
  likelihood. No standard error is reported (autocorrelated, dependent
  replicas).
- Meaning: the identity follows from
  `integral p L^beta L^(beta' - beta) dx / Z(beta)`; it is the incremental
  weight of [EQ-SMC-TEMPER-001] averaged over Markov chain draws instead of
  particles. The estimate of each ratio is unbiased for independent
  stationary draws; its logarithm is biased low by about half its variance.
- Code: `inference.ParallelTemperingResult.log_evidence`,
  `inference.parallel_tempering`.
- Source: derived here from the tempered path of [REF-SYED-ETAL-2022];
  the increment is that of [REF-DELMORAL-DOUCET-JASRA-2006].

## Multi-fidelity surrogates, stochastic kriging, Bayesian quadrature, and Bayesian optimization (ADR-0125)

### EQ-SUR-MF-001 — Recursive AR(1) co-kriging predictor

`Z_1 ~ GP(b_1, k_1)` and, for `t = 2..s`,
`Z_t(x) = rho_(t-1) Z_(t-1)(x) + delta_t(x)` with
`delta_t ~ GP(b_t, k_t)` independent of `Z_(t-1)`. On nested designs
`D_s subset ... subset D_1`, with `(m_1, s_1^2)` the GP posterior of `Z_1`
given `z_1` and `(m_delta_t, s_delta_t^2)` the GP posterior of `delta_t`
given `z_t - rho_(t-1) z_(t-1)(D_t)`:
`m_t(x) = rho_(t-1) m_(t-1)(x) + m_delta_t(x)`,
`s_t^2(x) = rho_(t-1)^2 s_(t-1)^2(x) + s_delta_t^2(x)`.

- Domain: nested designs (every point of `D_t` is a point of `D_(t-1)`);
  `rho`, `b_t`, and the kernel hyperparameters fixed (plug-in variance).
- Meaning: the map `(z_1, ..., z_s) -> (z_1, z_2 - rho_1 z_1(D_2), ...)` is
  a bijection onto independent data sets, so the joint Gaussian conditional
  with the block AR(1) covariance factorizes into `s` ordinary GP
  regressions; the recursion equals the joint co-kriging predictor.
- Code: `surrogates.RecursiveCoKriging.level_predictions`,
  `surrogates.RecursiveCoKriging.predict_with_variance`,
  `surrogates.RecursiveCoKriging.predict`,
  `surrogates.fit_recursive_cokriging`,
  `surrogates.gaussian_process_from_hyperparameters`.
- Source: [REF-KENNEDY-OHAGAN-2000] (autoregressive model) and
  [REF-LE-GRATIET-GARNIER-2014] (recursive formulation).

### EQ-SUR-MF-002 — Generalized least-squares scale factor

With `H = [1, z_(t-1)(D_t)]` and `R` the correlation matrix of `delta_t` on
`D_t`: `(b_t, rho_(t-1))' = (H' R^-1 H)^-1 H' R^-1 z_t`,
`sigma_t^2 = (z_t - H beta)' R^-1 (z_t - H beta) / n_t`; the length scales
maximize the concentrated likelihood [EQ-SUR-UK-001], [EQ-SUR-UK-002].

- Domain: `n_t >= 3` points in `D_t`; lower-fidelity responses not constant
  on `D_t` (otherwise `H` is rank deficient).
- Meaning: universal kriging of level `t` with the observed lower-fidelity
  responses as a regressor; the lower code enters only through its runs at
  `D_t`, which is why nesting is required.
- Code: `surrogates.fit_recursive_cokriging`.
- Source: [REF-LE-GRATIET-GARNIER-2014] and [REF-KENNEDY-OHAGAN-2000].

### EQ-SUR-SK-001 — Stochastic kriging predictor

`Ybar_i = (1/n_i) sum_j Y_j(x_i)`, `Sigma = S_M + S_e` with
`S_M[i][j] = tau^2 r(x_i, x_j)` and `S_e = diag(V(x_i) / n_i)`, `V(x_i)`
replaced by the sample variance of the replications:
`Yhat(x0) = b0 + S_M(x0, .)' Sigma^-1 (Ybar - b0 1)`; when `b0` is not given,
`b0 = 1' Sigma^-1 Ybar / 1' Sigma^-1 1`.

- Domain: independent replications (no common random numbers), `n_i >= 2`
  to estimate `V(x_i)`; `Sigma` positive definite.
- Meaning: best linear predictor of the mean response from sample means with
  heteroscedastic noise; with equal `V / n` it is GP regression with a
  homoscedastic noise variance.
- Code: `surrogates.StochasticKriging.predict_with_variance`,
  `surrogates.StochasticKriging.predict`,
  `surrogates.fit_stochastic_kriging`,
  `surrogates.stochastic_kriging_from_summaries`.
- Source: [REF-ANKENMAN-NELSON-STAUM-2010].

### EQ-SUR-SK-002 — Stochastic kriging mean squared error

With `c = S_M(x0, .)`:
`MSE(x0) = tau^2 - c' Sigma^-1 c + (1 - 1' Sigma^-1 c)^2 / (1' Sigma^-1 1)`;
the last term is dropped when `b0` is known.

- Domain: `S_e` and the kernel hyperparameters treated as known.
- Meaning: variance of `Y(x0) - Yhat(x0)` for the mean response surface; the
  last term is the variance contribution of the generalized least-squares
  estimate of `b0`, obtained from the unbiased linear predictor with weights
  `lambda = Sigma^-1 c + Sigma^-1 1 (1 - 1' Sigma^-1 c) / (1' Sigma^-1 1)`.
- Code: `surrogates.StochasticKriging.predict_with_variance`.
- Source: [REF-ANKENMAN-NELSON-STAUM-2010].

### EQ-SUR-SK-003 — Profile likelihood of the extrinsic hyperparameters

`log L(tau^2, ell) = -(1/2) (log det Sigma + (Ybar - b0 1)' Sigma^-1
(Ybar - b0 1) + k log 2 pi)` with `Sigma = S_M(tau^2, ell) + S_e`, `S_e`
fixed, and `b0` the generalized least-squares estimate at each
`(tau^2, ell)`.

- Domain: at least two design points with distinct sample means and
  non-constant inputs.
- Meaning: Gaussian likelihood of the sample means with the intrinsic
  variances plugged in.
- Code: `surrogates.stochastic_kriging_from_summaries`,
  `surrogates.fit_stochastic_kriging`.
- Source: [REF-ANKENMAN-NELSON-STAUM-2010].

### EQ-SUR-BQ-001 — Bayesian quadrature posterior

For `f ~ GP(m, k)`, `y_i = f(x_i)`, and a probability measure `pi`:
`z_i = int k(x, x_i) pi(dx)`, `kk = int int k(x, x') pi(dx) pi(dx')`,
`E[I | y] = m + z' K^-1 (y - m 1)`, `Var[I | y] = kk - z' K^-1 z`.

- Domain: positive-definite `K` (plus an optional noise diagonal); kernel
  hyperparameters fixed.
- Meaning: `I = int f dpi` is a linear functional of a Gaussian process, so
  it is Gaussian; the weights `K^-1 z` do not depend on the data, and the
  variance cannot increase when nodes are added.
- Code: `surrogates.bayesian_quadrature`,
  `surrogates.BayesianQuadratureResult.standard_deviation`.
- Source: [REF-OHAGAN-1991].

### EQ-SUR-BQ-002 — Squared-exponential kernel integrals, Gaussian measure

For `k(x, x') = exp(-(x - x')^2 / (2 ell^2))` and `pi = N(b, s^2)`:
`z(x) = sqrt(ell^2 / (ell^2 + s^2)) exp(-(x - b)^2 / (2 (ell^2 + s^2)))`,
`kk = sqrt(ell^2 / (ell^2 + 2 s^2))`. In `d` dimensions with a product
measure both are products over the coordinates, times `sigma_f^2`.

- Domain: `ell > 0`, `s > 0`.
- Meaning: the kernel is `ell sqrt(2 pi)` times the `N(x', ell^2)` density,
  so `z` is a Gaussian convolution; `kk` follows from `X - X' ~ N(0, 2 s^2)`.
- Code: `surrogates.kernel_mean`, `surrogates.kernel_double_integral`.
- Source: [REF-OHAGAN-1991] for the rule; the closed forms are standard
  Gaussian integrals, verified against `numerics.integrate` in
  `tests/test_multifidelity_surrogates.py`.

### EQ-SUR-BQ-003 — Squared-exponential kernel integrals, uniform measure

For the same kernel and `pi` uniform on `[a, c]`, `w = c - a`:
`z(x) = ell sqrt(pi/2) / w (erf((c - x) / (sqrt(2) ell))
- erf((a - x) / (sqrt(2) ell)))`,
`kk = (2 / w^2) (w ell sqrt(pi/2) erf(w / (sqrt(2) ell))
- ell^2 (1 - exp(-w^2 / (2 ell^2))))`.

- Domain: `ell > 0`, `a < c`.
- Meaning: `z` integrates a Gaussian bump over an interval; `kk` uses the
  triangular density `2 (w - v) / w^2` of `|X - X'|` on `[0, w]`.
- Code: `surrogates.kernel_mean`, `surrogates.kernel_double_integral`.
- Source: derived for this library from [REF-NIST-DLMF, Section 7.2] (error
  function); verified against `numerics.integrate` in
  `tests/test_multifidelity_surrogates.py`.

### EQ-DES-BO-001 — Expected improvement

For `F ~ N(mu, s^2)` and incumbent `f*`:
`EI = E[max(F - f*, 0)] = s h(z)`, `h(z) = phi(z) + z Phi(z)`,
`z = (mu - f*) / s` (maximization); for minimization
`EI = E[max(f* - F, 0)]` with `z = (f* - mu) / s`. `EI = max(+-(mu - f*), 0)`
when `s = 0`.

- Domain: `s >= 0`, finite `mu` and `f*`.
- Meaning: `h(z) = E[max(z + Z, 0)]` for standard normal `Z`; `h' = Phi`.
- Code: `design.expected_improvement`, `design.improvement_function`,
  `design.bayesian_optimization`.
- Source: [REF-JONES-SCHONLAU-WELCH-1998].

### EQ-DES-BO-002 — Stable logarithm of the improvement function

For `z <= -1`, `t = -z`, and the Mills ratio
`R(t) = (1 - Phi(t)) / phi(t) = 1 / (t + c(t))`,
`c(t) = 1 / (t + 2 / (t + 3 / (t + ...)))`:
`h(z) = phi(t) (1 - t R(t)) = phi(t) c(t) / (t + c(t))`, so
`log h(z) = -t^2/2 - log sqrt(2 pi) + log c(t) - log(t + c(t))`. For
`z > -1`, `log h(z) = log(phi(z) + z Phi(z))` directly.
`log EI = log s + log h(z)`.

- Domain: every real `z`; the continued fraction is truncated after
  `30 + 300 / t^2` terms.
- Meaning: `phi(z) + z Phi(z)` cancels to `phi(z) / z^2` in the lower tail
  and underflows near `z = -38`; the continued-fraction form has no
  subtraction (`log h(-40) = -808.2986`).
- Code: `design.log_improvement_function`,
  `design.log_expected_improvement`, `design.improvement_function`.
- Source: [REF-AMENT-ETAL-2023] (log expected improvement) and
  [REF-NIST-DLMF, Section 7.9] (continued fraction of the complementary
  error function); the continued-fraction form of `log h` is this library's
  derivation, verified against 50-digit arithmetic in
  `tests/test_bayesian_optimization.py`.

### EQ-DES-BO-003 — Confidence bounds and the GP-UCB schedule

`UCB(x) = mu(x) + sqrt(beta) s(x)` (maximization),
`LCB(x) = mu(x) - sqrt(beta) s(x)` (minimization); for a finite decision set
`D` and round `t`, `beta_t = 2 log(|D| t^2 pi^2 / (6 delta))`.

- Domain: `beta >= 0`; `t >= 1`, `|D| >= 1`, `0 < delta < 1`.
- Meaning: optimism in the face of uncertainty; the schedule gives a
  high-probability regret bound for a GP with known kernel on a finite set,
  and is a heuristic otherwise.
- Code: `design.confidence_bound`, `design.gp_ucb_beta`,
  `design.bayesian_optimization`.
- Source: [REF-SRINIVAS-ETAL-2010].

### EQ-DES-BO-004 — Constrained expected improvement

With constraints `c_k(x) <= t_k` modelled by independent Gaussian laws
`N(mu_k, s_k^2)`: `cEI = EI * prod_k Phi((t_k - mu_k) / s_k)`, with `f*` the
best feasible value.
