- Domain: independent objective and constraint models.
- Meaning: expected feasible improvement; equals `EI` when every constraint
  is certainly satisfied and zero when one is certainly violated.
- Code: `design.constrained_expected_improvement`,
  `design.probability_of_feasibility`, `design.bayesian_optimization`.
- Source: [REF-GARDNER-ETAL-2014].

### EQ-DES-BO-005 — Knowledge gradient for independent normal beliefs

For beliefs `theta_x ~ N(mu_x, s_x^2)` and measurement noise variance
`lambda_x`: `st_x = s_x^2 / sqrt(s_x^2 + lambda_x)`,
`zeta_x = -|mu_x - max_(y != x) mu_y| / st_x`,
`KG_x = st_x h(zeta_x)` with `h` of [EQ-DES-BO-001].

- Domain: at least two alternatives; `s_x >= 0`, `lambda_x >= 0`.
- Meaning: after one measurement of `x` the posterior mean is
  `mu_x + st_x Z`, so `KG_x = E[max_y mu'_y] - max_y mu_y`.
- Code: `design.knowledge_gradient`.
- Source: [REF-FRAZIER-POWELL-DAYANIK-2008].

### EQ-DES-BO-006 — Joint GP posterior draw on a finite set

For candidates `x_1..x_m`: `mean_i = mu(x_i)`,
`C_ij = k(x_i, x_j) - k_i' K^-1 k_j`, and a draw `f = mean + L z` with
`L L' = C` and `z ~ N(0, I)`; Thompson sampling evaluates
`argmin_i f_i` (or `argmax_i f_i`).

- Domain: fitted GP; `C` positive semidefinite (a relative jitter `1e-10`
  on the diagonal absorbs rounding).
- Meaning: a candidate is selected with its posterior probability of being
  the best of the candidate set.
- Code: `design.gaussian_process_joint_posterior`,
  `design.thompson_sample`, `design.bayesian_optimization`.
- Source: [REF-RASMUSSEN-WILLIAMS-2006, Section 2.2].

## Multifidelity Monte Carlo, approximate control variates, and MLBLUE (ADR-0117)

Models are indexed from zero in the code and in these records: model 0 is
the high-fidelity model (model 1 of the sources). `C_ij = Cov(f_i, f_j)`,
`s_i = sqrt(C_ii)`, `rho_i = C_0i / (s_0 s_i)`, and `w_i` is the cost of one
evaluation of model `i`.

### EQ-MC-MF-001 — Pilot statistics of several models

For `k` models evaluated on the same `n` inputs,
`ybar_i = (1/n) sum_j y_i^(j)`,
`C_ij = (1/(n-1)) sum_j (y_i^(j) - ybar_i)(y_j^(j) - ybar_j)`, and
`rho_ij = C_ij / sqrt(C_ii C_jj)`.

- Domain: `n >= 2` independent inputs; a positive-definite `C` needs
  `n > k`; the correlation needs `C_ii > 0`.
- Meaning: the covariance that fixes the weights and allocations of the
  multifidelity estimators. The pilot sample must be independent of the
  estimation samples; variances predicted from a pilot `C` are estimates.
- Code: `monte_carlo.pilot_statistics`,
  `monte_carlo.PilotStatistics.correlation`,
  `monte_carlo.PilotStatistics.standard_deviations`.
- Source: [REF-PEHERSTORFER-WILLCOX-GUNZBURGER-2016, Section 3] (pilot
  estimates of the correlations and variances).

### EQ-MC-MF-002 — Multifidelity Monte Carlo estimator and its variance

With nested samples `m_0 <= m_1 <= ... <= m_(q-1)` (model `i` is evaluated
on the first `m_i` shared inputs) and coefficients `a_i`,
`s = ybar^0_(m_0) + sum_(i=1..q-1) a_i (ybar^i_(m_i) - ybar^i_(m_(i-1)))`,
`E[s] = E[f_0]`, and
`Var(s) = C_00 / m_0 + sum_(i=1..q-1) (1/m_(i-1) - 1/m_i)
(a_i^2 C_ii - 2 a_i C_0i)`.
The formula follows from
`Cov(ybar^i_m, ybar^j_n) = C_ij / max(m, n)` on nested samples; the
differences of different models are uncorrelated.

- Domain: independent identically distributed inputs, finite second
  moments, coefficients fixed with respect to the samples.
- Meaning: the low-fidelity models enter through differences of two means
  of the same model, so their unknown means cancel and the estimator is
  unbiased for any `a_i`.
- Code: `monte_carlo.mfmc_estimate`, `monte_carlo.mfmc_variance`,
  `monte_carlo.MultifidelityEstimate.standard_error`.
- Source: [REF-PEHERSTORFER-WILLCOX-GUNZBURGER-2016, Section 3]; re-derived
  and checked against exact covariances of sample means in
  `tests/test_multifidelity.py`.

### EQ-MC-MF-003 — Optimal MFMC coefficients and sample allocation

`a_i = rho_i s_0 / s_i`,
`r_i = m_i / m_0 = sqrt(w_0 (rho_i^2 - rho_(i+1)^2) / (w_i (1 - rho_1^2)))`
with `rho_q = 0`, `m_0 = p / sum_i w_i r_i`, and the minimal variance
`C_00 (sum_(i=0..q-1) sqrt(w_i (rho_i^2 - rho_(i+1)^2)))^2 / p`.
Integer sample sizes are `floor(m_i)`.

- Domain: models ordered and admissible as in [EQ-MC-MF-004]; budget
  `p >= sum_i w_i r_i` so that `m_0 >= 1`.
- Meaning: minimizes [EQ-MC-MF-002] over coefficients and real sample sizes
  subject to `sum_i w_i m_i = p` and nested samples; plain Monte Carlo with
  the same budget has variance `C_00 w_0 / p`.
- Code: `monte_carlo.mfmc_allocation`,
  `monte_carlo.MFMCAllocation.variance_ratio`.
- Source: [REF-PEHERSTORFER-WILLCOX-GUNZBURGER-2016, Section 3].

### EQ-MC-MF-004 — MFMC admissibility and model selection

The allocation [EQ-MC-MF-003] is the optimum when
`1 = |rho_0| > |rho_1| > ... > |rho_(q-1)| > 0` and
`w_(i-1) / w_i > (rho_(i-1)^2 - rho_i^2) / (rho_i^2 - rho_(i+1)^2)` for
`i = 1..q-1` (`rho_q = 0`). Model selection orders every subset that
contains model 0 by decreasing `|rho_i|`, keeps the admissible subsets, and
returns the one with the smallest value of
`(sum_i sqrt(w_i (rho_i^2 - rho_(i+1)^2)))^2`.

- Domain: at most 12 models (exhaustive search over `2^(k-1)` subsets).
- Meaning: the cost condition is equivalent to strictly increasing ratios
  `r_i`; a model that is too expensive for its correlation is left out.
- Code: `monte_carlo.mfmc_admissible`, `monte_carlo.select_mfmc_models`.
- Source: [REF-PEHERSTORFER-WILLCOX-GUNZBURGER-2016, Section 3].

### EQ-MC-MF-005 — Approximate control variate, optimal weights, variance

`Q = Q_0 + sum_i alpha_i D_i` with `Q_0 = mean_N f_0`,
`D_i = mean_N f_i - mu_hat_i`, where `mu_hat_i` is the mean of `f_i` over
`r_i N` inputs. `alpha* = -Cov(D, D)^-1 Cov(D, Q_0)` and
`Var(Q) = C_00 / N - Cov(D, Q_0)' Cov(D, D)^-1 Cov(D, Q_0)`. As all
`r_i -> infinity`, `Var -> (C_00 - c' C_LL^-1 c) / N` with
`c_i = C_0i` and `C_LL` the low-fidelity block.

- Domain: `r_i > 1`; weights fixed with respect to the samples.
- Meaning: a control variate whose control means are estimated from extra
  low-fidelity samples; `E[D_i] = 0`, so the estimator is unbiased.
- Code: `monte_carlo.acv_design`, `monte_carlo.acv_estimate`,
  `monte_carlo.ACVDesign.variance_ratio`.
- Source: [REF-GORODETSKY-GERACI-ELDRED-JAKEMAN-2020].

### EQ-MC-MF-006 — ACV-IS covariances

`mu_hat_i` uses the `N` shared inputs and `(r_i - 1) N` inputs drawn
independently for model `i`. With `f_i = (r_i - 1) / r_i`:
`N Cov(D_i, Q_0) = f_i C_0i`, `N Var(D_i) = f_i C_ii`, and
`N Cov(D_i, D_j) = f_i f_j C_ij` for `i != j`.

- Domain: `r_i > 1`, independent extra samples per model.
- Meaning: `D_i = f_i (mean_N f_i - mean_extra f_i)`, from which the three
  covariances follow directly.
- Code: `monte_carlo.acv_design`.
- Source: [REF-GORODETSKY-GERACI-ELDRED-JAKEMAN-2020]; derived as stated and
  confirmed by exact covariances of sample means and replicate simulation.

### EQ-MC-MF-007 — ACV-MF covariances

`mu_hat_i` uses the first `r_i N` inputs of one shared sequence that starts
with the `N` high-fidelity inputs. Then
`N Cov(D_i, Q_0) = ((r_i - 1) / r_i) C_0i` and
`N Cov(D_i, D_j) = F_ij C_ij` with
`F_ij = (min(r_i, r_j) - 1) / min(r_i, r_j)`.

- Domain: `r_i > 1`, nested low-fidelity samples.
- Meaning: from `Cov(mean_m f_i, mean_n f_j) = C_ij / max(m, n)`:
  `1/N - 1/(r_i N) - 1/(r_j N) + 1/(max(r_i, r_j) N)
  = (1 - 1/min(r_i, r_j)) / N`.
- Code: `monte_carlo.acv_design`.
- Source: [REF-GORODETSKY-GERACI-ELDRED-JAKEMAN-2020]; derived as stated and
  confirmed by exact covariances of sample means and replicate simulation.

### EQ-MC-MF-008 — ACV budget allocation by budget shares

For a subset `S` of controls and shares `theta = softmax(z)`,
`N = p theta_0 / (w_0 + sum_(i in S) w_i)` and
`r_i = 1 + p theta_i / (N w_i)`, so that
`N (w_0 + sum_S w_i r_i) = p`; `log Var` of [EQ-MC-MF-005] is minimized
over `z` by Nelder-Mead from several starts, every subset `S` is tried, and
designs are rounded to `N = floor(N_c)`,
`n_i = max(N + 1, floor(r_i N_c))`.

- Domain: at most 12 models; budget `p >= w_0`.
- Meaning: a heuristic local search. The problem is not convex and the
  ACV-MF objective has kinks where two ratios cross, so no optimality
  certificate is given; plain Monte Carlo is always a candidate.
- Code: `monte_carlo.acv_allocation`.
- Source: [REF-GORODETSKY-GERACI-ELDRED-JAKEMAN-2020] (the allocation is
  posed there as a numerical optimization; the parametrization is a library
  choice) and [REF-NELDER-MEAD-1965].

### EQ-MC-MF-009 — Multilevel best linear unbiased estimator

For model groups `S_k` with `n_k` independent group samples `Y_k^(i)`,
selection matrices `P_k`, and `C_k = P_k C P_k'`:
`Psi = sum_k n_k P_k' C_k^-1 P_k`,
`y = sum_k P_k' C_k^-1 sum_i Y_k^(i)`, `mu_hat = Psi^-1 y`,
`Cov(mu_hat) = Psi^-1`, and `Var(mu_hat_0) = [Psi^-1]_00`. Models that no
sampled group contains are removed from `Psi`.

- Domain: positive-definite `C`; at least one sampled group contains
  model 0; `C` fixed with respect to the samples.
- Meaning: generalized least squares for the model means; among linear
  unbiased estimators that use the same group samples none has a smaller
  variance when `C` is the true covariance. MLMC, MFMC, and ACV estimators
  are linear unbiased estimators on particular group structures.
- Code: `monte_carlo.mlblue_variance`, `monte_carlo.mlblue_estimate`.
- Source: [REF-SCHADEN-ULLMANN-2020].

### EQ-MC-MF-010 — MLBLUE sample allocation on the budget simplex

`min_n [Psi(n)^-1]_00` subject to `sum_k n_k W_k <= p`, `n >= 0`,
`W_k = sum_(i in S_k) w_i`. With `theta_k = n_k W_k / p` on the unit
simplex, `Var = (C_00 w_0 / p) g(theta)`,
`g = [Phi^-1]_00`, `Phi = sum_k theta_k A_k`,
`A_k = (w_0 C_00 / W_k) P_k' C_k^-1 P_k`. With `v = Phi^-1 e_0` and
`d_k = v' A_k v`: `dg / dtheta_k = -d_k`, `sum_k theta_k d_k = g`, and
`g(theta') >= g(theta)^2 / max_k d_k` for every feasible `theta'`.
The simplex is parametrized as
`theta_k = (1 - eps) z_k^2 / |z|^2 + eps / K` and
`d log g / d z_j = 2 (1 - eps) z_j (dbar - d_j) / (g |z|^2)`,
`dbar = sum_k z_k^2 d_k / |z|^2`.

- Domain: at least one group contains model 0; `eps` is a quarter of the
  requested relative tolerance.
- Meaning: the objective is convex and homogeneous of degree `-1` in `n`,
  so the budget is active. The bound follows from
  `g(theta') = max_u (u' e_0)^2 / (u' Phi(theta') u)` (Cauchy-Schwarz)
  evaluated at `u = v`; it certifies the BFGS solution of the relaxation.
  Rounding (floors plus a greedy use of the released budget) is a heuristic.
- Code: `monte_carlo.mlblue_allocation`,
  `monte_carlo.MLBLUEAllocation.relative_gap`.
- Source: [REF-SCHADEN-ULLMANN-2020] (objective and sample allocation
  problem) and [REF-CROCI-WILLCOX-WRIGHT-2023] (problem statement; the
  semidefinite program of that paper is replaced by this smooth nonlinear
  program, and the lower bound is derived here).

### EQ-MC-MF-011 — Comparison at a fixed budget

Plain Monte Carlo with budget `p`: `n = floor(p / w_0)`,
`Var = C_00 / n` (real-valued: `C_00 w_0 / p`). The variance ratio of a
method is its predicted variance divided by the plain Monte Carlo variance
for the same budget.

- Domain: `p >= w_0`.
- Meaning: the common yardstick of the comparison table; a ratio below one
  is the factor by which the mean squared error falls at equal cost.
- Code: `monte_carlo.compare_multifidelity_estimators`,
  `monte_carlo.MultifidelityComparison.format`,
  `monte_carlo.MLBLUEAllocation.variance_ratio`.
- Source: [REF-PEHERSTORFER-WILLCOX-GUNZBURGER-2016, Section 3] (variance
  reduction relative to Monte Carlo at equal budget).

## Quasi-experimental and debiased causal estimators

### EQ-CAUSAL-OVB-001 — Partial R-squared from a t statistic

`R^2_{Y~D|X} = t_D^2 / (t_D^2 + df)`, with `t_D` the classical t statistic
of `D` in the regression of `Y` on `(D, X)` and `df` its residual degrees of
freedom. Follows from `t_D^2 = df (RSS_X - RSS_{D,X}) / RSS_{D,X}`.

- Domain: least-squares regression with `df >= 1`.
- Meaning: share of the outcome variance not explained by `X` that `D`
  explains; also the strength with the treatment that a confounder
  explaining all residual outcome variance would need to remove the
  estimate.
- Code: `causal.partial_r2`, `causal.sensitivity_statistics`.
- Source: [REF-CINELLI-HAZLETT-2020]; re-derived and checked against the
  drop in residual sum of squares of fitted regressions.

### EQ-CAUSAL-OVB-002 — Omitted-variable bias in partial R-squared form

For the long regression `Y = tau D + X'beta + gamma Z + e` and the short one
without `Z`, `tau_res - tau = gamma delta` with `delta` the coefficient of
`D` in the regression of `Z` on `(D, X)`, and

`|tau_res - tau| = se(tau_res) sqrt(df) sqrt(R^2_{Y~Z|D,X} R^2_{D~Z|X} /
(1 - R^2_{D~Z|X}))`,

with `se` and `df` from the short regression.

- Domain: `R^2_{D~Z|X} < 1`; classical (homoskedastic) standard error.
- Meaning: an exact sample identity, not a bound, when the two partial
  R-squared values are those of the omitted regressor; a bound on the bias
  when they are upper bounds on its strength. The sign of the bias is not
  determined by the partial R-squared values.
- Code: `causal.omitted_variable_bias`, `causal.adjust_for_confounder`.
- Source: [REF-CINELLI-HAZLETT-2020]; re-derived from the least-squares
  algebra and confirmed to `1e-12` by omitting a simulated confounder.

### EQ-CAUSAL-OVB-003 — Robustness value

`RV_q = (sqrt(f_q^4 + 4 f_q^2) - f_q^2) / 2`, `f_q = q |t_D| / sqrt(df)`:
the positive root of `R^2 + f_q^2 R - f_q^2 = 0`, i.e. of
`R / sqrt(1 - R) = f_q`.

- Domain: `q > 0`, `df >= 1`.
- Meaning: a confounder whose partial R-squared with both the treatment and
  the outcome equals `RV_q` changes the estimate by the fraction `q`
  (`q = 1`: to zero); confounders weaker than `RV_q` on both counts cannot.
- Code: `causal.robustness_value`, `causal.sensitivity_statistics`.
- Source: [REF-CINELLI-HAZLETT-2020]; follows from [EQ-CAUSAL-OVB-002] with
  equal strengths.

### EQ-CAUSAL-OVB-004 — Standard error and t statistic adjusted for a confounder

`se(tau) = se(tau_res) sqrt((1 - R^2_{Y~Z|D,X}) / (1 - R^2_{D~Z|X}))
sqrt(df / (df - 1))`, `tau = tau_res -+ |bias|` ([EQ-CAUSAL-OVB-002]),
`t = tau / se(tau)` on `df - 1` degrees of freedom.

- Domain: `df >= 2`, `R^2_{D~Z|X} < 1`.
- Meaning: what the long regression would report; an exact sample identity
  for an actual omitted regressor.
- Code: `causal.adjust_for_confounder`.
- Source: [REF-CINELLI-HAZLETT-2020]; re-derived from
  `RSS_long = RSS_short (1 - R^2_{Y~Z|D,X})` and
  `SS(D | X, Z) = SS(D | X)(1 - R^2_{D~Z|X})`.

### EQ-CAUSAL-OVB-005 — Robustness value for statistical significance

With `f_q = q |t_D| / sqrt(df)` and `f* = t*_{alpha, df-1} / sqrt(df - 1)`
(`t*` the two-sided Student-t critical value):
`RV_{q,alpha} = 0` if `f_q <= f*`;
`RV_{q,alpha} =` [EQ-CAUSAL-OVB-003] at `f_{q,alpha} = f_q - f*` if
`f* < f_q <= 1 / f*`;
`RV_{q,alpha} = (f_q^2 - f*^2) / (1 + f_q^2)` if `f_q > 1 / f*`.

- Domain: `df >= 2`, `0 < alpha < 1`.
- Meaning: the smallest `R` such that a confounder with
  `R^2_{Y~Z|D,X} <= R` and `R^2_{D~Z|X} <= R` can bring the adjusted t
  statistic for `H0: tau = (1 - q) tau_res` to the critical value. From
  [EQ-CAUSAL-OVB-002] and [EQ-CAUSAL-OVB-004] the adjusted t over
  `sqrt(df - 1)` is `(f_q sqrt(1 - R2_D) - sqrt(R2_Y R2_D)) / sqrt(1 - R2_Y)`.
  It is minimized at equal strengths when `f_q <= 1 / f*`; otherwise at
  `R2_Y = R2_D / (f_q^2 (1 - R2_D)) < R2_D`, where it equals
  `sqrt(f_q^2 (1 - R2_D) - R2_D)`. The third branch is absent from the
  formula printed in the paper and present in the authors' `sensemakr`
  software (`robustness_value`); the equal-strength formula alone
  overstates the value there (0.983 instead of 0.964 at `t = 20`,
  `df = 5`).
- Code: `causal.robustness_value`, `causal.sensitivity_statistics`.
- Source: [REF-CINELLI-HAZLETT-2020]; derived here from
  [EQ-CAUSAL-OVB-002] and [EQ-CAUSAL-OVB-004] and checked by a grid search
  over both strengths.

### EQ-CAUSAL-DML-001 — Partialling-out estimator of the partially linear model

For `Y = theta D + g(X) + e`, `D = m(X) + v`, `l(X) = E[Y | X]`: residuals
`Y~ = Y - l_hat(X)`, `D~ = D - m_hat(X)` with `l_hat`, `m_hat` fitted on the
folds not containing the unit, and `theta_hat = sum(D~ Y~) / sum(D~^2)`,
the root of the pooled score `sum (Y~ - theta D~) D~ = 0`.

- Domain: `sum(D~^2) > 0`; `K >= 2` folds for cross-fitting (`K = 1` uses
  in-sample fits).
- Meaning: the score is Neyman orthogonal (its derivative with respect to
  `(l, m)` vanishes at the truth), so nuisance errors enter only through
  their product; with linear in-sample nuisances it is the least-squares
  coefficient of `D` (Frisch-Waugh-Lovell).
- Code: `causal.dml_partially_linear`.
- Source: [REF-CHERNOZHUKOV-ET-AL-2018].

### EQ-CAUSAL-DML-002 — Asymptotic variance of the partialling-out estimator

`se^2 = mean(D~^2 (Y~ - theta_hat D~)^2) / (n mean(D~^2)^2)`.

- Domain: [EQ-CAUSAL-DML-001]; i.i.d. units; nuisance errors with product
  `o(n^(-1/2))`.
- Meaning: heteroskedasticity-robust sandwich variance of the orthogonal
  score; asymptotic only. With linear in-sample nuisances it equals the HC0
  variance of the least-squares coefficient.
- Code: `causal.dml_partially_linear`,
  `causal.DoubleMLResult.confidence_interval`.
- Source: [REF-CHERNOZHUKOV-ET-AL-2018].

### EQ-CAUSAL-DML-003 — Cross-fitted augmented IPW average treatment effect

`psi_i = m_1(x_i) - m_0(x_i) + T_i (Y_i - m_1(x_i)) / e(x_i) -
(1 - T_i)(Y_i - m_0(x_i)) / (1 - e(x_i))` with `m_1`, `m_0`, `e` fitted on
the folds not containing unit `i`; `tau = mean(psi)`,
`se = sd(psi) / sqrt(n)`.

- Domain: binary treatment; propensities clipped to `[c, 1 - c]`.
- Meaning: [EQ-CAUSAL-AIPW-001] with out-of-fold nuisances from arbitrary
  learners (the interactive regression model).
- Code: `causal.dml_average_treatment_effect`.
- Source: [REF-CHERNOZHUKOV-ET-AL-2018],
  [REF-ROBINS-ROTNITZKY-ZHAO-1994].

### EQ-CAUSAL-KNN-001 — k-nearest-neighbour regression

`f_hat(x) = (1/k) sum_{i in N_k(x)} y_i`, with `N_k(x)` the `k` training
points closest to `x` in Euclidean distance after dividing each coordinate
by its training standard deviation.

- Domain: `1 <= k <= n_train`; ties broken by training order.
- Meaning: a local average; a nonparametric nuisance learner whose error
  shrinks slowly in many dimensions.
- Code: `causal.knn_learner`.
- Source: [REF-HASTIE-TIBSHIRANI-FRIEDMAN-2009, Section 2.3].

### EQ-CAUSAL-DID-001 — Canonical 2x2 difference-in-differences

`DiD = (Ybar_{1,post} - Ybar_{1,pre}) - (Ybar_{0,post} - Ybar_{0,pre})
= mean(d_i | treated) - mean(d_i | control)`, `d_i = Y_i,post - Y_i,pre`,
`se = sqrt(s_1^2 / n_1 + s_0^2 / n_0)` with the sample variances of `d_i`.

- Domain: two periods, a balanced panel, at least two units per group.
- Meaning: the ATT under parallel trends and no anticipation; the standard
  error assumes independent units.
- Code: `causal.did_two_by_two`.
- Source: [REF-ROTH-ET-AL-2023].

### EQ-CAUSAL-DID-002 — Group-time average treatment effect

`ATT(g, t) = E[Y_t - Y_{g-1} | G = g] - E[Y_t - Y_{g-1} | C]`, `t >= g`,
estimated by sample means, with `C = {G = inf}` (never treated) or
`C = {G > t}` (not yet treated, including never treated).

- Domain: balanced panel, absorbing treatment, `g` later than the first
  period, a non-empty comparison set; no covariates.
- Meaning: effect at period `t` for units first treated at `g`, under
  parallel trends between the group and the comparison units and no
  anticipation.
- Code: `causal.group_time_effects`, `causal.GroupTimeEffects.effect`.
- Source: [REF-CALLAWAY-SANTANNA-2021].

### EQ-CAUSAL-DID-003 — Influence-function standard errors

For a cell with long differences `d_i`, group mean `mu_g` and comparison
mean `mu_C`: `psi_i = (n / n_g) 1{G_i = g}(d_i - mu_g) - (n / n_C)
1{i in C}(d_i - mu_C)`, `se = sqrt(sum_i psi_i^2) / n`. For an aggregate
`theta = sum_c w_c ATT_c` with `w_c = n_{g(c)} / sum_{c'} n_{g(c')}`:
`psi_i = sum_c w_c psi_{c,i} + sum_c (ATT_c - theta) 1{G_i = g(c)} / P`,
`P = sum_c n_{g(c)} / n`.

- Domain: independent units; fixed number of periods; at least two units
  in the group and in the comparison set (otherwise the standard error is
  `nan`).
- Meaning: asymptotic standard errors; the second term of the aggregate is
  the delta method for the estimated group shares. Pointwise, not
  simultaneous. Too small for small arms (divisor-`n` variances and a
  normal critical value): 86 to 91 % coverage of nominal 95 % intervals
  with 5 never-treated units among 100.
- Code: `causal.group_time_effects`, `causal.GroupTimeEffects.event_study`,
  `causal.GroupTimeEffects.overall`.
- Source: [REF-CALLAWAY-SANTANNA-2021] (influence-function approach); the
  unconditional forms are derived here and checked by Monte Carlo.

### EQ-CAUSAL-DID-004 — Event-study aggregation

`theta(e) = sum_g w_g ATT(g, g + e)`, `w_g = n_g / sum_{g'} n_{g'}` over the
groups whose cell at exposure `e` was estimated.

- Domain: `e >= 0`, counted in positions of the period grid.
- Meaning: average effect `e` periods after adoption; different `e` average
  different groups.
- Code: `causal.GroupTimeEffects.event_study`.
- Source: [REF-CALLAWAY-SANTANNA-2021].

### EQ-CAUSAL-DID-005 — Overall aggregation over post-treatment cells

`theta = sum_{(g,t): t >= g} w_{g,t} ATT(g, t)`,
`w_{g,t} = n_g / sum_{(g',t')} n_{g'}` over all estimated cells.

- Domain: at least one estimated cell.
- Meaning: group-size-weighted mean of all post-treatment cells; a group
  counts in proportion to its size times its number of post periods.
- Code: `causal.GroupTimeEffects.overall`.
- Source: [REF-CALLAWAY-SANTANNA-2021].

### EQ-CAUSAL-SC-001 — Synthetic control weights

`w* = argmin_w (x1 - X0 w)' V (x1 - X0 w)` subject to `w_j >= 0`,
`sum_j w_j = 1`, `V` diagonal and non-negative. With gradient
`g = -2 X0' V (x1 - X0 w)`, `w` is optimal iff `g_j = min_i g_i` whenever
`w_j > 0` (KKT), and `g'w - min_j g_j >= f(w) - f(w*)` for any feasible
`w`.

- Domain: `J >= 1` donors, `k >= 1` predictors; `V` user-supplied.
- Meaning: the convex combination of donors closest to the treated unit;
  unique fitted values, weights unique when `X0' V X0` is positive
  definite.
- Code: `causal.synthetic_control_weights`, `causal.synthetic_control`.
- Source: [REF-ABADIE-DIAMOND-HAINMUELLER-2010] (problem),
  [REF-NOCEDAL-WRIGHT-2006, Chapter 16] (optimality conditions).

### EQ-CAUSAL-SC-002 — Euclidean projection onto the simplex

`P(v)_j = max(v_j - theta, 0)` with `theta = (sum_{i<=rho} u_i - 1) / rho`,
`u` the entries of `v` in decreasing order and
`rho = max{j : u_j - (sum_{i<=j} u_i - 1) / j > 0}`.

- Domain: finite `v` of length at least one.
- Meaning: the KKT solution of `min |w - v|^2` on the simplex; the
  projection step of projected gradient.
- Code: `causal.project_to_simplex`.
- Source: derived from the KKT conditions in
  [REF-NOCEDAL-WRIGHT-2006, Chapter 16].

### EQ-CAUSAL-SC-003 — Synthetic control effect path and RMSPE

`tau_t = Y_1t - sum_j w_j Y_jt`; `RMSPE_pre = sqrt(mean_{t <= T0} tau_t^2)`,
`RMSPE_post = sqrt(mean_{t > T0} tau_t^2)`.

- Domain: `1 <= T0 < T`.
- Meaning: gap between the treated unit and its synthetic control; the
  pre-period RMSPE measures the quality of the match.
- Code: `causal.synthetic_control`.
- Source: [REF-ABADIE-DIAMOND-HAINMUELLER-2010].

### EQ-CAUSAL-SC-004 — Placebo rank p-value

`r_j = RMSPE_post,j / RMSPE_pre,j` for the treated unit (`j = 1`) and for
each donor treated as a placebo; `p = #{j : r_j >= r_1} / (J + 1)`.

- Domain: `J >= 2` donors.
- Meaning: rank of the treated unit among in-space placebos; a
  randomization p-value only under random assignment of the intervention,
  never smaller than `1 / (J + 1)`, and not a sampling-based p-value.
- Code: `causal.synthetic_control_placebo`.
- Source: [REF-ABADIE-DIAMOND-HAINMUELLER-2010].

### EQ-CAUSAL-IV-001 — Two-stage least squares

With `X = [D, W]` (endogenous and included exogenous regressors) and
`Zf = [Z, W]`: `Xhat = Zf (Zf'Zf)^-1 Zf'X`,
`beta = (Xhat'X)^-1 Xhat'y = (Xhat'Xhat)^-1 Xhat'y`. Exactly identified:
`beta = (Zf'X)^-1 Zf'y`; one binary instrument and an intercept: the Wald
ratio `(E[Y|Z=1] - E[Y|Z=0]) / (E[D|Z=1] - E[D|Z=0])`.

- Domain: at least as many excluded instruments as endogenous regressors;
  `Zf` and `Xhat` of full column rank.
- Meaning: consistent (not unbiased) for the structural coefficients under
  instrument relevance, exclusion and exchangeability with homogeneous
  effects.
- Code: `causal.two_stage_least_squares`.
- Source: [REF-HERNAN-ROBINS-2020, Chapter 16] (instrumental conditions,
  the usual IV estimand and the two-stage estimator for one instrument and
  one treatment). The matrix form with several endogenous regressors and
  included exogenous covariates is the same projection written out here;
  it was checked against a direct matrix computation, not against a
  source text.

### EQ-CAUSAL-IV-002 — Heteroskedasticity-robust covariance of 2SLS

`Cov(beta) = (Xhat'Xhat)^-1 (sum_i e_i^2 xhat_i xhat_i') (Xhat'Xhat)^-1`,
`e = y - X beta` (observed regressors); `HC1` multiplies by `n / (n - K)`.

- Domain: [EQ-CAUSAL-IV-001].
- Meaning: sandwich covariance of the moment condition `E[xhat u] = 0`;
  asymptotic, and unreliable with weak instruments. In the exactly
  identified case it equals `(Zf'X)^-1 (sum e_i^2 z_i z_i') (X'Zf)^-1`.
- Code: `causal.two_stage_least_squares`,
  `causal.InstrumentalVariablesResult.confidence_interval`.
- Source: [REF-WHITE-1980] (heteroskedasticity-consistent covariance),
  applied to the second-stage regressors.

### EQ-CAUSAL-IV-003 — First-stage F statistic of the excluded instruments

`F = ((RSS_W - RSS_Zf) / q) / (RSS_Zf / (n - q - k_W))` for the regression
of an endogenous regressor on `Zf = [Z, W]` against its regression on `W`.

- Domain: `n > q + k_W`.
- Meaning: strength of the instruments; values below about 10 are a common
  rule-of-thumb warning of weak instruments (a heuristic).
- Code: `causal.two_stage_least_squares`.
- Source: [REF-HERNAN-ROBINS-2020, Chapter 16],
  [REF-MONTGOMERY-PECK-VINING-2021, Chapter 3] (extra-sum-of-squares F).

## Contextual bandits, off-policy evaluation, and Markov decision processes (ADR-0126)

### EQ-RISK-LINUCB-001 — LinUCB estimate and upper confidence score

`A_a = I + sum_{t: a_t = a} x_t x_t'`, `b_a = sum_{t: a_t = a} r_t x_t`,
`theta_a = A_a^-1 b_a`; play
`argmax_a theta_a' x_{t,a} + alpha sqrt(x_{t,a}' A_a^-1 x_{t,a})`.

- Domain: `K >= 2` arms, feature vectors in `R^d`, finite rewards,
  exploration weight `alpha >= 0` chosen by the user.
- Meaning: one ridge regression per arm; the bonus is `alpha` times the
  standard deviation scale of the predicted reward and shrinks in the
  directions the arm has explored. For `d = 1`, `x = 1` it reduces to
  `theta = sum r / (n + 1)` and bonus `alpha / sqrt(n + 1)`.
- Code: `risk.LinUCB`, `risk.LinUCB.theta`, `risk.LinUCB.scores`,
  `risk.LinUCB.select`, `risk.simulate_linear_bandit`.
- Source: [REF-LI-ETAL-2010].

### EQ-RISK-LINUCB-002 — Rank-one update of the inverse design matrix

`(A + x x')^-1 = A^-1 - u u' / (1 + x' u)` with `u = A^-1 x`.

- Domain: symmetric positive-definite `A`, so `1 + x' A^-1 x >= 1`.
- Meaning: Sherman-Morrison update; verified by multiplying
  `(A + x x') (A^-1 - u u' / (1 + x' u)) = I + x u' - x u' = I`. Keeps the
  cost of one LinUCB round at `O(d^2)` per arm.
- Code: `risk.LinUCB.update`, `risk.LinUCB.inverse_design`.
- Source: [REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013]; derivation above.

### EQ-RISK-LINUCB-003 — Pseudo-regret in a linear environment

`Regret(T) = sum_{t=1}^T (max_a m_t(a) - m_t(a_t))`,
`m_t(a) = theta_a' x_{t,a}`.

- Domain: a simulation with known parameters `theta_a` (one per arm or one
  shared vector).
- Meaning: expected reward lost against the best arm of each round; a
  learning policy has `Regret(T) / T` decreasing in `T`, uniform play does
  not.
- Code: `risk.simulate_linear_bandit`, `risk.LinearBanditRun.regret_per_round`,
  `risk.LinearBanditRun.final_regret`.
- Source: [REF-LI-ETAL-2010]; [REF-AGRAWAL-GOYAL-2013].

### EQ-RISK-LINTS-001 — Linear Thompson sampling

`B = I + sum_t x_t x_t'`, `f = sum_t r_t x_t`, `mu_hat = B^-1 f`,
`theta_tilde ~ N(mu_hat, v^2 B^-1)`; play `argmax_a x_{t,a}' theta_tilde`.

- Domain: one shared parameter in `R^d`, feature vectors of the played arms
  `x_t`, scale `v > 0` chosen by the user.
- Meaning: posterior sampling; with `v = 1` the sampling law is the exact
  posterior of a `N(0, I)` prior under unit-variance Gaussian rewards. The
  value of `v` used in the regret analysis of the source depends on the
  horizon and the confidence level and is not reproduced.
- Code: `risk.LinearThompsonSampling`,
  `risk.LinearThompsonSampling.posterior_mean`,
  `risk.LinearThompsonSampling.posterior_covariance`,
  `risk.LinearThompsonSampling.sample_parameter`,
  `risk.LinearThompsonSampling.select`.
- Source: [REF-AGRAWAL-GOYAL-2013].

### EQ-RISK-OPE-001 — Inverse propensity scoring

`V_IPS = (1/n) sum_i w_i r_i`, `w_i = pi(a_i | x_i) / p(a_i | x_i)`.

- Domain: independent records `(x_i, a_i, r_i)` with `a_i ~ p(. | x_i)`;
  `p(a | x) > 0` wherever `pi(a | x) > 0`; the logged propensities are the
  true ones.
- Meaning: unbiased estimate of `V(pi) = E_x sum_a pi(a | x) E[r | x, a]`,
  because `E[w r | x] = sum_a p(a | x) (pi(a | x) / p(a | x)) E[r | x, a]`.
- Code: `risk.inverse_propensity_score`.
- Source: [REF-DUDIK-LANGFORD-LI-2011].

### EQ-RISK-OPE-002 — Self-normalized inverse propensity scoring

`V_SNIPS = sum_i w_i r_i / sum_i w_i`,
`se = sqrt(sum_i w_i^2 (r_i - V_SNIPS)^2) / sum_i w_i`.

- Domain: as [EQ-RISK-OPE-001], with at least one positive weight.
- Meaning: ratio estimator; consistent, biased for finite `n`, bounded by
  the observed rewards, and equivariant under `r -> r + c`. The standard
  error is the delta-method value for a ratio of means.
- Code: `risk.self_normalized_ips`.
- Source: [REF-OWEN-2013].

### EQ-RISK-OPE-003 — Direct method

`V_DM = (1/n) sum_i sum_a pi(a | x_i) q(x_i, a)`.

- Domain: a reward model `q(x, a)` fixed independently of the evaluated
  records.
- Meaning: plug-in estimate; unbiased only if `q(x, a) = E[r | x, a]`.
- Code: `risk.direct_method`.
- Source: [REF-DUDIK-LANGFORD-LI-2011].

### EQ-RISK-OPE-004 — Doubly robust estimator

`V_DR = (1/n) sum_i [sum_a pi(a | x_i) q(x_i, a) + w_i (r_i - q(x_i, a_i))]`.

- Domain: as [EQ-RISK-OPE-001] and [EQ-RISK-OPE-003]; stated here for a
  stochastic target policy (the source writes it for a deterministic one).
- Meaning: unbiased if the propensities are correct, since
  `E[w (r - q) | x] = sum_a pi(a | x) (E[r | x, a] - q(x, a))` cancels the
  model error, or if `q = E[r | x, a]`, since the correction then has
  conditional mean zero for any weights.
- Code: `risk.doubly_robust`.
- Source: [REF-DUDIK-LANGFORD-LI-2011].

### EQ-RISK-OPE-005 — Standard error, weight clipping, and effective sample size

`se = s / sqrt(n)` with `s^2 = sum_i (t_i - t_bar)^2 / (n - 1)` of the
per-record terms `t_i`; clipped weights `min(w_i, M)`;
`ESS = (sum_i w_i)^2 / sum_i w_i^2`.

- Domain: `n >= 2` independent records; cap `M > 0`.
- Meaning: sampling error of a mean of independent terms. Clipping lowers
  the variance and introduces bias. The effective sample size
  ([EQ-MC-ESS-001]) is a heuristic measure of weight concentration.
- Code: `risk.OffPolicyEstimate`, `risk.OffPolicyEstimate.interval`,
  `risk.inverse_propensity_score`, `risk.doubly_robust`.
- Source: [REF-DUDIK-LANGFORD-LI-2011]; [REF-OWEN-2013].

### EQ-RISK-MDP-001 — Policy evaluation

`(I - gamma P_pi) V_pi = r_pi`, `P_pi(s, s') = sum_a pi(a | s) P_a(s, s')`,
`r_pi(s) = sum_a pi(a | s) r_a(s)`, `r_a(s) = sum_s' P_a(s, s') R_a(s, s')`.

- Domain: finite state and action sets, stochastic matrices `P_a`,
  `0 <= gamma < 1`.
- Meaning: expected discounted reward of a stationary policy; the matrix is
  strictly diagonally dominant, so the solution exists and is unique. One
  state with reward 1 gives `V = 1 / (1 - gamma)`.
- Code: `risk.FiniteMDP`, `risk.policy_evaluation`.
- Source: [REF-NORRIS-1997].

### EQ-RISK-MDP-002 — Action values, greedy policy, and Bellman optimality

`Q(s, a) = r_a(s) + gamma sum_s' P_a(s, s') V(s')`,
`(T V)(s) = max_a Q(s, a)`, `V* = T V*`, `pi(s) = argmax_a Q(s, a)`.

- Domain: as [EQ-RISK-MDP-001].
- Meaning: `T` is a `gamma`-contraction in the sup norm with the optimal
  value function as its unique fixed point; a policy that is greedy for
  `V*` is optimal.
- Code: `risk.action_values`, `risk.greedy_policy`, `risk.bellman_residual`,
  `risk.MDPSolution`.
- Source: [REF-NORRIS-1997].

### EQ-RISK-MDP-003 — Value iteration and its stopping rule

`V_{k+1} = T V_k`; stop when
`|V_{k+1} - V_k|_inf < eps (1 - gamma) / (2 gamma)`.

- Domain: as [EQ-RISK-MDP-001], `eps > 0`; with `gamma = 0` one sweep is
  exact.
- Meaning: at the stop the greedy policy for `V_{k+1}` is within `eps` of
  optimal in every state and `V_{k+1}` is within `eps / 2` of `V*`, by
  [EQ-RISK-MDP-006] with residual at most `gamma |V_{k+1} - V_k|_inf`.
- Code: `risk.value_iteration`.
- Source: [REF-PUTERMAN-1994, Chapter 6]; [REF-NORRIS-1997, Section 5.4];
  the bound is derived in `risk.markov_decision`.

### EQ-RISK-MDP-004 — Policy iteration

`V_k` solves [EQ-RISK-MDP-001] for `pi_k`;
`pi_{k+1}(s) = argmax_a Q_k(s, a)`, keeping `pi_k(s)` unless another action
is strictly better; stop when `pi_{k+1} = pi_k`.

- Domain: as [EQ-RISK-MDP-001].
- Meaning: every change strictly improves the value function, so no
  deterministic policy repeats and the method stops at an optimal policy
  after at most `|A|^|S|` steps.
- Code: `risk.policy_iteration`.
- Source: [REF-PUTERMAN-1994, Chapter 6]; [REF-NORRIS-1997, Section 5.4].

### EQ-RISK-MDP-005 — Finite-horizon backward induction

`V_N = g`, `V_t(s) = max_a [r_a(s) + gamma sum_s' P_a(s, s') V_{t+1}(s')]`
for `t = N - 1, ..., 0`.

- Domain: `N >= 1` stages, terminal values `g`, `0 <= gamma <= 1`.
- Meaning: optimal expected (discounted) reward of the remaining stages and
  an optimal stage-dependent policy.
- Code: `risk.backward_induction`, `risk.FiniteHorizonSolution`.
- Source: [REF-NORRIS-1997].

### EQ-RISK-MDP-006 — Error bounds from the Bellman residual

With `rho = |T V - V|_inf` and `pi` greedy for `V`:
`|V - V*|_inf <= rho / (1 - gamma)`, `|V_pi - V|_inf <= rho / (1 - gamma)`,
`|V_pi - V*|_inf <= 2 rho / (1 - gamma)`.

- Domain: any `V`; `0 <= gamma < 1`.
- Meaning: follows from the contraction property:
  `|V - V*| <= |V - T V| + |T V - T V*| <= rho + gamma |V - V*|`, and
  `|V_pi - V| <= |T_pi V_pi - T_pi V| + |T V - V|` because `T_pi V = T V`.
- Code: `risk.MDPSolution.value_error_bound`,
  `risk.MDPSolution.policy_loss_bound`, `risk.bellman_residual`.
- Source: derivation in `risk.markov_decision`;
  [REF-PUTERMAN-1994, Chapter 6] and [REF-NORRIS-1997, Section 5.4] for the
  setting.

### EQ-RISK-SH-001 — Sequential halving schedule

Rounds `r = 0, ..., ceil(log2 n) - 1`; each arm of `S_r` is pulled
`floor(T / (|S_r| ceil(log2 n)))` times; the `ceil(|S_r| / 2)` arms with the
largest round averages form `S_{r+1}`.

- Domain: `n >= 2` arms, budget `T >= n ceil(log2 n)`.
- Meaning: fixed-budget best-arm identification using at most `T` pulls;
  for bounded rewards the error probability is exponentially small in
  `T / (H_2 log2 n)`, see the source.
- Code: `risk.sequential_halving`, `risk.SequentialHalvingResult`,
  `risk.HalvingRound`.
- Source: [REF-KARNIN-KOREN-SOMEKH-2013].

## Rank-based, moment-independent, kernel and active-subspace sensitivity (ADR-0123)

### EQ-SENS-RANKSOBOL-001 — Rank-based first-order Sobol index

Sort the rows by `x_i`, giving `y_(1), ..., y_(n)`, with `y_(n+1) = y_(1)`:
`S_i = [(1/n) sum_j y_(j) y_(j+1) - ybar^2] / [(1/n) sum_j y_j^2 - ybar^2]`.
With `c = y - ybar` this equals `sum_j c_(j) c_(j+1) / sum_j c_j^2`.

- Domain: `n >= 8` i.i.d. rows, a continuous `X_i` (ties are ordered at
  random), `E[Y^2] < inf`, non-constant output; inputs may be dependent.
- Meaning: neighbours in the order of `x_i` act as a pick-freeze pair that
  shares `X_i`, so the lag-one product estimates `E[E[Y | X_i]^2]`; all
  `d` first-order indices use the same `n` runs and no tuning parameter.
  The cyclic lag-one autocorrelation form is an exact rewriting.
- Code: `sensitivity.rank_sobol_indices`,
  `sensitivity.model_rank_sobol_indices`.
- Source: [REF-GAMBOA-ETAL-2022]; the neighbour construction is that of
  [REF-CHATTERJEE-2021].

### EQ-SENS-RANKSOBOL-002 — Disjoint-block standard error of a rank statistic

Cut the rows, in the order given, into `B` disjoint blocks of `m = floor(n / B)`
rows; with `S^(b)` the estimate of [EQ-SENS-RANKSOBOL-001] on block `b` and
`Sbar` their mean, `se = sqrt(sum_b (S^(b) - Sbar)^2 / ((B - 1) B))`.

- Domain: i.i.d. rows in an order unrelated to their values, `2 <= B <= n / 8`.
- Meaning: the standard error of the mean of `B` independent block
  estimates; it describes the full-sample estimate through the `sqrt(n)`
  rate of the estimator. It replaces the ordinary bootstrap, which is
  invalid here because repeated rows become neighbours after sorting and
  inflate the lag-one product. A diagnostic with `B - 1` degrees of
  freedom, not the asymptotic variance of the published central limit
  theorem.
- Code: `sensitivity.rank_sobol_indices` (`blocks=`),
  `sensitivity.RankSobolResult`.
- Source: [REF-GAMBOA-ETAL-2022] (rate and central limit theorem); the
  block form is the standard error of a mean of independent replicates,
  [REF-OWEN-2013, Chapter 2].

### EQ-SENS-XI-001 — Chatterjee's rank correlation without ties

Sort the pairs by `x`; with `r_j` the rank of the `j`-th output in that
order, `xi_n = 1 - 3 sum_{j=1}^{n-1} |r_(j+1) - r_(j)| / (n^2 - 1)`. For a
strictly monotone relation `sum |r_(j+1) - r_(j)| = n - 1` and
`xi_n = 1 - 3 / (n + 1)`.

- Domain: `n >= 3` i.i.d. pairs without ties in `y`; ties in `x` are
  ordered uniformly at random.
- Meaning: consistent estimator of
  `xi = int Var(E[1{Y >= t} | X]) dmu(t) / int Var(1{Y >= t}) dmu(t)`
  (`mu` the law of `Y`), which is 0 if and only if `X` and `Y` are
  independent and 1 if and only if `Y` is a measurable function of `X`.
  Not symmetric in `X` and `Y`.
- Code: `sensitivity.chatterjee_xi`, `sensitivity.chatterjee_indices`.
- Source: [REF-CHATTERJEE-2021].

### EQ-SENS-XI-002 — Chatterjee's rank correlation with ties

With `r_j = #{k : y_k <= y_(j)}` and `l_j = #{k : y_k >= y_(j)}` in the
order of `x`: `xi_n = 1 - n sum_{j=1}^{n-1} |r_(j+1) - r_(j)| / (2 sum_j l_j (n - l_j))`.
Without ties `sum_j l_j (n - l_j) = n (n^2 - 1) / 6`, which gives
[EQ-SENS-XI-001].

- Domain: `n >= 3` i.i.d. pairs, non-constant `y`.
- Meaning: the same functional as [EQ-SENS-XI-001] for outputs with atoms.
  Derivation: `sum_k 1{min(y_(j), y_(j+1)) >= y_k} = min(r_(j), r_(j+1))
  = (r_(j) + r_(j+1) - |r_(j+1) - r_(j)|) / 2` turns the neighbour
  estimate of `int E[P(Y >= t | X)^2] dmu(t)` into the sum of rank jumps,
  and `sum_j l_j (n - l_j) / n^3` estimates `int Var(1{Y >= t}) dmu(t)`.
  A two-level function of `x` with equal halves gives `1 - 2 / n`.
- Code: `sensitivity.chatterjee_xi`, `sensitivity.chatterjee_indices`.
- Source: [REF-CHATTERJEE-2021].

### EQ-SENS-XI-003 — Independence null law and p-value of xi

Under independence and a continuous `Y`, `sqrt(n) xi_n -> N(0, 2/5)`;
`p = 1 - Phi(xi_n sqrt(5 n / 2))`.

- Domain: i.i.d. pairs, continuous `Y` (no ties); for tied outputs the
  null variance depends on the tie pattern and the permutation p-value of
  [EQ-SENS-HSIC-004] applied to `xi_n` is used instead.
- Meaning: a one-sided test of independence that needs no resampling;
  simulation at `n = 200` gives `n Var(xi_n) = 0.396`, the asymptotic value
  being approached from below.
- Code: `sensitivity.chatterjee_indices`,
  `sensitivity.ChatterjeeResult.dependent`.
- Source: [REF-CHATTERJEE-2021].

### EQ-SENS-ACTIVE-001 — Gradient moment matrix and active subspace

`C = E[grad f(X) grad f(X)'] = W Lambda W'`,
`C_M = (1/M) sum_m grad f(x_m) grad f(x_m)'`,
`lambda_j = E[(w_j' grad f)^2]`; active variables `y = W_1' x` with `W_1`
the first `k` eigenvectors.

- Domain: differentiable `f` with square-integrable gradient; `x_m`
  independent draws of the input density; coordinates of comparable scale.
- Meaning: the eigenvalue is the mean squared directional derivative, so
  directions with small eigenvalues leave `f` nearly unchanged on average;
  `f = h(a'x)` gives a rank-one `C` with `w_1 = a / |a|`, and
  `f = x'Ax/2` with `X ~ N(0, I)` gives `C = A^2`.
- Code: `sensitivity.active_subspace_from_gradients`,
  `sensitivity.active_subspace`,
  `sensitivity.ActiveSubspaceResult.active_variables`,
  `sensitivity.ActiveSubspaceResult.sufficient_summary`,
  `sensitivity.ActiveSubspaceResult.explained_fraction`.
- Source: [REF-CONSTANTINE-DOW-WANG-2014].

### EQ-SENS-ACTIVE-002 — Activity scores

`alpha_i(k) = sum_{j=1}^{k} lambda_j w_ij^2`; `alpha_i(d) = C_ii = E[(df/dx_i)^2]`.

- Domain: eigenpairs of [EQ-SENS-ACTIVE-001], `1 <= k <= d`.
- Meaning: the part of the mean squared partial derivative of coordinate
  `i` that lies in the active subspace; with `k = d` the score is the
  diagonal of `C`, i.e. the derivative-based measure of
  [EQ-SENS-DGSM-001] (from `C = sum_j lambda_j w_j w_j'`).
- Code: `sensitivity.active_subspace_from_gradients`,
  `sensitivity.ActiveSubspaceResult.as_mapping`.
- Source: derived here from the spectral decomposition of the matrix of
  [REF-CONSTANTINE-DOW-WANG-2014] ([REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013, Section 8.1]).
  The score is not claimed to be defined in that paper; no source for the
  name could be verified.

### EQ-SENS-ACTIVE-003 — Bootstrap subspace distance and eigenvalue intervals

For a resample of the gradients with eigenvectors `W*`:
`dist_k = |W_1 W_1' - W_1* W_1*'|_2 = sqrt(1 - sigma_min(W_1' W_1*)^2)`;
`subspace_error_k = mean over replicates of dist_k`; eigenvalue interval
`[q_{alpha/2}(lambda_j*), q_{1 - alpha/2}(lambda_j*)]`.

- Domain: `M >= 2` gradients resampled with replacement; `k < d`.
- Meaning: the distance is the sine of the largest principal angle between
  the estimated and the resampled `k`-dimensional subspace; it is small
  where the gap `lambda_k - lambda_{k+1}` is large. A heuristic measure of
  sampling variability only (sample eigenvalues are biased).
- Code: `sensitivity.active_subspace_from_gradients` (`bootstrap=`).
- Source: [REF-EFRON-TIBSHIRANI-1993] (nonparametric bootstrap and
  percentile interval, applied here to the gradient sample of
  [REF-CONSTANTINE-DOW-WANG-2014]) and [REF-GOLUB-VANLOAN-2013, Section
  2.5.3] (distance between subspaces). That the 2014 paper itself contains
  this bootstrap could not be verified, so it is not attributed to it.

### EQ-SENS-ACTIVE-004 — Gradient in standard-normal space

For independent inputs `x_i = F_i^-1(Phi(u_i))` and `g(u) = f(x(u))`:
`dg/du_i = (df/dx_i) phi(u_i) / f_i(x_i)`.

- Domain: continuous marginals with `f_i(x_i) > 0`; independent inputs
  (dependent inputs use central differences of `g` in `u`).
- Meaning: the chain rule with the inverse-function derivative of the
  marginal map ([EQ-CAL-AD-001] with `L = I`); every coordinate `u_i` has
  unit variance, which removes the dependence of the eigenvectors on the
  physical units.
- Code: `sensitivity.active_subspace`.
- Source: [REF-LIU-DERKIUREGHIAN-1986] (the map) and
  [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002, Section 2.1] (derivative of an inverse
  transformation).

### EQ-SENS-DELTA-001 — Borgonovo's delta and its class-partition estimator

`delta_i = (1/2) E_{X_i}[int |f_Y(y) - f_{Y | X_i}(y)| dy]`; estimator
`delta_i = (1/2) sum_m (n_m / n) int |f(y) - f_m(y)| dy` over `M`
equal-count classes of `x_i`, with `int |f - f_m| dy = sum_b |p_b - p_mb|`
for a histogram on `B` bins of equal pooled frequency
(`bin(y_k) = floor(B #{j : y_j < y_k} / n)`), or a trapezoidal integral of
Gaussian kernel density estimates.

- Domain: `n` i.i.d. rows, at least ten rows per class, non-constant
  output; continuous `x_i`.
- Meaning: the expected total-variation distance between the conditional
  and the unconditional output law; in `[0, 1]`, zero if and only if `Y`
  and `X_i` are independent, invariant under strictly monotone
  transformations of `Y`. For `Y = a_1 X_1 + a_2 X_2` with standard normal
  inputs `Y | X_1 = x ~ N(a_1 x, a_2^2)` and `delta_1` is a
  two-dimensional quadrature (0.5055 for `a = (2, 1)`). The estimator is
  positive for an irrelevant input (sampling noise of order
  `sqrt(B / n_m)`) and too low for a strongly influential one (class
  averaging).
- Code: `sensitivity.borgonovo_delta`.
- Source: [REF-BORGONOVO-2007] (index) and
  [REF-PLISCHKE-BORGONOVO-SMITH-2013] (estimation from given data by class
  partition).

### EQ-SENS-DELTA-002 — Permutation null level of a partition-based index

For `P` random assignments `pi_p` of the outputs to the classes and an
index `T`: `null = (1/P) sum_p T(pi_p)`, `corrected = T - null`,
`p = (1 + #{p : T(pi_p) >= T}) / (P + 1)`.

- Domain: i.i.d. rows; equal class sizes for all inputs, so one set of
  assignments serves every input.
- Meaning: the value the estimator takes when the output does not depend
  on the input; the p-value has exact level. `corrected` is a heuristic
  that over-corrects influential inputs, whose noise bias is smaller than
  the null level.
- Code: `sensitivity.borgonovo_delta`, `sensitivity.pawn_indices`
  (`permutations=`).
- Source: [REF-PHIPSON-SMYTH-2010] (p-value); the null-level subtraction
  is a library choice.

### EQ-SENS-PAWN-001 — PAWN index from a class partition

`KS_m = max_y |F_n(y) - F_m(y)|` with `F_n` the empirical distribution
function of all outputs and `F_m` that of class `m` of `x_i`;
`PAWN_i = stat_m KS_m`, `stat` the median, mean, or maximum.

- Domain: `n` i.i.d. rows, `M >= 2` equal-count classes of at least five
  rows, non-constant output.
- Meaning: the Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between the conditional and
  the unconditional output distribution, summarized over the conditioning
  classes; depends on the outputs only through their order, hence exactly
  invariant under strictly monotone transformations of `Y`. Positive for
  an irrelevant input (order `sqrt(1 / n_m)`).
- Code: `sensitivity.pawn_indices`.
- Source: [REF-PIANOSI-WAGENER-2015]; the class-partition estimate from a
  generic sample is the library's adaptation of their conditional design.

### EQ-SENS-KERNEL-001 — Kernel (MMD) first-order index

`S_i^k = E_{X_i}[MMD_k^2(P_Y, P_{Y | X_i})] / (E[k(Y, Y)] - E[k(Y, Y')])
= (E[k(Y, Y^i)] - E[k(Y, Y')]) / (E[k(Y, Y)] - E[k(Y, Y')])`,
with `Y^i` sharing only `X_i` with `Y` and `Y'` an independent copy.

- Domain: independent inputs, a symmetric positive-definite kernel with
  `E[k(Y, Y)] < inf` and a non-degenerate output.
- Meaning: with mean embeddings `mu_P = E_P[k(Y, .)]`,
  `E[k(Y, Y^i)] = E|mu_{Y | X_i}|^2` and `E[k(Y, Y')] = |mu_Y|^2`, so the
  numerator is `E|mu_{Y | X_i} - mu_Y|^2`. The linear kernel gives the
  first-order Sobol index [EQ-SENS-FIRST-001]; a characteristic kernel
  gives an index that vanishes only under independence.
- Code: `sensitivity.kernel_sobol_indices`,
  `sensitivity.model_kernel_sobol_indices`.
- Source: [REF-DA-VEIGA-2021].

### EQ-SENS-KERNEL-002 — Pooled pick-freeze estimator of the kernel index

With `y_B`, `y_i = f(A_B^(i))` and the pooled outputs `z = (y_B, y_i)`:
`T1 = (1/N) sum_n k(y_B,n, y_i,n)`, `T0 = (1/(2N)^2) sum_{a,b} k(z_a, z_b)`,
`T2 = (1/(2N)) sum_a k(z_a, z_a)`, `S_i^k = (T1 - T0) / (T2 - T0)`.
Gaussian kernel `k(y, y') = exp(-(y - y')^2 / (2 h^2))` with `h` the median
pairwise distance of `y_B` by default.

- Domain: `N >= 4` rows per base matrix, `T2 > T0`.
- Meaning: a V-statistic with `O(1/N)` bias and `N (d + 1)` model runs; for
  the linear kernel `T0` is the squared pooled mean and the estimator is
  exactly that of [EQ-SENS-EST-006].
- Code: `sensitivity.kernel_sobol_indices`,
  `sensitivity.model_kernel_sobol_indices`.
- Source: [REF-DA-VEIGA-2021] (pick-freeze form), [REF-JANON-ETAL-2014]
  (pooled symmetric estimator) and [REF-GRETTON-ETAL-2008] (median
  heuristic).

## Robust means, shrinkage covariance, dependence measures, and sliced and unbalanced transport (ADR-0127)

### EQ-STAT-ROB-001 — Median-of-means estimator

Split `x_1..x_n` into `k` disjoint blocks `B_1..B_k` with
`|B_j| in {floor(n/k), ceil(n/k)}`;
`mu_hat = median(Z_1, ..., Z_k)`, `Z_j = (1/|B_j|) sum_{i in B_j} x_i`
(the mean of the two middle values for even `k`).

- Domain: `1 <= k <= n`; the block assignment must not depend on the values
  (seeded random permutation, or sequential for data whose order carries no
  information).
- Meaning: a mean estimator whose deviations have a logarithmic dependence
  on the confidence level under a finite variance only; `k = 1` is the
  sample mean and `k = n` the sample median.
- Code: `statistics.median_of_means`, `statistics.MedianOfMeansResult`.
- Source: [REF-LUGOSI-MENDELSON-2019].

### EQ-STAT-ROB-002 — Median-of-means deviation bound

For independent observations with mean `mu` and variance at most `sigma^2`
and `m = min_j |B_j| = floor(n/k)`:
`P(|mu_hat - mu| > 2 sigma / sqrt(m)) <= exp(-k/8)`, so
`k = ceil(8 log(1/delta))` gives failure probability at most `delta`.
Derivation: by Chebyshev `P(|Z_j - mu| > 2 sigma/sqrt(m)) <= 1/4` for every
block; the median (also the mid-point form for even `k`) can miss by more
than that only if at least `k/2` blocks do; the blocks are independent, and
Hoeffding's inequality gives
`P(Bin(k, 1/4) >= k/2) <= exp(-2 k (1/4)^2) = exp(-k/8)`.

- Domain: independent observations with a common mean, finite variance,
  blocks chosen independently of the values, `0 < delta < 1`.
- Meaning: with `k` of order `log(1/delta)` the error is of order
  `sigma sqrt(log(1/delta)/n)`; the constants of this elementary argument
  are not sharp.
- Code: `statistics.median_of_means_block_count`,
  `statistics.MedianOfMeansResult.deviation_bound`.
- Source: [REF-LUGOSI-MENDELSON-2019] (the estimator and the argument); the
  constants printed here are the ones derived above.

### EQ-STAT-ROB-003 — Catoni's M-estimator of the mean

`theta_hat` solves `sum_{i=1}^n psi(a (x_i - theta)) = 0`,
`psi(x) = sign(x) log(1 + |x| + x^2/2)`.

- Domain: `a > 0`; the left-hand side is continuous and strictly decreasing
  in `theta`, non-negative at `min x_i` and non-positive at `max x_i`, so
  the root is unique and lies in the sample range.
- Meaning: a soft truncation of large deviations; `psi(x) = x - x^3/6 +
  O(x^4)`, so `theta_hat` tends to the sample mean as `a -> 0`. Translation
  equivariant; scale equivariant only if `a` is rescaled with the data.
- Code: `statistics.catoni_mean`, `statistics.catoni_influence`,
  `statistics.CatoniMeanResult`.
- Source: [REF-CATONI-2012]; the root is found with [EQ-OPT-BRENT-001].

### EQ-STAT-ROB-004 — Default scale of Catoni's estimator

`a = sqrt(2 log(1/delta) / (n v))`.

- Domain: `n >= 1`, variance bound `v > 0`, `0 < delta < 1`.
- Meaning: a scale of the order analysed in the source, for which the error
  is of order `sqrt(v log(1/delta)/n)` with probability `1 - delta`; the
  source gives the exact constants and conditions, which are not reproduced
  here. Without a supplied `v` the library plugs in the unbiased sample
  variance, a heuristic.
- Code: `statistics.catoni_scale`, `statistics.catoni_mean`.
- Source: [REF-CATONI-2012].

### EQ-STAT-LW-001 — Ledoit-Wolf linear shrinkage towards a scaled identity

With rows `x_k` in `R^p`, `S = (1/n) sum_k x_k x_k'`,
`||A||^2 = tr(A A')/p`: `m = tr(S)/p`, `d^2 = ||S - m I||^2`,
`bbar^2 = (1/n^2) sum_k ||x_k x_k' - S||^2`, `b^2 = min(bbar^2, d^2)`,
`Sigma_hat = (b^2/d^2) m I + (1 - b^2/d^2) S`.
Evaluated with `sum_k ||x_k x_k' - S||^2 = (sum_k |x_k|^4 - n tr(S^2))/p`.

- Domain: `n >= 1` rows with mean zero (the source's setting), or `n >= 2`
  rows centred by their column means (library default; an `O(1/n)` relative
  effect not analysed in the source); divisor `n`; `d^2 > 0` (for `d^2 = 0`
  the intensity is set to 0 and `Sigma_hat = S = m I`).
- Meaning: the eigenvalues of `S` are pulled towards their mean; the result
  is positive definite when the intensity and `m` are positive, also for
  `p > n`, and asymptotically minimizes the expected Frobenius loss among
  linear combinations of `I` and `S`.
- Code: `statistics.ledoit_wolf_covariance`, `statistics.LedoitWolfResult`.
- Source: [REF-LEDOIT-WOLF-2004].

### EQ-STAT-DEP-001 — Chatterjee's rank correlation

Order the pairs so that `x_(1) <= ... <= x_(n)` and let `r_i` be the rank of
the `i`-th `y` in that order: `xi_n = 1 - 3 sum_{i=1}^{n-1} |r_{i+1} - r_i|
/ (n^2 - 1)`. For a strictly monotone relation `r_i = i` or `n + 1 - i`,
the sum is `n - 1`, and `xi_n = 1 - 3/(n + 1) = (n - 2)/(n + 1)`.

- Domain: `n >= 2` pairs without ties in `y`; ties in `x` are broken
  uniformly at random.
- Meaning: converges to a limit that is 0 if and only if `x` and `y` are
  independent and 1 if and only if `y` is a measurable function of `x`; not
  symmetric in its arguments.
- Code: `statistics.chatterjee_correlation`, `statistics.ChatterjeeResult`.
- Source: [REF-CHATTERJEE-2021].

### EQ-STAT-DEP-002 — Null distribution of Chatterjee's coefficient

Under independence with continuous `y`: `sqrt(n) xi_n -> N(0, 2/5)` in
distribution; `z = sqrt(5 n / 2) xi_n`, one-sided `p = 1 - Phi(z)`.

- Domain: independent pairs, no ties in `y`, large `n`.
- Meaning: an asymptotic test of independence that rejects for large
  `xi_n`.
- Code: `statistics.chatterjee_correlation`.
- Source: [REF-CHATTERJEE-2021].

### EQ-STAT-DEP-003 — Sample distance covariance

`a_kl = |x_k - x_l|`, `A_kl = a_kl - abar_k. - abar_.l + abar_..`, likewise
`B` from `y`; `dCov_n^2(x, y) = (1/n^2) sum_{k,l} A_kl B_kl`,
`dVar_n^2(x) = dCov_n^2(x, x)`.

- Domain: `n >= 2` paired observations in `R^p` and `R^q` with Euclidean
  norms; `O(n^2)` time and memory.
- Meaning: the V-statistic estimator of the squared distance covariance,
  non-negative and biased upwards under independence.
- Code: `statistics.distance_correlation`,
  `statistics.DistanceCorrelationResult`.
- Source: [REF-SZEKELY-RIZZO-BAKIROV-2007].

### EQ-STAT-DEP-004 — Distance correlation and its permutation test

`dCor_n = dCov_n(x, y) / sqrt(dVar_n(x) dVar_n(y))` (0 when a distance
variance is 0); with `R` uniform random permutations `pi_r` of the `y`
observations, `p = (1 + #{r : dCov_n^2(x, y o pi_r) >= dCov_n^2(x, y)}) /
(1 + R)`.

- Domain: as [EQ-STAT-DEP-003]; exchangeable pairs for the test.
- Meaning: `0 <= dCor_n <= 1`, equal to 1 for `y = a + b x` with scalar
  `b != 0`, invariant to translations, orthogonal transformations, and
  positive rescaling; the population value is 0 if and only if the vectors
  are independent (finite first moments).
- Code: `statistics.distance_correlation`.
- Source: [REF-SZEKELY-RIZZO-BAKIROV-2007].

### EQ-STAT-DEP-005 — Distance correlation of a bivariate normal pair

`dCor^2 = (rho asin(rho) + sqrt(1 - rho^2) - rho asin(rho/2)
- sqrt(4 - rho^2) + 1) / (1 + pi/3 - sqrt(3))`.
Derivation: `dCov^2 = E|X-X'||Y-Y'| + E|X-X'| E|Y-Y'| - 2 E|X-X'||Y-Y''|`
with independent copies, `E|UV| = (2/pi)(sqrt(1 - r^2) + r asin(r))` for a
standard bivariate normal pair with correlation `r`, differences of
variance 2 with correlations `rho` and `rho/2`, and `E|X-X'| = 2/sqrt(pi)`
give `dCov^2 = (4/pi)` times the numerator; `rho = 1` gives the
denominator.

- Domain: `-1 <= rho <= 1`; any means and positive scales.
- Meaning: even and increasing in `|rho|` and at most `|rho|`.
- Code: `statistics.distance_correlation_bivariate_normal`.
- Source: [REF-SZEKELY-RIZZO-BAKIROV-2007]; re-derived as stated and
  checked by quadrature in the tests.

### EQ-OT-SW-001 — One-dimensional Wasserstein distance between discrete laws

For `mu = sum_i a_i delta_{x_i}` and `nu = sum_j b_j delta_{y_j}` on the
line with unit masses: `W_p^p = int_0^1 |Q_mu(u) - Q_nu(u)|^p du
= sum_k (c_k - c_{k-1}) |x_(i(k)) - y_(j(k))|^p`, where `c_k` are the merged
cumulative weights and `i(k)`, `j(k)` the atoms whose quantile level
contains `(c_{k-1}, c_k)`. For `n` equally weighted atoms each:
`W_p^p = (1/n) sum_i |x_(i) - y_(i)|^p`.

- Domain: `p >= 1`; non-negative weights normalized to one.
- Meaning: the monotone coupling is optimal on the line
  ([EQ-OT-W1D-001]); for step quantile functions the integral is a finite
  sum after sorting.
- Code: `information.empirical_wasserstein_1d`,
  `information.sliced_wasserstein`.
- Source: [REF-PEYRE-CUTURI-2019]; [REF-VILLANI-2009, Chapter 6].

### EQ-OT-SW-002 — Sliced Wasserstein distance

`SW_p^p(mu, nu) = E_theta[W_p^p(theta_# mu, theta_# nu)]`, `theta` uniform
on the unit sphere of `R^d`, `theta_#` the push-forward by `x -> theta'x`;
estimated by `(1/L) sum_l W_p^p(theta_l# mu, theta_l# nu)` with
`theta_l = z_l/|z_l|`, `z_l ~ N(0, I_d)`, and standard error
`s/sqrt(L)` from the sample standard deviation `s` of the `L` terms. For
`nu = mu` translated by `t`: `W_2^2(theta_# mu, theta_# nu) = (theta't)^2`
and `E[(theta't)^2] = |t|^2/d` (by symmetry `E[theta theta'] = I/d`), so
`SW_2^2 = |t|^2/d`.

- Domain: discrete measures in `R^d` with unit mass, `p >= 1`, `L >= 2`
  directions; exact for `d = 1`.
- Meaning: a metric bounded above by `W_p` that costs a sort per direction;
  the standard error covers the random directions only.
- Code: `information.sliced_wasserstein`,
  `information.SlicedWassersteinResult`.
- Source: [REF-BONNEEL-ETAL-2015].

### EQ-OT-UB-001 — Unbalanced entropic transport objective

`min_{P >= 0} <C, P> + eps KL(P | a b') + rho KL(P 1 | a) + rho KL(P' 1 | b)`
with `KL(p | q) = sum_i (p_i log(p_i/q_i) - p_i + q_i)` and `0 log 0 = 0`.

- Domain: non-negative weights `a`, `b` with positive, possibly different,
  total masses; finite cost; `eps > 0`, `rho > 0`.
- Meaning: transport with marginals relaxed by Kullback-Leibler penalties;
  strictly convex, so the minimizer is unique. The entropy is taken
  relative to `a b'` (the convention of `information.sinkhorn`); the
  counting-measure convention changes the objective by terms that depend on
  the marginals.
- Code: `information.unbalanced_sinkhorn`,
  `information.UnbalancedSinkhornResult`.
- Source: [REF-CHIZAT-ETAL-2018].

### EQ-OT-UB-002 — Unbalanced Sinkhorn (scaling) iteration

Stationarity of [EQ-OT-UB-001] in `P_ij`:
`C_ij + eps log(P_ij/(a_i b_j)) + rho log((P1)_i/a_i)
+ rho log((P'1)_j/b_j) = 0`, so
`P_ij = a_i b_j exp((f_i + g_j - C_ij)/eps)` with
`f_i = -rho log((P1)_i/a_i)`, `g_j = -rho log((P'1)_j/b_j)`. Substituting
the row sum gives `f = lambda T(g)`, `g = lambda T(f)` with
`lambda = rho/(rho + eps)`,
`T(g)_i = -eps log sum_j b_j exp((g_j - C_ij)/eps)`,
`T(f)_j = -eps log sum_i a_i exp((f_i - C_ij)/eps)`; with `u = exp(f/eps)`,
`v = exp(g/eps)`, `K = exp(-C/eps)`: `u = (1/(K (b v)))^lambda`,
`v = (1/(K' (a u)))^lambda` (for entropy relative to the counting measure
the same steps give `u = (a/(K v))^lambda`, `v = (b/(K' u))^lambda`).

- Domain: as [EQ-OT-UB-001]; evaluated with log-sum-exp.
- Meaning: alternating exact maximization of the dual in `f` and `g`; each
  half-step is `lambda` times a sup-norm non-expansive map, so the
  iteration contracts at least by `lambda^2` per pair, and `lambda -> 1`
  recovers balanced Sinkhorn ([EQ-OT-SINK-001]).
- Code: `information.unbalanced_sinkhorn`.
- Source: [REF-CHIZAT-ETAL-2018]; derived as stated for the reference
  measure `a b'`.

### EQ-OT-UB-003 — Dual objective and translation step

`D(f, g) = rho sum_i a_i (1 - exp(-f_i/rho)) + rho sum_j b_j (1 -
exp(-g_j/rho)) - eps sum_ij a_i b_j (exp((f_i + g_j - C_ij)/eps) - 1)`;
`D(f, g) <= min` of [EQ-OT-UB-001] with equality at the fixed point of
[EQ-OT-UB-002]. Along `(f + c, g - c)` the last term is constant and
`dD/dc = 0` gives
`c = (rho/2) log(sum_i a_i exp(-f_i/rho) / sum_j b_j exp(-g_j/rho))`.

- Domain: as [EQ-OT-UB-001].
- Meaning: the duality gap is a computable optimality certificate; the
  translation step removes the direction along which the plain iteration
  contracts only by `lambda^2`, which is close to 1 for `rho >> eps`. A
  fixed point has `c = 0`.
- Code: `information.unbalanced_sinkhorn`,
  `information.UnbalancedSinkhornResult.duality_gap`.
- Source: [REF-CHIZAT-ETAL-2018] (dual formulation); the closed-form
  translation step is derived here.

## Smoothed-indicator rare-event methods and BUS (ADR-0124)

### EQ-REL-ICE-001 — Smoothed failure indicator and intermediate targets

`h_k(u) = Phi(-G(u) / sigma_k) phi_n(u) / P_k`,
`P_k = E_phi[Phi(-G(u) / sigma_k)]`, `sigma_0 = inf > sigma_1 > ... > 0`;
`Phi(-G / sigma) -> I(G <= 0)` as `sigma -> 0` for `G != 0`, and
`Phi(-G / inf) = 1/2`, so `h_0 = phi_n`.

- Domain: independent standard-normal coordinates `u`, failure set
  `G <= 0`, `sigma > 0`.
- Meaning: a sequence of smooth densities from the nominal law to the
  optimal importance-sampling density `I(G <= 0) phi_n / P_f`; every sample
  has a positive weight at every level.
- Code: `reliability.improved_cross_entropy`,
  `reliability.sequential_importance_sampling`.
- Source: [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-PAPADIMITRIOU-STRAUB-2016];
  [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-GEYER-STRAUB-2019].

### EQ-REL-ICE-002 — Smoothing scale from a target weight variation

`sigma_(k+1) < sigma_k` solves `cv(W_1(sigma), ..., W_N(sigma)) = delta`,
`W_i(sigma) = Phi(-G(u_i) / sigma) b_i`, with the base weights
`b_i = phi_n(u_i) / q_k(u_i)` (parametric proposal `q_k`) or
`b_i = 1 / Phi(-G(u_i) / sigma_k)` (sample from `h_k`; `b_i = 1` at level 0);
`cv` is the population standard deviation over the mean.

- Domain: `delta > 0` (default `1.5`); the search scans `sigma` downward by
  a factor `0.7` and bisects the first crossing on `log sigma`.
- Meaning: the step between two levels is as large as a prescribed
  degeneracy of the importance weights allows, which fixes the effective
  sample size `N / (1 + delta^2)` of each update.
- Code: `reliability.smoothing_scale`.
- Source: [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-PAPADIMITRIOU-STRAUB-2016];
  [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-GEYER-STRAUB-2019].

### EQ-REL-ICE-003 — Weighted maximum likelihood of the proposal

Maximize `sum_i W_i log q(u_i; v)`. Single Gaussian:
`mu = sum W_i u_i / sum W_i`,
`Sigma = sum W_i (u_i - mu)(u_i - mu)' / sum W_i`. Gaussian mixture
`q = sum_j pi_j N(mu_j, Sigma_j)` by EM: `gamma_ij` proportional to
`pi_j N(u_i; mu_j, Sigma_j)` with `sum_j gamma_ij = 1`, then
`pi_j = sum_i W_i gamma_ij / sum_i W_i`,
`mu_j = sum_i W_i gamma_ij u_i / sum_i W_i gamma_ij`,
`Sigma_j = sum_i W_i gamma_ij (u_i - mu_j)(u_i - mu_j)' / sum_i W_i gamma_ij`.

- Domain: weights `W_i >= 0` of [EQ-REL-ICE-002] with a positive sum;
  optional eigenvalue floor above `1/2` on every covariance (a library
  guard, [EQ-REL-CE-003]).
- Meaning: the sample version of minimizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence
  from `h_(k+1)` to the parametric family; the EM iteration does not
  decrease the weighted log-likelihood.
- Code: `reliability.improved_cross_entropy`.
- Source: [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-GEYER-STRAUB-2019];
  [REF-DEMPSTER-LAIRD-RUBIN-1977].

### EQ-REL-ICE-004 — Stopping criterion of the smooth levels

Stop at level `k` when
`cv(I(G(u_i) <= 0) / Phi(-G(u_i) / sigma_k), i = 1..N) <= delta`.

- Domain: a sample drawn from the proposal fitted to `h_k` (improved cross
  entropy) or approximately from `h_k` (sequential importance sampling);
  the value is infinite when no sample failed.
- Meaning: `I(G <= 0) / Phi(-G / sigma_k)` is proportional to the density
  ratio of the optimal importance-sampling density and `h_k`, so a small
  variation means that `h_k` is close to the optimal density.
- Code: `reliability.improved_cross_entropy`,
  `reliability.sequential_importance_sampling`.
- Source: [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-GEYER-STRAUB-2019];
  [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-PAPADIMITRIOU-STRAUB-2016].

### EQ-REL-ICE-005 — Mixture-proposal importance-sampling estimate

`P_f_hat = (1/N) sum_i I(G(u_i) <= 0) phi_n(u_i) / q(u_i)`, `u_i ~ q`,
`q(u) = sum_j pi_j N(u; mu_j, L_j L_j')`,
`log N(u; mu_j, L_j L_j') = -||L_j^-1 (u - mu_j)||^2 / 2 - log det L_j
- (n/2) log 2 pi`; standard error from the sample variance of the terms.

- Domain: positive-definite component covariances; finite variance needs
  every covariance eigenvalue above `1/2` ([EQ-REL-CE-003] applied to each
  component).
- Meaning: unbiased given the proposal, which was fitted to earlier samples
  only; the `2 pi` constants of numerator and denominator cancel.
- Code: `reliability.improved_cross_entropy`.
- Source: [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-GEYER-STRAUB-2019]; [REF-OWEN-2013, Chapter 9].

### EQ-REL-SIS-001 — Sequential importance-sampling estimator

With `eta_0 = phi_n`, `eta_k = Phi(-G / sigma_k) phi_n` and normalizing
constants `P_0 = 1`, `P_k = E_phi[Phi(-G / sigma_k)]`:
`P_f = (prod_(k=1..L) P_k / P_(k-1)) E_(h_L)[I(G <= 0) / Phi(-G / sigma_L)]`,
estimated by `S_k = mean(w_k)` over the sample of level `k - 1` with
`w_1 = Phi(-G / sigma_1)` and
`w_k = Phi(-G / sigma_k) / Phi(-G / sigma_(k-1))` for `k >= 2`, and by the
sample mean of `I(G <= 0) / Phi(-G / sigma_L)` over level `L`.

- Domain: level samples distributed as `h_k` [EQ-REL-ICE-001]. The level-0
  factor is `1`, not `Phi(-G / inf) = 1/2`, because `h_0 = phi_n` has
  `P_0 = 1`.
- Meaning: a telescoping product of ratios of normalizing constants; the
  identity is exact because `I(G <= 0) phi_n = [I(G <= 0) / Phi(-G /
  sigma_L)] eta_L`.
- Code: `reliability.sequential_importance_sampling`.
- Source: [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-PAPADIMITRIOU-STRAUB-2016].

### EQ-REL-SIS-002 — Conditional-sampling Metropolis step for a smooth target

`v = rho u + sqrt(1 - rho^2) z`, `z ~ N(0, I)`; accept `v` with probability
`min(1, Phi(-G(v) / sigma) / Phi(-G(u) / sigma))`.

- Domain: `0 <= rho < 1`, `sigma > 0`.
- Meaning: the proposal density `q(v | u)` satisfies
  `phi_n(u) q(v | u) = phi_n(v) q(u | v)`, so the Metropolis-Hastings ratio
  of the target `Phi(-G / sigma) phi_n` reduces to the ratio of the smooth
  indicators and `h_k` is invariant; with `sigma -> 0` it becomes the
  accept-inside step of [EQ-REL-SUBSET-004].
- Code: `reliability.sequential_importance_sampling`.
- Source: [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-PAPADIMITRIOU-STRAUB-2016];
  [REF-COTTER-ROBERTS-STUART-WHITE-2013].

### EQ-REL-SIS-003 — Resampling and chain layout of a level

`N_c = N f` seeds are drawn with replacement with probabilities
`w_k(u_i) / sum_j w_k(u_j)`; each seed runs `b` discarded steps of
[EQ-REL-SIS-002] and then contributes `N / N_c` consecutive states. The
spread `sqrt(1 - rho^2) = min(lambda, 1)` follows
`ln lambda <- ln lambda + (a_hat - a*) / sqrt(i + 1)` after every `N_a`
chains with their mean acceptance rate `a_hat`, as in [EQ-REL-SUBSET-005].

- Domain: `N_c >= 2` divides `N`; library defaults `f = 0.02`, `b = 10`,
  `N_a = 2`, `a* = 0.44`, `lambda = 0.6` at the first level and carried on.
- Meaning: weighted resampling turns a sample of `h_(k-1)` into an
  approximate sample of `h_k`; the chains restore diversity. Consistent as
  `N -> infinity`; for finite `N` a level sample that lags behind its target
  biases the following ratios in the same direction.
- Code: `reliability.sequential_importance_sampling`.
- Source: [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-PAPADIMITRIOU-STRAUB-2016];
  [REF-PAPAIOANNOU-BETZ-ZWIRGLMAIER-STRAUB-2015].

### EQ-REL-SIS-004 — Batch-means c.o.v. of the sequential estimate

`delta^2 = sum_(k=1..L+1) s_k^2 / (N_c,k m_k^2)`, where for factor `k` the
`m_kc` are the means of its terms over each chain (single draws at level 0),
`m_k` their mean, `s_k^2` their sample variance, and `N_c,k` their number.

- Domain: at least two chains per level.
- Meaning: a heuristic first-order c.o.v. of the product: batch means absorb
  the correlation inside a chain, while the dependence between factors and
  between chains started from the same resampled point is ignored, so the
  value understates the scatter between independent runs.
- Code: `reliability.sequential_importance_sampling`.
- Source: [REF-GEYER-1992] (batch means); the combination is a convention
  of this library.

### EQ-REL-BUS-001 — BUS acceptance event as a limit state

`g(u, u_p) = log Phi(u_p) - log c - log L(theta(u))`, `theta(u) = T^-1(u)`
the prior's map from standard-normal space; `g <= 0` if and only if
`p <= c L(theta)` with `p = Phi(u_p) ~ U(0, 1)`.

- Domain: `c > 0` with `c L(theta) <= 1` for every `theta`; `u_p`
  independent of `u`.
- Meaning: `theta` conditional on `g <= 0` follows the posterior
  `L(theta) pi(theta) / Z`, because
  `P(p <= c L(theta) | theta) = c L(theta)`; the source states the event as
  `p - c L(theta) <= 0`, of which this is the logarithmic form. If
  `c L > 1` somewhere the conditional law is the posterior of
  `min(L, 1/c)`.
- Code: `reliability.bus_limit_state`, `reliability.bus_subset_simulation`.
- Source: [REF-STRAUB-PAPAIOANNOU-2015].

### EQ-REL-BUS-002 — Evidence from the acceptance probability

`Z = E_prior[L(theta)] = P(p <= c L(theta)) / c`.

- Domain: as [EQ-REL-BUS-001].
- Meaning: the model evidence is the probability of the acceptance event
  divided by the constant, so its relative error is that of the rare-event
  estimate.
- Code: `reliability.bus_subset_simulation`.
- Source: [REF-STRAUB-PAPAIOANNOU-2015].

### EQ-REL-BUS-003 — Check of the BUS constant

`max_i (log c + log L(theta_i)) <= 0` over every evaluated point
`theta_i`.

- Domain: the points evaluated in one run.
- Meaning: a necessary condition for `c <= 1 / sup L` that costs no extra
  likelihood call; a violation shows that the constant is too large, a clean
  check does not prove that it is small enough.
- Code: `reliability.bus_subset_simulation`.
- Source: [REF-STRAUB-PAPAIOANNOU-2015] (requirement `c L <= 1`); the
  run-time check is a convention of this library.

## Competing risks, restricted-mean contrasts, online change points, and forecast reconciliation (ADR-0128)

### EQ-SURV-CIF-001 — Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence function

`F_k(t) = sum_{t_j <= t} S(t_j-) d_kj / n_j`, with
`S(t) = prod_{t_j <= t} (1 - d_j / n_j)` the all-cause Kaplan-Meier
estimator and `d_j = sum_k d_kj`; hence `sum_k F_k(t) = 1 - S(t)`.

- Domain: right-censored competing-risks data, censoring independent of the
  event process; `t_j` the distinct event times of any cause.
- Meaning: the probability of failing from cause `k` by `t` in the presence
  of the other causes. The complement of a Kaplan-Meier curve that censors
  the competing events is never smaller, and it estimates a different
  quantity.
- Code: `inference.survival.cumulative_incidence`,
  `inference.survival.cumulative_incidence_curves`,
  `inference.survival.CumulativeIncidenceEstimate.incidence_at`.
- Source: [REF-AALEN-JOHANSEN-1978].

### EQ-SURV-CIF-002 — Delta-method variance of the cumulative incidence

`Var F_k(t) = sum_{t_j <= t} [ (F_k(t) - F_k(t_j))^2 d_j / (n_j (n_j - d_j))
+ S(t_j-)^2 d_kj (n_j - d_kj) / n_j^3
- 2 (F_k(t) - F_k(t_j)) S(t_j-) d_kj / n_j^2 ]`; interval
`F_k +/- z sqrt(Var)` clipped to `[0, 1]`.

- Domain: [EQ-SURV-CIF-001]; large samples. The term of the last event time
  has `F_k(t) - F_k(t_j) = 0`, so `n_j = d_j` causes no division by zero.
- Meaning: first-order (delta-method) variance obtained by treating the
  counts `(d_kj, d_j - d_kj, n_j - d_j)` at different event times as
  independent multinomials given the risk sets, the argument behind
  Greenwood's formula. Without censoring it equals `F_k (1 - F_k) / n`; with
  one cause it equals [EQ-SURV-KM-002]. Derived in ADR-0128 and checked
  against replicate simulation.
- Code: `inference.survival.cumulative_incidence`,
  `inference.survival.CumulativeIncidenceEstimate.interval_at`.
- Source: [REF-GREENWOOD-1926] (the variance argument),
  [REF-AALEN-JOHANSEN-1978] (the estimator); derivation in ADR-0128.

### EQ-SURV-RMST-002 — Difference and ratio of restricted means

`D = mu_1(tau) - mu_2(tau)`, `se(D) = sqrt(V_1 + V_2)`,
`R = mu_1(tau) / mu_2(tau)`, `se(log R) = sqrt(V_1 / mu_1^2 + V_2 / mu_2^2)`;
intervals `D +/- z se(D)` and `R exp(+/- z se(log R))`; test statistic
`D / se(D) ~ N(0, 1)` under `mu_1 = mu_2`.

- Domain: two independent right-censored samples; `tau` inside the follow-up
  of both; `mu_i` and `V_i` from [EQ-SURV-RMST-001].
- Meaning: the gain in expected event-free time within `tau`, on the
  additive and on the relative scale, without a proportional-hazards
  assumption. The estimand depends on `tau`.
- Code: `inference.survival.compare_restricted_means`,
  `inference.survival.restricted_mean_survival`.
- Source: [REF-KLEIN-MOESCHBERGER-2003, Chapter 4] (restricted mean and its
  variance), [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002] (delta method).

### EQ-TS-BOCPD-001 — Run-length recursion with a constant hazard

`P(r_t = r + 1, x_1:t) = P(r_(t-1) = r, x_1:(t-1)) pi_r(x_t) (1 - H)`,
`P(r_t = 0, x_1:t) = H sum_r P(r_(t-1) = r, x_1:(t-1)) pi_r(x_t)`,
`P(r_0 = 0) = 1`; `P(x_1:t) = sum_r P(r_t = r, x_1:t)` and
`P(r_t | x_1:t) = P(r_t, x_1:t) / P(x_1:t)`.

- Domain: product partition model; `pi_r` the posterior predictive given the
  `r` most recent observations; `0 <= H <= 1`.
- Meaning: `r_t` counts the observations up to `t` in the segment that also
  generates `x_(t+1)`. The evidence equals
  `sum over segmentations of H^m (1 - H)^(t-1-m) prod_segments p(x_segment)`.
  `P(r_t = 0 | x_1:t) = H` for all `t`; changes show as mass on short
  positive run lengths. Dropping run lengths above a bound makes the
  evidence a lower bound.
- Code: `timeseries.bayesian_online_changepoint`,
  `timeseries.OnlineChangePointResult.segment_start_probability`,
  `timeseries.OnlineChangePointResult.run_length_probability`,
  `timeseries.OnlineChangePointResult.map_change_points`.
- Source: [REF-ADAMS-MACKAY-2007].

### EQ-TS-BOCPD-002 — Normal-inverse-gamma predictive and evidence

Prior `sigma^2 ~ IG(alpha_0, beta_0)`, `mu | sigma^2 ~ N(m_0, sigma^2 / kappa_0)`.
Update with `x`: `m' = (kappa m + x) / (kappa + 1)`, `kappa' = kappa + 1`,
`alpha' = alpha + 1/2`, `beta' = beta + kappa (x - m)^2 / (2 (kappa + 1))`.
Predictive: Student-t with `2 alpha` degrees of freedom, location `m`,
squared scale `beta (kappa + 1) / (alpha kappa)`. Evidence:
`p(x_1:n) = Gamma(alpha_n) / Gamma(alpha_0) * beta_0^alpha_0 / beta_n^alpha_n
* sqrt(kappa_0 / kappa_n) * (2 pi)^(-n/2)`.

- Domain: `kappa_0, alpha_0, beta_0 > 0`; real observations.
- Meaning: conjugate updating for a Gaussian segment with unknown mean and
  variance; the product of the one-step predictives equals the evidence.
- Code: `timeseries.NormalInverseGammaPrior.log_predictive`,
  `timeseries.NormalInverseGammaPrior.log_marginal_likelihood`,
  `timeseries.bayesian_online_changepoint`.
- Source: [REF-MURPHY-2007].

### EQ-TS-BOCPD-003 — Gamma-Poisson predictive and evidence

Prior `lambda ~ Gamma(a_0, b_0)` (rate `b_0`). Update with a count `x`:
`a' = a + x`, `b' = b + 1`. Predictive:
`p(x) = Gamma(a + x) / (Gamma(a) x!) * (b / (b + 1))^a * (b + 1)^(-x)`.
Evidence: `p(x_1:n) = Gamma(a_0 + s) / Gamma(a_0) * b_0^a_0 /
(b_0 + n)^(a_0 + s) / prod_i x_i!`, `s = sum x_i`.

- Domain: `a_0, b_0 > 0`; non-negative integer counts.
- Meaning: conjugate updating for a Poisson segment; the predictive is
  negative binomial.
- Code: `timeseries.GammaPoissonPrior.log_predictive`,
  `timeseries.GammaPoissonPrior.log_marginal_likelihood`,
  `timeseries.bayesian_online_changepoint`.
- Source: [REF-GELMAN-ETAL-2013].

### EQ-TS-RECON-001 — Coherence and linear reconciliation

Coherent series satisfy `y = S b`; a linear reconciler is
`y_tilde = S G y_hat`, and it preserves unbiasedness iff `G S = I`.
Bottom-up: `G` selects the bottom-level rows of `y_hat`.

- Domain: `S` the `n x m` summing matrix of full column rank; `b` the `m`
  bottom-level series.
- Meaning: `S G` is then a projection onto the column space of `S`
  (idempotent, and the identity on coherent forecasts).
- Code: `timeseries.reconcile_forecasts`,
  `timeseries.hierarchy_summing_matrix`,
  `timeseries.HierarchyStructure.aggregate`,
  `timeseries.ReconciliationResult.projection`.
- Source: [REF-WICKRAMASURIYA-ATHANASOPOULOS-HYNDMAN-2019].

### EQ-TS-RECON-002 — Minimum-trace (generalized least squares) reconciler

`G = (S' W^-1 S)^-1 S' W^-1`; reconciled error covariance
`Var(y - y_tilde) = S G W G' S'`. `W = I` gives OLS, `W = diag(w)` WLS.

- Domain: `W` symmetric positive definite, the covariance of the
  base-forecast errors; [EQ-TS-RECON-001].
- Meaning: among all `G` with `G S = I` this choice minimizes
  `tr(S G W G' S')`, the sum of the reconciled error variances. The
  guarantee is for the true `W`, not for an estimate.
- Code: `timeseries.reconcile_forecasts`,
  `timeseries.ReconciliationResult.error_covariance`,
  `timeseries.ReconciliationResult.total_error_variance`.
- Source: [REF-WICKRAMASURIYA-ATHANASOPOULOS-HYNDMAN-2019].

### EQ-TS-RECON-003 — Covariance shrinkage towards the diagonal

`W = lambda diag(C) + (1 - lambda) C` for the sample covariance `C`. Among
fixed `lambda` the risk `sum_(i != j) E[((1 - lambda) r_ij - rho_ij)^2]` of
the shrunk correlations is minimal at
`lambda* = sum_(i != j) Var(r_ij) / sum_(i != j) E[r_ij^2]` for unbiased
`r_ij`. Plug-in: `lambda_hat = sum_(i != j) Var_hat(r_ij) / sum_(i != j) r_ij^2`
clipped to `[0, 1]`, `Var_hat(r_ij) = N / (N - 1)^3 sum_k (w_kij - w_bar_ij)^2`,
`w_kij = z_ki z_kj` with standardized residuals `z`.

- Domain: `N >= 2` residual vectors with positive variances.
- Meaning: variances are kept and covariances damped, which makes `W`
  positive definite for `lambda > 0` even when `N < n`. `lambda*` follows by
  setting the derivative of the risk to zero (ADR-0128); the plug-in ignores
  the error of the standardization. It coincides with the Schäfer-Strimmer
  intensity for a correlation matrix shrunk towards the identity, applied to
  centred residuals with divisor `N - 1` (MinT software commonly uses
  uncentred residuals with divisor `N`, which gives a different value).
- Code: `timeseries.shrink_covariance`.
- Source: [REF-SCHAFER-STRIMMER-2005] (the intensity);
  [REF-WICKRAMASURIYA-ATHANASOPOULOS-HYNDMAN-2019] (use of a covariance
  shrunk towards its diagonal in MinT); re-derived in ADR-0128.

## Flow matching and neural simulation-based inference (ADR-0129)

### EQ-GEN-FM-001 — Straight-line conditional path and its target velocity

`x_t = (1 - (1 - s) t) x_0 + t x_1`, `x_0 ~ N(0, I)`, `0 <= t <= 1`;
`u = d x_t / dt = x_1 - (1 - s) x_0`. As a field in `x` for fixed `x_1`:
`u_t(x | x_1) = (x_1 - (1 - s) x) / (1 - (1 - s) t)`.

- Domain: `x_0, x_1` in `R^d`; `0 <= s < 1` (`s = sigma_min`).
- Meaning: given `x_1` the path law is `N(t x_1, (1 - (1 - s) t)^2 I)`,
  which starts at `N(0, I)` and ends at `N(x_1, s^2 I)`. The velocity
  follows by differentiating the path in `t` at fixed `(x_0, x_1)`; the
  field form follows from `x_0 = (x - t x_1) / (1 - (1 - s) t)`.
- Code: `generative.conditional_flow_path`, `generative.fit_flow_matching`.
- Source: derivation in `generative.flow_matching` from the path of
  [REF-LIPMAN-ETAL-2023].

### EQ-GEN-FM-002 — Conditional flow-matching loss and the sampling ODE

`L(theta) = E |v_theta(t, x_t) - u|^2` with `t ~ U(0, 1)`, `x_0 ~ N(0, I)`,
`x_1 ~ data`, and `(x_t, u)` from EQ-GEN-FM-001. Minimizer over all
functions: `v*(t, x) = E[u | x_t = x]`. Sampling: `x(0) ~ N(0, I)`,
`dx/dt = v_theta(t, x)`, `x(1)` is the draw.

- Domain: data with finite second moments; mini-batches of size `B`, the
  loss estimated by the batch mean.
- Meaning: a squared-error regression is minimized by the conditional
  expectation of its target. The law `p_t` of `x_t` and `v*` satisfy the
  continuity equation `d p_t / dt + div(p_t v*) = 0` (average the
  conditional continuity equations over `x_1`), so the ODE with `v*`
  carries `N(0, I)` to the law of `x_1 + s x_0`, the data convolved with
  `N(0, s^2 I)`. The loss does not tend to zero: its minimum is
  `E Var(u | x_t)`.
- Code: `generative.fit_flow_matching`,
