  `generative.flow_matching_loss_and_gradient`, `generative.integrate_flow`,
  `generative.FlowMatchingFit`, `generative.VelocityNetwork`.
- Source: [REF-LIPMAN-ETAL-2023]; Adam by EQ-OPT-ADAM-002, the ODE by
  EQ-NUM-ODE-001.

### EQ-GEN-FM-003 — Marginal velocity field for Gaussian data

For `x_1 ~ N(m, sd^2)` in one coordinate, `a(t) = 1 - (1 - s) t`,
`V(t) = a(t)^2 + t^2 sd^2`:
`v(t, x) = m + c(t) (x - t m)`, `c(t) = (t sd^2 - (1 - s) a(t)) / V(t)
= V'(t) / (2 V(t))`. Flow map: `x(1) = m + sqrt(sd^2 + s^2) x(0)`;
`int_0^1 c(t) dt = log sqrt(sd^2 + s^2)`.

- Domain: `sd > 0`, `0 <= s < 1`, `0 <= t <= 1`; independent coordinates
  are treated one by one.
- Meaning: `x_t = a x_0 + t x_1` and `u = x_1 - (1 - s) x_0` are jointly
  Gaussian with `E x_t = t m`, `Var x_t = V`, `E u = m`,
  `Cov(u, x_t) = t sd^2 - (1 - s) a`, so `E[u | x_t]` is the linear
  regression above. A linear field `m + c (x - t m)` moves the mean at
  speed `m` and scales the deviation by `exp(int c) = sqrt(V(1) / V(0))`.
- Code: `generative.GaussianMarginalVelocity`.
- Source: derivation in `generative.flow_matching` from EQ-GEN-FM-001 and
  EQ-GEN-FM-002; verified numerically in `tests/test_flow_matching_sbi.py`.

### EQ-GEN-FM-004 — Log-density by the instantaneous change of variables

Along `dx/dt = v(t, x)`: `d log p_t(x(t)) / dt = -div v(t, x(t))`, hence
`log p_1(x(1)) = log N(x(0); 0, I) - int_0^1 div v(t, x(t)) dt`.

- Domain: `v` continuously differentiable in `x`; `x(0)` is found by
  integrating the ODE backward from the query point.
- Meaning: the continuity equation `d p_t / dt = -div(p_t v)` gives
  `d p_t / dt + v . grad p_t = -p_t div v`; the left side is the derivative
  of `p_t` along a trajectory. The divergence is exact (forward-mode
  differentiation) for the fitted networks and for velocity functions
  written with arithmetic operators, or by central differences on request;
  both time integrals use the fixed-step solver of EQ-NUM-ODE-001 without
  error control.
- Code: `generative.flow_log_density`,
  `generative.FlowMatchingFit.log_density`,
  `generative.FlowMatchingPosterior.log_density`,
  `generative.VelocityNetwork.divergence`.
- Source: derivation above; [REF-LIPMAN-ETAL-2023] for continuous
  normalizing flows as the model class.

### EQ-GEN-FM-005 — Backpropagation through a tanh network

Layers `z_l = W_l a_{l-1} + b_l`, `a_l = tanh(z_l)` for hidden layers and
`a_L = z_L`. With `delta_L = d loss / d a_L`:
`d loss / d W_l = delta_l a_{l-1}'`, `d loss / d b_l = delta_l`,
`delta_{l-1} = (W_l' delta_l) * (1 - a_{l-1}^2)` (elementwise product).

- Domain: the multilayer perceptron of EQ-NN-MLP-001 with `tanh` hidden
  units and an identity output, evaluated on floats.
- Meaning: the chain rule applied layer by layer; the same gradient as the
  reverse sweep of EQ-AD-REVERSE-001 without recording a tape (the tests
  compare the two).
- Code: `generative.flow_matching_loss_and_gradient`,
  `generative.ratio_loss_and_gradient`.
- Source: [REF-GOODFELLOW-BENGIO-COURVILLE-2016, Section 6.5].

### EQ-GEN-FMPE-001 — Flow-matching posterior estimation

`L(phi) = E |v_phi(t, theta_t, x) - (theta_1 - (1 - s) theta_0)|^2` with
`theta_1 ~ p(theta)`, `x ~ p(x | theta_1)`, `theta_0 ~ N(0, I)`,
`t ~ U(0, 1)`, `theta_t = (1 - (1 - s) t) theta_0 + t theta_1`. Posterior
draw for `x_obs`: `theta(0) ~ N(0, I)`,
`d theta / dt = v_phi(t, theta, x_obs)`, return `theta(1)`.

- Domain: a prior that can be sampled and a simulator; parameters and
  observations of fixed finite widths, standardized by their training
  moments.
- Meaning: EQ-GEN-FM-002 applied conditionally on `x`: given `x`, the end
  point `theta_1` is distributed as `p(theta | x)`, so the minimizer is the
  field that carries `N(0, I)` to the posterior (convolved with
  `N(0, s^2 I)` in standardized units) for every `x` at once. Training
  uses `N` simulator runs; no likelihood is evaluated.
- Code: `generative.fit_flow_matching_posterior`,
  `generative.FlowMatchingPosterior`.
- Source: [REF-WILDBERGER-ETAL-2023]; path and loss from
  [REF-LIPMAN-ETAL-2023].

### EQ-GEN-NRE-001 — Classifier logit as the likelihood-to-evidence ratio

`L(d) = -E_{p(theta, x)} log d(theta, x) - E_{p(theta) p(x)} log(1 - d(theta, x))`
is minimized by `d* = p(theta, x) / (p(theta, x) + p(theta) p(x))`, so
`logit d* = log p(x | theta) / p(x) = log p(theta | x) / p(theta)`.
With the logit `f` as network output, a joint pair contributes
`log(1 + exp(-f))` and a product pair `log(1 + exp(f))`.

- Domain: equal numbers of joint pairs and of pairs with `theta` permuted
  within the mini-batch (a cyclic shift, so no pair is left in place).
- Meaning: pointwise, `-a log d - b log(1 - d)` has derivative zero at
  `d = a / (a + b)`. The estimate is trustworthy only where simulated pairs
  are dense. Linear-Gaussian check: for `theta ~ N(0, tau^2)`,
  `x = a theta + N(0, sigma^2)`, the exact value is
  `-(x - a theta)^2 / (2 sigma^2) + x^2 / (2 (a^2 tau^2 + sigma^2))
  + log((a^2 tau^2 + sigma^2) / sigma^2) / 2`.
- Code: `generative.fit_ratio_estimator`, `generative.RatioEstimator`,
  `generative.ratio_loss_and_gradient`.
- Source: [REF-HERMANS-BEGY-LOUPPE-2020].

### EQ-GEN-NRE-002 — Posterior from an estimated ratio

`log p(theta | x_obs) = log p(theta) + log r(theta, x_obs)`, sampled by
random-walk Metropolis (EQ-MCMC-MH-001) or, for scalar `theta`, tabulated
on a grid and normalized by the trapezoidal rule. Diagnostic:
`int p(theta) r(theta, x_obs) d theta = 1` for the exact ratio.

- Domain: a prior density that can be evaluated (normalized, if the
  diagnostic is to be read); a grid covering the posterior mass.
- Meaning: Bayes' rule with `r = p(x | theta) / p(x)`. The samples are
  exact for the estimated ratio, not for the true posterior; the
  diagnostic measures the error of the classifier at `x_obs` after
  averaging over the prior and does not certify the shape of the posterior.
- Code: `generative.RatioEstimator.posterior_on_grid`,
  `generative.RatioEstimator.sample_posterior`, `generative.GridPosterior`.
- Source: [REF-HERMANS-BEGY-LOUPPE-2020].

## Interacting particle samplers and unscented inversion (ADR-0130)

### EQ-INV-ALDI-001 — Affine-invariant interacting Langevin dynamics

For members `u_j`, `j = 1..J`, in `R^d` with mean `m`, covariance
`C = sum_k (u_k - m)(u_k - m)' / J` and potential
`Phi(u) = |Gamma^-1/2 (y - G(u))|^2 / 2 + |u|^2 / 2`:
`du_j = -C grad Phi(u_j) dt + ((d + 1)/J)(u_j - m) dt + sqrt(2) C^1/2 dW_j`,
with `C^1/2 = (u_1 - m, ..., u_J - m) / sqrt(J)` a `d x J` matrix and `W_j`
independent `J`-dimensional Brownian motions. The correction is the
divergence `div_{u_j} C = ((d + 1)/J)(u_j - m)`.

- Domain: `J >= d + 2` (non-singular `C`); prior `N(0, I)` in `u`; `Gamma`
  symmetric positive definite (here diagonal, known Gaussian noise).
- Meaning: the noise of member `j` has covariance `2 C dt` and is
  independent across members, so the probability flux of member `j` in the
  Fokker-Planck equation of the ensemble is
  `rho (-C grad_j Phi + div_j C) - div_j (C rho) = -rho C grad_j Phi - C grad_j rho`,
  which vanishes at `rho = prod_j exp(-Phi(u_j))`: the product of posteriors
  is invariant at every finite ensemble size. The dynamics is invariant
  under affine changes of `u`, so its relaxation rate does not depend on the
  conditioning of the posterior.
- Code: `inverse.interacting_langevin_sampler`.
- Source: [REF-GARBUNO-INIGO-NUSKEN-REICH-2020] (corrected dynamics);
  [REF-GARBUNO-INIGO-ETAL-2020] (dynamics without the correction). The flux
  argument is rederived in ADR-0130.

### EQ-INV-ALDI-002 — Gradient-free drift of the interacting Langevin sampler

With `g_k = G(u_k)`, mean `g_bar` and
`C^ug = sum_k (u_k - m)(g_k - g_bar)' / J`:
`C grad Phi(u_j) ~ C^ug Gamma^-1 (g_j - y) + C u_j`, i.e. the data part is
`(1/J) sum_k <g_k - g_bar, g_j - y>_Gamma (u_k - m)` and the prior part
`C u_j` is exact.

- Domain: as [EQ-INV-ALDI-001].
- Meaning: for an affine map `G(u) = A u + b`, `C^ug = C A'` and the
  expression equals `C A' Gamma^-1 (g_j - y) + C u_j = C grad Phi(u_j)`
  without error, so the invariance of [EQ-INV-ALDI-001] carries over. For a
  nonlinear map it is a statistical linearization and the stationary law is
  an approximation of the posterior.
- Code: `inverse.interacting_langevin_sampler`.
- Source: [REF-GARBUNO-INIGO-ETAL-2020] and
  [REF-GARBUNO-INIGO-NUSKEN-REICH-2020].

### EQ-INV-ALDI-003 — Euler-Maruyama step, step rule and time averages

`u_j <- u_j - h_n [C^ug Gamma^-1 (g_j - y) + C u_j - kappa (u_j - m)]
+ sqrt(2 h_n / J) sum_k (u_k - m) xi_jk`, `xi_jk ~ N(0, 1)`,
`kappa = (d + 1)/J` (or 0 without the correction). Adaptive step
`h_n = eta / (tr C + tr C^gg)` with
`C^gg = sum_k Gamma^-1/2 (g_k - g_bar)(g_k - g_bar)' Gamma^-1/2 / J`.
Estimates: `E[f] ~ sum_n h_n (1/J) sum_j f(u_j^n) / sum_n h_n` over the
ensembles after the burn-in.

- Domain: `0 < eta < 2`, or a fixed `h > 0`.
- Meaning: for an affine map the drift matrix is `C (I + A' Gamma^-1 A)`,
  whose eigenvalues are positive with sum `tr C + tr C^gg`, so
  `h_n lambda_max <= eta` and the deterministic part of the step is stable;
  in stationarity `h_n ~ eta / d`. A heuristic, not an error-controlled
  integrator: the discrete chain has an `O(h)` bias, and because `h_n`
  depends on the state the averages are weighted by `h_n`.
- Code: `inverse.interacting_langevin_sampler`,
  `inverse.InteractingLangevinResult`.
- Source: library discretization (ADR-0130) of the dynamics of
  [REF-GARBUNO-INIGO-NUSKEN-REICH-2020]; [REF-GARBUNO-INIGO-ETAL-2020] use
  an adaptive step inversely proportional to a norm of the drift.

### EQ-INV-ALDI-004 — Covariance deficit without the finite-ensemble correction

Without the term `((d + 1)/J)(u_j - m)` and for a Gaussian posterior
`N(mu, Sigma)` the invariant density of the ensemble is
`prod_j pi(u_j) det(C)^(-(d + 1)/2)`, so `J C ~ Wishart(Sigma, J - d - 2)`,
`m ~ N(mu, Sigma / J)` independently, `E[C] = ((J - d - 2)/J) Sigma`, and the
pooled covariance of the members is `((J - d - 1)/J) Sigma`.

- Domain: affine forward map; `J > 2 d + 1` for a normalizable density.
- Meaning: with `rho = prod_j pi(u_j) phi(U)` the flux of
  [EQ-INV-ALDI-001] without the correction is
  `-prod pi (C grad_j phi + phi div_j C)`, which vanishes for
  `grad_j log phi = -((d + 1)/J) C^-1 (u_j - m) = -((d + 1)/2) grad_j log det C`.
  The uncorrected ensemble Kalman sampler therefore underestimates the
  posterior covariance, by half for `J = 6`, `d = 2`; the deficit vanishes
  as `J -> infinity`.
- Code: `inverse.interacting_langevin_sampler`.
- Source: derived in ADR-0130 from the dynamics of
  [REF-GARBUNO-INIGO-ETAL-2020]; the need for the correction is the subject
  of [REF-GARBUNO-INIGO-NUSKEN-REICH-2020].

### EQ-INV-UKI-001 — Unscented Kalman inversion iteration

Prediction `m^ = m_n`, `C^ = 2 C_n`. Analysis with the augmented map
`G_a(u) = (G(u), u)`, data `y_a = (y, 0)` and `Gamma_a = diag(Gamma, I)`:
`m_{n+1} = m^ + C^uy (C^yy + 2 Gamma_a)^-1 (y_a - y^)`,
`C_{n+1} = C^ - C^uy (C^yy + 2 Gamma_a)^-1 C^uy'`, where `y^`, `C^uy`, `C^yy`
are the sigma-point moments of `G_a` under `N(m^, C^)`
([EQ-INV-UKI-002]). Start: `m_0 = 0`, `C_0 = I` (the prior).

- Domain: prior `N(0, I)` in `u`; `Gamma` positive definite.
- Meaning: the general scheme `m^ = alpha m + (1 - alpha) r_0`,
  `C^ = alpha^2 C + Sigma_w`, analysis with `Sigma_nu`, specialized to
  `alpha = 1`, `Sigma_w = C_n`, `Sigma_nu = 2 Gamma_a`, the choice for which
  the fixed point is the posterior in the affine case
  ([EQ-INV-UKI-003]). Each iteration costs `2 d + 1` forward evaluations.
- Code: `inverse.unscented_kalman_inversion`.
- Source: [REF-HUANG-SCHNEIDER-STUART-2022]; the hyperparameters are
  rederived in ADR-0130.

### EQ-INV-UKI-002 — Sigma points and weights of the unscented transform

For `N(m, C)` with `C = L L'`: points `m` and `m +/- sqrt(d + kappa) L e_i`,
`i = 1..d`; weights `kappa / (d + kappa)` for the centre and
`1 / (2 (d + kappa))` for the others, used for means and covariances alike.

- Domain: `kappa >= 0` (non-negative weights); `C` positive definite.
- Meaning: the weighted mean and covariance of the points are `m` and `C`
  exactly, so the moments of an affine map are exact; for a nonlinear map
  the transform matches the Taylor expansion of the mean to second order.
- Code: `inverse.unscented_kalman_inversion`.
- Source: [REF-JULIER-UHLMANN-2004].

### EQ-INV-UKI-003 — Linear fixed point of unscented Kalman inversion

For `G(u) = A u + b`, `P = A' Gamma^-1 A + I`:
`C_{n+1}^-1 = (C_n^-1 + P) / 2` and
`C_{n+1}^-1 m_{n+1} = (C_n^-1 m_n + A' Gamma^-1 (y - b)) / 2`.

- Domain: affine forward map.
- Meaning: the Kalman analysis in information form is
  `C_{n+1}^-1 = (2 C_n)^-1 + A_a' (2 Gamma_a)^-1 A_a` with
  `A_a' Gamma_a^-1 A_a = P`. The unique fixed point is `C = P^-1`,
  `m = P^-1 A' Gamma^-1 (y - b)`, the posterior covariance and mean, and the
  errors of the precision and of the precision-weighted mean halve at every
  iteration. With `alpha < 1` and `r_0 = 0` the same computation gives the
  fixed-point mean `P^-1 A' Gamma^-1 (y - b) / (2 - alpha)`, which is why
  `alpha = 1` is fixed.
- Code: `inverse.unscented_kalman_inversion`.
- Source: derived in ADR-0130 for the scheme of
  [REF-HUANG-SCHNEIDER-STUART-2022].

### EQ-INV-CBS-001 — Consensus weights and weighted moments

`w_j = exp(-beta Phi(u_j)) / sum_k exp(-beta Phi(u_k))`,
`m_b = sum_j w_j u_j`, `C_b = sum_j w_j (u_j - m_b)(u_j - m_b)'`,
`J_eff = 1 / sum_j w_j^2`, with `Phi` of [EQ-INV-ALDI-001].

- Domain: `beta > 0`; the library uses the largest
  `beta <= inverse_temperature` with `J_eff >= f J` (bisection), a heuristic.
- Meaning: importance weights of the tempered posterior relative to the
  current ensemble; only values of `Phi` are needed.
- Code: `inverse.consensus_based_sampling`.
- Source: [REF-CARRILLO-ETAL-2022].

### EQ-INV-CBS-002 — Consensus-based sampling update

`u_j <- m_b + alpha (u_j - m_b) + sqrt((1 - alpha^2) / lambda) C_b^1/2 xi_j`,
`xi_j ~ N(0, I)`, with `lambda = 1 / (1 + beta)` (sampling) or `lambda = 1`
(optimization).

- Domain: `0 <= alpha < 1`; `C_b` positive definite.
- Meaning: relaxation towards the weighted mean plus noise shaped by the
  weighted covariance; `alpha = 0` redraws the ensemble from
  `N(m_b, C_b / lambda)`.
- Code: `inverse.consensus_based_sampling`.
- Source: [REF-CARRILLO-ETAL-2022].

### EQ-INV-CBS-003 — Gaussian fixed point of consensus-based sampling

If the ensemble law is `N(m, C)` and
`Phi(u) = (u - mu)' Sigma^-1 (u - mu) / 2 + const`, then
`C_b^-1 = C^-1 + beta Sigma^-1`, `m_b = C_b (C^-1 m + beta Sigma^-1 mu)`, and
the update of [EQ-INV-CBS-002] gives the law
`N(m_b + alpha (m - m_b), alpha^2 C + (1 - alpha^2) C_b / lambda)`.

- Domain: mean-field (infinite-ensemble) iteration; quadratic `Phi`.
- Meaning: a fixed point needs `m = mu` and
  `(1 - lambda) C^-1 = lambda beta Sigma^-1`. With `lambda = 1 / (1 + beta)`
  this is `C = Sigma` for every `beta`: the posterior `N(mu, Sigma)` is
  stationary (the reweighted covariance of the target is
  `Sigma / (1 + beta)`). With `lambda = 1` only `C = 0` is fixed and the
  mean tends to the minimizer `mu`. For `J` members `C_b` is low by about
  `1 / J_eff`, which shifts the fixed point to about
  `(1 - (1 + beta) / (beta J_eff)) Sigma`. For a non-Gaussian posterior the
  method is an approximation.
- Code: `inverse.consensus_based_sampling`.
- Source: derived in ADR-0130; Gaussian steady states are the subject of
  [REF-CARRILLO-ETAL-2022].

## Lattice rules and median quasi-Monte Carlo

### EQ-SAMP-LATTICE-001 — Rank-1 lattice points and their random shift

`x_k = frac(k z / n)`, `k = 0, ..., n - 1`, for an integer generating vector
`z`; shifted points `frac(x_k + Delta)` with one `Delta ~ U[0,1)^s` for the
whole point set.

- Domain: `n >= 1`, every `z_j` coprime to `n` (so each coordinate takes the
  `n` values `m / n` once).
- Meaning: the points form a group under addition modulo one, hence
  `(1/n) sum_k exp(2 pi i h.x_k)` equals 1 if `h.z = 0 (mod n)` and 0
  otherwise: the rule integrates every trigonometric monomial exactly except
  those with a nonzero frequency in the dual lattice. With the shift every
  point is uniform on the cube and the equal-weight rule is unbiased.
- Code: `sampling.rank1_lattice`, `sampling.LatticeRule.points`.
- Source: [REF-CRANLEY-PATTERSON-1976] (the random shift);
  [REF-L-ECUYER-2018]. The character-sum identity is checked by enumeration
  in `tests/test_lattice_and_median_qmc.py`.

### EQ-SAMP-LATTICE-002 — Shift-averaged squared worst-case error

`e^2(z) = -1 + (1/n) sum_(k=0..n-1) prod_j (1 + gamma_j B_2(frac(k z_j / n)))`,
`B_2(x) = x^2 - x + 1/6`.

- Domain: `n >= 1`, `z_j` coprime to `n`, product weights `gamma_j > 0`.
- Meaning: `E_Delta sup_(|f| <= 1) (Q_Delta f - int f)^2` for the randomly
  shifted lattice rule `Q_Delta` over the unit ball of the reproducing-kernel
  Hilbert space with kernel
  `K(x, y) = prod_j (1 + gamma_j (B_1(x_j) B_1(y_j) + B_2(|x_j - y_j|) / 2))`,
  `B_1(x) = x - 1/2`, i.e. the per-coordinate inner product
  `(int f)(int g) + (1 / gamma_j) int f' g'`. Averaging `K` over the shift
  gives the shift-invariant kernel `prod_j (1 + gamma_j B_2(frac(x_j - y_j)))`
  and the group structure reduces the double sum over points to a single
  one. In one dimension `e^2 = gamma / (6 n^2)`. Other texts scale the
  weights differently; this record fixes the normalization used here.
- Code: `sampling.lattice_squared_error`, `sampling.LatticeRule`.
- Source: derived in ADR-0118 from the kernel above; the reproducing
  property, the shift average, and the single-sum reduction are each checked
  numerically in `tests/test_lattice_and_median_qmc.py`. Random shifts:
  [REF-CRANLEY-PATTERSON-1976].

### EQ-SAMP-LATTICE-003 — Component-by-component construction

`z_1 = 1`; `z_d = argmin_(1 <= z <= n-1) e^2(z_1, ..., z_(d-1), z)` for
`d = 2, ..., s`, with `e^2` of [EQ-SAMP-LATTICE-002] in dimension `d`.

- Domain: prime `n`; product weights in the order in which the components
  are chosen. Ties go to the smallest `z` (`z` and `n - z` always tie).
- Meaning: a greedy search with `O(s n^2)` operations in this naive form. It
  attains the minimum of `e^2` over all vectors for `s <= 2` and is a
  heuristic for larger `s`.
- Code: `sampling.cbc_generating_vector`.
- Source: specified in ADR-0118 (greedy minimization of
  [EQ-SAMP-LATTICE-002]); lattice rules for randomized quasi-Monte Carlo in
  general: [REF-L-ECUYER-2018].

### EQ-SAMP-LATTICE-004 — Korobov generating vectors

`z(a) = (1, a, a^2, ..., a^(s-1)) mod n`; `a* = argmin_(1 <= a <= n-1)
e^2(z(a))`.

- Domain: `a` coprime to `n`; the search requires a prime `n`. Ties go to
  the smallest `a` (`a` and `n - a` always tie).
- Meaning: a one-parameter family of generating vectors searched
  exhaustively at `O(s n^2)` operations.
- Code: `sampling.korobov_vector`, `sampling.korobov_generating_vector`.
- Source: [REF-L-ECUYER-2018]; the criterion is [EQ-SAMP-LATTICE-002].

### EQ-SAMP-RQMC-002 — Replicate mean, standard error, and t interval

`Q_r = (1/n) sum_k f(x_k^(r))` for `R` independent randomizations;
`mu_hat = (1/R) sum_r Q_r`, `se = s / sqrt(R)`,
`s^2 = sum_r (Q_r - mu_hat)^2 / (R - 1)`, interval
`mu_hat +- t_(R-1, (1+c)/2) se`.

- Domain: `R >= 2`; a randomization that makes each point uniform on the
  cube; square-integrable `f`.
- Meaning: `mu_hat` is unbiased and `se^2` is an unbiased estimate of its
  variance. The interval is exact only for normal `Q_r`; with few
  non-normal replicates its coverage is approximate and can be below `c`.
  Cost `R n` evaluations.
- Code: `sampling.rqmc_mean`, `sampling.RQMCResult`.
- Source: [REF-CRANLEY-PATTERSON-1976], [REF-L-ECUYER-2018]; interval
  caution: [REF-LECUYER-NAKAYAMA-OWEN-TUFFIN-2023].

### EQ-SAMP-RQMC-003 — Median of independently randomized rules

`mu_tilde = median(Q_1, ..., Q_R)` for odd `R`.

- Domain: odd `R >= 3`; `Q_r` as in [EQ-SAMP-RQMC-002].
- Meaning: the estimate is wrong by more than `eps` only if more than half
  of the replicates are, so rare bad randomizations do not matter. It
  estimates the median of the law of `Q_r`, which is the integral only if
  that law is symmetric about it; no standard error or interval is attached.
- Code: `sampling.rqmc_median`, `sampling.median_random_lattice`.
- Source: [REF-PAN-OWEN-2023], [REF-GODA-LECUYER-2022].

### EQ-SAMP-RQMC-004 — Median rule with random generating vectors

`z^(r) ~ U({1, ..., n-1}^s)` independently for `r = 1, ..., R`;
`Q_r = (1/n) sum_k f(frac(k z^(r) / n + Delta^(r)))`; estimate
[EQ-SAMP-RQMC-003].

- Domain: prime `n >= 3`, odd `R >= 3`. `Delta^(r) ~ U[0,1)^s` independent
  (the library default) or `Delta^(r) = 0`.
- Meaning: no generating vector is constructed and no weights are chosen;
  the median discards the replicates with a bad random vector.
- Code: `sampling.median_random_lattice`.
- Source: [REF-GODA-LECUYER-2022]. The additional random shift per
  replicate is a convention of this library.

## Batch evaluation contract

### EQ-BATCH-001 — Request and response of a batch procedure

`request_k = (x_1, ..., x_m; label)`; `response_k = (y_1, ..., y_m)` with
`y_i = f_label(x_i)`.

- Domain: `m >= 1` points of equal dimension; `label` names one model of the
  caller; the response has exactly `m` entries in request order.
- Meaning: an algorithm is a sequence of requests whose points may depend on
  all earlier responses. Its result is a function of the responses only, so
  it does not depend on how, where, or in how many chunks a request was
  evaluated. This is a software contract, not a statistical statement.
- Code: `foundations.EvaluationRequest`, `foundations.request`,
  `foundations.run_procedure`, `foundations.AskTellSession`,
  `foundations.batch_from_pointwise`, `foundations.scalar_outputs`,
  `foundations.vector_outputs`.
- Source: [REF-PEP-342].

## Credibility assessment scales

### EQ-VAL-CRED-001 — Minimum roll-up of ordinal factor levels

`L_overall = min_i L_i` over the assessed factors `i`; for a category `C`,
`L_C = min_(i in C) L_i`.

- Domain: ordinal levels `L_i` of factors of one scale; every factor assessed
  (or the roll-up restricted to the assessed ones on request).
- Meaning: the weakest-link statement. Only an order statistic is used, so
  no cardinal meaning of a level is assumed. It is defined by the source for
  the 2008 NASA scale and refused for scales whose source says factors must
  not be combined.
- Code: `validation.credibility_scale.CredibilityAssessment.overall`,
  `validation.credibility_scale.CredibilityAssessment.category_minimum`.
- Source: [REF-BABULA-ETAL-2009, Roll-up Processes];
  [REF-NASA-STD-7009B-2024, Appendix E.2].

### EQ-VAL-CRED-002 — PCMM aggregation triple

`PCMM_hat = (min_i s_i, (1/n) sum_i s_i, max_i s_i)` over the `n` scores `s_i`
being aggregated (elements of one or several subsystems).

- Domain: `n >= 1` finite scores on the 0-3 maturity scale (tenths allowed).
- Meaning: when aggregation is demanded the source asks for the three numbers
  together so that the worst score stays visible; the mean alone is
  meaningless on an ordinal scale. The worked example of the source (four
  subsystems, six elements each) gives `(0.0, 1.1, 2.0)`.
- Code: `validation.credibility_scale.pcmm_aggregate_triple`,
  `validation.credibility_scale.CredibilityAssessment.overall`.
- Source: [REF-OBERKAMPF-PILCH-TRUCANO-2007, Section 5.2, Eq. (1)].

### EQ-VAL-CRED-003 — Cap of validation and UQ by verification (PCMM)

`s_V <= min(s_code, s_solution) + 2` and `s_UQ <= min(s_code, s_solution) + 2`.

- Domain: scores of code verification, solution verification, model
  validation, and uncertainty quantification and sensitivity analysis.
- Meaning: validation and uncertainty-quantification evidence is credible
  only to the extent that the numerical and software assumptions beneath it
  hold; a score above the cap is rejected, not clipped.
- Code: `validation.credibility_scale.LevelCap`,
  `validation.credibility_scale.CredibilityAssessment`.
- Source: [REF-OBERKAMPF-PILCH-TRUCANO-2007, Section 4.2.5].

### EQ-VAL-CRED-004 — Weighted evidence and review factor level (2008 NASA scale)

`L = (1 - w) L_evidence + w L_review`, `0 <= w <= 0.3`.

- Domain: levels of the two sub-factors of one factor; review weight `w`.
- Meaning: technical review tunes the evidence score by at most 30 percent
  of the gap between them (evidence 0 and review 4 give 1.2 at `w = 0.3`).
- Code: `validation.credibility_scale.weighted_evidence_review_level`.
- Source: [REF-BABULA-ETAL-2009, Roll-up Processes].

### EQ-VAL-CRED-005 — Level shortfall against a target profile

`gap_i = max(0, r_i - a_i)` for required level `r_i` and achieved level `a_i`;
a required factor with no assessment has an unknown gap and is listed.

- Domain: finite levels of one scale; `r_i > 0`.
- Meaning: the gap between assessed and threshold levels that the standard
  asks to be reported with the levels. Neither shipped source defines the
  thresholds, and the improvement order (unassessed first, then decreasing
  gap) is a convention of this library.
- Code: `validation.credibility_scale.level_gaps`,
  `validation.credibility_scale.improvement_plan`,
  `validation.credibility_scale.is_sufficient`.
- Source: [REF-NASA-STD-7009B-2024, Sections 4.3.8.4-4.3.8.5 and Appendix E.5].

### EQ-VAL-CRED-006 — Criticality matrix of decision consequence and M&S influence

`rating = T[influence, consequence]` with `T` the 5 by 5 table of Figure 1:
rows influence 5..1 read `GYRRR`, `GYYRR`, `GYYYR`, `GGGYY`, `GGGGY` across
consequence I..V.

- Domain: integer consequence and influence levels in `1..5`.
- Meaning: red marks M&S that are clear candidates for full adherence to the
  standard, yellow leaves adherence to programme management and the technical
  authority, green has no critical driving force. The matrix may be adjusted
  by a programme; the table is a default lookup.
- Code: `validation.credibility_scale.criticality_assessment`,
  `validation.credibility_scale.criticality_matrix`.
- Source: [REF-NASA-STD-7009B-2024, Appendix D, Figure 1].
## Chance constraints and reliability-based design optimisation

### EQ-REL-SCENARIO-001 — Scenario violation bound

`P^N{ V(x*_N) > eps } <= beta(N, d, eps) = sum_(i=0)^(d-1) C(N, i) eps^i (1 - eps)^(N - i)`
`= P(Binomial(N, eps) <= d - 1)`, where `V(x) = P{ xi : g(x, xi) > 0 }`.

- Domain: convex program in `d` variables with `N` independent constraint
  samples, a unique solution for every sample; `0 < eps < 1`. The bound holds
  with equality for fully-supported problems.
- Meaning: confidence `1 - beta` that the solution violates a fresh
  constraint with probability at most `eps`; inverting it gives the sample
  size and the a-priori violation level for a given `N`.
- Code: `reliability.scenario_confidence`,
  `reliability.scenario_violation_bound`, `reliability.scenario_sample_size`.
- Source: [REF-CAMPI-GARATTI-2008].

### EQ-REL-SCENARIO-002 — Explicit sufficient scenario sample size

`N >= (2 / eps) (d - 1 + ln(1 / beta))` implies
`P(Binomial(N, eps) <= d - 1) <= beta`.

- Domain: `0 < eps, beta < 1`, `d >= 1`.
- Meaning: from the multiplicative Chernoff bound
  `P(X <= a) <= exp(-(N eps - a)^2 / (2 N eps))` for `a < N eps`; with
  `a = d - 1` and `N eps >= 2 (a + ln(1/beta))` the exponent is at least
  `ln(1/beta)`. Never smaller than the exact size.
- Code: `reliability.scenario_sample_size` (`explicit_size`).
- Source: derived in this library from the Chernoff bound. It has the form of
  the explicit size `(2 / eps)(ln(1 / beta) + d)` of Eq. (4) of
  [REF-CAMPI-GARATTI-PRANDINI-2009] with `d - 1` in place of `d` (so it is
  `2 / eps` samples smaller, and still never below the exact size);
  [REF-CAMPI-GARATTI-2008] states the exact condition.

### EQ-REL-SCENARIO-003 — Wait-and-judge violation level

`eps(k) = 1 - t(k)`, `t(k)` the unique root in `(0, 1)` of
`beta/(N+1) sum_(m=k)^N C(m, k) t^(m-k) - C(N, k) t^(N-k) = 0`; then
`P^N{ V(x*_N) > eps(s*_N) } <= beta` for the number `s*_N` of support
constraints of the computed solution.

- Domain: convex program with a unique solution and the non-degeneracy
  assumption of the paper; `0 <= k <= min(d, N - 1)`.
- Meaning: the violation level may be chosen after the solution is seen, from
  the observed number of support constraints instead of the worst case `d`.
- Code: `reliability.scenario_posterior_violation_bound`.
- Source: [REF-CAMPI-GARATTI-2018].

### EQ-REL-SAA-001 — Sampled chance constraint as an order statistic

`(1/N) #{ s : h_s(x) > 0 } <= gamma` if and only if
`h_(q+1)(x) <= 0` with `h_s(x) = max_i g_i(x, xi_s)`, `q = floor(gamma N)`, and
`h_(r)` the `r`-th largest of the `N` values.

- Domain: `N` independent draws, `0 <= gamma < 1`; `gamma = 0` is the scenario
  program `max_s h_s(x) <= 0`.
- Meaning: the sample-average approximation of a single or joint chance
  constraint is one piecewise-smooth, generally non-convex constraint, so no
  smoothing of the indicator is needed.
- Code: `reliability.solve_chance_constrained`.
- Source: elementary; the same sample approximation is defined in Section 2
  of [REF-LUEDTKE-AHMED-2008] (preprint read), with `gamma = 0` the scenario
  program.

### EQ-REL-CHANCE-NORMAL-001 — Linear chance constraint with normal coefficients

`P(a'x <= b) >= 1 - eps` with `a ~ N(mu, Sigma)` if and only if
`mu'x + Phi^-1(1 - eps) sqrt(x' Sigma x) <= b`; the exact violation
probability is `Phi(-(b - mu'x) / sqrt(x' Sigma x))`.

- Domain: `Sigma` symmetric positive semidefinite, `0 < eps < 1`; the
  feasible set is convex (second-order cone) for `eps <= 1/2`.
- Meaning: `a'x` is a normal variable with mean `mu'x` and variance
  `x' Sigma x`.
- Code: `reliability.normal_linear_chance_margin`,
  `reliability.normal_linear_violation_probability`.
- Source: elementary; the convexity for normal coefficients and a violation
  level of at most one half is stated in the introduction of
  [REF-NEMIROVSKI-SHAPIRO-2006] (preprint read).

### EQ-REL-CHANCE-FREE-001 — Distribution-free chance constraint

`P(a'x > b) <= eps` for every law of `a` with mean `mu` and covariance
`Sigma` if `mu'x + kappa sqrt(x' Sigma x) <= b`, with
`kappa = sqrt((1 - eps)/eps)` (Cantelli, attained by a two-point law) or
`kappa = 1 / sqrt(eps)` (Chebyshev).

- Domain: `0 < eps < 1`, finite second moments; `b > mu'x`.
- Meaning: Cantelli's inequality `P(Y - m >= t) <= s^2/(s^2 + t^2)` solved for
  `t`; Chebyshev's is the two-sided inequality, more conservative.
- Code: `reliability.distribution_free_chance_margin`.
- Source: elementary (Cantelli's and Chebyshev's inequalities).

### EQ-REL-AUGLAG-001 — Augmented Lagrangian for inequality constraints

`L(x; lam, mu) = f(x) + (1 / (2 mu)) sum_j [ max(0, lam_j + mu c_j(x))^2 - lam_j^2 ]`;
multiplier update `lam_j <- max(0, lam_j + mu c_j(x))` after minimising `L`
in `x`.

- Domain: `c_j(x) <= 0` feasible; `mu > 0`; a smooth objective and constraints
  for the inner BFGS solve.
- Meaning: at a regular local solution `x*` with multipliers `lam*`,
  `grad f + sum_j lam*_j grad c_j = 0` and `lam*_j c_j(x*) = 0`.
- Code: `reliability.minimize_constrained`.
- Source: [REF-NOCEDAL-WRIGHT-2006, Section 17.4].

### EQ-REL-SORA-001 — Shifted deterministic constraint of one SORA cycle

`g_j(mu_j(d) - s_j^k; d) >= 0`, `s_j^k = mu_j(d^(k-1)) - x*_j(d^(k-1))`,
with `x*_j` the inverse-FORM most-probable target point on the sphere
`||u|| = beta_target_j`.

- Domain: continuous inputs; `g_j <= 0` is failure.
- Meaning: the reliability constraint `beta_j(d) >= beta_target_j` is replaced
  by a deterministic one evaluated at the mean shifted by the distance to the
  most-probable target point of the previous design; exact for a limit state
  linear in normal inputs with design-independent standard deviations.
- Code: `reliability.rbdo_sora`.
- Source: [REF-DU-CHEN-2004] (bibliographic), [REF-TU-CHOI-PARK-1999].

### EQ-REL-RBDO-002 — Reliability-index (double-loop) constraint

`beta_target_j - beta_j(d) <= 0`, `beta_j(d)` the FORM index of limit state `j`
at design `d`.

- Domain: a converged FORM analysis at every trial design.
- Meaning: the nested formulation; one FORM run per constraint evaluation.
- Code: `reliability.rbdo_double_loop`.
- Source: [REF-TU-CHOI-PARK-1999], [REF-AOUES-CHATEAUNEUF-2010].
### EQ-PROP-TOL-001 — One-sided exact normal tolerance factor

`k(n, p, gamma) = t'_(gamma; n-1, delta) / sqrt(n)` with `delta = z_p sqrt(n)`;
the bound is `xbar + k s` (upper) or `xbar - k s` (lower).

- Domain: `n >= 2` independent draws of a normal law, `0 < p < 1`,
  `0 < gamma < 1`; `t'_(gamma; nu, delta)` is the `gamma`-quantile of the
  noncentral `t` law with `nu` degrees of freedom and noncentrality `delta`.
- Meaning: `(xbar - mu - z_p sigma) / (s / sqrt(n))` is `T' - delta` with
  `T'` noncentral `t`, so `P(xbar + k s >= mu + z_p sigma) = gamma` exactly:
  the bound exceeds the `p`-quantile with probability `gamma`.
- Code: `propagation.normal_tolerance_factor`,
  `propagation.normal_tolerance_bound`,
  `propagation.tolerance._noncentral_t_quantile`.
- Source: [REF-NIST-SEMATECH-HANDBOOK] (formula and worked values 1.8740 and
  4.4111), [REF-YOUNG-2016] (Eq. 6 and eight printed values, reproduced to six
  decimals), [REF-KRISHNAMOORTHY-MATHEW-2009] (not opened).

### EQ-PROP-TOL-002 — Noncentral t distribution function as a chi integral

`P(T' <= t) = int_0^inf Phi(t s - delta) f_S(s) ds`, with
`f_S(s) = 2 nu s f_V(nu s^2)` the density of `S = sqrt(V / nu)` for
`V ~ chi2(nu)`.

- Domain: `nu >= 1` integer, `delta` and `t` real.
- Meaning: given `S = s`, `T' = (Z + delta) / s` is below `t` exactly when
  `Z <= t s - delta` with `Z` standard normal, so the distribution function
  is the average of `Phi(t s - delta)` over the law of `S`. The integral is
  truncated where `V` has `1e-17` of its mass on each side.
- Code: `propagation.tolerance._noncentral_t_cdf`.
- Source: [REF-KRISHNAMOORTHY-MATHEW-2009] (definition of the noncentral
  `t` law; the integral form is derived here).

### EQ-PROP-TOL-003 — Two-sided exact normal tolerance factor

`2 int_0^inf phi(z) P(chi2_nu >= nu r(z)^2 / k^2) dz = gamma`, `nu = n - 1`,
where `r(z)` solves `Phi(z / sqrt(n) + r) - Phi(z / sqrt(n) - r) = p`.

- Domain: `n >= 2`, `0 < p < 1 - 1e-10`, `0 < gamma < 1`.
- Meaning: write `xbar = mu + sigma z / sqrt(n)` and `s = sigma S`. The
  content of `[xbar - k s, xbar + k s]` is
  `Phi(z / sqrt(n) + k S) - Phi(z / sqrt(n) - k S)`, increasing in `k S`, so
  it reaches `p` exactly when `k S >= r(z)`. Averaging over `z ~ N(0, 1)`
  and the chi law of `S` gives the probability that the interval holds at
  least `p` of the law; its root in `k` is the exact two-sided factor.
- Code: `propagation.normal_tolerance_factor`,
  `propagation.normal_tolerance_interval`,
  `propagation.tolerance._two_sided_exact_factor`.
- Source: [REF-YOUNG-2016] (Eq. 7, a different representation of the same
  defining probability; the exact interval it prints for the milk data is
  reproduced to six decimals), [REF-KRISHNAMOORTHY-MATHEW-2009] and
  [REF-ODEH-OWEN-1980] (neither opened); the integral equation of this form is
  derived here.

### EQ-PROP-TOL-004 — Howe approximation of the two-sided factor

`k_Howe = z_((1+p)/2) sqrt(nu (1 + 1/n) / chi2_(1-gamma; nu))`, `nu = n - 1`,
with `chi2_(1-gamma; nu)` the `(1 - gamma)`-quantile of the chi-square law.

- Domain: `n >= 2`, `0 < p < 1`, `0 < gamma < 1`.
- Meaning: a closed form that replaces the sample-mean deviation by its
  scale `sqrt(1 + 1/n)`. At `p = gamma = 0.95` it is 2.1 % above the exact
  factor at `n = 3` and 0.3 % below it at `n = 10`, so the stated confidence
  is slightly missed for moderate `n`.
- Code: `propagation.normal_tolerance_factor` (`method="howe"`),
  `propagation.tolerance._howe_factor`.
- Source: [REF-NIST-SEMATECH-HANDBOOK] (formula and the worked value 2.217),
  [REF-HOWE-1969] (not opened).

### EQ-PROP-MARGIN-001 — Margin, uncertainty, and confidence ratio

Upper limit `L`: `M = L - y*`, `U = y_bound - y*`. Lower limit: `M = y* - L`,
`U = y* - y_bound`. Confidence ratio `M / U` (``+inf`` for `M > 0`, `U <= 0`).

- Domain: finite best estimate `y*`; `y_bound` a stated bound of the
  performance on the unsafe side, for example a Wilks or normal tolerance
  bound of the `p`-quantile at confidence `gamma`; a band applies each side
  separately and the side with the smallest ratio binds.
- Meaning: the margin is the room between the estimate and the limit, the
  uncertainty the room that the stated bound of the performance uses; a
  ratio above one means the margin covers the bound. For nested
  aleatory-epistemic studies `U = U_aleatory + U_epistemic` with
  `U_aleatory` taken at the most favourable outer point.
- Code: `propagation.Requirement`, `propagation.quantify_margin`,
  `propagation.quantify_margin_mixed`,
  `propagation.TechnicalPerformanceMeasure`.
- Source: [REF-PILCH-TRUCANO-HELTON-2006] (read: margin as the distance
  beyond the threshold, or below a limit, and margin/uncertainty ratios; the
  report gives no formula for the uncertainty, so `U` is this library's
  definition), [REF-NASA-SEH-2016] (read: tracking of performance measures and
  margins), [REF-HELTON-2011] (not opened).

### EQ-PROP-MARGIN-002 — Growth allowance and system margin arithmetic

`predicted = basic (1 + g)`; relative to the estimate
`allocation = predicted (1 + m)`; relative to the allocation
`allocation = predicted / (1 - m)`; conversion
`m_alloc = m_est / (1 + m_est)`.

- Domain: `basic > 0`, `g >= 0`, `m >= 0` (`m < 1` relative to the
  allocation); the percentages are user inputs.
- Meaning: the same physical margin is `25 %` relative to the estimate and
  `20 %` relative to the allocation; stating the basis removes the
  ambiguity.
- Code: `propagation.apply_contingency`,
  `propagation.allocation_margin_fraction`,
  `propagation.convert_margin_fraction`.
- Source: [REF-NASA-SEH-2016] (practice of margins on resources; the
  arithmetic is elementary).

### EQ-PROP-MARGIN-003 — Contingency as a confidence level

`c(a) = q_a / y* - 1` with `q_a` the `a`-quantile of the performance;
conversely `a(c) = P(Y <= y* (1 + c))`, estimated by `K / n` with the
Clopper-Pearson interval of EQ-INF-CI-CP-001.

- Domain: `y* > 0`, `0 < a < 1`, independent samples.
- Meaning: a fixed contingency percentage is read as the probability that
  the performance stays within it, and a probability level is read as the
  percentage that achieves it; with a Wilks bound the level holds with a
  further statistical confidence.
- Code: `propagation.contingency_for_confidence`,
  `propagation.confidence_of_contingency`,
  `propagation.compliance_probability`.
- Source: [REF-CLOPPER-PEARSON-1934], [REF-WILKS-1941].
### EQ-UQ-BUDGET-001 — Law of propagation of uncertainty with correlation

`u_c^2(y) = sum_i sum_j c_i c_j u(x_i) u(x_j) r(x_i, x_j)` with
`c_i = df/dx_i` at the input estimates and `r_ii = 1`; for independent inputs
`u_c^2 = sum_i (c_i u_i)^2`. For a budget with a correlation matrix `R` this
is `(c * u)' R (c * u)`.

- Domain: finite `c_i`, `u_i >= 0`, symmetric positive-semidefinite `R` with
  unit diagonal; first-order Taylor expansion of `f`, exact for linear `f`.
- Meaning: the standard uncertainty of the output of a model when the
  uncertainties of its inputs are known; the model is linearised at the
  estimates, so curvature is ignored (see EQ-UQ-BUDGET-006).
- Code: `uq.UncertaintyBudget.combined_variance`,
  `uq.UncertaintyBudget.combined_standard_uncertainty`,
  `uq.UncertaintyBudget.law_of_propagation`, `uq.budget_from_model`,
  `uq.BudgetEntry`.
- Source: [REF-JCGM-100-2008, Sections 5.1.2 and 5.2.2].

### EQ-UQ-BUDGET-002 — Welch-Satterthwaite effective degrees of freedom and expanded uncertainty

`nu_eff = u_c^4 / sum_i (c_i u_i)^4 / nu_i`, `k = t_((1+p)/2)(nu_eff)`,
`U = k u_c`; infinite `nu_i` contribute nothing to the sum and the normal
quantile replaces the t quantile when `nu_eff` is infinite.

- Domain: uncorrelated inputs. With a correlation matrix the code evaluates
  the same expression with the correlated `u_c` in the numerator, a heuristic
  that the result flags in its warnings.
- Meaning: approximates the law of `(y - Y) / u_c` by a Student-t law so that
  `y +/- U` has approximately coverage `p`.
- Code: `uq.UncertaintyBudget.effective_degrees_of_freedom`,
  `uq.UncertaintyBudget.expanded_uncertainty`, `uq.ExpandedUncertainty`.
- Source: [REF-JCGM-100-2008, Sections 6.2 and G.4.1],
  [REF-WELCH-1947], [REF-SATTERTHWAITE-1946].

### EQ-UQ-BUDGET-003 — Standard uncertainty of a Type A or Type B evaluation

Rectangular on `[-a, a]`: `u = a / sqrt(3)`; symmetric triangular:
`u = a / sqrt(6)`; arcsine (U-shaped): `u = a / sqrt(2)`; quoted expanded
uncertainty `U` with coverage factor `k`: `u = U / k`; any law: `u` is its
standard deviation. Type A from `n` readings: `u = s / sqrt(n)` with
`s^2 = sum (q_j - mean)^2 / (n - 1)` and `nu = n - 1`.

- Domain: `a >= 0`, `k > 0`, `n >= 2`, finite standard deviation.
- Meaning: converts the information about an input (limits, a certificate, a
  distribution, repeated readings) into a standard uncertainty.
- Code: `uq.BudgetEntry.rectangular`, `uq.BudgetEntry.triangular`,
  `uq.BudgetEntry.arcsine`, `uq.BudgetEntry.normal`,
  `uq.BudgetEntry.from_distribution`, `uq.BudgetEntry.from_observations`.
- Source: [REF-JCGM-100-2008, Sections 4.2.1-4.2.3, 4.3.4, 4.3.7 and 4.3.9],
  [REF-JCGM-101-2008, Sections 6.4.2, 6.4.5 and 6.4.6].

### EQ-UQ-BUDGET-004 — Combination rules: root-sum-square, linear sum, mixed

Root-sum-square: `sqrt(sum (c_i u_i)^2)`. Linear sum of absolute
contributions: `sum |c_i| a_i` over half-widths `a_i` (a bound) or
`sum |c_i| u_i` over standard uncertainties (the largest `u_c` under any
correlation, by the triangle inequality). Mixed rule at standard level:
`sum_(bias) |c_i| u_i + sqrt(sum_(random) (c_j u_j)^2)`; at bound level:
`sum_(bias) |c_i| a_i + k sqrt(sum_(random) (c_j u_j)^2)` with `k` stated.

- Domain: finite `c_i`, `u_i >= 0`, `a_i >= 0`, `k > 0`; the bound forms need
  a half-width for every (bias) entry.
- Meaning: conventions of system engineering for adding budget terms. Each
  result carries its kind (standard uncertainty or worst-case bound) so that
  values of different kinds are not combined silently. The mixed rule is a
  convention, not a result of the Guide.
- Code: `uq.UncertaintyBudget.root_sum_square`,
  `uq.UncertaintyBudget.worst_case_sum`, `uq.UncertaintyBudget.mixed_rule`,
  `uq.CombinedUncertainty`, `uq.QuantityKind`.
- Source: [REF-JCGM-100-2008, Sections 5.1.2 and 5.2.2].

### EQ-UQ-BUDGET-005 — Variance share of a budget entry

`share_i = c_i u_i (sum_j r_ij c_j u_j) / u_c^2`; the shares add to one,
reduce to `(c_i u_i)^2 / u_c^2` for independent inputs, and can be negative or
above one under correlation.

- Domain: `u_c > 0`; undefined (`nan`) when `u_c = 0`.
- Meaning: apportions the combined variance to the entries by splitting each
  covariance term equally between its two inputs.
- Code: `uq.UncertaintyBudget.contributions`, `uq.Contribution`,
  `uq.UncertaintyBudget.to_rows`, `uq.UncertaintyBudget.to_markdown`.
- Source: [REF-JCGM-100-2008, Sections 5.1.3 and 5.2.2].

### EQ-UQ-BUDGET-006 — Second-order check of the linearisation

For Gaussian inputs with covariance `S` and Hessian `H` of the model:
mean shift `tr(H S) / 2`, extra variance `tr(H S H S) / 2`, linear variance
`c' S c`; ratios `|shift| / u_c` and `sqrt(1 + extra / u_c^2) - 1` are
compared with a tolerance.

- Domain: Gaussian input approximation, twice-differentiable model; the
  third-derivative terms of the full second-order propagation are not
  included.
- Meaning: diagnoses a poor first-order propagation (curvature matters
  relative to the input spread); it does not replace the Monte Carlo
  validation of EQ-UQ-BUDGET-009.
- Code: `uq.budget_from_model`, `uq.LinearizationCheck`, `uq.ModelBudget`.
- Source: [REF-JCGM-100-2008, Section 5.1.2, Note],
  [REF-JCGM-101-2008, Section 5.8].

### EQ-UQ-BUDGET-007 — Monte Carlo estimate, standard uncertainty and coverage intervals

`y = (1/M) sum y_r`, `u^2(y) = sum (y_r - y)^2 / (M - 1)`. With sorted values
`y_(1) <= ... <= y_(M)`, `q = pM` (integer part of `pM + 1/2` otherwise), the
interval `[y_(r), y_(r+q)]` is a `100p %` coverage interval; symmetric:
`r = (M - q)/2` (integer part of `(M - q + 1)/2` otherwise); shortest: the
`r` minimising `y_(r+q) - y_(r)`. Monte Carlo errors: `u(y)/sqrt(M)` for `y`,
`u(y) sqrt((kurtosis - 1)/(4M))` for `u(y)`, and
`sqrt(a(1-a)/M) / g` for an endpoint at level `a` with the output density `g`
estimated from the spacing of order statistics.

- Domain: `M >= 20`, `0 < p < 1`, `M - q >= 1`, finite model values; the
  moments must exist.
- Meaning: summarises the discrete representation of the output distribution
  obtained by propagating the input distributions through the model.
- Code: `uq.monte_carlo_budget`, `uq.MonteCarloResult`,
  `uq.sample_coverage_intervals`.
- Source: [REF-JCGM-101-2008, Sections 5.3, 7.6 and 7.7.2],
  [REF-DAVID-NAGARAJA-2003].

### EQ-UQ-BUDGET-008 — Gaussian copula of correlated inputs

`z = L e` with `L L' = R` and `e ~ N(0, I)`, `u_i = Phi(z_i)`,
`x_i = F_i^(-1)(u_i)`. Marginals are the stated laws `F_i`; the dependence is
that of a Gaussian vector with correlation `R` on the normal scores. For
normal margins `R` is the Pearson correlation; the Spearman correlation of a
pair is `(6/pi) asin(r/2)`.

- Domain: `R` symmetric positive semidefinite with unit diagonal; margins
  with a quantile function.
- Meaning: one way to generate dependent inputs with prescribed margins; a
  modelling choice, not implied by a correlation coefficient alone.
- Code: `uq.monte_carlo_budget`.
- Source: [REF-NELSEN-2006], [REF-JCGM-101-2008, Section 6.4.8].

### EQ-UQ-BUDGET-009 — Validation of the GUM uncertainty framework by Monte Carlo

Numerical tolerance: write `u(y) = c x 10^l` with `c` an integer of `ndig`
decimal digits, then `delta = 10^l / 2`. The GUM interval is `y +/- U_p`;
`d_low = |y - U_p - y_low|`, `d_high = |y + U_p - y_high|`; the framework is
validated for the stated `p` if both are at most `delta`.

- Domain: `u(y) > 0`, `ndig >= 1`; holds for the stated coverage probability
  only.
- Meaning: compares the interval of the law of propagation with a Monte
  Carlo interval to the number of significant digits wanted in `u(y)`. For an
  adaptive Monte Carlo result (EQ-UQ-BUDGET-010) the flag
  `monte_carlo_adequate` is the Supplement's own test, twice each
  stabilisation deviation at most `delta / 5` (Section 8.2); for a result of
  fixed size it is a proxy built from the Monte Carlo standard errors.
- Code: `uq.compare_with_law_of_propagation`, `uq.numerical_tolerance`,
  `uq.GumValidation`.
- Source: [REF-JCGM-101-2008, Sections 7.9.2, 8.1.3 and 8.2].
## Schedule risk analysis

### EQ-COST-CPM-001 — Critical path method with precedence relations and lags

`ES_j = max(0, max over predecessors i of: EF_i + l (FS), ES_i + l (SS), EF_i + l - d_j (FF))`,
`EF_j = ES_j + d_j`, `T = max_j EF_j`; backward `LF_i = min(T, min over
successors j of: LS_j - l (FS), LS_j - l + d_i (SS), LF_j - l (FF))`,
`LS_i = LF_i - d_i`; total float `TF_i = LS_i - ES_i`; free float is the
smallest slack of the outgoing relations (`ES_j - EF_i - l`, `ES_j - ES_i - l`,
`EF_j - EF_i - l`, and `T - EF_i` for a sink).

- Domain: acyclic precedence graph, finite lags, non-negative durations.
- Meaning: an activity is critical when `TF_i = 0`; a critical path is a
  chain of critical activities joined by zero-slack relations, and its
  length is the project duration `T`.
- Code: `cost.critical_path`, `cost.ActivityNetwork`, `cost.Activity`,
  `cost.Precedence`.
- Source: [REF-KELLEY-WALKER-1959].

### EQ-COST-PERT-001 — Classical PERT normal approximation

`mu_T = sum_(i on path) mu_i`, `sigma_T^2 = sum_(i on path) sigma_i^2`,
`P(T <= t) ~ Phi((t - mu_T) / sigma_T)`; three-point estimates
`mu = (a + 4 m + b) / 6`, `sigma^2 = ((b - a) / 6)^2`.

- Domain: finish-to-start relations, independent durations, one critical path
  of the mean-duration network.
- Meaning: exact mean and variance for a series network of independent
  activities; otherwise optimistic, because `E max(T_1, T_2) >= max(E T_1,
  E T_2)` (Jensen) so the mean is biased low where paths merge, and the
  variance ignores the competing paths.
- Code: `cost.pert_estimate`, `cost.PertEstimate`, `cost.pert_three_point`.
- Source: [REF-MALCOLM-1959], [REF-MACCRIMMON-RYAVEC-1964].

### EQ-COST-SRA-001 — Criticality, cruciality, and schedule sensitivity index

`CI_i = P(TF_i = 0)`, estimated by the fraction of draws with zero total
float; cruciality `rho_i = corr(d_i, T)` (Pearson, and Spearman rank);
schedule sensitivity index `SSI_i = CI_i * sd(d_i) / sd(T)`.

- Domain: `n` independent draws of the network; `rho_i` and `SSI_i` are zero
  when `d_i` or `T` is constant.
- Meaning: probability that an activity lies on a critical path (Van Slyke),
  strength of the linear (or monotone) link between its duration and the
  completion time (Williams), and the criticality-weighted share of the
  completion spread an activity can explain. The SSI is a convention of
  schedule risk software, defined here, not quoted from a source.
- Code: `cost.simulate_schedule`, `cost.ActivityRisk`.
- Source: [REF-VAN-SLYKE-1963], [REF-WILLIAMS-1992], [REF-ELMAGHRABY-2000],
  [REF-GAO-16-89G].

### EQ-COST-SRA-002 — Completion-time distribution and deadline probability

`P(T <= t) = X / n` with `X ~ Binomial(n, P(T <= t))`; exact interval
`[Beta(alpha/2; X, n - X + 1), Beta(1 - alpha/2; X + 1, n - X)]`; quantile
interval from order statistics `[T_(l), T_(u)]` with exact coverage
`B(u - 1) - B(l - 1)`.

- Domain: independent draws; the Clopper-Pearson interval is conservative.
- Meaning: the empirical S-curve of the completion time, the confidence of
  meeting a deadline, and a distribution-free interval for any completion
  quantile.
- Code: `cost.ScheduleRiskResult.probability_by`,
  `cost.ScheduleRiskResult.quantile`, `cost.ScheduleRiskResult.s_curve`,
  `cost.DeadlineProbability`.
- Source: [REF-CLOPPER-PEARSON-1934], [REF-DAVID-NAGARAJA-2003],
  [REF-GAO-16-89G].

### EQ-COST-SRA-003 — Discrete schedule risk event

`d_i' = d_i + B * V`, `B ~ Bernoulli(p)`, `V` an impact law with quantile
function `Q`, drawn as `V = Q(U)` for `U ~ Uniform(0, 1)`.

- Domain: `0 <= p <= 1`, non-negative impacts, events independent of each
  other and of the durations.
- Meaning: a risk register entry that adds time to one activity when it
  occurs, so it enters both the critical path and the cost burn.
- Code: `cost.ScheduleRiskEvent`.
- Source: [REF-GAO-16-89G], [REF-NASA-PRA-2011].

### EQ-COST-LOAD-001 — Cost loading and joint cost-schedule confidence

`C = c_0 + sum_i F_i + sum_i r_i d_i + r_p T`, `JCL(C*, D) = P(C <= C*, T <= D)
<= min(P(C <= C*), P(T <= D))`, with equality to the product of marginals
only under independence.

- Domain: time-independent costs `F_i`, burn rates `r_i`, project rate `r_p`,
  each a number or a law drawn independently of the durations.
- Meaning: the pair (cost, completion) of one draw; because the burn terms
  grow with the durations, cost and completion are positively dependent. The
  iso-confidence frontier lists the smallest sampled cost with `JCL >= q` for
  each deadline.
- Code: `cost.cost_schedule_samples`, `cost.joint_cost_schedule_confidence`,
  `cost.cost_schedule_frontier`, `cost.IsoConfidenceFrontier`.
- Source: [REF-NASA-CEH-2015] (Appendix J, read: the joint confidence level
  as the probability of meeting both the cost and the schedule target, and
  probabilistic cost loading of a probabilistic schedule with time-dependent
  and time-independent costs, Section J.1.6.3, which is the structure of the
  sum above); the inequality is the probability identity stated.
### EQ-INF-ELICIT-001 — Quantile-function least squares for elicited judgements

`min_theta sum_i w_i (Q(p_i; theta) - v_i)^2` over the parameters `theta` of a
family with quantile function `Q`, for elicited pairs `(p_i, v_i)`. When `Q`
is linear in `theta` (`Q = a + b z(p)` with `z` the standard quantile:
normal, Student-t at fixed degrees of freedom, uniform with `z = p`) the
minimiser is the weighted regression line `b = S_zv / S_zz`,
`a = v_bar - b z_bar`; the residuals then satisfy `sum w r = 0` and
`sum w r z = 0`. The reported misfit is `sqrt(sum w r^2 / sum w)`.

- Domain: `2 <= n` strictly increasing probabilities in `(0, 1)` and
  strictly increasing values; at least as many pairs as free parameters;
  positive values for lognormal, gamma and Weibull; a stated interval for
  beta.
- Meaning: the law whose quantiles come closest, in value units, to the
  expert's statements; zero residual when the statements are exactly those
  of a member of the family.
- Code: `inference.fit_from_quantiles`, `inference.compare_elicited_fits`,
  `inference.elicitation._linear_fit`, `inference.elicitation._refine`.
- Source: [REF-OHAGAN-ETAL-2006], [REF-SHELF-OAKLEY-OHAGAN], [REF-MORE-1978].

### EQ-INF-ELICIT-002 — Three-point law from a mode and two quantiles

For a law `X = low + W B_m` with `B_m` on `[0, 1]` and mode fraction
`m = (mode - low)/W`, two stated quantiles `q_l`, `q_h` at `p_l < p_h` give
`(mode - q_l)/(q_h - q_l) = (m - B_m(p_l)) / (B_m(p_h) - B_m(p_l))`, solved for
`m in [0, 1]` by Brent's method, then
`W = (q_h - q_l)/(B_m(p_h) - B_m(p_l))` and `low = mode - m W`,
`high = low + W`.

- Domain: `q_l < q_h`, `0 < p_l < p_h < 1`, and a mode inside the interval
  the equation allows (it may lie below `q_l` or above `q_h` for skewed
  laws); otherwise there is no solution and the error states the interval.
- Meaning: the absolute bounds of a PERT or triangular law implied by a
  most likely value and, for example, 5 % and 95 % quantiles.
- Code: `inference.pert_from_quantiles`, `inference.triangular_from_quantiles`,
  `inference.elicitation._solve_three_point`.
- Source: [REF-MALCOLM-1959], [REF-VOSE-2008], [REF-KOTZ-VANDORP-2004].

### EQ-INF-ELICIT-003 — Linear and logarithmic opinion pools

Linear pool `f = sum_i w_i f_i`. Logarithmic pool
`g(x) = prod_i f_i(x)^(w_i) / Z`, `Z = int prod_i f_i^(w_i) dx`, with
`sum_i w_i = 1`. For normal experts `g` is normal with precision
`sum_i w_i / sigma_i^2` and mean `sum_i w_i mu_i / sigma_i^2` divided by that
precision. With a likelihood `L`, `prod_i (f_i L)^(w_i) = L prod_i f_i^(w_i)`,
so the logarithmic pool is externally Bayesian; the linear pool is not (its
posterior reweights `w_i` by the evidence of `f_i`).

- Domain: positive weights (normalised to sum one); the logarithmic pool
  needs experts whose densities overlap.
- Meaning: two ways of combining experts' densities; the linear pool keeps
  marginals and is multimodal under disagreement, the logarithmic pool
  concentrates between the experts.
- Code: `inference.linear_opinion_pool`, `inference.logarithmic_opinion_pool`,
  `inference.LogarithmicPool`.
- Source: [REF-GENEST-ZIDEK-1986], [REF-CLEMEN-WINKLER-1999].

### EQ-INF-ELICIT-004 — Quantile averaging (Vincentization)

`Q(p) = sum_i w_i Q_i(p)`, so `E[X] = sum_i w_i mu_i` and the density at
`x = Q(p)` is `1 / sum_i (w_i / f_i(Q_i(p)))`. For normal experts the pool is
`N(sum w_i mu_i, (sum w_i sigma_i)^2)`.

- Domain: positive weights summing to one; every `Q_i` finite on `(0, 1)`.
- Meaning: the pool of quantile functions keeps a location-scale family
  closed and averages scales, not variances.
- Code: `inference.quantile_average`, `inference.VincentizedLaw`.
- Source: [REF-CLEMEN-WINKLER-1999], [REF-GENEST-ZIDEK-1986].

### EQ-INF-ELICIT-005 — Cooke calibration score

With stated probabilities `p_1 < ... < p_k` the bins have theoretical
probabilities `pi_j = p_j - p_(j-1)` (`p_0 = 0`, `p_(k+1) = 1`) and empirical
frequencies `s_j` of the `N` realizations; `I(s, pi) = sum_j s_j ln(s_j / pi_j)`
(`0 ln 0 = 0`), and the calibration is
`C = 1 - F_(chi2, k)(2 N I(s, pi))`.

- Domain: `N >= 1` seed realizations, strictly increasing quantile rows.
- Meaning: the p-value of the likelihood-ratio test that the realizations are
  independent draws from the expert's stated bin probabilities (a
  chi-square approximation, adequate for moderate `N`); `C = 1` when
  `s = pi`.
- Code: `inference.cooke_calibration`, `inference.cooke_bin_probabilities`.
- Source: [REF-HANEA-NANE-2021] (Section 3.2.1, Eq. 1: statistic, bins and 3
  degrees of freedom for three percentiles; worked values 0.83 and 0.39
  reproduced), [REF-COOKE-1991] (not opened), [REF-CASELLA-BERGER-2002].

### EQ-INF-ELICIT-006 — Cooke information score and intrinsic range

On item `i` with intrinsic range `[L_i, U_i]` and expert quantiles
`q_1 < ... < q_k` the expert's density is uniform within each bin of
`(L_i, q_1, ..., q_k, U_i)` with mass `pi_j`; its relative information to the
uniform background is `sum_j pi_j ln(pi_j / mu_j)`, `mu_j` the background
measure of bin `j` (`(b - a)/(U - L)`, or `ln(b/a)/ln(U/L)` for the
log-uniform background). The score is the mean over items. The intrinsic
range is the hull of all experts' quantiles and the realization extended on
each side by `overshoot` times its width (on the log scale for the
log-uniform background).

- Domain: quantiles strictly inside the range; positive values for the
  log-uniform background.
- Meaning: how much narrower than the background the expert's statements
  are; independent of the realizations except through the range.
- Code: `inference.cooke_information`, `inference.cooke_intrinsic_ranges`,
  `inference.elicitation._item_information`.
- Source: [REF-HANEA-NANE-2021] (Section 3.1: intrinsic range and the 10 %
  overshoot default; Section 3.2.2, Eq. 2 and Table 2: information, reproduced
  to within one unit of the second decimal; the first two published entries
  are truncated, not rounded). The log-scale overshoot for the log-uniform
  background is a convention of this library. [REF-COOKE-1991] (not opened).

### EQ-INF-ELICIT-007 — Cooke weights and the global-weights decision maker

`w_e = C_e I_e 1{C_e >= alpha} / sum_k C_k I_k 1{C_k >= alpha}`. The decision
maker's density is `sum_e w_e f_e`, constant on the cells cut by all experts'
bin edges, with calibration and information computed from its own quantiles
and density on the seed items. The cut-off `alpha` is chosen among the
experts' calibration scores to maximise the decision maker's calibration
times information (the smaller cut-off on a tie).

- Domain: at least one expert with positive weight at the cut-off.
- Meaning: performance-based pooling that gives no weight to experts whose
  statistical accuracy is rejected at level `alpha`, with global (not
  item-specific) weights.
- Code: `inference.cooke_weights`, `inference.cooke_classical_model`,
  `inference.cooke_decision_maker_law`,
  `inference.elicitation._decision_maker_item`.
- Source: [REF-HANEA-NANE-2021] (Sections 3.3, 4 and 4.1: combined score,
  global weights, cut-off at the calibration scores, optimised decision
  maker), [REF-COOKE-1991] (not opened), [REF-NASA-PRA-2011].
## One-at-a-time swings and Fourier amplitude sensitivity testing

### EQ-SENS-TORNADO-001 — One-at-a-time swing and share of squared half-swings

`y_i^- = g(x_0 with x_i = a_i)`, `y_i^+ = g(x_0 with x_i = b_i)`,
`Delta_i = y_i^+ - y_i^-`, `share_i = (Delta_i / 2)^2 / sum_j (Delta_j / 2)^2`.

- Domain: a scalar function `g`, a baseline point `x_0`, and low and high
  values `a_i`, `b_i` per input (marginal quantiles at levels `p_- < p_+`, or
  explicit values); `1 + 2 d` evaluations.
- Meaning: the swing is the change of the output when one input moves alone
  between two values with the others held at the baseline; for a response
  linear in every input `Delta_i = c_i (b_i - a_i)` exactly, and the shares
  are the quadratic-sum shares of the linear model. It carries no
  information on interactions, on dependence between inputs, or on the
  response between `a_i` and `b_i`.
- Code: `sensitivity.tornado_analysis`, `sensitivity.tornado_function`,
  `sensitivity.TornadoBar`, `visualization.plot_tornado`.
- Source: [REF-HOWARD-1988] (display; bibliographic), [REF-SALTELLI-2008,
  Chapter 1]. The definition is elementary.

### EQ-SENS-TORNADO-002 — Non-monotonicity check from the baseline output

`flag_i = [ y_0 < min(y_i^-, y_i^+) or y_0 > max(y_i^-, y_i^+) ]` when
`a_i <= x_0,i <= b_i`.

- Domain: the baseline lies between the low and the high value of the input.
- Meaning: if `g` restricted to the segment were monotone, the value at an
  interior point would lie between the two end values; a violation proves an
  extremum inside `[a_i, b_i]`. The converse fails: an S-shaped response
  passes the check.
- Code: `sensitivity.tornado._bars`, `sensitivity.TornadoBar.nonmonotone`.
- Source: elementary (intermediate-value argument).

### EQ-SENS-FAST-001 — FAST search curve with random phase

`u_k(s) = 1/2 + arcsin(sin(omega_k s + phi_k)) / pi`, `x_k = F_k^-1(u_k)`,
`s_j = 2 pi (j - (N - 1)/2) / N`, `j = 0, ..., N - 1`, `N` odd.

- Domain: `s` uniform on `(-pi, pi)`, integer frequencies `omega_k`, phases
  `phi_k` uniform on `(0, 2 pi)`, independent inputs with quantile functions
  `F_k^-1`.
- Meaning: for every `k` the point `u_k(s)` is uniform on `(0, 1)` when `s`
  is uniform, so `x_k` has the law `F_k`; for incommensurate integer
  frequencies the curve fills the unit cube in the sense of Weyl's
  equidistribution theorem (exact quadrature of low-order trigonometric
  polynomials on the grid `s_j`).
- Code: `sensitivity.fast._triangle`, `sensitivity.fast._extended_fast`.
- Source: [REF-CUKIER-1973], [REF-SALTELLI-TARANTOLA-CHAN-1999] (both
  bibliographic); re-derived.

### EQ-SENS-FAST-002 — Partial variances and indices of extended FAST

`c_k = (1/N) sum_j y_j exp(-i k s_j)`, `A_k = 2 |c_k|^2`,
`V = sum_(k=1)^((N-1)/2) A_k` (Parseval, equal to the population variance),
`V_i = sum_(p=1)^M A_(p omega_i)`, `V_(-i) = sum_(k=1)^(floor(omega_i / 2)) A_k`,
`S_i = V_i / V`, `S_Ti = 1 - V_(-i) / V`.

- Domain: `omega_i` the high frequency of the input of interest, all other
  frequencies at most `omega_i / (2 M)`, and `M omega_i <= (N - 1) / 2`.
- Meaning: the harmonics of `omega_i` carry the part of the output variance
  that depends on `x_i` alone (first order); everything that does not depend
  on `x_i` lives at frequencies reachable from the low-frequency set, that
  is up to `M omega_c <= omega_i / 2`, so one minus its share is the total
  effect. Truncation at `M` harmonics biases both estimates for responses
  with sharp features; the error is set by `M`, not by `N`.
- Code: `sensitivity.fast_analysis`, `sensitivity.fast_indices`,
  `sensitivity.FastResult`.
- Source: [REF-CUKIER-1973], [REF-SALTELLI-TARANTOLA-CHAN-1999]
  (bibliographic); [REF-SALTELLI-2008, Chapter 5]. Re-derived.

### EQ-SENS-FAST-003 — Frequency plan and sample-size rule

`omega_max = floor((N - 1) / (2 M))`, complementary frequencies distinct
integers in `1 .. floor(omega_max / (2 M))`, equally spaced and, for `d >= 3`,
at least two apart; hence `N >= 2 M omega_max + 1` and
`N >= 4 M^2 max(2 d - 3, 1) + 1`.

- Domain: `M >= 1` harmonics, `d` inputs, `N` odd.
- Meaning: the highest analysed harmonic `M omega_max` must stay below the
  Nyquist index `N / 2`; the `d - 1` low frequencies must be distinct (equal
  frequencies make two inputs move along one line); the harmonics of the low
  set up to order `M` then end at `omega_max / 2`, below `omega_max`. The
  spacing of at least two is an empirical rule of this library: with the
  consecutive pair (1, 2) the largest Ishigami first-order error over twenty
  seeds (`M = 4`, three resamples) was 0.18 at `N = 129`, 193 and 385, with
  (1, 3) it was 0.03. It is not part of the published frequency plan: the
  open descriptions of extended FAST give `omega = (N - 1) / (2 M)`, a largest
  complementary frequency `omega / (2 M)` and the others spread uniformly
  between 1 and it (a set that coincides with this one wherever this library
  accepts the curve length) and no spacing rule, so they accept shorter curves.
- Code: `sensitivity.fast_sample_size`, `sensitivity.fast_frequencies`.
- Source: [REF-SALTELLI-TARANTOLA-CHAN-1999] (the paper itself was not opened;
  the frequency plan was compared with the OpenTURNS theory page and the R
  `sensitivity::fast99` source, which implement it); re-derived.

### EQ-SENS-RBD-001 — Random balance design first-order estimator

`u_i(k) = tau(s_(sigma_i(k)))` with `tau(s) = 1/2 + arcsin(sin s) / pi`,
independent random permutations `sigma_i` of `0 .. N - 1`;
`y'_j = y_(sigma_i^-1(j))`, `c_m = (1/N) sum_j y'_j exp(-i m s_j)`,
`S_i^raw = (2 sum_(m=1)^M |c_m|^2) / V`.

- Domain: independent inputs, `N` odd, `2 M < N`.
- Meaning: after re-ordering the output along input `i` the first harmonics
  of frequency one carry the variance explained by `x_i`; the other inputs
  are in random order and add noise to the spectrum.
- Code: `sensitivity.rbd_fast_analysis`, `sensitivity.rbd_fast_indices`,
  `sensitivity.RBDFastResult`.
- Source: [REF-TARANTOLA-GATELLI-MARA-2006] (bibliographic),
  [REF-TISSOT-PRIEUR-2012] (Eqs. 21-23, read). Re-derived.

### EQ-SENS-RBD-002 — Bias correction of the random balance estimator

`E|c_m|^2 = |c_m^true|^2 + V_(-i) / N`, hence
`E[S_i^raw] = S_i + lambda (1 - S_i)`, `lambda = 2 M / N`, and
`S_i^corr = (S_i^raw - lambda) / (1 - lambda)`.

- Domain: `2 M < N`; `V_(-i) = V (1 - S_i)` is the variance not due to `x_i`
  alone.
- Meaning: the discrete transform of white noise of variance `V_(-i)` has
  expected power `V_(-i) / N` at each frequency, and `2 M` coefficients are
  summed, so the raw estimator is biased upwards by `lambda (1 - S_i)`; the
  correction inverts that relation. It can return small negative values for
  an input without effect.
- Code: `sensitivity.fast._rbd`.
- Source: [REF-TISSOT-PRIEUR-2012] (Eqs. 26-31, read); the white-noise
  derivation is elementary.
### EQ-MVN-DISC-001 — Gaussian probability of a disc by rotated one-dimensional quadrature

`P(||X|| <= R) = int_(-R)^(R) phi((u - a1)/s1)/s1 * [Phi((h(u) - a2)/s2) - Phi((-h(u) - a2)/s2)] du`,
`h(u) = sqrt(R^2 - u^2)`, with `(a1, a2) = V'mu` and `(s1^2, s2^2)` the
eigenvalues of `Sigma = V diag(s1^2, s2^2) V'`; evaluated with `u = R sin(theta)`.

- Domain: `X ~ N(mu, Sigma)` in two dimensions, `Sigma` symmetric positive
  definite, `R > 0`; the range is cut to `a1 +/- 40 s1`.
- Meaning: the coordinates along the principal axes are independent normal;
  the inner integral over the chord at abscissa `u` is a normal interval
  probability. It is the short-encounter collision probability when `X` is the
  miss vector in the encounter plane and `R` the combined hard-body radius.
  The error reported is the Gauss-Kronrod estimate, not a bound.
- Code: `multivariate.gaussian_disc_probability`,
  `multivariate.ball_probability._normal_interval`.
- Source: [REF-NASA-CARA-HANDBOOK] (Appendix N, Eq. N-1: the disc integral
  of Foster and Estes; Eq. N-2: the error-function form of Alfano, used as a
  test oracle), [REF-FOSTER-ESTES-1992] and [REF-ALFANO-2005] (neither
  opened). The rotated quadrature itself is derived here.

### EQ-MVN-RICE-001 — Isotropic ball probability as a noncentral chi-square law

`P(||X|| <= R) = sum_(j>=0) e^(-lambda/2) (lambda/2)^j / j! * P(chi2_(n+2j) <= R^2/s^2)`,
`lambda = ||mu||^2 / s^2`, for `X ~ N(mu, s^2 I_n)`; for `n = 2` equal to
`1 - Q_1(||mu||/s, R/s)`.

- Domain: `s > 0`, `R > 0`, integer `n >= 1`.
- Meaning: `||X||^2/s^2` is noncentral chi-square; the Poisson mixture
  representation gives a truncation bound (neglected Poisson tail mass
  times the largest neglected chi-square value); the reported estimate adds an
  empirical rounding allowance and is not labelled rigorous.
- Code: `multivariate.isotropic_gaussian_ball_probability`,
  `multivariate.noncentral_chi_square_cdf`,
  `multivariate.ball_probability._poisson_chi_square`.
- Source: [REF-JOHNSON-KOTZ-BALAKRISHNAN-1995]; derived here (the Rice-law
  form could not be attributed to [REF-CHAN-2008], which was not opened).

### EQ-MVN-BALL-001 — Ruben series for a positive-definite quadratic form

`P(sum_i lambda_i (z_i + b_i)^2 <= x) = sum_(k>=0) a_k P(chi2_(n+2k) <= x/beta)`,
`a_0 = prod_i sqrt(beta/lambda_i) e^(-b_i^2/2)`, `a_k = (1/k) sum_(j=1)^k d_j a_(k-j)`,
`d_j = sum_i [ r_i^j/2 + j b_i^2 (1 - r_i) r_i^(j-1)/2 ]`, `r_i = 1 - beta/lambda_i`,
`0 < beta <= lambda_min`. Truncation after `K` terms is bounded by
`(1 - sum_(k<K) a_k) P(chi2_(n+2K) <= x/beta)`.

- Domain: `lambda_i > 0`, real `b_i`, `x > 0`. With `r_i in [0, 1)` the
  Laplace transform of the form equals `sum_k a_k (1 + 2 s beta)^(-(n+2k)/2)`
  with `a_k >= 0` and `sum a_k = 1` (a product of power series with
  non-negative coefficients evaluating to one at `v = 1`).
- Meaning: the squared norm of `N(mu, Sigma)` is a non-negative mixture of
  scaled central chi-square laws, which gives `P(||X|| <= R)` in any
  dimension with a rigorous error bound (up to rounding of the weight sum).
- Code: `multivariate.gaussian_ball_probability`.
- Source: [REF-RUBEN-1962], [REF-SHEIL-OMUIRCHEARTAIGH-1977], [REF-IMHOF-1961].

### EQ-MVN-SMALLDISC-001 — Small-disc approximation and its first correction

`int_(||x||<=R) f dx = pi R^2 f(0) + (pi R^4/8) Laplacian f(0) + O(R^6)`;
for the Gaussian `f(0) = exp(-m'S^-1 m/2) / (2 pi sqrt(det S))` and
`Laplacian f(0) = f(0) (||S^-1 m||^2 - tr S^-1)`.

- Domain: two dimensions, smooth density on the disc, `R` small against the
  scales of `f`.
- Meaning: density at the disc centre times its area, with the mean-value
  expansion of a smooth function over a disc supplying the stated error.
- Code: `multivariate.small_disc_probability`.
- Source: elementary (mean-value expansion of a smooth function over a
  disc); not attributed to [REF-CHAN-2008] (not opened).

### EQ-MVN-DILUTION-001 — Maximum disc probability over a covariance scale

`p_max = max_(c > 0) P(||X_c|| <= R)`, `X_c ~ N(mu, c Sigma)`, `||mu|| > R`;
for `Sigma = s^2 I` and `R << ||mu||` the maximum is `R^2 / (e ||mu||^2)` at
`c s^2 = ||mu||^2 / 2`.

- Domain: two dimensions, mean outside the disc (for `||mu|| < R` the
  supremum is one, approached as `c -> 0`; for `||mu|| = R` it is one half,
  the half disc seen from the boundary point).
- Meaning: the probability vanishes at both ends of the scale range, so a
  larger covariance can raise it ("dilution"). Located numerically; for the
  small isotropic disc the closed form follows from maximising
  `(R^2/(2t)) exp(-||mu||^2/(2t))` over `t = c s^2`.
- Code: `multivariate.maximum_disc_probability`.
- Source: [REF-ALFANO-2005B] (not opened; the maximum over the covariance
  scale and the term probability dilution are attributed to it in Section
  M.4 of [REF-NASA-CARA-HANDBOOK], which was read); derived and tested here.

### EQ-FILT-NEES-001 — Normalised squared error

`epsilon = e' P^-1 e`, `e = x - x_hat`; for `e ~ N(0, P)` in `n` dimensions
`epsilon ~ chi2(n)`. With an innovation `v` and its covariance `S` the same
form is the NIS, `v' S^-1 v ~ chi2(m)`.

- Domain: `P` symmetric positive definite; Gaussian error under the null.
- Meaning: squared Mahalanobis length of the error, computed through the
  Cholesky factor `P = L L'` as `||L^-1 e||^2`.
- Code: `filtering.nees`, `filtering.nees_series`,
  `filtering.nees_from_filter`, `filtering.nis_series`.
- Source: [REF-BAR-SHALOM-LI-KIRUBARAJAN-2001], [REF-MARDIA-KENT-BIBBY-1979].

### EQ-FILT-NEES-002 — Monte-Carlo average NEES acceptance interval

`N * mean_i epsilon_(i,k) ~ chi2(N n)`; acceptance interval
`[chi2_(alpha/2)(N n)/N, chi2_(1-alpha/2)(N n)/N]` at each step `k`.

- Domain: `N` independent runs with a consistent filter; the time mean of the
  averages is compared with the same interval (conservative because its
  variance does not exceed the per-step variance).
- Meaning: above the interval the covariance is too small (optimistic), below
  too large (pessimistic).
- Code: `filtering.nees_test`, `filtering.nees_test_from_filters`.
- Source: [REF-BAR-SHALOM-LI-KIRUBARAJAN-2001].

### EQ-FILT-NIS-001 — Time-average NIS acceptance interval

`sum_k v_k' S_k^-1 v_k ~ chi2(D)`, `D = sum_k m_k`; the mean over `T` steps lies
in `[chi2_(alpha/2)(D)/T, chi2_(1-alpha/2)(D)/T]` for white, correctly scaled
innovations.

- Domain: one run, independent Gaussian innovations with the stated
  covariances; missing steps are omitted.
- Meaning: a truth-free consistency check of the innovation covariance.
- Code: `filtering.nis_test`, `filtering.nis_test_from_filter`.
- Source: [REF-BAR-SHALOM-LI-KIRUBARAJAN-2001].

### EQ-FILT-WHITE-001 — Innovation autocorrelation and portmanteau statistic

`rho(tau) = sum_k z_k' z_(k+tau) / sum_k z_k' z_k`, `z_k = L_k^-1 v_k`;
per-lag bound `z_((1+c)/2)/sqrt(T m)`; `Q = T m (T + 2) sum_(tau=1)^L rho(tau)^2/(T - tau)`
approximately `chi2(L)`.

- Domain: standardised innovations of dimension `m`, `T` observed steps.
- Meaning: tests that the innovations are serially uncorrelated, the
  assumption behind the NIS interval.
- Code: `filtering.innovation_whiteness_test`.
- Source: [REF-BAR-SHALOM-LI-KIRUBARAJAN-2001], [REF-LJUNG-BOX-1978].

### EQ-FILT-REALISM-001 — Covariance scale factor and its confidence interval

`s = (1/(N n)) sum_i d_i^2`, `d_i^2 = e_i' P_i^-1 e_i`; if `Cov(e_i) = c P_i`
then `N n s / c ~ chi2(N n)` and
`c in [N n s/chi2_(1-alpha/2)(N n), N n s/chi2_(alpha/2)(N n)]`.

- Domain: `N` independent Gaussian errors; shape judged by Kolmogorov-Smirnov,
  Cramer-von Mises [EQ-INF-GOF-CVM-004] and Anderson-Darling tests of
  `d_i^2` against `chi2(n)`.
- Meaning: the multiplier by which the covariances should be inflated
  (above one: too small).
- Code: `filtering.covariance_realism`.
- Source: [REF-NASA-CARA-HANDBOOK] (Appendix I: squared Mahalanobis
  distances against a chi-square law, the first-moment scale factor, and
  empirical-distribution tests; the handbook has no confidence interval for
  the factor and recommends Cramer-von Mises, offered as
  `test="cramer-von-mises"`),
  [REF-HORWOOD-ETAL-2014] (not opened), [REF-BAR-SHALOM-LI-KIRUBARAJAN-2001].

### EQ-FILT-GMSPLIT-001 — Univariate Gaussian splitting by L2 minimisation

`J(w) = int (sum_i w_i N(x; i h, s^2) - N(x; 0, 1))^2 dx
= sum_(i,j) w_i w_j N(h(i - j); 0, 2 s^2) - 2 sum_i w_i N(i h; 0, 1 + s^2) + N(0; 0, 2)`,
minimised over symmetric positive weights with `h^2 sum_i w_i i^2 = 1 - s^2`.

- Domain: odd `N`, `i = -K..K`, `0 < s < 1`.
- Meaning: the product integral of two Gaussians is a Gaussian value, so the
  distance is a finite double sum; the variance condition fixes the spacing,
  and symmetry fixes the mean, so every candidate has the exact mean 0 and
  variance 1 of the standard normal.
- Code: `filtering.univariate_splitting`,
  `filtering.gaussian_mixture._squared_l2`.
- Source: derived here. Published libraries read for comparison: Table 3 of
  [REF-ZANETTI-ETAL-PREPRINT] (Kullback-Leibler, variance preserved, consistent
  with the spacing relation to nine digits), its Table 2 (the library of
  [REF-DEMARS-BISHOP-JAH-2013], paper not read; second moment 0.9548 as
  printed) and Table I of [REF-HUBER-ETAL-2008] (second moment 0.9273).

### EQ-FILT-GMSPLIT-002 — Multivariate split along a direction

`m_i = m + h_i d/sqrt(q)`, `C = P - (1 - s^2) d d'/q`, `q = d' P^-1 d`; then
`sum_i w_i m_i = m` and `sum_i w_i [C + (m_i - m)(m_i - m)'] = P`.

- Domain: `P` positive definite, `d != 0`.
- Meaning: the split acts on the unit vector `P^-1/2 d` in whitened
  coordinates; the variance along it shrinks to `s^2`, orthogonal directions
  are untouched, and `sum_i w_i h_i^2 = 1 - s^2` restores the covariance.
- Code: `filtering.split_gaussian`.
- Source: [REF-DEMARS-BISHOP-JAH-2013], [REF-VITTALDEV-RUSSELL-2016].

### EQ-FILT-GMPROP-001 — Mixture moments and component-wise unscented propagation

`m = sum_i w_i m_i`, `P = sum_i w_i [P_i + (m_i - m)(m_i - m)']`; the image
of component `i` under `g` has mean and covariance from the unscented
transform of `N(m_i, C_i)`.

- Domain: weights non-negative summing to one.
- Meaning: law of total expectation and variance; for an affine `g` the
  result is `A m + b` and `A P A'` exactly.
- Code: `filtering.GaussianMixtureState.mean`,
  `filtering.GaussianMixtureState.covariance`,
  `filtering.propagate_gaussian_mixture`,
  `filtering.propagate_gaussian_mixture_procedure`.
- Source: [REF-SORENSON-ALSPACH-1971], [REF-JULIER-UHLMANN-2004].

### EQ-FILT-GMPROP-002 — Relative curvature index of a map over a Gaussian

`kappa = max_i || (g(m + s_i) + g(m - s_i))/2 - g(m) || / sqrt(tr C_y)`,
`s_i` the unscented sigma-point offsets, `C_y` the unscented output covariance.

- Domain: deterministic `g`, positive-definite input covariance.
- Meaning: zero for an affine `g`; the second-order part of the image
  relative to its spread, available without extra evaluations. It drives the
  recursive refinement and is a design choice of this library, not a
  published criterion.
- Code: `filtering.nonlinearity_index`,
  `filtering.gaussian_mixture._curvature_index`.
- Source: [REF-JULIER-UHLMANN-2004], [REF-DEMARS-BISHOP-JAH-2013].

### EQ-UQ-BUDGET-010 — Adaptive Monte Carlo procedure and its stopping rule

Run batches of `M = max(ceil(100 / (1 - p)), 10^4)` trials; batch `r` gives
`y^(r)`, `u(y^(r))` and the endpoints `y_low^(r)`, `y_high^(r)` of a `100p %`
coverage interval. After `h >= 2` batches, for each of the four per-batch
quantities `v^(r)`: `s_v^2 = sum_r (v^(r) - vbar)^2 / (h (h - 1))`. With
`u(y)` from all `h M` values written `c x 10^l` (`c` an integer of `ndig`
digits), `delta = 10^l / 2`. The computation has stabilised when
`2 s_y`, `2 s_u(y)`, `2 s_ylow` and `2 s_yhigh` are all at most `delta`
(it continues if any *exceeds* `delta`); the result is then computed from all
`h M` values. Validating the GUM framework uses `delta / 5` (Section 8.2).

- Domain: `0 < p < 1`, `ndig >= 1`, finite model values with `u(y) > 0`,
  `M >= 20`. The clause gives no probability that the stabilised numbers meet
  `delta` (Section 7.9.3, Note 1); when the batch limit is reached first the
  record says `stabilized = False`.
- Meaning: the sample standard deviation of the average of `h` independent
  batch values, used as the Monte Carlo error of each of the four reported
  numbers; the factor 2 is a Gaussian 95 % rule (Note 6). Stopping at the
  earliest `h` at which the test passes makes the realised error somewhat
  larger than the nominal one.
- Code: `uq.adaptive_monte_carlo_budget`,
  `uq.adaptive_monte_carlo_budget_procedure`, `uq.AdaptiveMonteCarloResult`,
  `uq.average_standard_deviation`, `uq.adaptive_stopping_rule`,
  `uq.budget._clause_batch_size`.
- Source: [REF-JCGM-101-2008, Sections 7.9.2-7.9.4 and 8.2].

### EQ-INF-GOF-CVM-002 — Limiting Cramer-von Mises distribution (Bessel series)

`V(x) = lim P(W_n^2 <= x) = (pi^(3/2) sqrt(x))^(-1) sum_(j>=0)
(Gamma(j + 1/2)/j!) sqrt(4j + 1) exp(-q_j) K_(1/4)(q_j)`,
`q_j = (4j + 1)^2/(16 x)`, the law of `sum_(k>=1) Z_k^2/(k pi)^2` with
independent standard normal `Z_k`. `K_nu(z) = int_0^inf exp(-z cosh t)
cosh(nu t) dt` is evaluated by the trapezoidal rule.

- Domain: `x > 0`; fully specified continuous null, `n -> infinity`.
- Meaning: the null law of the Cramer-von Mises statistic for a large sample;
  its mean is `1/6`, its second moment `1/20`, and its 95 and 99 percent
  points are `0.461361` and `0.743459`. The trapezoidal Bessel evaluation
  agrees with the reference function to about `1e-15` relative.
- Code: `inference.cramer_von_mises_asymptotic_cdf`,
  `inference.cramer_von_mises_asymptotic_sf`.
- Source: [REF-ANDERSON-DARLING-1952] (the limit law) and
  [REF-CSORGO-FARAWAY-1996, equations 1.2 and 1.3] (the series, confirmed
  bibliographically; checked here against a 60-digit evaluation).

### EQ-INF-GOF-CVM-003 — Upper tail of the limiting Cramer-von Mises law
